passages.original: “It was because I heard father and mother,” he explained in a low voice, “talking about what I was to be when I became a man.” He was extraordinarily agitated now. “I don’t want ever to be a man,” he said with passion. “I want always to be a little boy and to have fun. So I ran away to Kensington Gardens and lived a long long time among the fairies.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗰個係因為我聽到爸爸媽媽,」佢低聲解釋,「喺談我長大成人後該做乜嘢。」佢而家異常激動。「我永遠唔想長大,」佢激動地講。「我想永遠做一個小男孩,玩得開心。所以我逃到肯辛頓花園,喺仙子哋中間生活咗好長好長時間。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那是因為我聽到爸爸媽媽,」他低聲解釋,「在談我長大成人後該做什麼。」他現在異常激動。「我永遠不想長大,」他激動地說。「我想永遠做一個小男孩,玩得開心。所以我逃到肯辛頓花園,在仙子們中間生活了很長很長時間。」

passages.original: She gave him a look of the most intense admiration, and he thought it was because he had run away, but it was really because he knew fairies. Wendy had lived such a home life that to know fairies struck her as quite delightful. She poured out questions about them, to his surprise, for they were rather a nuisance to him, getting in his way and so on, and indeed he sometimes had to give them a hiding. Still, he liked them on the whole, and he told her about the beginning of fairies.
passages.vernacular: 佢畀咗佢一個最強烈欽佩嘅眼神,佢以為嗰個係因為佢逃走喇,但其實係因為佢認識仙子。溫蒂過嘅係咁居家嘅生活,能認識仙子喺佢睇來相當令人愉快。佢對仙子連珠炮似地提問,呢使佢食驚,因為仙子對佢來講相當討厭,擋佢嘅路等等,事實上佢有時唔得不揍佢哋一頓。不過,總嘅來講佢定係鍾意佢哋,佢告訴佢仙子嘅起源。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她給了他一個最強烈欽佩的眼神,他以為那是因為他逃走了,但其實是因為他認識仙子。溫蒂過的是那麼居家的生活,能認識仙子在她看來相當令人愉快。她對仙子連珠炮似地提問,這使他吃驚,因為仙子對他來說相當討厭,擋他的路等等,事實上他有時不得不揍她們一頓。不過,總的來說他還是喜歡她們,他告訴她仙子的起源。

passages.original: “You see, Wendy, when the first baby laughed for the first time, its laugh broke into a thousand pieces, and they all went skipping about, and that was the beginning of fairies.”
passages.vernacular: 「你睇,溫蒂,第一個嬰兒第一次笑嘅時候,佢嘅笑聲碎成一千片,佢哋都蹦蹦跳跳地跑開,嗰個就係仙子嘅開始。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你看,溫蒂,第一個嬰兒第一次笑的時候,他的笑聲碎成一千片,它們都蹦蹦跳跳地跑開,那就是仙子的開始。」

passages.original: Tedious talk this, but being a stay-at-home she liked it.
passages.vernacular: 呢話好乏味,但作為一個宅喺家裡嘅人,佢鍾意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這話很乏味,但作為一個宅在家裡的人,她喜歡。

passages.original: “And so,” he went on good-naturedly, “there ought to be one fairy for every boy and girl.”
passages.vernacular: 「所以,」佢和氣地繼續講,「每個男孩同女孩都應該有一個仙子。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「所以,」他和氣地繼續說,「每個男孩和女孩都應該有一個仙子。」

passages.original: “Ought to be? Isn’t there?”
passages.vernacular: 「應該有?冇嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「應該有?沒有嗎?」

passages.original: “No. You see children know such a lot now, they soon don’t believe in fairies, and every time a child says, ‘I don’t believe in fairies,’ there is a fairy somewhere that falls down dead.”
passages.vernacular: 「冇。你睇而家細路哋懂得咁多,佢哋好快就不相信仙子喇,每次有細路講『我不相信仙子』,某處就有一個仙子倒下死去。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「沒有。你看現在孩子們懂得那麼多,他們很快就不相信仙子了,每次有孩子說『我不相信仙子』,某處就有一個仙子倒下死去。」

passages.original: Really, he thought they had now talked enough about fairies, and it struck him that Tinker Bell was keeping very quiet. “I can’t think where she has gone to,” he said, rising, and he called Tink by name. Wendy’s heart went flutter with a sudden thrill.
passages.vernacular: 講真嘅,佢認為佢哋而家關於仙子談得夠多喇,佢突然覺得叮噹好安靜。「我想不出佢去邊度喇,」佢站起來講,叫咗叮嘅名字。溫蒂嘅心突然一陣激動地撲通撲通跳。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 說真的,他認為他們現在關於仙子談得夠多了,他突然覺得叮噹很安靜。「我想不出她去哪裡了,」他站起來說,叫了叮的名字。溫蒂的心突然一陣激動地撲通撲通跳。

passages.original: “Peter,” she cried, clutching him, “you don’t mean to tell me that there is a fairy in this room!”
passages.vernacular: 「彼得,」佢抓住佢喊道,「你唔係要告訴我呢個房間裡有一個仙子吧!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「彼得,」她抓住他喊道,「你不是要告訴我這個房間裡有一個仙子吧!」

passages.original: “She was here just now,” he said a little impatiently. “You don’t hear her, do you?” and they both listened.
passages.vernacular: 「佢頭先仲喺呢度,」佢有點不耐煩地講。「你聽唔到佢嗎?」佢哋都聽住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她剛才還在這裡,」他有點不耐煩地說。「你聽不到她嗎?」他們都聽著。

passages.original: “The only sound I hear,” said Wendy, “is like a tinkle of bells.”
passages.vernacular: 「我唯一聽到嘅聲音,」溫蒂講,「像鈴鐺嘅叮噹聲。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我唯一聽到的聲音,」溫蒂說,「像鈴鐺的叮噹聲。」

passages.original: “Well, that’s Tink, that’s the fairy language. I think I hear her too.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,嗰個就係叮,嗰個係仙子語。我想我都聽到佢喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,那就是叮,那是仙子語。我想我也聽到她了。」

passages.original: The sound came from the chest of drawers, and Peter made a merry face. No one could ever look quite so merry as Peter, and the loveliest of gurgles was his laugh. He had his first laugh still.
passages.vernacular: 聲音來自五斗櫃,彼得做咗個開心嘅臉。冇人能像彼得嗰樣開心,佢嘅笑聲係最可愛嘅咯咯聲。佢仲有佢嘅第一次笑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 聲音來自五斗櫃,彼得做了個開心的臉。沒有人能像彼得那樣開心,他的笑聲是最可愛的咯咯聲。他還有他的第一次笑。

passages.original: “Wendy,” he whispered gleefully, “I do believe I shut her up in the drawer!”
passages.vernacular: 「溫蒂,」佢高興地低語,「我真嘅相信我把佢關喺抽屜裡喇!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「溫蒂,」他高興地低語,「我真的相信我把她關在抽屜裡了!」

passages.original: He let poor Tink out of the drawer, and she flew about the nursery screaming with fury. “You shouldn’t say such things,” Peter retorted. “Of course I’m very sorry, but how could I know you were in the drawer?”
passages.vernacular: 佢把可憐嘅叮從抽屜裡放出嚟,佢喺育兒室裡飛嚟飛去,憤怒地尖叫。「你不該講呢種話,」彼得反駁。「我當然好抱歉,但我點知道你喺抽屜裡?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他把可憐的叮從抽屜裡放出來,她在育兒室裡飛來飛去,憤怒地尖叫。「你不該說這種話,」彼得反駁。「我當然很抱歉,但我怎麼知道你在抽屜裡?」

passages.original: Wendy was not listening to him. “O Peter,” she cried, “if she would only stand still and let me see her!”
passages.vernacular: 溫蒂冇聽佢講話。「哦,彼得,」佢喊道,「要係佢能停一停讓我睇睇佢就好喇!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 溫蒂沒有聽他說話。「哦,彼得,」她喊道,「要是她能停一停讓我看看她就好了!」

passages.original: “They hardly ever stand still,” he said, but for one moment Wendy saw the romantic figure come to rest on the cuckoo clock. “O the lovely!” she cried, though Tink’s face was still distorted with passion.
passages.vernacular: 「佢哋幾乎從不停下嚟,」佢講,但溫蒂有一刻睇到嗰浪漫嘅身影停喺布穀鳥鐘上。「哦,多可愛!」佢喊道,雖然叮嘅臉仍因憤怒而扭曲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她們幾乎從不停下來,」他說,但溫蒂有一刻看到那浪漫的身影停在布穀鳥鐘上。「哦,多可愛!」她喊道,雖然叮的臉仍因憤怒而扭曲。

passages.original: “Tink,” said Peter amiably, “this lady says she wishes you were her fairy.”
passages.vernacular: 「叮,」彼得和藹地講,「呢位女士講佢希望你係佢嘅仙子。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「叮,」彼得和藹地說,「這位女士說她希望你是她的仙子。」

passages.original: Tinker Bell answered insolently.
passages.vernacular: 叮噹無禮地回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 叮噹無禮地回答。

passages.original: “What does she say, Peter?”
passages.vernacular: 「佢講乜嘢,彼得?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她說什麼,彼得?」

passages.original: He had to translate. “She is not very polite. She says you are a great ugly girl, and that she is my fairy.”
passages.vernacular: 佢唔得不翻譯。「佢不太禮貌。佢講你係個又大又醜嘅女孩,講佢係我嘅仙子。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他不得不翻譯。「她不太禮貌。她說你是個又大又醜的女孩,說她是我的仙子。」

passages.original: He tried to argue with Tink. “You know you can’t be my fairy, Tink, because I am an gentleman and you are a lady.”
passages.vernacular: 佢試圖同叮爭論。「你知道你唔能夠做我嘅仙子,叮,因為我係紳士而你係女士。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他試圖同叮爭論。「你知道你不能做我的仙子,叮,因為我是紳士而你是女士。」

passages.original: To this Tink replied in these words, “You silly ass,” and disappeared into the bathroom. “She is quite a common fairy,” Peter explained apologetically, “she is called Tinker Bell because she mends the pots and kettles.”
passages.vernacular: 對此叮用呢啲話回答:「你呢個蠢驢,」然後消失喺浴室裡。「佢係個相當平凡嘅仙子,」彼得抱歉地解釋,「佢叫叮噹,因為佢修補鍋碗壺罐。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 對此叮用這些話回答:「你這個蠢驢,」然後消失在浴室裡。「她是個相當平凡的仙子,」彼得抱歉地解釋,「她叫叮噹,因為她修補鍋碗壺罐。」

passages.original: They were together in the armchair by this time, and Wendy plied him with more questions.
passages.vernacular: 呢陣佢哋一起坐喺扶手椅裡,溫蒂不斷向佢提出更多問題。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這時他們一起坐在扶手椅裡,溫蒂不斷向他提出更多問題。

passages.original: “If you don’t live in Kensington Gardens now—”
passages.vernacular: 「如果你而家不住喺肯辛頓花園——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「如果你現在不住在肯辛頓花園——」

passages.original: “Sometimes I do still.”
passages.vernacular: 「有時我仲住嗰度。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「有時我還住那裡。」

passages.original: “But where do you live mostly now?”
passages.vernacular: 「但你而家大部分時間住邊度?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但你現在大部分時間住哪裡?」

passages.original: “With the lost boys.”
passages.vernacular: 「同迷失嘅男孩哋喺一起。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「同迷失的男孩們在一起。」

passages.original: “Who are they?”
passages.vernacular: 「佢哋係邊個?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他們是誰?」

passages.original: “They are the children who fall out of their perambulators when the nurse is looking the other way. If they are not claimed in seven days they are sent far away to the Neverland to defray expenses. I’m captain.”
passages.vernacular: 「佢哋係保姆睇向別處時從嬰兒車裡掉出嚟嘅細路。如果七天內冇人認領,佢哋就被送到好遠嘅永無島去抵償開支。我係隊長。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他們是保姆看向別處時從嬰兒車裡掉出來的孩子。如果七天內沒人認領,他們就被送到很遠的永無島去抵償開支。我是隊長。」

passages.original: “What fun it must be!”
passages.vernacular: 「嗰一定好有趣!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那一定很有趣!」

passages.original: “Yes,” said cunning Peter, “but we are rather lonely. You see we have no female companionship.”
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,」狡猾嘅彼得講,「但我哋相當孤單。你睇我哋冇女性陪伴。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,」狡猾的彼得說,「但我們相當孤單。你看我們沒有女性陪伴。」

passages.original: “Are none of the others girls?”
passages.vernacular: 「其他人冇女孩嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「其他人沒有女孩嗎?」

passages.original: “Oh, no; girls, you know, are much too clever to fall out of their prams.”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,冇;你知道,女孩哋太聰明喇,唔會從嬰兒車裡掉出嚟。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,沒有;你知道,女孩們太聰明了,不會從嬰兒車裡掉出來。」

passages.original: This flattered Wendy immensely. “I think,” she said, “it is perfectly lovely the way you talk about girls; John there just despises us.”
passages.vernacular: 呢極大地奉承咗溫蒂。「我想,」佢講,「你談論女孩嘅方式真係太可愛喇;嗰邊嘅約翰就鄙視我哋。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這極大地奉承了溫蒂。「我想,」她說,「你談論女孩的方式真是太可愛了;那邊的約翰就鄙視我們。」

passages.original: For reply Peter rose and kicked John out of bed, blankets and all; one kick. This seemed to Wendy rather forward for a first meeting, and she told him with spirit that he was not captain in her house. However, John continued to sleep so placidly on the floor that she allowed him to remain there. “And I know you meant to be kind,” she said, relenting, “so you may give me a kiss.”
passages.vernacular: 作為回答,彼得站起嚟,把約翰連毯子一起踢下床;一腳。喺初次見面來講,呢喺溫蒂睇來相當冒昧,佢精神十足地告訴佢,喺佢嘅家裡佢唔係隊長。不過,約翰喺地板上瞓得咁安詳,佢就允許佢留喺嗰度。「我知道你本意係好嘅,」佢心軟地講,「所以你可以畀我一個吻。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 作為回答,彼得站起來,把約翰連毯子一起踢下床;一腳。在初次見面來說,這在溫蒂看來相當冒昧,她精神十足地告訴他,在她的家裡他不是隊長。不過,約翰在地板上睡得那麼安詳,她就允許他留在那裡。「我知道你本意是好的,」她心軟地說,「所以你可以給我一個吻。」

passages.original: For the moment she had forgotten his ignorance about kisses. “I thought you would want it back,” he said a little bitterly, and offered to return her the thimble.
passages.vernacular: 呢一刻佢忘咗佢對吻嘅無知。「我以為你想要回去,」佢有點苦澀地講,提出把頂針還畀佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這一刻她忘了他對吻的無知。「我以為你想要回去,」他有點苦澀地說,提出把頂針還給她。

passages.original: “Oh dear,” said the nice Wendy, “I don’t mean a kiss, I mean a thimble.”
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀,」好心嘅溫蒂講,「我唔係講吻,我係講頂針。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀,」好心的溫蒂說,「我不是說吻,我是說頂針。」

passages.original: “What’s that?”
passages.vernacular: 「嗰個係乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那是什麼?」

passages.original: “It’s like this.” She kissed him.
passages.vernacular: 「係咁樣嘅。」佢吻咗佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是這樣的。」她吻了他。

passages.original: “Funny!” said Peter gravely. “Now shall I give you a thimble?”
passages.vernacular: 「真有趣!」彼得嚴肅地講。「而家我畀你一個頂針好嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「真有趣!」彼得嚴肅地說。「現在我給你一個頂針好嗎?」

passages.original: “If you wish to,” said Wendy, keeping her head erect this time.
passages.vernacular: 「如果你想畀嘅話,」溫蒂講,呢次把頭抬得直直嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「如果你想給的話,」溫蒂說,這次把頭抬得直直的。

passages.original: Peter thimbled her, and almost immediately she screeched. “What is it, Wendy?”
passages.vernacular: 彼得畀佢「頂針」,幾乎即刻佢就尖叫起嚟。「點喇,溫蒂?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 彼得給她「頂針」,幾乎馬上她就尖叫起來。「怎麼了,溫蒂?」

passages.original: “It was exactly as if someone were pulling my hair.”
passages.vernacular: 「就像有人喺扯我嘅頭髮一樣。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「就像有人在扯我的頭髮一樣。」

passages.original: “That must have been Tink. I never knew her so naughty before.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗰一定係叮。我從冇見過佢咁淘氣。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那一定是叮。我從沒見過她這麼淘氣。」

passages.original: And indeed Tink was darting about again, using offensive language.
passages.vernacular: 確實,叮又飛嚟飛去,講住難聽嘅話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 確實,叮又飛來飛去,說著難聽的話。

passages.original: “She says she will do that to you, Wendy, every time I give you a thimble.”
passages.vernacular: 「佢講我每次畀你頂針,佢都會嗰樣對你,溫蒂。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她說我每次給你頂針,她都會那樣對你,溫蒂。」

passages.original: “But why?”
passages.vernacular: 「但點解?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但為什麼?」

passages.original: “Why, Tink?”
passages.vernacular: 「點解,叮?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「為什麼,叮?」

passages.original: Again Tink replied, “You silly ass.” Peter could not understand why, but Wendy understood, and she was just slightly disappointed when he admitted that he came to the nursery window not to see her but to listen to stories.
passages.vernacular: 叮又回答:「你呢個蠢驢。」彼得不明白點解,但溫蒂明白,當佢承認佢嚟育兒室窗口唔係嚟睇佢,而係嚟聽故事時,佢稍微有點失望。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 叮又回答:「你這個蠢驢。」彼得不明白為什麼,但溫蒂明白,當他承認他來育兒室窗口不是來看她,而是來聽故事時,她稍微有點失望。

passages.original: “You see, I don’t know any stories. None of the lost boys knows any stories.”
passages.vernacular: 「你睇,我唔知道任何故事。迷失嘅男孩哋冇一個知道任何故事。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你看,我不知道任何故事。迷失的男孩們沒有一個知道任何故事。」

passages.original: “How perfectly awful,” Wendy said.
passages.vernacular: 「嗰真係太可怕喇,」溫蒂講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那真是太可怕了,」溫蒂說。

passages.original: “Do you know,” Peter asked “why swallows build in the eaves of houses? It is to listen to the stories. O Wendy, your mother was telling you such a lovely story.”
passages.vernacular: 「你知道嗎,」彼得問,「燕子點解喺房子嘅屋簷下築巢?係為了聽故事。哦,溫蒂,你媽媽畀你講嘅嗰個故事真可愛。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你知道嗎,」彼得問,「燕子為什麼在房子的屋簷下築巢?是為了聽故事。哦,溫蒂,你媽媽給你講的那個故事真可愛。」

passages.original: “Which story was it?”
passages.vernacular: 「係邊個故事?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是哪個故事?」

passages.original: “About the prince who couldn’t find the lady who wore the glass slipper.”
passages.vernacular: 「關於嗰個找唔到穿玻璃鞋嘅女士嘅王子。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「關於那個找不到穿玻璃鞋的女士的王子。」

passages.original: “Peter,” said Wendy excitedly, “that was Cinderella, and he found her, and they lived happily ever after.”
passages.vernacular: 「彼得,」溫蒂興奮地講,「嗰個係灰姑娘,佢找到咗佢,佢哋從此過住幸福嘅生活。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「彼得,」溫蒂興奮地說,「那是灰姑娘,他找到了她,他們從此過著幸福的生活。」

passages.original: Peter was so glad that he rose from the floor, where they had been sitting, and hurried to the window.
passages.vernacular: 彼得高興極喇,佢從佢哋坐住嘅地板上站起嚟,匆匆走向窗子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 彼得高興極了,他從他們坐著的地板上站起來,匆匆走向窗子。

passages.original: “Where are you going?” she cried with misgiving.
passages.vernacular: 「你要去邊度?」佢不安地喊道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你要去哪裡?」她不安地喊道。

passages.original: “To tell the other boys.”
passages.vernacular: 「去告訴其他男孩。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「去告訴其他男孩。」

passages.original: “Don’t go Peter,” she entreated, “I know such lots of stories.”
passages.vernacular: 「別走,彼得,」佢懇求,「我知道好多好多故事。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「別走,彼得,」她懇求,「我知道好多好多故事。」

passages.original: Those were her precise words, so there can be no denying that it was she who first tempted him.
passages.vernacular: 呢啲正是佢嘅原話,所以唔能夠否認,係佢首先誘惑咗佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這些正是她的原話,所以不能否認,是她首先誘惑了他。

passages.original: He came back, and there was a greedy look in his eyes now which ought to have alarmed her, but did not.
passages.vernacular: 佢回嚟喇,眼睛裡有一種貪婪嘅神色,本該嚇到佢,但並冇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他回來了,眼睛裡有一種貪婪的神色,本該嚇到她,但並沒有。

passages.original: “Oh, the stories I could tell to the boys!” she cried, and then Peter gripped her and began to draw her toward the window.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,我能講畀男孩哋聽嘅故事!」佢喊道,然後彼得抓住佢,開始把佢拉向窗子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,我能講給男孩們聽的故事!」她喊道,然後彼得抓住她,開始把她拉向窗子。

passages.original: “Let me go!” she ordered him.
passages.vernacular: 「放開我!」佢命令佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「放開我!」她命令他。

passages.original: “Wendy, do come with me and tell the other boys.”
passages.vernacular: 「溫蒂,嚟吧,跟我嚟,講畀其他男孩聽。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「溫蒂,來吧,跟我來,講給其他男孩聽。」

passages.original: Of course she was very pleased to be asked, but she said, “Oh dear, I can’t. Think of mummy! Besides, I can’t fly.”
passages.vernacular: 當然佢好高興被邀請,但佢講:「哎呀,我唔能夠。想想媽咪!而且,我唔會飛。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當然她很高興被邀請,但她說:「哎呀,我不能。想想媽咪!而且,我不會飛。」

passages.original: “I’ll teach you.”
passages.vernacular: 「我教你。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我教你。」

passages.original: “Oh, how lovely to fly.”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,飛起嚟多可愛。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,飛起來多可愛。」

passages.original: “I’ll teach you how to jump on the wind’s back, and then away we go.”
passages.vernacular: 「我教你點跳上風嘅背,然後我哋就走喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我教你怎麼跳上風的背,然後我們就走了。」

passages.original: “Oo!” she exclaimed rapturously.
passages.vernacular: 「哦!」佢狂喜地喊道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦!」她狂喜地喊道。

passages.original: “Wendy, Wendy, when you are sleeping in your silly bed you might be flying about with me saying funny things to the stars.”
passages.vernacular: 「溫蒂,溫蒂,你瞓喺你嗰愚蠢嘅床上時,可以同我一起飛,對星星講有趣嘅話。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「溫蒂,溫蒂,你睡在你那愚蠢的床上時,可以同我一起飛,對星星說有趣的話。」

passages.original: “Oo!”
“And, Wendy, there are mermaids.”
passages.vernacular: 「而且,溫蒂,有美人魚。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「而且,溫蒂,有美人魚。」

passages.original: “Mermaids! With tails?”
passages.vernacular: 「美人魚!有尾巴嘅嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「美人魚!有尾巴的嗎?」

passages.original: “Such long tails.”
passages.vernacular: 「咁長嘅尾巴。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那麼長的尾巴。」

passages.original: “Oh,” cried Wendy, “to see a mermaid!”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,」溫蒂喊道,「能睇到美人魚!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,」溫蒂喊道,「能看到美人魚!」

passages.original: He had become frightfully cunning. “Wendy,” he said, “how we should all respect you.”
passages.vernacular: 佢變得極其狡猾。「溫蒂,」佢講,「我哋都會幾咁尊敬你。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他變得極其狡猾。「溫蒂,」他說,「我們都會多麼尊敬你。」

passages.original: She was wriggling her body in distress. It was quite as if she were trying to remain on the nursery floor.
passages.vernacular: 佢痛苦地扭動住身體。簡直就像係佢喺努力留喺育兒室嘅地板上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她痛苦地扭動著身體。簡直就像是她在努力留在育兒室的地板上。

passages.original: But he had no pity for her.
passages.vernacular: 但佢對佢毫不憐憫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但他對她毫不憐憫。

passages.original: “Wendy,” he said, the sly one, “you could tuck us in at night.”
passages.vernacular: 「溫蒂,」佢講,呢個狡猾嘅傢伙,「你可以晚上畀我哋蓋被子。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「溫蒂,」他說,這個狡猾的傢伙,「你可以晚上給我們蓋被子。」

passages.original: “Oo!”
“None of us has ever been tucked in at night.”
passages.vernacular: 「我哋冇一個人晚上被蓋過被子。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們沒有一個人晚上被蓋過被子。」

passages.original: “Oo,” and her arms went out to him.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,」佢向佢伸出咗手臂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,」她向他伸出了手臂。

passages.original: “And you could darn our clothes, and make pockets for us. None of us has any pockets.”
passages.vernacular: 「而且你可以補我哋嘅衣服,畀我哋做口袋。我哋冇一個人有口袋。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「而且你可以補我們的衣服,給我們做口袋。我們沒有一個人有口袋。」

passages.original: How could she resist. “Of course it’s awfully fascinating!” she cried. “Peter, would you teach John and Michael to fly too?”
passages.vernacular: 佢怎能抗拒。「當然係好迷人嘅!」佢喊道。「彼得,你都會教約翰同邁克爾飛嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她怎能抗拒。「當然是非常迷人的!」她喊道。「彼得,你也會教約翰和邁克爾飛嗎?」

passages.original: “If you like,” he said indifferently, and she ran to John and Michael and shook them. “Wake up,” she cried, “Peter Pan has come and he is to teach us to fly.”
passages.vernacular: 「如果你鍾意,」佢漠不關心地講,佢跑到約翰同邁克爾嗰度,搖佢哋。「醒醒,」佢喊道,「彼得潘嚟喇,佢要教我哋飛。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「如果你喜歡,」他漠不關心地說,她跑到約翰和邁克爾那裡,搖他們。「醒醒,」她喊道,「彼得潘來了,他要教我們飛。」

passages.original: John rubbed his eyes. “Then I shall get up,” he said. Of course he was on the floor already. “Hallo,” he said, “I am up!”
passages.vernacular: 約翰揉揉眼睛。「嗰我就起嚟,」佢講。當然佢已經喺地板上喇。「喂,」佢講,「我起嚟喇!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 約翰揉揉眼睛。「那我就起來,」他說。當然他已經在地板上了。「喂,」他說,「我起來了!」

passages.original: Michael was up by this time also, looking as sharp as a knife with six blades and a saw, but Peter suddenly signed silence. Their faces assumed the awful craftiness of children listening for sounds from the grown-up world. All was as still as salt. Then everything was right. No, stop! Everything was wrong. Nana, who had been barking distressfully all the evening, was quiet now. It was her silence they had heard.
passages.vernacular: 邁克爾呢陣都起嚟喇,睇上去精明得像一把有六片刀刃同一把鋸嘅小刀,但彼得突然示意安靜。佢哋嘅臉露出細路哋聽大人世界動靜時嗰種可怕嘅狡猾。一切像鹽一樣靜止。然後一切都對喇。不,等等!一切都不對喇。整個晚上一直痛苦地吠住嘅娜娜而家安靜喇。佢哋聽到嘅就係佢嘅沉默。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 邁克爾這時也起來了,看上去精明得像一把有六片刀刃和一把鋸的小刀,但彼得突然示意安靜。他們的臉露出孩子們聽大人世界動靜時那種可怕的狡猾。一切像鹽一樣靜止。然後一切都對了。不,等等!一切都不對了。整個晚上一直痛苦地吠著的娜娜現在安靜了。他們聽到的就是她的沉默。

passages.original: “Out with the light! Hide! Quick!” cried John, taking command for the only time throughout the whole adventure. And thus when Liza entered, holding Nana, the nursery seemed quite its old self, very dark, and you would have sworn you heard its three wicked inmates breathing angelically as they slept. They were really doing it artfully from behind the window curtains.
passages.vernacular: 「把燈熄喇!躲起嚟!快!」約翰喊道,佢喺整個冒險中只有呢一次發號施令。因此,莉莎抱住娜娜走進嚟時,育兒室睇起嚟完全係原來嘅樣子,好黑暗,你會發誓你聽到佢三個淘氣嘅住客像天使一樣呼吸住瞓覺。佢哋其實係喺窗簾後面巧妙地做呢件事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「把燈熄了!躲起來!快!」約翰喊道,他在整個冒險中只有這一次發號施令。因此,莉莎抱著娜娜走進來時,育兒室看起來完全是原來的樣子,非常黑暗,你會發誓你聽到它三個淘氣的住客像天使一樣呼吸著睡覺。他們其實是在窗簾後面巧妙地做這件事。

passages.original: Liza was in a bad temper, for she was mixing the Christmas puddings in the kitchen, and had been drawn from them, with a raisin still on her cheek, by Nana’s absurd suspicions. She thought the best way of getting a little quiet was to take Nana to the nursery for a moment, but in custody of course.
passages.vernacular: 莉莎心情不好,因為佢正在廚房裡攪聖誕布丁,被娜娜荒唐嘅懷疑從布丁嗰度拉開,臉頰上仲黏住一粒葡萄乾。佢認為讓一切安靜啲嘅最好辦法係把娜娜帶到育兒室一會兒,當然係睇管住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 莉莎心情不好,因為她正在廚房裡攪聖誕布丁,被娜娜荒唐的懷疑從布丁那裡拉開,臉頰上還黏著一粒葡萄乾。她認為讓一切安靜一點的最好辦法是把娜娜帶到育兒室一會兒,當然是看管著。

passages.original: “There, you suspicious brute,” she said, not sorry that Nana was in disgrace. “They are perfectly safe, aren’t they? Every one of the little angels sound asleep in bed. Listen to their gentle breathing.”
passages.vernacular: 「睇吧,你呢個多疑嘅畜生,」佢講,對娜娜失寵並不遺憾。「佢哋好安全,唔係嗎?每一個小天使都喺床上瞓得香。聽佢哋輕柔嘅呼吸。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「看吧,你這個多疑的畜生,」她說,對娜娜失寵並不遺憾。「他們很安全,不是嗎?每一個小天使都在床上睡得香。聽他們輕柔的呼吸。」

passages.original: Here Michael, encouraged by his success, breathed so loudly that they were nearly detected. Nana knew that kind of breathing, and she tried to drag herself out of Liza’s clutches.
passages.vernacular: 呢陣邁克爾得意於佢嘅成功,呼吸得咁響,幾乎被發現。娜娜知道嗰種呼吸,佢試圖掙脫莉莎嘅掌握。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這時邁克爾得意於他的成功,呼吸得那麼響,幾乎被發現。娜娜知道那種呼吸,她試圖掙脫莉莎的掌握。

passages.original: But Liza was dense. “No more of it, Nana,” she said sternly, pulling her out of the room. “I warn you if you bark again I shall go straight for master and missus and bring them home from the party, and then, oh, won’t master whip you, just.”
passages.vernacular: 但莉莎好遲鈍。「唔好再嚟喇,娜娜,」佢嚴厲地講,把佢拉出房間。「我警告你,如果你再叫,我就直接去找主人同太太,把佢哋從宴會帶回家,嗰時,哦,主人不狠狠鞭你才怪。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但莉莎很遲鈍。「不要再來了,娜娜,」她嚴厲地說,把她拉出房間。「我警告你,如果你再叫,我就直接去找主人和太太,把他們從宴會帶回家,那時,哦,主人不狠狠鞭你才怪。」

passages.original: She tied the unhappy dog up again, but do you think Nana ceased to bark? Bring master and missus home from the party! Why, that was just what she wanted. Do you think she cared whether she was whipped so long as her charges were safe? Unfortunately Liza returned to her puddings, and Nana, seeing that no help would come from her, strained and strained at the chain until at last she broke it. In another moment she had burst into the dining-room of 27 and flung up her paws to heaven, her most expressive way of making a communication. Mr. and Mrs. Darling knew at once that something terrible was happening in their nursery, and without a good-bye to their hostess they rushed into the street.
passages.vernacular: 佢又把不快樂嘅狗拴上,但你以為娜娜停止吠叫咗嗎?把主人同太太從宴會帶回家!哎呀,呢正是佢想要嘅。你以為只要佢照睇嘅細路哋安全,佢仲在乎被鞭打嗎?不幸嘅係莉莎回去弄佢嘅布丁,娜娜睇到佢唔會幫忙,拼命地拉鏈子,拉啊拉,最後把佢拉斷喇。轉眼佢就衝進咗二十七號嘅餐廳,舉起爪子向天,呢個係佢最有表現力嘅溝通方式。達玲先生同達玲太太即刻知道佢哋嘅育兒室發生咗可怕嘅事,冇向女主人道別就衝到街上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她又把不快樂的狗拴上,但你以為娜娜停止吠叫了嗎?把主人和太太從宴會帶回家!哎呀,這正是她想要的。你以為只要她照看的孩子們安全,她還在乎被鞭打嗎?不幸的是莉莎回去弄她的布丁,娜娜看到她不會幫忙,拼命地拉鏈子,拉啊拉,最後把它拉斷了。轉眼她就衝進了二十七號的餐廳,舉起爪子向天,這是她最有表現力的溝通方式。達玲先生和達玲太太馬上知道他們的育兒室發生了可怕的事,沒向女主人道別就衝到街上。

passages.original: But it was now ten minutes since three scoundrels had been breathing behind the curtains, and Peter Pan can do a great deal in ten minutes.
passages.vernacular: 但嗰時,三個小淘氣喺窗簾後面呼吸已經過咗好鐘,而彼得潘喺好鐘裡可以做好多事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但那時,三個小淘氣在窗簾後面呼吸已經過了十分鐘,而彼得潘在十分鐘裡可以做很多事。

passages.original: We now return to the nursery.
passages.vernacular: 我哋而家回到育兒室。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們現在回到育兒室。

passages.original: “It’s all right,” John announced, emerging from his hiding-place. “I say, Peter, can you really fly?”
passages.vernacular: 「冇事喇,」約翰宣布,從藏身處出嚟。「我講,彼得,你真嘅會飛嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「沒事了,」約翰宣布,從藏身處出來。「我說,彼得,你真的會飛嗎?」

passages.original: Instead of troubling to answer him Peter flew around the room, taking the mantelpiece on the way.
passages.vernacular: 彼得不費心回答佢,而係喺房間裡飛咗一圈,順便經過壁爐台。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 彼得不費心回答他,而是在房間裡飛了一圈,順便經過壁爐台。

passages.original: “How topping!” said John and Michael.
passages.vernacular: 「太棒喇!」約翰同邁克爾講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「太棒了!」約翰和邁克爾說。

passages.original: “How sweet!” cried Wendy.
passages.vernacular: 「太可愛喇!」溫蒂喊道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「太可愛了!」溫蒂喊道。

passages.original: “Yes, I’m sweet, oh, I am sweet!” said Peter, forgetting his manners again.
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,我可愛,哦,我可愛!」彼得講,又忘咗禮貌。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,我可愛,哦,我可愛!」彼得說,又忘了禮貌。

passages.original: It looked delightfully easy, and they tried it first from the floor and then from the beds, but they always went down instead of up.
passages.vernacular: 睇起嚟輕鬆得令人愉快,佢哋先從地板上試,然後從床上試,但總是往下掉而唔係往上飛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 看起來輕鬆得令人愉快,他們先從地板上試,然後從床上試,但總是往下掉而不是往上飛。

passages.original: “I say, how do you do it?” asked John, rubbing his knee. He was quite a practical boy.
passages.vernacular: 「我講,你係點做嘅?」約翰問,揉住膝蓋。佢係個相當實際嘅男孩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我說,你是怎麼做的?」約翰問,揉著膝蓋。他是個相當實際的男孩。

passages.original: “You just think lovely wonderful thoughts,” Peter explained, “and they lift you up in the air.”
passages.vernacular: 「你只要想可愛奇妙嘅念頭,」彼得解釋,「佢哋就會把你抬到空中。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你只要想可愛奇妙的念頭,」彼得解釋,「它們就會把你抬到空中。」

passages.original: He showed them again.
passages.vernacular: 佢又示範咗一次。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他又示範了一次。

passages.original: “You’re so nippy at it,” John said, “couldn’t you do it very slowly once?”
passages.vernacular: 「你做得太快喇,」約翰講,「你能慢慢做一次嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你做得太快了,」約翰說,「你能慢慢做一次嗎?」

passages.original: Peter did it both slowly and quickly. “I’ve got it now, Wendy!” cried John, but soon he found he had not. Not one of them could fly an inch, though even Michael was in words of two syllables, and Peter did not know A from Z.
passages.vernacular: 彼得慢慢地做,都快快地做。「我而家會喇,溫蒂!」約翰喊道,但好快佢發現自己冇。佢哋冇一個人能飛起一英寸,雖然連邁克爾都能講兩個音節嘅字,而彼得連A同Z都分不清。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 彼得慢慢地做,也快快地做。「我現在會了,溫蒂!」約翰喊道,但很快他發現自己沒有。他們沒有一個人能飛起一英寸,雖然連邁克爾都能說兩個音節的字,而彼得連A和Z都分不清。

passages.original: Of course Peter had been trifling with them, for no one can fly unless the fairy dust has been blown on him. Fortunately, as we have mentioned, one of his hands was messy with it, and he blew some on each of them, with the most superb results.
passages.vernacular: 當然彼得一直喺逗弄佢哋,因為除非吹過仙塵,冇人能飛。幸運嘅係,如我哋提到過嘅,佢嘅一隻手沾滿咗仙塵,佢向每個人吹咗啲,結果極好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當然彼得一直在逗弄他們,因為除非吹過仙塵,沒有人能飛。幸運的是,如我們提到過的,他的一隻手沾滿了仙塵,他向每個人吹了一些,結果極好。

passages.original: “Now just wiggle your shoulders this way,” he said, “and let go.”
passages.vernacular: 「而家就咁樣扭動肩膀,」佢講,「然後鬆手。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「現在就這樣扭動肩膀,」他說,「然後鬆手。」

passages.original: They were all on their beds, and gallant Michael let go first. He did not quite mean to let go, but he did it, and immediately he was borne across the room.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋都喺床上,英勇嘅邁克爾先鬆手。佢唔係真嘅想鬆手,但佢鬆喇,即刻就被帶住飛過房間。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們都在床上,英勇的邁克爾先鬆手。他不是真的想鬆手,但他鬆了,立刻就被帶著飛過房間。

passages.original: “I flewed!” he screamed while still in mid-air.
passages.vernacular: 「我飛喇!」佢喺半空中尖叫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我飛了!」他在半空中尖叫。

passages.original: John let go and met Wendy near the bathroom.
passages.vernacular: 約翰鬆手,喺浴室附近遇到溫蒂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 約翰鬆手,在浴室附近遇到溫蒂。

passages.original: “Oh, lovely!”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,太可愛喇!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,太可愛了!」

passages.original: “Oh, ripping!”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,太棒喇!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,太棒了!」

passages.original: “Look at me!”
passages.vernacular: 「睇我!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「看我!」

passages.original: “Look at me!”
passages.vernacular: 「睇我!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「看我!」

passages.original: “Look at me!”
passages.vernacular: 「睇我!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「看我!」

passages.original: They were not nearly so elegant as Peter, they could not help kicking a little, but their heads were bobbing against the ceiling, and there is almost nothing so delicious as that. Peter gave Wendy a hand at first, but had to desist, Tink was so indignant.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋遠不如彼得優雅,不禁有點亂踢,但佢哋嘅頭撞喺天花板上,幾乎冇乜嘢比呢更美妙嘅喇。起初彼得拉住溫蒂嘅手,但唔得不放開,叮噹太氣憤喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們遠不如彼得優雅,不禁有點亂踢,但他們的頭撞在天花板上,幾乎沒有什麼比這更美妙的了。起初彼得拉著溫蒂的手,但不得不放開,叮噹太氣憤了。

passages.original: Up and down they went, and round and round. Heavenly was Wendy’s word.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋上上下下,轉咗又轉。溫蒂講嘅係「天堂般嘅」。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們上上下下,轉了又轉。溫蒂說的是「天堂般的」。

passages.original: “I say,” cried John, “why shouldn’t we all go out?”
passages.vernacular: 「我講,」約翰喊道,「我哋點解不都出去?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我說,」約翰喊道,「我們為什麼不都出去?」

passages.original: Of course it was to this that Peter had been luring them.
passages.vernacular: 當然呢正是彼得一直喺引誘佢哋嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當然這正是彼得一直在引誘他們的。

passages.original: Michael was ready: he wanted to see how long it took him to do a billion miles. But Wendy hesitated.
passages.vernacular: 邁克爾準備好喇:佢想睇睇佢走十億英里要多久。但溫蒂猶豫喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 邁克爾準備好了:他想看看他走十億英里要多久。但溫蒂猶豫了。

passages.original: “Mermaids!” said Peter again.
passages.vernacular: 「美人魚!」彼得又講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「美人魚!」彼得又說。

passages.original: “Oo!”
“And there are pirates.”
passages.vernacular: 「而且有海盜。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「而且有海盜。」

passages.original: “Pirates,” cried John, seizing his Sunday hat, “let us go at once.”
passages.vernacular: 「海盜,」約翰喊道,抓起佢嘅主日帽子,「我哋即刻去。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「海盜,」約翰喊道,抓起他的主日帽子,「我們馬上去。」

passages.original: It was just at this moment that Mr. and Mrs. Darling hurried with Nana out of 27. They ran into the middle of the street to look up at the nursery window; and, yes, it was still shut, but the room was ablaze with light, and most heart-gripping sight of all, they could see in shadow on the curtain three little figures in night attire circling round and round, not on the floor but in the air.
passages.vernacular: 就喺呢陣,達玲先生同達玲太太帶住娜娜匆匆跑出二十七號。佢哋跑到街中心,抬頭睇育兒室嘅窗子;係嘅,佢仲關住,但房間裡燈火通明,最揪心嘅景象係,佢哋能喺窗簾上睇到三個穿瞓衣嘅小身影嘅影子,喺唔係喺地板上而係喺空中轉圈。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就在這時,達玲先生和達玲太太帶著娜娜匆匆跑出二十七號。他們跑到街中心,抬頭看育兒室的窗子;是的,它還關著,但房間裡燈火通明,最揪心的景象是,他們能在窗簾上看到三個穿睡衣的小身影的影子,在不是在地板上而是在空中轉圈。

passages.original: Not three figures, four!
passages.vernacular: 唔係三個身影,係四個!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不是三個身影,是四個!

passages.original: In a tremble they opened the street door. Mr. Darling would have rushed upstairs, but Mrs. Darling signed him to go softly. She even tried to make her heart go softly.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋顫抖住打開咗街門。達玲先生本想衝上樓,但達玲太太示意佢輕輕地走。佢甚至試圖讓佢嘅心都輕輕地跳。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們顫抖著打開了街門。達玲先生本想衝上樓,但達玲太太示意他輕輕地走。她甚至試圖讓她的心也輕輕地跳。

passages.original: Will they reach the nursery in time? If so, how delightful for them, and we shall all breathe a sigh of relief, but there will be no story. On the other hand, if they are not in time, I solemnly promise that it will all come right in the end.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋能及時趕到育兒室嗎?如果可以,對佢哋幾咁令人愉快,我哋都會鬆一口氣,但就冇故事喇。另一方面,如果佢哋趕不上,我鄭重承諾,最後一切都會好嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們能及時趕到育兒室嗎?如果可以,對他們多麼令人愉快,我們都會鬆一口氣,但就沒有故事了。另一方面,如果他們趕不上,我鄭重承諾,最後一切都會好的。

passages.original: They would have reached the nursery in time had it not been that the little stars were watching them. Once again the stars blew the window open, and that smallest star of all called out:
passages.vernacular: 佢哋本來能及時趕到育兒室嘅,要唔係小星星哋喺睇住佢哋。星星哋又一次把窗子吹開,嗰顆最小嘅星星喊道:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們本來能及時趕到育兒室的,要不是小星星們在看著他們。星星們又一次把窗子吹開,那顆最小的星星喊道:

passages.original: “Cave, Peter!”
passages.vernacular: 「小心,彼得!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「小心,彼得!」

passages.original: Then Peter knew that there was not a moment to lose. “Come,” he cried imperiously, and soared out at once into the night, followed by John and Michael and Wendy.
passages.vernacular: 然後彼得知道一刻都唔能夠耽擱喇。「嚟,」佢專橫地喊道,即刻飛進夜空,約翰、邁克爾同溫蒂跟喺後面。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後彼得知道一刻也不能耽擱了。「來,」他專橫地喊道,立刻飛進夜空,約翰、邁克爾和溫蒂跟在後面。

passages.original: Mr. and Mrs. Darling and Nana rushed into the nursery too late. The birds were flown.
passages.vernacular: 達玲先生、達玲太太同娜娜衝進育兒室,太遲喇。鳥兒已經飛走喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 達玲先生、達玲太太和娜娜衝進育兒室,太遲了。鳥兒已經飛走了。

chapters.title: Chapter IV: The Flight 第四章:飛行

passages.original: “Second to the right, and straight on till morning.”
passages.vernacular: 「右邊第二個,然後一直走到天亮。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「右邊第二個,然後一直走到天亮。」

passages.original: That, Peter had told Wendy, was the way to the Neverland; but even birds, carrying maps and consulting them at windy corners, could not have sighted it with these instructions. Peter, you see, just said anything that came into his head.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係彼得告訴溫蒂去永無島嘅路;但即使係帶住地圖、喺多風嘅轉角查睇嘅鳥兒,根據呢啲指示都唔可能睇到佢。你睇,彼得只係想到乜嘢就講乜嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是彼得告訴溫蒂去永無島的路;但即使是帶著地圖、在多風的轉角查看的鳥兒,根據這些指示也不可能看到它。你看,彼得只是想到什麼就說什麼。

passages.original: At first his companions trusted him implicitly, and so great were the delights of flying that they wasted time circling round church spires or any other tall objects on the way that took their fancy.
passages.vernacular: 起初佢嘅同伴哋完全信任佢,飛行嘅樂趣咁大,佢哋把時間浪費喺繞住教堂尖塔或路上任何其他吸引佢哋嘅高物體打轉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 起初他的同伴們完全信任他,飛行的樂趣那麼大,他們把時間浪費在繞著教堂尖塔或路上任何其他吸引他們的高物體打轉。

passages.original: John and Michael raced, Michael getting a start.
passages.vernacular: 約翰同邁克爾比賽,邁克爾先出發。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 約翰和邁克爾比賽,邁克爾先出發。

passages.original: They recalled with contempt that not so long ago they had thought themselves fine fellows for being able to fly round a room.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋輕蔑地回想起,不久之前佢哋仲以為自己能喺房間裡飛一圈就好了不起。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們輕蔑地回想起,不久之前他們還以為自己能在房間裡飛一圈就很了不起。

passages.original: Not long ago. But how long ago? They were flying over the sea before this thought began to disturb Wendy seriously. John thought it was their second sea and their third night.
passages.vernacular: 不久之前。但係多久以前?佢哋飛到海上時,呢個念頭才開始嚴重困擾溫蒂。約翰認為嗰個係佢哋嘅第二片海同第三個夜晚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不久之前。但是多久以前?他們飛到海上時,這個念頭才開始嚴重困擾溫蒂。約翰認為那是他們的第二片海和第三個夜晚。

passages.original: Sometimes it was dark and sometimes light, and now they were very cold and again too warm. Did they really feel hungry at times, or were they merely pretending, because Peter had such a jolly new way of feeding them? His way was to pursue birds who had food in their mouths suitable for humans and snatch it from them; then the birds would follow and snatch it back; and they would all go chasing each other gaily for miles, parting at last with mutual expressions of good-will. But Wendy noticed with gentle concern that Peter did not seem to know that this was rather an odd way of getting your bread and butter, nor even that there are other ways.
passages.vernacular: 有時天黑,有時天亮,而家佢哋好冷,又覺得太暖。佢哋有時真嘅餓喇,定係只係假裝,因為彼得有一個咁有趣嘅新方法餵佢哋?佢嘅方法係追逐嘴裡叼住適合人食嘅食物嘅鳥,從牠哋嗰度搶過嚟;然後鳥會追上嚟搶回去;佢哋都愉快地互相追逐幾英里,最後彼此表示善意地分開。但溫蒂溫和而擔憂地注意到,彼得似乎唔知道呢個係一種相當奇怪嘅獲取麵包同牛油嘅方式,甚至唔知道仲有別嘅方式。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有時天黑,有時天亮,現在他們很冷,又覺得太暖。他們有時真的餓了,還是只是假裝,因為彼得有一個那麼有趣的新方法餵他們?他的方法是追逐嘴裡叼著適合人吃的食物的鳥,從牠們那裡搶過來;然後鳥會追上來搶回去;他們都愉快地互相追逐幾英里,最後彼此表示善意地分開。但溫蒂溫和而擔憂地注意到,彼得似乎不知道這是一種相當奇怪的獲取麵包和牛油的方式,甚至不知道還有別的方式。

passages.original: Certainly they did not pretend to be sleepy, they were sleepy; and that was a danger, for the moment they popped off, down they fell. The awful thing was that Peter thought this funny.
passages.vernacular: 當然,佢哋唔係假裝睏,佢哋係真嘅睏喇;呢個係一種危險,因為一打瞌瞓,就掉下去喇。可怕嘅係,彼得覺得呢個好好笑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當然,他們不是假裝睏,他們是真的睏了;這是一種危險,因為一打瞌睡,就掉下去了。可怕的是,彼得覺得這很好笑。

passages.original: “There he goes again!” he would cry gleefully, as Michael suddenly dropped like a stone.
passages.vernacular: 「佢又嚟喇!」邁克爾突然像石頭一樣掉下去時,佢會高興地喊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他又來了!」邁克爾突然像石頭一樣掉下去時,他會高興地喊。

passages.original: “Save him, save him!” cried Wendy, looking with horror at the cruel sea far below. Eventually Peter would dive through the air, and catch Michael just before he could strike the sea, and it was lovely the way he did it; but he always waited till the last moment, and you felt it was his cleverness that interested him and not the saving of human life. Also he was fond of variety, and the sport that engrossed him one moment would suddenly cease to engage him, so there was always the possibility that the next time you fell he would let you go.
passages.vernacular: 「救佢,救佢!」溫蒂喊道,恐懼地睇住遠喺下面殘酷嘅海。最後彼得會喺空中俯衝,喺邁克爾撞到海面之前接住佢,佢做呢件事嘅樣子好可愛;但佢總是等到最後一刻,你覺得佢感興趣嘅係佢嘅聰明,而唔係救人嘅命。而且佢鍾意變化,佢某一刻沉迷嘅遊戲會突然唔再吸引佢,所以總有可能下次你掉下去時佢會讓你掉下去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「救他,救他!」溫蒂喊道,恐懼地看著遠在下面殘酷的海。最後彼得會在空中俯衝,在邁克爾撞到海面之前接住他,他做這件事的樣子很可愛;但他總是等到最後一刻,你覺得他感興趣的是他的聰明,而不是救人的命。而且他喜歡變化,他某一刻沉迷的遊戲會突然不再吸引他,所以總有可能下次你掉下去時他會讓你掉下去。

passages.original: He could sleep in the air without falling, by merely lying on his back and floating, but this was, partly at least, because he was so light that if you got behind him and blew he went faster.
passages.vernacular: 佢可以喺空中瞓覺而不掉下嚟,只要仰面躺住漂浮,但呢至少部分係因為佢太輕喇,如果你到佢後面吹氣,佢就走得更快。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他可以在空中睡覺而不掉下來,只要仰面躺著漂浮,但這至少部分是因為他太輕了,如果你到他後面吹氣,他就走得更快。

passages.original: “Do be more polite to him,” Wendy whispered to John, when they were playing “Follow my Leader.”
passages.vernacular: 「對佢禮貌啲,」溫蒂喺佢哋玩「跟住領袖走」時,對約翰低聲講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「對他禮貌一點,」溫蒂在他們玩「跟著領袖走」時,對約翰低聲說。

passages.original: “Then tell him to stop showing off,” said John.
passages.vernacular: 「嗰就叫佢別炫耀,」約翰講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那就叫他別炫耀,」約翰說。

passages.original: When playing Follow my Leader, Peter would fly close to the water and touch each shark’s tail in passing, just as in the street you may run your finger along an iron railing. They could not follow him in this with much success, so perhaps it was rather like showing off, especially as he kept looking behind to see how many tails they missed.
passages.vernacular: 玩跟住領袖走時,彼得會貼近水面飛,路過時碰每條鯊魚嘅尾巴,就像你喺街上沿住鐵欄杆滑過手指一樣。佢哋喺呢啲上跟不上佢,所以呢確實有點像炫耀,特別係佢不斷回頭睇佢哋漏掉咗多少條尾巴。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 玩跟著領袖走時,彼得會貼近水面飛,路過時碰每條鯊魚的尾巴,就像你在街上沿著鐵欄杆滑過手指一樣。他們在這一點上跟不上他,所以這確實有點像炫耀,特別是他不斷回頭看他們漏掉了多少條尾巴。

passages.original: “You must be nice to him,” Wendy impressed on her brothers. “What could we do if he were to leave us!”
passages.vernacular: 「你哋必須對佢好,」溫蒂對弟弟哋強調。「如果佢離開我哋,我哋點算!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你們必須對他好,」溫蒂對弟弟們強調。「如果他離開我們,我們怎麼辦!」

passages.original: “We could go back,” Michael said.
passages.vernacular: 「我哋可以回去,」邁克爾講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們可以回去,」邁克爾說。

passages.original: “How could we ever find our way back without him?”
passages.vernacular: 「冇佢,我哋點找得到回去嘅路?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「沒有他,我們怎麼找得到回去的路?」

passages.original: “Well, then, we could go on,” said John.
passages.vernacular: 「嗰,我哋可以繼續走,」約翰講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那,我們可以繼續走,」約翰說。

passages.original: “That is the awful thing, John. We should have to go on, for we don’t know how to stop.”
passages.vernacular: 「呢個就係可怕嘅地方,約翰。我哋得繼續走,因為我哋唔知道點停下嚟。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這就是可怕的地方,約翰。我們得繼續走,因為我們不知道怎麼停下來。」

passages.original: This was true, Peter had forgotten to show them how to stop.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係真嘅,彼得忘咗教佢哋點停下嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是真的,彼得忘了教他們怎麼停下來。

passages.original: John said that if the worst came to the worst, all they had to do was to go straight on, for the world was round, and so in time they must come back to their own window.
passages.vernacular: 約翰講,如果最壞嘅情況發生,佢哋要做嘅只係一直直飛,因為世界係圓嘅,所以時間久咗佢哋一定會回到自己嘅窗口。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 約翰說,如果最壞的情況發生,他們要做的只是一直直飛,因為世界是圓的,所以時間久了他們一定會回到自己的窗口。

passages.original: “And who is to get food for us, John?”
passages.vernacular: 「約翰,邊個嚟畀我哋弄食嘅?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「約翰,誰來給我們弄吃的?」

passages.original: “I nipped a bit out of that eagle’s mouth pretty neatly, Wendy.”
passages.vernacular: 「我從嗰隻鷹嘴裡搶咗啲,搶得挺利落嘅,溫蒂。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我從那隻鷹嘴裡搶了一點,搶得挺利落的,溫蒂。」

passages.original: “After the twentieth try,” Wendy reminded him. “And even though we became good at picking up food, see how we bump against clouds and things if he is not near to give us a hand.”
passages.vernacular: 「試咗第二十次之後,」溫蒂提醒佢。「而且即使我哋學會咗抓食物,睇睇如果佢不喺附近幫我哋,我哋撞到雲乜嘢嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「試了第二十次之後,」溫蒂提醒他。「而且即使我們學會了抓食物,看看如果他不在附近幫我們,我們撞到雲什麼的。」

passages.original: Indeed they were constantly bumping. They could now fly strongly, though they still kicked far too much; but if they saw a cloud in front of them, the more they tried to avoid it, the more certainly did they bump into it. If Nana had been with them, she would have had a bandage round Michael’s forehead by this time.
passages.vernacular: 確實佢哋不斷喺撞。佢哋而家能飛得好有力喇,雖然定係亂踢太多;但如果佢哋睇到前面有一朵雲,越想避開,越肯定會撞上去。如果娜娜同佢哋喺一起,呢陣佢早就畀邁克爾嘅額頭綁上繃帶喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 確實他們不斷在撞。他們現在能飛得很有力了,雖然還是亂踢太多;但如果他們看到前面有一朵雲,越想避開,越肯定會撞上去。如果娜娜同他們在一起,這時她早就給邁克爾的額頭綁上繃帶了。

passages.original: Peter was not with them for the moment, and they felt rather lonely up there by themselves. He could go so much faster than they that he would suddenly shoot out of sight, to have some adventure in which they had no share. He would come down laughing over something fearfully funny he had been saying to a star, but he had already forgotten what it was, or he would come up with mermaid scales still sticking to him, and yet not be able to say for certain what had been happening. It was really rather irritating to children who had never seen a mermaid.
passages.vernacular: 彼得呢會兒不喺佢哋身邊,佢哋喺上面獨自一人,覺得相當孤單。佢飛得比佢哋快得多,會突然射出視線之外,去經歷啲佢哋冇份嘅冒險。佢會笑住下嚟,為了佢對一顆星星講嘅某件好好笑嘅事,但佢已經忘咗係乜嘢;或者佢上嚟時身上仲黏住美人魚嘅鱗片,卻唔能夠確切講出發生咗乜嘢事。呢對從冇見過美人魚嘅細路哋來講相當令人惱火。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 彼得這會兒不在他們身邊,他們在上面獨自一人,覺得相當孤單。他飛得比他們快得多,會突然射出視線之外,去經歷一些他們沒份的冒險。他會笑著下來,為了他對一顆星星說的某件非常好笑的事,但他已經忘了是什麼;或者他上來時身上還黏著美人魚的鱗片,卻不能確切說出發生了什麼事。這對從沒見過美人魚的孩子們來說相當令人惱火。

passages.original: “And if he forgets them so quickly,” Wendy argued, “how can we expect that he will go on remembering us?”
passages.vernacular: 「如果佢咁快就忘咗佢哋,」溫蒂爭辯,「我哋怎能指望佢一直記得我哋?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「如果他這麼快就忘了她們,」溫蒂爭辯,「我們怎能指望他一直記得我們?」

passages.original: Indeed, sometimes when he returned he did not remember them, at least not well. Wendy was sure of it. She saw recognition come into his eyes as he was about to pass them the time of day and go on; once even she had to call him by name.
passages.vernacular: 確實,有時佢回嚟時不記得佢哋,至少記得不好。溫蒂好肯定。佢睇到佢正要同佢哋打聲招呼就繼續走時,認出佢哋嘅神情才進入佢嘅眼睛;有一次佢甚至唔得不叫佢嘅名字。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 確實,有時他回來時不記得他們,至少記得不好。溫蒂很肯定。她看到他正要同他們打聲招呼就繼續走時,認出他們的神情才進入他的眼睛;有一次她甚至不得不叫他的名字。

passages.original: “I’m Wendy,” she said agitatedly.
passages.vernacular: 「我係溫蒂,」佢激動地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我是溫蒂,」她激動地說。

passages.original: He was very sorry. “I say, Wendy,” he whispered to her, “always if you see me forgetting you, just keep on saying ‘I’m Wendy,’ and then I’ll remember.”
passages.vernacular: 佢好抱歉。「我講,溫蒂,」佢對佢低聲講,「如果你睇到我忘咗你,就不停地講『我係溫蒂』,我就會記起嚟。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他非常抱歉。「我說,溫蒂,」他對她低聲說,「如果你看到我忘了你,就不停地說『我是溫蒂』,我就會記起來。」

passages.original: Of course this was rather unsatisfactory. However, to make amends he showed them how to lie out flat on a strong wind that was going their way, and this was such a pleasant change that they tried it several times and found that they could sleep thus with security. Indeed they would have slept longer, but Peter tired quickly of sleeping, and soon he would cry in his captain voice, “We get off here.” So with occasional tiffs, but on the whole rollicking, they drew near the Neverland; for after many moons they did reach it, and, what is more, they had been going pretty straight all the time, not perhaps so much owing to the guidance of Peter or Tink as because the island was looking for them. It is only thus that any one may sight those magic shores.
passages.vernacular: 當然呢相當唔能夠令人滿意。不過,為了補償,佢教佢哋點樣平躺喺一股順路嘅強風上,呢個係咁愉快嘅改變,佢哋試咗好幾次,發現佢哋可以咁樣安全地瞓覺。確實佢哋本來可以瞓得更久,但彼得好快就瞓膩喇,好快佢會用隊長嘅聲音喊:「我哋喺呢度下去。」所以有偶爾嘅爭吵,但總嘅來講好歡樂,佢哋接近咗永無島;因為過咗許多個月亮之後,佢哋確實到達喇,而且,佢哋一直飛得相當直,或者同其講係彼得或叮嘅指引,不如講係因為島正在尋找佢哋。只有咁樣,任何人才能睇見嗰啲魔法海岸。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當然這相當不能令人滿意。不過,為了補償,他教他們怎樣平躺在一股順路的強風上,這是那麼愉快的改變,他們試了好幾次,發現他們可以這樣安全地睡覺。確實他們本來可以睡得更久,但彼得很快就睡膩了,很快他會用隊長的聲音喊:「我們在這裡下去。」所以有偶爾的爭吵,但總的來說很歡樂,他們接近了永無島;因為過了許多個月亮之後,他們確實到達了,而且,他們一直飛得相當直,也許與其說是彼得或叮的指引,不如說是因為島正在尋找他們。只有這樣,任何人才能看見那些魔法海岸。

passages.original: “There it is,” said Peter calmly.
passages.vernacular: 「就喺嗰度,」彼得平靜地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「就在那裡,」彼得平靜地說。

passages.original: “Where, where?”
passages.vernacular: 「邊度,邊度?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哪裡,哪裡?」

passages.original: “Where all the arrows are pointing.”
passages.vernacular: 「所有箭頭指嘅地方。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「所有箭頭指的地方。」

passages.original: Indeed a million golden arrows were pointing it out to the children, all directed by their friend the sun, who wanted them to be sure of their way before leaving them for the night.
passages.vernacular: 確實有一百萬支金箭向細路哋指出佢,都由佢哋嘅朋友太陽指揮,太陽希望佢哋喺離開佢哋過夜之前確定路。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 確實有一百萬支金箭向孩子們指出它,都由他們的朋友太陽指揮,太陽希望他們在離開他們過夜之前確定路。

passages.original: Wendy and John and Michael stood on tip-toe in the air to get their first sight of the island. Strange to say, they all recognized it at once, and until fear fell upon them they hailed it, not as something long dreamt of and seen at last, but as a familiar friend to whom they were returning home for the holidays.
passages.vernacular: 溫蒂、約翰同邁克爾喺空中踮起腳尖,第一次睇到呢座島。講來奇怪,佢哋全都即刻認出咗佢,直到恐懼降臨佢哋之前,佢哋歡呼佢,唔係作為長久夢想而終於睇見嘅嘢,而係作為佢哋回家過假期時要見嘅熟悉嘅朋友。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 溫蒂、約翰和邁克爾在空中踮起腳尖,第一次看到這座島。說來奇怪,他們全都馬上認出了它,直到恐懼降臨他們之前,他們歡呼它,不是作為長久夢想而終於看見的東西,而是作為他們回家過假期時要見的熟悉的朋友。

passages.original: “John, there’s the lagoon.”
passages.vernacular: 「約翰,嗰個係潟湖。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「約翰,那是潟湖。」

passages.original: “Wendy, look at the turtles burying their eggs in the sand.”
passages.vernacular: 「溫蒂,睇嗰啲海龜喺沙裡埋蛋。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「溫蒂,看那些海龜在沙裡埋蛋。」

passages.original: “I say, John, I see your flamingo with the broken leg!”
passages.vernacular: 「我講,約翰,我睇到你嗰隻斷咗腿嘅火烈鳥!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我說,約翰,我看到你那隻斷了腿的火烈鳥!」

passages.original: “Look, Michael, there’s your cave!”
passages.vernacular: 「睇,邁克爾,嗰個係你嘅洞穴!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「看,邁克爾,那是你的洞穴!」

passages.original: “John, what’s that in the brushwood?”
passages.vernacular: 「約翰,灌木叢裡嗰個係乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「約翰,灌木叢裡那是什麼?」

passages.original: “It’s a wolf with her whelps. Wendy, I do believe that’s your little whelp!”
passages.vernacular: 「係一隻帶住幼崽嘅狼。溫蒂,我真嘅相信嗰個係你嘅小崽子!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是一隻帶著幼崽的狼。溫蒂,我真的相信那是你的小崽子!」

passages.original: “There’s my boat, John, with her sides stove in!”
passages.vernacular: 「我嘅船喺嗰度,約翰,佢嘅船身被撞破喇!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我的船在那裡,約翰,她的船身被撞破了!」

passages.original: “No, it isn’t. Why, we burned your boat.”
passages.vernacular: 「不,唔係。哎呀,我哋把你嘅船燒喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不,不是。哎呀,我們把你的船燒了。」

passages.original: “That’s her, at any rate. I say, John, I see the smoke of the redskin camp!”
passages.vernacular: 「無論如何嗰個係佢。我講,約翰,我睇到紅番營地嘅煙喇!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「無論如何那是她。我說,約翰,我看到紅番營地的煙了!」

passages.original: “Where? Show me, and I’ll tell you by the way smoke curls whether they are on the war-path.”
passages.vernacular: 「邊度?指畀我睇,我可以從煙捲嘅樣子告訴你佢哋係咪喺戰爭路上。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哪裡?指給我看,我可以從煙捲的樣子告訴你他們是否在戰爭路上。」

passages.original: “There, just across the Mysterious River.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗰度,就喺神祕河對面。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那裡,就在神祕河對面。」

passages.original: “I see now. Yes, they are on the war-path right enough.”
passages.vernacular: 「我而家睇到喇。係嘅,佢哋確實在戰爭路上。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我現在看到了。是的,他們確實在戰爭路上。」

passages.original: Peter was a little annoyed with them for knowing so much, but if he wanted to lord it over them his triumph was at hand, for have I not told you that anon fear fell upon them?
passages.vernacular: 彼得對佢哋知道咁多有點惱火,但如果佢想喺佢哋面前逞威風,佢嘅勝利就喺眼前,因為我唔係告訴過你不久恐懼降臨到佢哋身上嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 彼得對他們知道那麼多有點惱火,但如果他想在他們面前逞威風,他的勝利就在眼前,因為我不是告訴過你不久恐懼降臨到他們身上嗎?

passages.original: It came as the arrows went, leaving the island in gloom.
passages.vernacular: 佢像箭一樣離去而嚟,使島陷入黑暗。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它像箭一樣離去而來,使島陷入黑暗。

passages.original: In the old days at home the Neverland had always begun to look a little dark and threatening by bedtime. Then unexplored patches arose in it and spread, black shadows moved about in them, the roar of the beasts of prey was quite different now, and above all, you lost the certainty that you would win. You were quite glad that the night-lights were on. You even liked Nana to say that this was just the mantelpiece over here, and that the Neverland was all make-believe.
passages.vernacular: 喺家裡嘅舊日子裡,永無島到咗瞓覺時間總是開始顯得有點黑暗同有威脅。然後喺佢裡面出現咗未探索嘅地方並擴散,黑影喺其中移動,猛獸嘅吼聲而家完全不同喇,最重要嘅係,你失去咗會贏的確定感。你好高興夜燈係亮住嘅。你甚至鍾意娜娜講呢度只係壁爐台,永無島全係假裝出嚟嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在家裡的舊日子裡,永無島到了睡覺時間總是開始顯得有點黑暗和有威脅。然後在它裡面出現了未探索的地方並擴散,黑影在其中移動,猛獸的吼聲現在完全不同了,最重要的是,你失去了會贏的確定感。你很高興夜燈是亮著的。你甚至喜歡娜娜說這裡只是壁爐台,永無島全是假裝出來的。

passages.original: Of course the Neverland had been make-believe in those days, but it was real now, and there were no night-lights, and it was getting darker every moment, and where was Nana?
passages.vernacular: 當然嗰時永無島係假裝出嚟嘅,但而家佢係真嘅,冇夜燈,而且每一刻都越嚟越黑,娜娜喺邊度?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當然那時永無島是假裝出來的,但現在它是真的,沒有夜燈,而且每一刻都越來越黑,娜娜在哪裡?

passages.original: They had been flying apart, but they huddled close to Peter now. His careless manner had gone at last, his eyes were sparkling, and a tingle went through them every time they touched his body. They were now over the fearsome island, flying so low that sometimes a tree grazed their feet. Nothing horrid was visible in the air, yet their progress had become slow and laboured, exactly as if they were pushing their way through hostile forces. Sometimes they hung in the air until Peter had beaten on it with his fists.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋原本飛得分開,但而家緊緊地擠喺彼得身邊。佢滿不在乎嘅態度終於消失喇,佢嘅眼睛喺閃爍,每次佢哋碰到佢嘅身體,一陣刺痛就傳過佢哋全身。佢哋而家喺可怕嘅島嶼上空,飛得咁低,有時一棵樹擦到佢哋嘅腳。空中睇唔到任何可怕嘅嘢,然而佢哋嘅前進變得緩慢費力,完全好像佢哋喺推開敵對嘅力量前進。有時佢哋懸喺空中,直到彼得用拳頭擊打佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們原本飛得分開,但現在緊緊地擠在彼得身邊。他滿不在乎的態度終於消失了,他的眼睛在閃爍,每次他們碰到他的身體,一陣刺痛就傳過他們全身。他們現在在可怕的島嶼上空,飛得那麼低,有時一棵樹擦到他們的腳。空中看不到任何可怕的東西,然而他們的前進變得緩慢費力,完全好像他們在推開敵對的力量前進。有時他們懸在空中,直到彼得用拳頭擊打它。

passages.original: “They don’t want us to land,” he explained.
passages.vernacular: 「佢哋唔想我哋降落,」佢解釋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他們不想我們降落,」他解釋。

passages.original: “Who are they?” Wendy whispered, shuddering.
passages.vernacular: 「佢哋係邊個?」溫蒂顫抖住低聲問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他們是誰?」溫蒂顫抖著低聲問。

passages.original: But he could not or would not say. Tinker Bell had been asleep on his shoulder, but now he wakened her and sent her on in front.
passages.vernacular: 但佢唔能夠或唔願講。叮噹原本瞓喺佢肩上,但而家佢叫醒佢,派佢喺前面領路。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但他不能或不願說。叮噹原本睡在他肩上,但現在他叫醒她,派她在前面領路。

passages.original: Sometimes he poised himself in the air, listening intently, with his hand to his ear, and again he would stare down with eyes so bright that they seemed to bore two holes to earth. Having done these things, he went on again.
passages.vernacular: 有時佢喺空中停住,專心聽住,手放喺耳邊,又有時佢會往下凝視,眼睛咁亮,似乎要喺地上鑽出兩個洞。做完呢啲事,佢又繼續前進。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有時他在空中停住,專心聽著,手放在耳邊,又有時他會往下凝視,眼睛那麼亮,似乎要在地上鑽出兩個洞。做完這些事,他又繼續前進。

passages.original: His courage was almost appalling. “Would you like an adventure now,” he said casually to John, “or would you like to have your tea first?”
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅勇氣幾乎驚人。「你而家想要一場冒險,」佢隨意地對約翰講,「定係想先飲茶?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他的勇氣幾乎驚人。「你現在想要一場冒險,」他隨意地對約翰說,「還是想先喝茶?」

passages.original: Wendy said “tea first” quickly, and Michael pressed her hand in gratitude, but the braver John hesitated.
passages.vernacular: 溫蒂趕緊講「先飲茶」,邁克爾感激地捏咗捏佢嘅手,但更勇敢嘅約翰猶豫喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 溫蒂趕緊說「先喝茶」,邁克爾感激地捏了捏她的手,但更勇敢的約翰猶豫了。

passages.original: “What kind of adventure?” he asked cautiously.
passages.vernacular: 「乜嘢樣嘅冒險?」佢謹慎地問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「什麼樣的冒險?」他謹慎地問。

passages.original: “There’s a pirate asleep in the pampas just beneath us,” Peter told him. “If you like, we’ll go down and kill him.”
passages.vernacular: 「我哋正下方嘅草原上有一個海盜喺瞓覺,」彼得告訴佢。「如果你鍾意,我哋下去殺咗佢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們正下方的草原上有一個海盜在睡覺,」彼得告訴他。「如果你喜歡,我們下去殺了他。」

passages.original: “I don’t see him,” John said after a long pause.
passages.vernacular: 「我冇睇見佢,」約翰停頓好久後講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我沒看見他,」約翰停頓很久後說。

passages.original: “I do.”
passages.vernacular: 「我睇見喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我看見了。」

passages.original: “Suppose,” John said, a little huskily, “he were to wake up.”
passages.vernacular: 「假如,」約翰有點沙啞地講,「佢醒嚟呢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「假如,」約翰有點沙啞地說,「他醒來呢。」

passages.original: Peter spoke indignantly. “You don’t think I would kill him while he was sleeping! I would wake him first, and then kill him. That’s the way I always do.”
passages.vernacular: 彼得氣憤地講。「你唔會以為我會喺佢瞓覺時殺佢吧!我會先把佢弄醒,然後再殺佢。我總是咁樣做。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 彼得氣憤地說。「你不會以為我會在他睡覺時殺他吧!我會先把他弄醒,然後再殺他。我總是這樣做。」

passages.original: “I say! Do you kill many?”
passages.vernacular: 「我講!你殺過好多嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我說!你殺過很多嗎?」

passages.original: “Tons.”
passages.vernacular: 「成噸。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「成噸。」

passages.original: John said “How ripping,” but decided to have tea first. He asked if there were many pirates on the island just now, and Peter said he had never known so many.
passages.vernacular: 約翰講「太棒喇」,但決定先飲茶。佢問島上而家係唔係有好多海盜,彼得講佢從冇見過咁多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 約翰說「太棒了」,但決定先喝茶。他問島上現在是不是有很多海盜,彼得說他從沒見過這麼多。

passages.original: “Who is captain now?”
passages.vernacular: 「而家邊個係船長?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「現在誰是船長?」

passages.original: “Hook,” answered Peter, and his face became very stern as he said that hated word.
passages.vernacular: 「虎克,」彼得回答,講呢個可恨嘅名字時,佢嘅臉變得好嚴厲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「虎克,」彼得回答,說這個可恨的名字時,他的臉變得非常嚴厲。

passages.original: “Jas. Hook?”
passages.vernacular: 「詹姆斯·虎克?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「詹姆斯·虎克?」

passages.original: “Ay.”
Then indeed Michael began to cry, and even John could speak in gulps only, for they knew Hook’s reputation.
passages.vernacular: 呢陣邁克爾真嘅哭咗起嚟,連約翰都只能斷斷續續地講話,因為佢哋知道虎克嘅名聲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這時邁克爾真的哭了起來,連約翰也只能斷斷續續地說話,因為他們知道虎克的名聲。

passages.original: “He was Blackbeard’s bo’sun,” John whispered huskily. “He is the worst of them all. He is the only man of whom Barbecue was afraid.”
passages.vernacular: 「佢係黑鬍子嘅水手長,」約翰沙啞地低聲講。「佢係佢哋所有人中最壞嘅。佢係巴比克唯一怕嘅人。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他是黑鬍子的水手長,」約翰沙啞地低聲說。「他是他們所有人中最壞的。他是巴比克唯一怕的人。」

passages.original: “That’s him,” said Peter.
passages.vernacular: 「就係佢,」彼得講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「就是他,」彼得說。

passages.original: “What is he like? Is he big?”
passages.vernacular: 「佢長乜嘢樣?佢好高大嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他長什麼樣?他很高大嗎?」

passages.original: “He is not so big as he was.”
passages.vernacular: 「佢冇以前咁高大喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他沒有以前那麼高大了。」

passages.original: “How do you mean?”
passages.vernacular: 「你呢個係乜嘢意思?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你這是什麼意思?」

passages.original: “I cut off a bit of him.”
passages.vernacular: 「我砍掉咗佢嘅一部分。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我砍掉了他的一部分。」

passages.original: “You!”
“Yes, me,” said Peter sharply.
passages.vernacular: 「對,我,」彼得尖銳地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「對,我,」彼得尖銳地說。

passages.original: “I wasn’t meaning to be disrespectful.”
passages.vernacular: 「我唔係有意不敬。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不是有意不敬。」

passages.original: “Oh, all right.”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,冇關係。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,沒關係。」

passages.original: “But, I say, what bit?”
passages.vernacular: 「但係,我講,係邊一部分?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但是,我說,是哪一部分?」

passages.original: “His right hand.”
passages.vernacular: 「佢嘅右手。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他的右手。」

passages.original: “Then he can’t fight now?”
passages.vernacular: 「嗰佢而家唔能夠打架喇?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那他現在不能打架了?」

passages.original: “Oh, can’t he just!”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,佢可厲害住呢!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,他可厲害著呢!」

passages.original: “Left-hander?”
passages.vernacular: 「左撇子?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「左撇子?」

passages.original: “He has an iron hook instead of a right hand, and he claws with it.”
passages.vernacular: 「佢有一個鐵鉤代替右手,用佢嚟抓。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他有一個鐵鉤代替右手,用它來抓。」

passages.original: “Claws!”
“I say, John,” said Peter.
passages.vernacular: 「我講,約翰,」彼得講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我說,約翰,」彼得說。

passages.original: “Yes.”
“Say, ‘Ay, ay, sir.’”
passages.vernacular: 「講『係,係,長官』。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「說『是,是,長官』。」

passages.original: “Ay, ay, sir.”
passages.vernacular: 「係,係,長官。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是,是,長官。」

passages.original: “There is one thing,” Peter continued, “that every boy who serves under me has to promise, and so must you.”
passages.vernacular: 「有一件事,」彼得繼續講,「每個喺我手下服務嘅男孩都必須答應,你都必須。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「有一件事,」彼得繼續說,「每個在我手下服務的男孩都必須答應,你也必須。」

passages.original: John paled.
passages.vernacular: 約翰臉色發白。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 約翰臉色發白。

passages.original: “It is this, if we meet Hook in open fight, you must leave him to me.”
passages.vernacular: 「就係呢個,如果我哋喺公開戰鬥中遇到虎克,你必須把佢留畀我。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「就是這個,如果我們在公開戰鬥中遇到虎克,你必須把他留給我。」

passages.original: “I promise,” John said loyally.
passages.vernacular: 「我答應,」約翰忠誠地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我答應,」約翰忠誠地說。

passages.original: For the moment they were feeling less eerie, because Tink was flying with them, and in her light they could distinguish each other. Unfortunately she could not fly so slowly as they, and so she had to go round and round them in a circle in which they moved as in a halo. Wendy quite liked it, until Peter pointed out the drawbacks.
passages.vernacular: 呢陣佢哋感覺冇咁陰森喇,因為叮噹同佢哋一起飛,喺佢嘅光下佢哋能認出彼此。不幸嘅係,佢唔能夠像佢哋咁慢地飛,所以佢唔得不繞住佢哋一圈一圈地轉,佢哋喺圓圈裡移動,像喺光環裡。溫蒂相當鍾意,直到彼得指出缺點。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這時他們感覺沒那麼陰森了,因為叮噹同他們一起飛,在她的光下他們能認出彼此。不幸的是,她不能像他們那麼慢地飛,所以她不得不繞著他們一圈一圈地轉,他們在圓圈裡移動,像在光環裡。溫蒂相當喜歡,直到彼得指出缺點。

passages.original: “She tells me,” he said, “that the pirates sighted us before the darkness came, and got Long Tom out.”
passages.vernacular: 「佢告訴我,」佢講,「海盜喺天黑前睇到咗我哋,把長湯姆攞出嚟喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她告訴我,」他說,「海盜在天黑前看到了我們,把長湯姆拿出來了。」

passages.original: “The big gun?”
passages.vernacular: 「嗰門大炮?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那門大炮?」

passages.original: “Yes. And of course they must see her light, and if they guess we are near it they are sure to let fly.”
passages.vernacular: 「對。而且佢哋當然一定會睇到佢嘅光,如果佢哋猜到我哋喺附近,肯定會開炮。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「對。而且他們當然一定會看到她的光,如果他們猜到我們在附近,肯定會開炮。」

passages.original: “Wendy!”
passages.vernacular: 「溫蒂!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「溫蒂!」

passages.original: “John!”
passages.vernacular: 「約翰!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「約翰!」

passages.original: “Michael!”
passages.vernacular: 「邁克爾!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「邁克爾!」

passages.original: “Tell her to go away at once, Peter,” the three cried simultaneously, but he refused.
passages.vernacular: 「叫佢即刻走開,彼得,」三個細路同時喊,但佢拒絕喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「叫她馬上走開,彼得,」三個孩子同時喊,但他拒絕了。

passages.original: “She thinks we have lost the way,” he replied stiffly, “and she is rather frightened. You don’t think I would send her away all by herself when she is frightened!”
passages.vernacular: 「佢認為我哋迷路喇,」佢生硬地回答,「佢相當害怕。你哋唔會以為我會喺佢害怕嘅時候把佢一個人送走吧!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她認為我們迷路了,」他生硬地回答,「她相當害怕。你們不會以為我會在她害怕的時候把她一個人送走吧!」

passages.original: For a moment the circle of light was broken, and something gave Peter a loving little pinch.
passages.vernacular: 光圈有一刻被打破喇,有乜嘢嘢愛憐地輕輕捏咗彼得一下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 光圈有一刻被打破了,有什麼東西愛憐地輕輕捏了彼得一下。

passages.original: “Then tell her,” Wendy begged, “to put out her light.”
passages.vernacular: 「咁告訴佢,」溫蒂懇求,「把佢嘅光熄掉。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那麼告訴她,」溫蒂懇求,「把她的光熄掉。」

passages.original: “She can’t put it out. That is about the only thing fairies can’t do. It just goes out of itself when she falls asleep, same as the stars.”
passages.vernacular: 「佢熄不喇。嗰幾乎係仙子唯一唔能夠做嘅事。佢瞓住時佢自己就會熄,同星星一樣。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她熄不了。那幾乎是仙子唯一不能做的事。她睡著時它自己就會熄,和星星一樣。」

passages.original: “Then tell her to sleep at once,” John almost ordered.
passages.vernacular: 「咁叫佢即刻瞓覺,」約翰幾乎係命令。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那麼叫她馬上睡覺,」約翰幾乎是命令。

passages.original: “She can’t sleep except when she’s sleepy. It is the only other thing fairies can’t do.”
passages.vernacular: 「佢只有睏嘅時候才能瞓。呢個係仙子唯一另一件唔能夠做嘅事。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她只有睏的時候才能睡。這是仙子唯一另一件不能做的事。」

passages.original: “Seems to me,” growled John, “these are the only two things worth doing.”
passages.vernacular: 「喺我睇來,」約翰咆哮,「呢個係僅有嘅兩件值得做嘅事。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「在我看來,」約翰咆哮,「這是僅有的兩件值得做的事。」

passages.original: Here he got a pinch, but not a loving one.
passages.vernacular: 呢陣佢挨咗一下捏,但唔係愛憐嘅嗰種。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這時他挨了一下捏,但不是愛憐的那種。

passages.original: “If only one of us had a pocket,” Peter said, “we could carry her in it.” However, they had set off in such a hurry that there was not a pocket between the four of them.
passages.vernacular: 「要係我哋有一個人有口袋,」彼得講,「我哋可以把佢放喺裡面帶住。」然而,佢哋出發得咁匆忙,佢哋四個人身上連一個口袋都冇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「要是我們有一個人有口袋,」彼得說,「我們可以把她放在裡面帶著。」然而,他們出發得那麼匆忙,他們四個人身上連一個口袋都沒有。

passages.original: He had a happy idea. John’s hat!
passages.vernacular: 佢想到一個好主意。約翰嘅帽子!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他想到一個好主意。約翰的帽子!

passages.original: Tink agreed to travel by hat if it was carried in the hand. John carried it, though she had hoped to be carried by Peter. Presently Wendy took the hat, because John said it struck against his knee as he flew; and this, as we shall see, led to mischief, for Tinker Bell hated to be under an obligation to Wendy.
passages.vernacular: 叮同意坐帽子旅行,只要用手攞住佢。約翰攞住佢,雖然佢本來希望由彼得攞。不久溫蒂接過帽子,因為約翰講飛嘅時候佢撞佢嘅膝蓋;而呢,我哋將會睇到,導致咗麻煩,因為叮噹討厭欠溫蒂嘅情。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 叮同意坐帽子旅行,只要用手拿著它。約翰拿著它,雖然她本來希望由彼得拿。不久溫蒂接過帽子,因為約翰說飛的時候它撞他的膝蓋;而這,我們將會看到,導致了麻煩,因為叮噹討厭欠溫蒂的情。

passages.original: In the black topper the light was completely hidden, and they flew on in silence. It was the stillest silence they had ever known, broken once by a distant lapping, which Peter explained was the wild beasts drinking at the ford, and again by a rasping sound that might have been the branches of trees rubbing together, but he said it was the redskins sharpening their knives.
passages.vernacular: 喺黑色嘅高帽子裡,光完全被遮住喇,佢哋默默地繼續飛。嗰個係佢哋所知道嘅最安靜嘅沉默,有一次被遠處嘅舔水聲打破,彼得解釋嗰個係野獸喺淺灘飲水,又有一次被刺耳嘅聲音打破,可能係樹枝互相摩擦,但佢講嗰個係紅番喺磨刀。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在黑色的高帽子裡,光完全被遮住了,他們默默地繼續飛。那是他們所知道的最安靜的沉默,有一次被遠處的舔水聲打破,彼得解釋那是野獸在淺灘喝水,又有一次被刺耳的聲音打破,可能是樹枝互相摩擦,但他說那是紅番在磨刀。

passages.original: Even these noises ceased. To Michael the loneliness was dreadful. “If only something would make a sound!” he cried.
passages.vernacular: 連呢啲聲音都停止喇。對邁克爾來講,孤寂係可怕嘅。「要係有乜嘢嘢發出聲音就好喇!」佢喊道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 連這些聲音也停止了。對邁克爾來說,孤寂是可怕的。「要是有什麼東西發出聲音就好了!」他喊道。

passages.original: As if in answer to his request, the air was rent by the most tremendous crash he had ever heard. The pirates had fired Long Tom at them.
passages.vernacular: 像係回應佢嘅請求,空氣被佢聽過最巨大嘅一聲撞擊撕裂喇。海盜向佢哋開咗長湯姆。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 像是回應他的請求,空氣被他聽過最巨大的一聲撞擊撕裂了。海盜向他們開了長湯姆。

passages.original: The roar of it echoed through the mountains, and the echoes seemed to cry savagely, “Where are they, where are they, where are they?”
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅轟鳴聲喺山間迴響,回聲似乎野蠻地喊住:「佢哋喺邊度,佢哋喺邊度,佢哋喺邊度?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它的轟鳴聲在山間迴響,回聲似乎野蠻地喊著:「他們在哪裡,他們在哪裡,他們在哪裡?」

passages.original: Thus sharply did the terrified three learn the difference between an island of make-believe and the same island come true.
passages.vernacular: 就咁樣,受驚嘅三個細路尖銳地學到咗假裝出嚟嘅島同成真嘅同一座島之間嘅區別。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就這樣,受驚的三個孩子尖銳地學到了假裝出來的島和成真的同一座島之間的區別。

passages.original: When at last the heavens were steady again, John and Michael found themselves alone in the darkness. John was treading the air mechanically, and Michael without knowing how to float was floating.
passages.vernacular: 當天空終於再次穩定下嚟時,約翰同邁克爾發現自己喺黑暗中獨自一人。約翰機械地踏住空氣,邁克爾唔知道點浮,卻浮住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當天空終於再次穩定下來時,約翰和邁克爾發現自己在黑暗中獨自一人。約翰機械地踏著空氣,邁克爾不知道怎麼浮,卻浮著。

passages.original: “Are you shot?” John whispered tremulously.
passages.vernacular: 「你中彈咗嗎?」約翰顫抖地低聲問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你中彈了嗎?」約翰顫抖地低聲問。

passages.original: “I haven’t tried yet,” Michael whispered back.
passages.vernacular: 「我仲冇試過,」邁克爾低聲回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我還沒試過,」邁克爾低聲回答。

passages.original: We know now that no one had been hit. Peter, however, had been carried by the wind of the shot far out to sea, while Wendy was blown upwards with no companion but Tinker Bell.
passages.vernacular: 我哋而家知道冇人被擊中。然而,彼得被炮彈嘅風吹到遠遠嘅海上,而溫蒂被吹向上方,只有叮噹作伴。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們現在知道沒有人被擊中。然而,彼得被炮彈的風吹到遠遠的海上,而溫蒂被吹向上方,只有叮噹作伴。

passages.original: It would have been well for Wendy if at that moment she had dropped the hat.
passages.vernacular: 如果嗰一刻溫蒂把帽子扔掉,對佢會係好事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果那一刻溫蒂把帽子扔掉,對她會是好事。

passages.original: I don’t know whether the idea came suddenly to Tink, or whether she had planned it on the way, but she at once popped out of the hat and began to lure Wendy to her destruction.
passages.vernacular: 我唔知道呢個主意係突然想到叮噹嘅,定係佢喺路上就計畫好嘅,但佢即刻從帽子裡彈出嚟,開始引誘溫蒂走向毀滅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不知道這個主意是突然想到叮噹的,還是她在路上就計畫好的,但她立刻從帽子裡彈出來,開始引誘溫蒂走向毀滅。

passages.original: Tink was not all bad; or, rather, she was all bad just now, but, on the other hand, sometimes she was all good. Fairies have to be one thing or the other, because being so small they unfortunately have room for one feeling only at a time. They are, however, allowed to change, only it must be a complete change. At present she was full of jealousy of Wendy. What she said in her lovely tinkle Wendy could not of course understand, and I believe some of it was bad words, but it sounded kind, and she flew back and forward, plainly meaning “Follow me, and all will be well.”
passages.vernacular: 叮噹唔係全壞;或者講,佢而家係全壞,但另一方面,有時佢係全好。仙子必須係咁樣或嗰樣,因為佢哋太小喇,不幸只有空間裝一種感情。然而,佢哋被允許改變,只係必須係完全嘅改變。目前佢對溫蒂充滿嫉妒。佢用佢可愛嘅叮噹聲講嘅話,溫蒂當然聽不懂,我相信其中啲係髒話,但聽起嚟好友好,佢飛嚟飛去,顯然意思係「跟我嚟,一切都會好嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 叮噹不是全壞;或者說,她現在是全壞,但另一方面,有時她是全好。仙子必須是這樣或那樣,因為她們太小了,不幸只有空間裝一種感情。然而,她們被允許改變,只是必須是完全的改變。目前她對溫蒂充滿嫉妒。她用她可愛的叮噹聲說的話,溫蒂當然聽不懂,我相信其中一些是髒話,但聽起來很友好,她飛來飛去,顯然意思是「跟我來,一切都會好的。」

passages.original: What else could poor Wendy do? She called to Peter and John and Michael, and got only mocking echoes in reply. She did not yet know that Tink hated her with the fierce hatred of a very woman. And so, bewildered, and now staggering in her flight, she followed Tink to her doom.
passages.vernacular: 可憐嘅溫蒂仲能點算?佢呼喚彼得、約翰同邁克爾,得到嘅只有嘲弄嘅回聲。佢仲唔知道叮噹用一個真正嘅女人嗰種強烈嘅恨意恨住佢。於是,佢困惑不解,而家飛行搖搖晃晃,跟住叮噹走向佢嘅厄運。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可憐的溫蒂還能怎麼辦?她呼喚彼得、約翰和邁克爾,得到的只有嘲弄的回聲。她還不知道叮噹用一個真正的女人那種強烈的恨意恨著她。於是,她困惑不解,現在飛行搖搖晃晃,跟著叮噹走向她的厄運。

chapters.title: Chapter V: The Island Come True 第五章:夢想成真的島

passages.original: Feeling that Peter was on his way back, the Neverland had again woke into life. We ought to use the pluperfect and say wakened, but woke is better and was always used by Peter.
passages.vernacular: 感覺到彼得正在回嚟嘅路上,永無島又甦醒過嚟喇。我哋本該用過去完成時講「已經被喚醒」,但「醒喇」更好,而且彼得一向用呢個詞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 感覺到彼得正在回來的路上,永無島又甦醒過來了。我們本該用過去完成時說「已經被喚醒」,但「醒了」更好,而且彼得一向用這個詞。

passages.original: In his absence things are usually quiet on the island. The fairies take an hour longer in the morning, the beasts attend to their young, the redskins feed heavily for six days and nights, and when pirates and lost boys meet they merely bite their thumbs at each other. But with the coming of Peter, who hates lethargy, they are under way again: if you put your ear to the ground now, you would hear the whole island seething with life.
passages.vernacular: 佢不喺時,島上通常好安靜。仙子哋早晨多花一個小時,野獸照顧幼崽,紅番連食六天六夜,海盜同迷失嘅男孩相遇時只係互相咬拇指表示挑釁。但彼得一來,佢討厭懶散,佢哋又動起嚟喇:如果你而家把耳朵貼喺地上,你會聽到整座島充滿生命地沸騰住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他不在時,島上通常很安靜。仙子們早晨多花一個小時,野獸照顧幼崽,紅番連吃六天六夜,海盜和迷失的男孩相遇時只是互相咬拇指表示挑釁。但彼得一來,他討厭懶散,他們又動起來了:如果你現在把耳朵貼在地上,你會聽到整座島充滿生命地沸騰著。

passages.original: On this evening the chief forces of the island were disposed as follows. The lost boys were out looking for Peter, the pirates were out looking for the lost boys, the redskins were out looking for the pirates, and the beasts were out looking for the redskins. They were going round and round the island, but they did not meet because all were going at the same rate.
passages.vernacular: 呢天晚上,島上嘅主要力量分佈如下。迷失嘅男孩哋出去找彼得,海盜哋出去找迷失嘅男孩,紅番哋出去找海盜,野獸哋出去找紅番。佢哋繞住島一圈一圈地走,但冇相遇,因為大家速度相同。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這天晚上,島上的主要力量分佈如下。迷失的男孩們出去找彼得,海盜們出去找迷失的男孩,紅番們出去找海盜,野獸們出去找紅番。他們繞著島一圈一圈地走,但沒有相遇,因為大家速度相同。

passages.original: All wanted blood except the boys, who liked it as a rule, but to-night were out to greet their captain. The boys on the island vary, of course, in numbers, according as they get killed and so on; and when they seem to be growing up, which is against the rules, Peter thins them out; but at this time there were six of them, counting the twins as two. Let us pretend to lie here among the sugar-cane and watch them as they steal by in single file, each with his hand on his dagger.
passages.vernacular: 除咗男孩哋,大家都想要血,男孩哋通常都鍾意,但今晚係出嚟迎接佢哋嘅隊長。島上嘅男孩人數當然有變化,睇佢哋被殺等情況而定;當佢哋似乎喺長大時,嗰個係違反規則嘅,彼得就把佢哋削減;但呢陣有六個,把雙胞胎算成兩個。讓我哋假裝躺喺呢甘蔗叢裡,睇住佢哋排成單行悄悄走過,每個人手放喺匕首上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 除了男孩們,大家都想要血,男孩們通常也喜歡,但今晚是出來迎接他們的隊長。島上的男孩人數當然有變化,看他們被殺等情況而定;當他們似乎在長大時,那是違反規則的,彼得就把他們削減;但這時有六個,把雙胞胎算成兩個。讓我們假裝躺在這甘蔗叢裡,看著他們排成單行悄悄走過,每個人手放在匕首上。

passages.original: They are forbidden by Peter to look in the least like him, and they wear the skins of the bears slain by themselves, in which they are so round and furry that when they fall they roll. They have therefore become very sure-footed.
passages.vernacular: 彼得禁止佢哋長得有啲像佢,佢哋穿住自己殺死嘅熊嘅皮,穿住佢哋咁圓、咁毛茸茸,跌倒時會滾。因此佢哋變得好穩當。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 彼得禁止他們長得有一點像他,他們穿著自己殺死的熊的皮,穿著它們那麼圓、那麼毛茸茸,跌倒時會滾。因此他們變得非常穩當。

passages.original: The first to pass is Tootles, not the least brave but the most unfortunate of all that gallant band. He had been in fewer adventures than any of them, because the big things constantly happened just when he had stepped round the corner; all would be quiet, he would take the opportunity of going off to gather a few sticks for firewood, and then when he returned the others would be sweeping up the blood. This ill-luck had given a gentle melancholy to his countenance, but instead of souring his nature had sweetened it, so that he was quite the humblest of the boys. Poor kind Tootles, there is danger in the air for you to-night. Take care lest an adventure is now offered you, which, if accepted, will plunge you in deepest woe. Tootles, the fairy Tink, who is bent on mischief this night is looking for a tool, and she thinks you are the most easily tricked of the boys. ’Ware Tinker Bell.
passages.vernacular: 第一個走過嘅係圖圖,佢唔係嗰群英勇夥伴中最不勇敢嘅,卻係最不幸嘅。佢經歷嘅冒險比佢哋任何人都少,因為大事總是恰好喺佢拐過街角時發生;一切都好平靜,佢趁機去撿幾根柴,等佢回嚟,其他人正在打掃血跡。呢種壞運氣畀佢嘅面容增添咗溫和嘅憂鬱,但並冇使佢嘅性格變酸,反而變甜,所以佢係男孩中最謙遜嘅。可憐嘅好心圖圖,今晚空氣中對你有危險。要小心,唔好畀人而家畀你一個冒險,如果你接受,會把你推入最深嘅悲痛。圖圖,仙子叮今晚一心搞惡作劇,正在找一個工具,佢認為你係男孩中最容易受騙嘅。提防叮噹。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 第一個走過的是圖圖,他不是那群英勇夥伴中最不勇敢的,卻是最不幸的。他經歷的冒險比他們任何人都少,因為大事總是恰好在他拐過街角時發生;一切都很平靜,他趁機去撿幾根柴,等他回來,其他人正在打掃血跡。這種壞運氣給他的面容增添了溫和的憂鬱,但並沒有使他的性格變酸,反而變甜,所以他是男孩中最謙遜的。可憐的好心圖圖,今晚空氣中對你有危險。要小心,別讓人現在給你一個冒險,如果你接受,會把你推入最深的悲痛。圖圖,仙子叮今晚一心搞惡作劇,正在找一個工具,她認為你是男孩中最容易受騙的。提防叮噹。

passages.original: Would that he could hear us, but we are not really on the island, and he passes by, biting his knuckles.
passages.vernacular: 真希望佢能聽到我哋,但我哋其實不喺島上,佢走過去喇,咬住指關節。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 真希望他能聽到我們,但我們其實不在島上,他走過去了,咬著指關節。

passages.original: Next comes Nibs, the gay and debonair, followed by Slightly, who cuts whistles out of the trees and dances ecstatically to his own tunes. Slightly is the most conceited of the boys. He thinks he remembers the days before he was lost, with their manners and customs, and this has given his nose an offensive tilt. Curly is fourth; he is a pickle, and so often has he had to deliver up his person when Peter said sternly, “Stand forth the one who did this thing,” that now at the command he stands forth automatically whether he has done it or not. Last come the Twins, who cannot be described because we should be sure to be describing the wrong one. Peter never quite knew what twins were, and his band were not allowed to know anything he did not know, so these two were always vague about themselves, and did their best to give satisfaction by keeping close together in an apologetic sort of way.
passages.vernacular: 接下嚟係尼布斯,快活而瀟灑,後面係輕輕,佢從樹上削哨子,隨住自己嘅曲子狂喜地跳舞。輕輕係男孩中最自負嘅。佢認為自己記得迷失之前嘅日子,以及佢哋嘅禮貌同習俗,呢使佢嘅鼻子有一種令人討厭嘅上翹。第四個係卷毛;佢係個淘氣包,彼得嚴厲地講「做呢件事嘅人站出嚟」時,佢經常唔得不交出自己,以致而家一聽到命令,不管係唔係佢做嘅,佢都自動站出嚟。最後係雙胞胎,無法描述,因為我哋一定會描述錯嗰一個。彼得從不太清楚雙胞胎係乜嘢,而佢嘅團隊不被允許知道任何佢唔知道嘅事,所以呢兩個人對自己總是模模糊糊嘅,盡力讓人滿意,以一種道歉似嘅方式緊緊靠喺一起。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 接下來是尼布斯,快活而瀟灑,後面是輕輕,他從樹上削哨子,隨著自己的曲子狂喜地跳舞。輕輕是男孩中最自負的。他認為自己記得迷失之前的日子,以及它們的禮貌和習俗,這使他的鼻子有一種令人討厭的上翹。第四個是卷毛;他是個淘氣包,彼得嚴厲地說「做這件事的人站出來」時,他經常不得不交出自己,以致現在一聽到命令,不管是不是他做的,他都自動站出來。最後是雙胞胎,無法描述,因為我們一定會描述錯那一個。彼得從不太清楚雙胞胎是什麼,而他的團隊不被允許知道任何他不知道的事,所以這兩個人對自己總是模模糊糊的,盡力讓人滿意,以一種道歉似的方式緊緊靠在一起。

passages.original: The boys vanish in the gloom, and after a pause, but not a long pause, for things go briskly on the island, come the pirates on their track. We hear them before they are seen, and it is always the same dreadful song:
passages.vernacular: 男孩哋消失喺昏暗中,停頓咗一下,但唔係好長嘅停頓,因為島上嘅事情進行得好快,海盜跟住佢哋嘅蹤跡嚟喇。我哋喺睇到佢哋之前就聽到佢哋,總是同樣可怕嘅歌:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 男孩們消失在昏暗中,停頓了一下,但不是很長的停頓,因為島上的事情進行得很快,海盜跟著他們的蹤跡來了。我們在看到他們之前就聽到他們,總是同樣可怕的歌:

passages.original: “Avast belay, yo ho, heave to, A-pirating we go, And if we’re parted by a shot We’re sure to meet below!”
passages.vernacular: 「停下,收帆,喲吼,停船,我哋去做海盜,如果被一發炮彈分開,我哋肯定喺地下相會!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「停下,收帆,喲吼,停船,我們去做海盜,如果被一發炮彈分開,我們肯定在地下相會!」

passages.original: A more villainous-looking lot never hung in a row on Execution dock. Here, a little in advance, ever and again with his head to the ground listening, his great arms bare, pieces of eight in his ears as ornaments, is the handsome Italian Cecco, who cut his name in letters of blood on the back of the governor of the prison at Gao. That gigantic black behind him has had many names since he dropped the one with which dusky mothers still terrify their children on the banks of the Guadjo-mo. Here is Bill Jukes, every inch of him tattooed, the same Bill Jukes who got six dozen on the Walrus from Flint before he would drop the bag of moidores; and Cookson, said to be Black Murphy’s brother (but this was never proved), and Gentleman Starkey, once an usher in a public school and still dainty in his ways of killing; and Skylights (Morgan’s Skylights); and the Irish bo’sun Smee, an oddly genial man who stabbed, so to speak, without offence, and was the only Non-conformist in Hook’s crew; and Noodler, whose hands were fixed on backwards; and Robt. Mullins and Alf Mason and many another ruffian long known and feared on the Spanish Main.
passages.vernacular: 冇比呢更凶惡嘅一夥人掛成一排喺處決碼頭上喇。喺呢度,稍微靠前啲,不時把頭貼喺地上聽住,露出粗壯嘅手臂,耳朵上戴住八里亞爾銀幣當裝飾,係英俊嘅意大利人切科,佢曾喺高監獄長嘅背上用血寫下自己嘅名字。佢後面嗰個巨大嘅黑人,自從佢放棄咗嗰個至今仲喺瓜吉莫河岸上被黑皮膚母親用嚟嚇唬細路哋嘅名字後,用過許多名字。呢度係比爾·朱克斯,全身每一寸都刺咗青,就係嗰個比爾·朱克斯,喺海象號上被弗林特打咗六十打鞭才肯放下嗰袋摩艾多金幣;仲有庫克森,據講係黑默菲嘅弟弟(但呢從未被證實),以及紳士斯塔基,曾係公學嘅助教,殺人時仍然文雅;仲有天窗(摩根嘅天窗);以及愛爾蘭水手長斯密,一個奇怪地和藹嘅人,佢刺人可以講毫無冒犯,係虎克船員中唯一嘅不從國教者;以及努德勒,佢嘅手係反住裝嘅;以及羅伯特·穆林斯、阿爾夫·梅森,以及許多其他喺西班牙海上久負盛名、令人聞風喪膽嘅惡棍。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒有比這更凶惡的一夥人掛成一排在處決碼頭上了。在這裡,稍微靠前一點,不時把頭貼在地上聽著,露出粗壯的手臂,耳朵上戴著八里亞爾銀幣當裝飾,是英俊的意大利人切科,他曾在高監獄長的背上用血寫下自己的名字。他後面那個巨大的黑人,自從他放棄了那個至今還在瓜吉莫河岸上被黑皮膚母親用來嚇唬孩子們的名字後,用過許多名字。這裡是比爾·朱克斯,全身每一寸都刺了青,就是那個比爾·朱克斯,在海象號上被弗林特打了六十打鞭才肯放下那袋摩艾多金幣;還有庫克森,據說是黑默菲的弟弟(但這從未被證實),以及紳士斯塔基,曾是公學的助教,殺人時仍然文雅;還有天窗(摩根的天窗);以及愛爾蘭水手長斯密,一個奇怪地和藹的人,他刺人可以說毫無冒犯,是虎克船員中唯一的不從國教者;以及努德勒,他的手是反著裝的;以及羅伯特·穆林斯、阿爾夫·梅森,以及許多其他在西班牙海上久負盛名、令人聞風喪膽的惡棍。

passages.original: In the midst of them, the blackest and largest in that dark setting, reclined James Hook, or as he wrote himself, Jas. Hook, of whom it is said he was the only man that the Sea-Cook feared. He lay at his ease in a rough chariot drawn and propelled by his men, and instead of a right hand he had the iron hook with which ever and anon he encouraged them to increase their pace. As dogs this terrible man treated and addressed them, and as dogs they obeyed him. In person he was cadaverous and blackavized, and his hair was dressed in long curls, which at a little distance looked like black candles, and gave a singularly threatening expression to his handsome countenance. His eyes were of the blue of the forget-me-not, and of a profound melancholy, save when he was plunging his hook into you, at which time two red spots appeared in them and lit them up horribly. In manner, something of the grand seigneur still clung to him, so that he even ripped you up with an air, and I have been told that he was a raconteur of repute. He was never more sinister than when he was most polite, which is probably the truest test of breeding; and the elegance of his diction, even when he was swearing, no less than the distinction of his demeanour, showed him one of a different cast from his crew. A man of indomitable courage, it was said that the only thing he shied at was the sight of his own blood, which was thick and of an unusual colour. In dress he somewhat aped the attire associated with the name of Charles II, having heard it said in some earlier period of his career that he bore a strange resemblance to the ill-fated Stuarts; and in his mouth he had a holder of his own contrivance which enabled him to smoke two cigars at once. But undoubtedly the grimmest part of him was his iron claw.
passages.vernacular: 喺佢哋中間,喺嗰黑暗嘅背景中最黑最大嘅,躺住詹姆斯·虎克,或者佢自己簽名寫作詹姆斯·虎克,據講佢係海上廚子唯一怕嘅人。佢舒適地躺喺一輛由佢嘅手下拉住同推住嘅簡陋馬車上,佢冇右手,有嘅係鐵鉤,佢不時用佢鼓勵佢哋加快步伐。呢個可怕嘅人像對狗一樣對待同稱呼佢哋,而佢哋像狗一樣服從佢。佢嘅身材瘦如枯骨,面色黝黑,頭髮梳成長長嘅捲髮,從稍遠處睇像黑蠟燭,畀佢英俊嘅面容增添咗一種奇特嘅威脅表情。佢嘅眼睛係勿忘我草嘅藍色,帶住深深嘅憂鬱,除咗把佢嘅鉤子扎進你身體時,嗰時兩個紅點出而家眼睛裡,把佢哋可怕地照亮。喺舉止上,佢身上仍有啲大領主嘅氣派,所以佢甚至帶住風度把你剖開,我聽講佢係個有名嘅健談者。佢最有禮貌嘅時候最陰險,呢大概係教養最真實嘅考驗;佢措辭嘅優雅,即使喺罵人時,以及佢舉止嘅高貴,都顯示佢同佢嘅船員係不同階層嘅人。佢係一個有不屈不撓嘅勇氣嘅人,據講佢唯一畏縮嘅係睇到自己嘅血,嗰血好濃,顏色不尋常。喺服裝上,佢有點模仿同查理二世聯繫喺一起嘅服飾,因為佢喺事業早期嘅某個時期聽人講過佢同不幸嘅斯圖亞特王朝有奇異嘅相似;佢嘴裡有一個自己設計嘅煙嘴,使佢可以同時抽兩支雪茄。但毫無疑問,佢身上最可怕嘅部分係佢嘅鐵爪。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在他們中間,在那黑暗的背景中最黑最大的,躺著詹姆斯·虎克,或者他自己簽名寫作詹姆斯·虎克,據說他是海上廚子唯一怕的人。他舒適地躺在一輛由他的手下拉著和推著的簡陋馬車上,他沒有右手,有的是鐵鉤,他不時用它鼓勵他們加快步伐。這個可怕的人像對狗一樣對待和稱呼他們,而他們像狗一樣服從他。他的身材瘦如枯骨,面色黝黑,頭髮梳成長長的捲髮,從稍遠處看像黑蠟燭,給他英俊的面容增添了一種奇特的威脅表情。他的眼睛是勿忘我草的藍色,帶著深深的憂鬱,除了把他的鉤子扎進你身體時,那時兩個紅點出現在眼睛裡,把它們可怕地照亮。在舉止上,他身上仍有一點大領主的氣派,所以他甚至帶著風度把你剖開,我聽說他是個有名的健談者。他最有禮貌的時候最陰險,這大概是教養最真實的考驗;他措辭的優雅,即使在罵人時,以及他舉止的高貴,都顯示他與他的船員是不同階層的人。他是一個有不屈不撓的勇氣的人,據說他唯一畏縮的是看到自己的血,那血很濃,顏色不尋常。在服裝上,他有點模仿與查理二世聯繫在一起的服飾,因為他在事業早期的某個時期聽人說過他與不幸的斯圖亞特王朝有奇異的相似;他嘴裡有一個自己設計的煙嘴,使他可以同時抽兩支雪茄。但毫無疑問,他身上最可怕的部分是他的鐵爪。

passages.original: Let us now kill a pirate, to show Hook’s method. Skylights will do. As they pass, Skylights lurches clumsily against him, ruffling his lace collar; the hook shoots forth, there is a tearing sound and one screech, then the body is kicked aside, and the pirates pass on. He has not even taken the cigars from his mouth.
passages.vernacular: 而家讓我哋殺一個海盜,嚟展示虎克嘅方法。天窗就行。佢哋經過時,天窗笨拙地踉蹌撞到佢身上,弄皺咗佢嘅蕾絲領子;鉤子射出,傳嚟撕裂聲同一聲尖叫,然後屍體被踢到一旁,海盜哋繼續前進。佢甚至冇把雪茄從嘴裡攞出嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在讓我們殺一個海盜,來展示虎克的方法。天窗就行。他們經過時,天窗笨拙地踉蹌撞到他身上,弄皺了他的蕾絲領子;鉤子射出,傳來撕裂聲和一聲尖叫,然後屍體被踢到一旁,海盜們繼續前進。他甚至沒有把雪茄從嘴裡拿出來。

passages.original: Such is the terrible man against whom Peter Pan is pitted. Which will win?
passages.vernacular: 呢個就係彼得潘要同之對抗嘅可怕嘅人。邊個會贏?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這就是彼得潘要與之對抗的可怕的人。誰會贏?

passages.original: On the trail of the pirates, stealing noiselessly down the war-path, which is not visible to inexperienced eyes, come the redskins, every one of them with his eyes peeled. They carry tomahawks and knives, and their naked bodies gleam with paint and oil. Strung around them are scalps, of boys as well as of pirates, for these are the Piccaninny tribe, and not to be confused with the softer-hearted Delawares or the Hurons. In the van, on all fours, is Great Big Little Panther, a brave of so many scalps that in his present position they somewhat impede his progress. Bringing up the rear, the place of greatest danger, comes Tiger Lily, proudly erect, a princess in her own right. She is the most beautiful of dusky Dianas and the belle of the Piccaninnies, coquettish, cold and amorous by turns; there is not a brave who would not have the wayward thing to wife, but she staves off the altar with a hatchet.
