Observe how they pass over fallen twigs without making the slightest noise. The only sound to be heard is their somewhat heavy breathing. The fact is that they are all a little fat just now after the heavy gorging, but in time they will work this off. For the moment, however, it constitutes their chief danger.
passages.vernacular: 海盜嘅蹤跡後面,沿住戰爭路悄悄走嚟嘅係紅番,戰爭路喺冇經驗嘅眼睛睇來係睇唔見嘅,佢哋每個人都睜大眼睛。佢哋帶住戰斧同刀,赤裸嘅身體因油彩同油脂而發亮。佢哋身上掛住頭皮,男孩嘅同海盜嘅都有,因為呢個係皮卡尼尼族,唔好同心腸較軟嘅特拉華人或休倫人混淆。走喺最前面、四肢住地嘅係大大小小豹,一個有咁多頭皮嘅勇士,喺佢而家嘅姿勢下,佢哋有點妨礙佢前進。殿後嘅係最危險嘅位置,走嚟嘅係虎百合,驕傲地直立住,係佢自己權利嘅公主。佢係黝黑嘅戴安娜哋中最美麗嘅,係皮卡尼尼族嘅美人,時而賣弄風情,時而冷淡,時而多情;冇一個勇士唔想娶呢任性嘅嘢為妻,但佢用斧頭把祭壇擋喺外面。睇佢哋點樣走過掉落嘅細枝而不發出啲聲音。唯一能聽到嘅聲音係佢哋有點沉重嘅呼吸。事實係佢哋而家都有點胖,因為剛大食咗一頓,但假以時日會消去。不過目前呢個係佢哋主要嘅危險。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 海盜的蹤跡後面,沿著戰爭路悄悄走來的是紅番,戰爭路在沒有經驗的眼睛看來是看不見的,他們每個人都睜大眼睛。他們帶著戰斧和刀,赤裸的身體因油彩和油脂而發亮。他們身上掛著頭皮,男孩的和海盜的都有,因為這是皮卡尼尼族,不要與心腸較軟的特拉華人或休倫人混淆。走在最前面、四肢著地的是大大小小豹,一個有那麼多頭皮的勇士,在他現在的姿勢下,它們有點妨礙他前進。殿後的是最危險的位置,走來的是虎百合,驕傲地直立著,是她自己權利的公主。她是黝黑的戴安娜們中最美麗的,是皮卡尼尼族的美人,時而賣弄風情,時而冷淡,時而多情;沒有一個勇士不想娶這任性的東西為妻,但她用斧頭把祭壇擋在外面。看他們怎樣走過掉落的細枝而不發出一點聲音。唯一能聽到的聲音是他們有點沉重的呼吸。事實是他們現在都有點胖,因為剛大吃了一頓,但假以時日會消去。不過目前這是他們主要的危險。

passages.original: The redskins disappear as they have come like shadows, and soon their place is taken by the beasts, a great and motley procession: lions, tigers, bears, and the innumerable smaller savage things that flee from them, for every kind of beast, and, more particularly, all the man-eaters, live cheek by jowl on the favoured island. Their tongues are hanging out, they are hungry to-night.
passages.vernacular: 紅番像嚟時一樣像影子般消失,不久佢哋嘅位置被野獸取代,一支龐大而雜亂嘅隊伍:獅子、老虎、熊,以及躲避佢哋嘅無數更小嘅野生動物,因為各種野獸,尤其係所有食人嘅,都喺呢個得天獨厚嘅島上並肩生活。牠哋嘅舌頭垂住,今晚牠哋好餓。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 紅番像來時一樣像影子般消失,不久他們的位置被野獸取代,一支龐大而雜亂的隊伍:獅子、老虎、熊,以及躲避他們的無數更小的野生動物,因為各種野獸,尤其是所有吃人的,都在這個得天獨厚的島上並肩生活。牠們的舌頭垂著,今晚牠們很餓。

passages.original: When they have passed, comes the last figure of all, a gigantic crocodile. We shall see for whom she is looking presently.
passages.vernacular: 牠哋過去後,嚟咗最後一個身影,一條巨大嘅鱷魚。我哋一會兒就會睇到佢喺找邊個。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 牠們過去後,來了最後一個身影,一條巨大的鱷魚。我們一會兒就會看到她在找誰。

passages.original: The crocodile passes, but soon the boys appear again, for the procession must continue indefinitely until one of the parties stops or changes its pace. Then quickly they will be on top of each other.
passages.vernacular: 鱷魚過去喇,但不久男孩哋又出現喇,因為呢個隊伍必須無限期地繼續,直到其中一方停下或改變速度。嗰時佢哋好快就會撞喺一起。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 鱷魚過去了,但不久男孩們又出現了,因為這個隊伍必須無限期地繼續,直到其中一方停下或改變速度。那時他們很快就會撞在一起。

passages.original: All are keeping a sharp look-out in front, but none suspects that the danger may be creeping up from behind. This shows how real the island was.
passages.vernacular: 大家都警惕地注視住前方,但冇人懷疑危險可能從後面悄悄逼近。呢顯示呢座島係幾咁真實。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 大家都警惕地注視著前方,但沒有人懷疑危險可能從後面悄悄逼近。這顯示這座島是多麼真實。

passages.original: The first to fall out of the moving circle was the boys. They flung themselves down on the sward, close to their underground home.
passages.vernacular: 第一個從移動嘅圓圈中掉出嚟嘅係男孩哋。佢哋倒喺靠近佢哋地下家園嘅草地上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 第一個從移動的圓圈中掉出來的是男孩們。他們倒在靠近他們地下家園的草地上。

passages.original: “I do wish Peter would come back,” every one of them said nervously, though in height and still more in breadth they were all larger than their captain.
passages.vernacular: 「我真希望彼得回嚟,」每個人都緊張地講,雖然喺身高,尤其係寬度上,佢哋都比佢哋嘅隊長大。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我真希望彼得回來,」每個人都緊張地說,雖然在身高,尤其是寬度上,他們都比他們的隊長大。

passages.original: “I am the only one who is not afraid of the pirates,” Slightly said, in the tone that prevented his being a general favourite; but perhaps some distant sound disturbed him, for he added hastily, “but I wish he would come back, and tell us whether he has heard anything more about Cinderella.”
passages.vernacular: 「我係唯一不怕海盜嘅人,」輕輕講,用嘅語氣使佢唔能夠成為大家嘅寵兒;但或者某個遠處嘅聲音使佢不安,佢連忙補充:「但我希望佢回嚟,告訴我哋佢有冇聽到更多關於灰姑娘嘅事。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我是唯一不怕海盜的人,」輕輕說,用的語氣使他不能成為大家的寵兒;但也許某個遠處的聲音使他不安,他連忙補充:「但我希望他回來,告訴我們他有沒有聽到更多關於灰姑娘的事。」

passages.original: They talked of Cinderella, and Tootles was confident that his mother must have been very like her.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋談論灰姑娘,圖圖確信佢母親一定好像佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們談論灰姑娘,圖圖確信他母親一定很像她。

passages.original: It was only in Peter’s absence that they could speak of mothers, the subject being forbidden by him as silly.
passages.vernacular: 只有喺彼得不喺時,佢哋才能談論母親,呢個話題被佢禁止,認為太蠢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 只有在彼得不在時,他們才能談論母親,這個話題被他禁止,認為太蠢。

passages.original: “All I remember about my mother,” Nibs told them, “is that she often said to my father, ‘Oh, how I wish I had a cheque-book of my own!’ I don’t know what a cheque-book is, but I should just love to give my mother one.”
passages.vernacular: 「我所記得嘅關於我母親嘅一切,」尼布斯告訴佢哋,「就係佢常對我父親講:『哎呀,我多希望有自己嘅支票簿!』我唔知道支票簿係乜嘢,但我好想畀我母親一本。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我所記得的關於我母親的一切,」尼布斯告訴他們,「就是她常對我父親說:『哎呀,我多希望有自己的支票簿!』我不知道支票簿是什麼,但我很想給我母親一本。」

passages.original: While they talked they heard a distant sound. You or I, not being wild things of the woods, would have heard nothing, but they heard it, and it was the grim song:
passages.vernacular: 佢哋講話時聽到一個遙遠嘅聲音。你或我,唔係林中嘅野生動物,唔會聽到任何聲音,但佢哋聽到喇,嗰個係可怕嘅歌:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們說話時聽到一個遙遠的聲音。你或我,不是林中的野生動物,不會聽到任何聲音,但他們聽到了,那是可怕的歌:

passages.original: “Yo ho, yo ho, the pirate life, The flag o’ skull and bones, A merry hour, a hempen rope, And hey for Davy Jones.”
passages.vernacular: 「喲吼,喲吼,海盜嘅生活,骷髏同交叉骨頭旗,一個快活嘅鐘頭,一根麻繩,嗨,去找戴維·瓊斯。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「喲吼,喲吼,海盜的生活,骷髏和交叉骨頭旗,一個快活的鐘頭,一根麻繩,嗨,去找戴維·瓊斯。」

passages.original: At once the lost boys—but where are they? They are no longer there. Rabbits could not have disappeared more quickly.
passages.vernacular: 迷失嘅男孩哋即刻——但佢哋喺邊度?佢哋不喺嗰度喇。兔子都唔可能消失得更快。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 迷失的男孩們立刻——但他們在哪裡?他們不在那裡了。兔子也不可能消失得更快。

passages.original: I will tell you where they are. With the exception of Nibs, who has darted away to reconnoitre, they are already in their home under the ground, a very delightful residence of which we shall see a good deal presently. But how have they reached it? for there is no entrance to be seen, not so much as a large stone, which if rolled away, would disclose the mouth of a cave. Look closely, however, and you may note that there are here seven large trees, each with a hole in its hollow trunk as large as a boy. These are the seven entrances to the home under the ground, for which Hook has been searching in vain these many moons. Will he find it tonight?
passages.vernacular: 我告訴你佢哋喺邊度。除咗尼布斯,佢飛奔出去偵察喇,佢哋已經喺佢哋嘅地下家園裡,嗰個係一個好令人愉快嘅住所,我哋不久會睇到好多。但佢哋係點到嗰度嘅?因為睇唔到入口,連一塊大石頭都冇,如果滾開就會露出洞口。不過仔細睇,你可以注意到呢度有七棵大樹,每棵樹嘅空心樹幹上都有一個同男孩一樣大嘅洞。呢個就係通往地下家園嘅七個入口,虎克喺呢許多個月亮裡一直喺徒勞地尋找。佢今晚會找到嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我告訴你他們在哪裡。除了尼布斯,他飛奔出去偵察了,他們已經在他們的地下家園裡,那是一個非常令人愉快的住所,我們不久會看到很多。但他們是怎麼到那裡的?因為看不到入口,連一塊大石頭都沒有,如果滾開就會露出洞口。不過仔細看,你可以注意到這裡有七棵大樹,每棵樹的空心樹幹上都有一個和男孩一樣大的洞。這就是通往地下家園的七個入口,虎克在這許多個月亮裡一直在徒勞地尋找。他今晚會找到嗎?

passages.original: As the pirates advanced, the quick eye of Starkey sighted Nibs disappearing through the wood, and at once his pistol flashed out. But an iron claw gripped his shoulder.
passages.vernacular: 海盜前進時,斯塔基敏銳嘅眼睛睇到尼布斯穿過樹林消失,佢即刻掏出手槍。但一隻鐵爪抓住咗佢嘅肩膀。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 海盜前進時,斯塔基敏銳的眼睛看到尼布斯穿過樹林消失,他馬上掏出手槍。但一隻鐵爪抓住了他的肩膀。

passages.original: “Captain, let go!” he cried, writhing.
passages.vernacular: 「船長,放手!」佢扭動住喊道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「船長,放手!」他扭動著喊道。

passages.original: Now for the first time we hear the voice of Hook. It was a black voice. “Put back that pistol first,” it said threateningly.
passages.vernacular: 而家我哋第一次聽到虎克嘅聲音。嗰個係一個黑色嘅聲音。「先把嗰把手槍放回去,」佢威脅地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在我們第一次聽到虎克的聲音。那是一個黑色的聲音。「先把那把手槍放回去,」它威脅地說。

passages.original: “It was one of those boys you hate. I could have shot him dead.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗰個係你哋恨嘅嗰啲男孩之一。我本可以把佢射死。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那是你們恨的那些男孩之一。我本可以把他射死。」

passages.original: “Ay, and the sound would have brought Tiger Lily’s redskins upon us. Do you want to lose your scalp?”
passages.vernacular: 「對,而槍聲會把虎百合嘅紅番引到我哋身上。你想丟掉你嘅頭皮嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「對,而槍聲會把虎百合的紅番引到我們身上。你想丟掉你的頭皮嗎?」

passages.original: “Shall I after him, Captain,” asked pathetic Smee, “and tickle him with Johnny Corkscrew?” Smee had pleasant names for everything, and his cutlass was Johnny Corkscrew, because he wiggled it in the wound. One could mention many lovable traits in Smee. For instance, after killing, it was his spectacles he wiped instead of his weapon.
passages.vernacular: 「要我去追佢嗎,船長,」可憐嘅斯密問,「用開瓶器強尼去搔佢癢?」斯密對一切嘢都有好聽嘅名字,佢嘅短彎刀叫開瓶器強尼,因為佢把佢喺傷口裡扭動。斯密身上可以舉出許多可愛嘅特點。例如,殺人後,佢擦嘅係佢嘅眼鏡而唔係武器。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「要我去追他嗎,船長,」可憐的斯密問,「用開瓶器強尼去搔他癢?」斯密對一切東西都有好聽的名字,他的短彎刀叫開瓶器強尼,因為他把它在傷口裡扭動。斯密身上可以舉出許多可愛的特點。例如,殺人後,他擦的是他的眼鏡而不是武器。

passages.original: “Johnny’s a silent fellow,” he reminded Hook.
passages.vernacular: 「強尼係個沉默嘅傢伙,」佢提醒虎克。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「強尼是個沉默的傢伙,」他提醒虎克。

passages.original: “Not now, Smee,” Hook said darkly. “He is only one, and I want to mischief all the seven. Scatter and look for them.”
passages.vernacular: 「而家不行,斯密,」虎克陰沉地講。「佢只係一個,我要搞掉全部七個。分頭去找佢哋。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「現在不行,斯密,」虎克陰沉地說。「他只是一個,我要搞掉全部七個。分頭去找他們。」

passages.original: The pirates disappeared among the trees, and in a moment their Captain and Smee were alone. Hook heaved a heavy sigh, and I know not why it was, perhaps it was because of the soft beauty of the evening, but there came over him a desire to confide to his faithful bo’sun the story of his life. He spoke long and earnestly, but what it was all about Smee, who was rather stupid, did not know in the least.
passages.vernacular: 海盜哋消失喺樹林間,轉眼只剩下佢哋嘅船長同斯密。虎克沉重地歎咗口氣,我唔知道點解,或者係因為夜晚柔和嘅美,佢產生咗一種向佢忠實嘅水手長傾訴佢一生故事嘅渴望。佢講咗好久,好認真,但講嘅係乜嘢,有點蠢嘅斯密完全唔知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 海盜們消失在樹林間,轉眼只剩下他們的船長和斯密。虎克沉重地歎了口氣,我不知道為什麼,也許是因為夜晚柔和的美,他產生了一種向他忠實的水手長傾訴他一生故事的渴望。他說了很久,很認真,但說的是什麼,有點蠢的斯密完全不知道。

passages.original: Anon he caught the word Peter.
passages.vernacular: 不久佢聽到咗彼得呢個詞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不久他聽到了彼得這個詞。

passages.original: “Most of all,” Hook was saying passionately, “I want their captain, Peter Pan. ’Twas he cut off my arm.” He brandished the hook threateningly. “I’ve waited long to shake his hand with this. Oh, I’ll tear him!”
passages.vernacular: 「最重要嘅係,」虎克激動地講,「我要佢哋嘅隊長彼得潘。係佢砍咗我嘅手臂。」佢威脅地揮舞住鉤子。「我等咗好久,要用呢個同佢握手。哦,我要撕咗佢!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「最重要的是,」虎克激動地說,「我要他們的隊長彼得潘。是他砍了我的手臂。」他威脅地揮舞著鉤子。「我等了很久,要用這個同他握手。哦,我要撕了他!」

passages.original: “And yet,” said Smee, “I have often heard you say that hook was worth a score of hands, for combing the hair and other homely uses.”
passages.vernacular: 「不過,」斯密講,「我常聽你講鉤子抵得上二十隻手,梳頭髮同其他家常用途都行。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「可是,」斯密說,「我常聽你說鉤子抵得上二十隻手,梳頭髮和其他家常用途都行。」

passages.original: “Ay,” the captain answered, “if I was a mother I would pray to have my children born with this instead of that,” and he cast a look of pride upon his iron hand and one of scorn upon the other. Then again he frowned.
passages.vernacular: 「對,」船長回答,「如果我係母親,我會祈禱我嘅細路生下嚟有呢個而唔係嗰個,」佢驕傲地睇咗一眼佢嘅鐵手,輕蔑地睇咗一眼另一隻手。然後佢又皺眉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「對,」船長回答,「如果我是母親,我會祈禱我的孩子生下來有這個而不是那個,」他驕傲地看了一眼他的鐵手,輕蔑地看了一眼另一隻手。然後他又皺眉。

passages.original: “Peter flung my arm,” he said, wincing, “to a crocodile that happened to be passing by.”
passages.vernacular: 「彼得把我嘅手臂,」佢畏縮地講,「扔畀咗一條碰巧經過嘅鱷魚。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「彼得把我的手臂,」他畏縮地說,「扔給了一條碰巧經過的鱷魚。」

passages.original: “I have often,” said Smee, “noticed your strange dread of crocodiles.”
passages.vernacular: 「我常常,」斯密講,「注意到你對鱷魚有一種奇怪嘅恐懼。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我常常,」斯密說,「注意到你對鱷魚有一種奇怪的恐懼。」

passages.original: “Not of crocodiles,” Hook corrected him, “but of that one crocodile.” He lowered his voice. “It liked my arm so much, Smee, that it has followed me ever since, from sea to sea and from land to land, licking its lips for the rest of me.”
passages.vernacular: 「唔係對鱷魚,」虎克糾正佢,「而係對嗰一條鱷魚。」佢壓低咗聲音。「佢咁鍾意我嘅手臂,斯密,從嗰以後一直跟住我,從海到海,從陸到陸,舔住嘴唇想要我嘅其餘部分。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不是對鱷魚,」虎克糾正他,「而是對那一條鱷魚。」他壓低了聲音。「它那麼喜歡我的手臂,斯密,從那以後一直跟著我,從海到海,從陸到陸,舔著嘴唇想要我的其餘部分。」

passages.original: “In a way,” said Smee, “it’s sort of a compliment.”
passages.vernacular: 「喺某種程度上,」斯密講,「呢算係一種恭維。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「在某種程度上,」斯密說,「這算是一種恭維。」

passages.original: “I want no such compliments,” Hook barked petulantly. “I want Peter Pan, who first gave the brute its taste for me.”
passages.vernacular: 「我唔好嗰種恭維,」虎克暴躁地吠道。「我要彼得潘,係佢讓呢畜生第一次嚐到我嘅味道。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不要那種恭維,」虎克暴躁地吠道。「我要彼得潘,是他讓這畜生第一次嚐到我的味道。」

passages.original: He sat down on a large mushroom, and now there was a quiver in his voice. “Smee,” he said huskily, “that crocodile would have had me before this, but by a lucky chance it swallowed a clock which goes tick tick inside it, and so before it can reach me I hear the tick and bolt.” He laughed, but in a hollow way.
passages.vernacular: 佢坐喺一朵大蘑菇上,而家佢嘅聲音裡有一絲顫抖。「斯密,」佢沙啞地講,「嗰條鱷魚早就該抓到我喇,但碰巧佢吞下咗一個鐘,喺佢肚子裡滴答滴答,所以佢仲冇靠近我,我就聽到滴答聲逃跑喇。」佢笑喇,但笑得空洞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他坐在一朵大蘑菇上,現在他的聲音裡有一絲顫抖。「斯密,」他沙啞地說,「那條鱷魚早就該抓到我了,但碰巧它吞下了一個鐘,在它肚子裡滴答滴答,所以它還沒靠近我,我就聽到滴答聲逃跑了。」他笑了,但笑得空洞。

passages.original: “Some day,” said Smee, “the clock will run down, and then he’ll get you.”
passages.vernacular: 「有一天,」斯密講,「鐘會走完,然後佢就會抓到你。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「有一天,」斯密說,「鐘會走完,然後它就會抓到你。」

passages.original: Hook wetted his dry lips. “Ay,” he said, “that’s the fear that haunts me.”
passages.vernacular: 虎克舔咗舔乾燥嘅嘴唇。「對,」佢講,「嗰個就係纏住我嘅恐懼。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 虎克舔了舔乾燥的嘴唇。「對,」他說,「那就是纏著我的恐懼。」

passages.original: Since sitting down he had felt curiously warm. “Smee,” he said, “this seat is hot.” He jumped up. “Odds bobs, hammer and tongs I’m burning.”
passages.vernacular: 自從坐下後,佢一直覺得奇怪地暖。「斯密,」佢講,「呢個座位係熱嘅。」佢跳咗起嚟。「天啊,見鬼,我住火喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 自從坐下後,他一直覺得奇怪地暖。「斯密,」他說,「這個座位是熱的。」他跳了起來。「天啊,見鬼,我著火了。」

passages.original: They examined the mushroom, which was of a size and solidity unknown on the mainland; they tried to pull it up, and it came away at once in their hands, for it had no root. Stranger still, smoke began at once to ascend. The pirates looked at each other. “A chimney!” they both exclaimed.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋檢查咗蘑菇,佢嘅大小同堅實程度係大陸上未見過嘅;佢哋試圖把佢拔起嚟,佢即刻就喺佢哋手裡掉咗出嚟,因為佢冇根。更奇怪嘅係,煙即刻開始冒起嚟。海盜哋互相睇住。「一個煙囪!」佢哋倆都喊道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們檢查了蘑菇,它的大小和堅實程度是大陸上未見過的;他們試圖把它拔起來,它馬上就在他們手裡掉了出來,因為它沒有根。更奇怪的是,煙馬上開始冒起來。海盜們互相看著。「一個煙囪!」他們倆都喊道。

passages.original: They had indeed discovered the chimney of the home under the ground. It was the custom of the boys to stop it with a mushroom when enemies were in the neighbourhood.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋確實發現咗地下家園嘅煙囪。男孩哋習慣喺附近有敵人時用蘑菇把佢堵住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們確實發現了地下家園的煙囪。男孩們習慣在附近有敵人時用蘑菇把它堵住。

passages.original: Not only smoke came out of it. There came also children’s voices, for so safe did the boys feel in their hiding-place that they were gaily chattering. The pirates listened grimly, and then replaced the mushroom. They looked around them and noted the holes in the seven trees.
passages.vernacular: 不只係煙從裡面出嚟。仲有細路哋嘅聲音傳出嚟,因為男孩哋覺得躲喺藏身處咁安全,正在快樂地閒聊。海盜哋陰沉地聽住,然後把蘑菇放回去。佢哋環顧四周,注意到七棵樹上嘅洞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不只是煙從裡面出來。還有孩子們的聲音傳出來,因為男孩們覺得躲在藏身處那麼安全,正在快樂地閒聊。海盜們陰沉地聽著,然後把蘑菇放回去。他們環顧四周,注意到七棵樹上的洞。

passages.original: “Did you hear them say Peter Pan’s from home?” Smee whispered, fidgeting with Johnny Corkscrew.
passages.vernacular: 「你聽到佢哋講彼得潘不喺家嗎?」斯密低聲講,擺弄住開瓶器強尼。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你聽到他們說彼得潘不在家嗎?」斯密低聲說,擺弄著開瓶器強尼。

passages.original: Hook nodded. He stood for a long time lost in thought, and at last a curdling smile lit up his swarthy face. Smee had been waiting for it. “Unrip your plan, captain,” he cried eagerly.
passages.vernacular: 虎克點頭。佢站咗好久,陷入沉思,最後一個令人毛骨悚然嘅微笑照亮咗佢黝黑嘅臉。斯密一直喺等呢個。「把你嘅計畫拆開講吧,船長,」佢急切地喊道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 虎克點頭。他站了很久,陷入沉思,最後一個令人毛骨悚然的微笑照亮了他黝黑的臉。斯密一直在等這個。「把你的計畫拆開說吧,船長,」他急切地喊道。

passages.original: “To return to the ship,” Hook replied slowly through his teeth, “and cook a large rich cake of a jolly thickness with green sugar on it. There can be but one room below, for there is but one chimney. The silly moles had not the sense to see that they did not need a door apiece. That shows they have no mother. We will leave the cake on the shore of the Mermaids’ Lagoon. These boys are always swimming about there, playing with the mermaids. They will find the cake and they will gobble it up, because, having no mother, they don’t know how dangerous ’tis to eat rich damp cake.” He burst into laughter, not hollow laughter now, but honest laughter. “Aha, they will die.”
passages.vernacular: 「回到船上,」虎克慢慢地咬住牙講,「烤一個又大又濃、厚度可觀嘅蛋糕,上面放綠色嘅糖。下面只可能有一個房間,因為只有一個煙囪。嗰啲愚蠢嘅鼴鼠冇頭腦睇出佢哋不需要每人一個門。呢顯示佢哋冇母親。我哋把蛋糕留喺美人魚潟湖嘅岸邊。呢啲男孩總是喺嗰度游嚟游去,同美人魚玩。佢哋會發現蛋糕,把佢吞下去,因為冇母親,佢哋唔知道食又濃又潮嘅蛋糕係幾咁危險。」佢爆發出大笑,而家唔係空洞嘅笑,而係真誠嘅笑。「啊哈,佢哋會死。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「回到船上,」虎克慢慢地咬著牙說,「烤一個又大又濃、厚度可觀的蛋糕,上面放綠色的糖。下面只可能有一個房間,因為只有一個煙囪。那些愚蠢的鼴鼠沒有頭腦看出他們不需要每人一個門。這顯示他們沒有母親。我們把蛋糕留在美人魚潟湖的岸邊。這些男孩總是在那裡游來游去,同美人魚玩。他們會發現蛋糕,把它吞下去,因為沒有母親,他們不知道吃又濃又潮的蛋糕是多麼危險。」他爆發出大笑,現在不是空洞的笑,而是真誠的笑。「啊哈,他們會死。」

passages.original: Smee had listened with growing admiration.
passages.vernacular: 斯密越聽越佩服。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 斯密越聽越佩服。

passages.original: “It’s the wickedest, prettiest policy ever I heard of!” he cried, and in their exultation they danced and sang:
passages.vernacular: 「呢個係我聽過最邪惡、最漂亮嘅計策!」佢喊道,佢哋興高采烈地跳舞唱歌:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這是我聽過最邪惡、最漂亮的計策!」他喊道,他們興高采烈地跳舞唱歌:

passages.original: “Avast, belay, when I appear, By fear they’re overtook; Nought’s left upon your bones when you Have shaken claws with Hook.”
passages.vernacular: 「停下,收帆,我一出現,恐懼就追上佢哋;你同虎克握過爪之後,骨頭上乜嘢都不剩。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「停下,收帆,我一出現,恐懼就追上他們;你同虎克握過爪之後,骨頭上什麼都不剩。」

passages.original: They began the verse, but they never finished it, for another sound broke in and stilled them. There was at first such a tiny sound that a leaf might have fallen on it and smothered it, but as it came nearer it was more distinct.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋開始唱呢一節,卻從冇唱完,因為另一個聲音插進嚟,使佢哋靜咗下嚟。起初聲音咁細微,一片葉子落喺上面就能蓋住佢,但越嚟越近時越嚟越清楚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們開始唱這一節,卻從沒唱完,因為另一個聲音插進來,使他們靜了下來。起初聲音那麼細微,一片葉子落在上面就能蓋住它,但越來越近時越來越清楚。

passages.original: Tick tick tick tick!
passages.vernacular: 滴答滴答滴答滴答!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 滴答滴答滴答滴答!

passages.original: Hook stood shuddering, one foot in the air.
passages.vernacular: 虎克站住發抖,一隻腳懸喺空中。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 虎克站著發抖,一隻腳懸在空中。

passages.original: “The crocodile!” he gasped, and bounded away, followed by his bo’sun.
passages.vernacular: 「鱷魚!」佢喘住氣講,蹦跳住逃走喇,水手長跟喺後面。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「鱷魚!」他喘著氣說,蹦跳著逃走了,水手長跟在後面。

passages.original: It was indeed the crocodile. It had passed the redskins, who were now on the trail of the other pirates. It oozed on after Hook.
passages.vernacular: 嗰確實係鱷魚。佢越過咗紅番,佢哋而家正追蹤其他海盜。佢慢慢滑行住跟喺虎克後面。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那確實是鱷魚。它越過了紅番,他們現在正追蹤其他海盜。它慢慢滑行著跟在虎克後面。

passages.original: Once more the boys emerged into the open; but the dangers of the night were not yet over, for presently Nibs rushed breathless into their midst, pursued by a pack of wolves. The tongues of the pursuers were hanging out; the baying of them was horrible.
passages.vernacular: 男孩哋又一次出而家空曠處;但夜晚嘅危險仲冇結束,不久尼布斯氣喘吁吁地衝進佢哋中間,後面係一群狼追趕住。追趕者嘅舌頭垂住;牠哋嘅吠叫聲令人恐怖。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 男孩們又一次出現在空曠處;但夜晚的危險還沒有結束,不久尼布斯氣喘吁吁地衝進他們中間,後面是一群狼追趕著。追趕者的舌頭垂著;牠們的吠叫聲令人恐怖。

passages.original: “Save me, save me!” cried Nibs, falling on the ground.
passages.vernacular: 「救我,救我!」尼布斯倒喺地上喊道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「救我,救我!」尼布斯倒在地上喊道。

passages.original: “But what can we do, what can we do?”
passages.vernacular: 「但我哋能做乜嘢,能做乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但我們能做什麼,能做什麼?」

passages.original: It was a high compliment to Peter that at that dire moment their thoughts turned to him.
passages.vernacular: 喺嗰危急關頭佢哋想到嘅係彼得,呢對彼得係好高嘅讚美。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在那危急關頭他們想到的是彼得,這對彼得是很高的讚美。

passages.original: “What would Peter do?” they cried simultaneously.
passages.vernacular: 「彼得會點做?」佢哋同時喊道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「彼得會怎麼做?」他們同時喊道。

passages.original: Almost in the same breath they cried, “Peter would look at them through his legs.”
passages.vernacular: 幾乎喺同一口氣裡,佢哋喊道:「彼得會從胯下睇牠哋。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 幾乎在同一口氣裡,他們喊道:「彼得會從胯下看牠們。」

passages.original: And then, “Let us do what Peter would do.”
passages.vernacular: 然後,「我哋做彼得會做嘅事。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後,「我們做彼得會做的事。」

passages.original: It is quite the most successful way of defying wolves, and as one boy they bent and looked through their legs. The next moment is the long one, but victory came quickly, for as the boys advanced upon them in the terrible attitude, the wolves dropped their tails and fled.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係對抗狼最成功嘅方法,佢哋像一個男孩似嘅彎下腰,從胯下睇。下一刻係漫長嘅一刻,但勝利好快到來,因為男孩哋以嗰可怕嘅姿勢向牠哋逼近時,狼垂下尾巴逃跑喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是對抗狼最成功的方法,他們像一個男孩似的彎下腰,從胯下看。下一刻是漫長的一刻,但勝利很快到來,因為男孩們以那可怕的姿勢向牠們逼近時,狼垂下尾巴逃跑了。

passages.original: Now Nibs rose from the ground, and the others thought that his staring eyes still saw the wolves. But it was not wolves he saw.
passages.vernacular: 而家尼布斯從地上站起嚟,其他人認為佢睜大嘅眼睛仲睇到狼。但佢睇到嘅唔係狼。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在尼布斯從地上站起來,其他人認為他睜大的眼睛還看到狼。但他看到的不是狼。

passages.original: “I have seen a wonderfuller thing,” he cried, as they gathered round him eagerly. “A great white bird. It is flying this way.”
passages.vernacular: 「我睇到咗更奇妙嘅嘢,」佢喊道,佢哋急切地圍住佢。「一隻大白鳥。佢正朝呢邊飛嚟。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我看到了更奇妙的東西,」他喊道,他們急切地圍著他。「一隻大白鳥。它正朝這邊飛來。」

passages.original: “What kind of a bird, do you think?”
passages.vernacular: 「你覺得係乜嘢鳥?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你覺得是什麼鳥?」

passages.original: “I don’t know,” Nibs said, awestruck, “but it looks so weary, and as it flies it moans, ‘Poor Wendy.’”
passages.vernacular: 「我唔知道,」尼布斯敬畏地講,「但佢睇起嚟咁疲倦,飛嘅時候呻吟住『可憐嘅溫蒂』。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不知道,」尼布斯敬畏地說,「但它看起來那麼疲倦,飛的時候呻吟著『可憐的溫蒂』。」

passages.original: “Poor Wendy?”
passages.vernacular: 「可憐嘅溫蒂?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「可憐的溫蒂?」

passages.original: “I remember,” said Slightly instantly, “there are birds called Wendies.”
passages.vernacular: 「我記得,」輕輕即刻講,「有一種鳥叫溫蒂。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我記得,」輕輕立刻說,「有一種鳥叫溫蒂。」

passages.original: “See, it comes!” cried Curly, pointing to Wendy in the heavens.
passages.vernacular: 「睇,佢嚟喇!」卷毛喊道,指住天空中嘅溫蒂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「看,它來了!」卷毛喊道,指著天空中的溫蒂。

passages.original: Wendy was now almost overhead, and they could hear her plaintive cry. But more distinct came the shrill voice of Tinker Bell. The jealous fairy had now cast off all disguise of friendship, and was darting at her victim from every direction, pinching savagely each time she touched.
passages.vernacular: 溫蒂而家幾乎喺佢哋頭頂上,佢哋能聽到佢哀怨嘅叫聲。但更清楚嘅係叮噹尖銳嘅聲音。嫉妒嘅仙子而家已經拋掉所有友誼嘅偽裝,從四面八方向佢嘅受害者飛撲,每次碰到都狠狠地捏。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 溫蒂現在幾乎在他們頭頂上,他們能聽到她哀怨的叫聲。但更清楚的是叮噹尖銳的聲音。嫉妒的仙子現在已經拋掉所有友誼的偽裝,從四面八方向她的受害者飛撲,每次碰到都狠狠地捏。

passages.original: “Hullo, Tink,” cried the wondering boys.
passages.vernacular: 「喂,叮,」好奇嘅男孩哋喊道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「喂,叮,」好奇的男孩們喊道。

passages.original: Tink’s reply rang out: “Peter wants you to shoot the Wendy.”
passages.vernacular: 叮嘅回答響咗起嚟:「彼得要你哋射嗰隻溫蒂。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 叮的回答響了起來:「彼得要你們射那隻溫蒂。」

passages.original: It was not in their nature to question when Peter ordered. “Let us do what Peter wishes!” cried the simple boys. “Quick, bows and arrows!”
passages.vernacular: 彼得下命令時佢哋嘅天性係不質疑嘅。「我哋做彼得想要嘅事!」單純嘅男孩哋喊道。「快,弓同箭!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 彼得下命令時他們的天性是不質疑的。「我們做彼得想要的事!」單純的男孩們喊道。「快,弓和箭!」

passages.original: All but Tootles popped down their trees. He had a bow and arrow with him, and Tink noted it, and rubbed her little hands.
passages.vernacular: 除咗圖圖,所有人都從佢哋嘅樹裡鑽咗出嚟。佢帶住弓同箭,叮噹注意到喇,搓住佢嘅小手。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 除了圖圖,所有人都從他們的樹裡鑽了出來。他帶著弓和箭,叮噹注意到了,搓著她的小手。

passages.original: “Quick, Tootles, quick,” she screamed. “Peter will be so pleased.”
passages.vernacular: 「快,圖圖,快,」佢尖叫。「彼得會好高興。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「快,圖圖,快,」她尖叫。「彼得會非常高興。」

passages.original: Tootles excitedly fitted the arrow to his bow. “Out of the way, Tink,” he shouted, and then he fired, and Wendy fluttered to the ground with an arrow in her breast.
passages.vernacular: 圖圖興奮地把箭搭喺弓上。「讓開,叮,」佢喊道,然後佢射喇,溫蒂胸口中箭,撲騰住落到地上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 圖圖興奮地把箭搭在弓上。「讓開,叮,」他喊道,然後他射了,溫蒂胸口中箭,撲騰著落到地上。

chapters.title: Chapter VI: The Little House 第六章:小房子

passages.original: Foolish Tootles was standing like a conqueror over Wendy’s body when the other boys sprang, armed, from their trees.
passages.vernacular: 傻傻嘅圖圖像一個征服者一樣站喺溫蒂嘅身體旁,呢陣其他男孩帶住武器從樹裡跳出嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 傻傻的圖圖像一個征服者一樣站在溫蒂的身體旁,這時其他男孩帶著武器從樹裡跳出來。

passages.original: “You are too late,” he cried proudly, “I have shot the Wendy. Peter will be so pleased with me.”
passages.vernacular: 「你哋嚟晚喇,」佢驕傲地喊道,「我射中咗嗰隻溫蒂。彼得會對我好滿意嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你們來晚了,」他驕傲地喊道,「我射中了那隻溫蒂。彼得會對我非常滿意的。」

passages.original: Overhead Tinker Bell shouted “Silly ass!” and darted into hiding. The others did not hear her. They had crowded round Wendy, and as they looked a terrible silence fell upon the wood. If Wendy’s heart had been beating they would all have heard it.
passages.vernacular: 頭頂上,叮噹喊住「蠢驢!」然後飛快地躲咗起嚟。其他人冇聽到佢。佢哋擠喺溫蒂周圍,佢哋睇住時,可怕嘅沉寂降臨喺樹林裡。如果溫蒂嘅心仲喺跳,佢哋都會聽到。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 頭頂上,叮噹喊著「蠢驢!」然後飛快地躲了起來。其他人沒聽到她。他們擠在溫蒂周圍,他們看著時,可怕的沉寂降臨在樹林裡。如果溫蒂的心還在跳,他們都會聽到。

passages.original: Slightly was the first to speak. “This is no bird,” he said in a scared voice. “I think this must be a lady.”
passages.vernacular: 輕輕第一個開口。「呢唔係鳥,」佢用驚恐嘅聲音講。「我想呢一定係位女士。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 輕輕第一個開口。「這不是鳥,」他用驚恐的聲音說。「我想這一定是位女士。」

passages.original: “A lady?” said Tootles, and fell a-trembling.
passages.vernacular: 「一位女士?」圖圖講,開始發抖。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「一位女士?」圖圖說,開始發抖。

passages.original: “And we have killed her,” Nibs said hoarsely.
passages.vernacular: 「而我哋殺咗佢,」尼布斯嘶啞地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「而我們殺了她,」尼布斯嘶啞地說。

passages.original: They all whipped off their caps.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋都摘下咗帽子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們都摘下了帽子。

passages.original: “Now I see,” Curly said: “Peter was bringing her to us.” He threw himself sorrowfully on the ground.
passages.vernacular: 「我而家明白喇,」卷毛講:「彼得係把佢帶嚟畀我哋嘅。」佢悲傷地撲倒喺地上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我現在明白了,」卷毛說:「彼得是把她帶來給我們的。」他悲傷地撲倒在地上。

passages.original: “A lady to take care of us at last,” said one of the twins, “and you have killed her!”
passages.vernacular: 「一位終於嚟照顧我哋嘅女士,」一個雙胞胎講,「而你把佢殺喇!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「一位終於來照顧我們的女士,」一個雙胞胎說,「而你把她殺了!」

passages.original: They were sorry for him, but sorrier for themselves, and when he took a step nearer them they turned from him.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋為佢難過,但更為自己難過,佢向佢哋走近一步時,佢哋轉身避開佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們為他難過,但更為自己難過,他向他們走近一步時,他們轉身避開他。

passages.original: Tootles’ face was very white, but there was a dignity about him now that had never been there before.
passages.vernacular: 圖圖嘅臉好蒼白,但佢而家有一種以前從未有過嘅尊嚴。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 圖圖的臉很蒼白,但他現在有一種以前從未有過的尊嚴。

passages.original: “I did it,” he said, reflecting. “When ladies used to come to me in dreams, I said, ‘Pretty mother, pretty mother.’ But when at last she really came, I shot her.”
passages.vernacular: 「係我幹嘅,」佢沉思住講。「以前女士哋喺夢裡嚟找我,我講:『漂亮嘅媽媽,漂亮嘅媽媽。』但當佢終於真嘅嚟喇,我卻射咗佢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是我幹的,」他沉思著說。「以前女士們在夢裡來找我,我說:『漂亮的媽媽,漂亮的媽媽。』但當她終於真的來了,我卻射了她。」

passages.original: He moved slowly away.
passages.vernacular: 佢慢慢地走開。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他慢慢地走開。

passages.original: “Don’t go,” they called in pity.
passages.vernacular: 「別走,」佢哋可憐地喊道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「別走,」他們可憐地喊道。

passages.original: “I must,” he answered, shaking; “I am so afraid of Peter.”
passages.vernacular: 「我必須走,」佢顫抖住回答;「我太怕彼得喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我必須走,」他顫抖著回答;「我太怕彼得了。」

passages.original: It was at this tragic moment that they heard a sound which made the heart of every one of them rise to his mouth. They heard Peter crow.
passages.vernacular: 就喺呢悲劇嘅時刻,佢哋聽到一個聲音,使佢哋每個人嘅心都跳到咗嘴邊。佢哋聽到彼得喺啼叫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就在這悲劇的時刻,他們聽到一個聲音,使他們每個人的心都跳到了嘴邊。他們聽到彼得在啼叫。

passages.original: “Peter!” they cried, for it was always thus that he signalled his return.
passages.vernacular: 「彼得!」佢哋喊道,因為佢總是咁樣發信號表示佢回嚟喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「彼得!」他們喊道,因為他總是這樣發信號表示他回來了。

passages.original: “Hide her,” they whispered, and gathered hastily around Wendy. But Tootles stood aloof.
passages.vernacular: 「把佢藏起嚟,」佢哋低聲講,匆忙聚喺溫蒂周圍。但圖圖站得遠遠嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「把她藏起來,」他們低聲說,匆忙聚在溫蒂周圍。但圖圖站得遠遠的。

passages.original: Again came that ringing crow, and Peter dropped in front of them. “Greetings, boys,” he cried, and mechanically they saluted, and then again was silence.
passages.vernacular: 嗰響亮嘅啼叫聲又嚟喇,彼得落喺佢哋面前。「你哋好,男孩哋,」佢喊道,佢哋機械地敬禮,然後又係沉默。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那響亮的啼叫聲又來了,彼得落在他們面前。「你們好,男孩們,」他喊道,他們機械地敬禮,然後又是沉默。

passages.original: He frowned.
passages.vernacular: 佢皺眉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他皺眉。

passages.original: “I am back,” he said hotly, “why do you not cheer?”
passages.vernacular: 「我回嚟喇,」佢生氣地講,「你哋點解不歡呼?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我回來了,」他生氣地說,「你們為什麼不歡呼?」

passages.original: They opened their mouths, but the cheers would not come. He overlooked it in his haste to tell the glorious tidings.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋張開嘴,但歡呼聲出不嚟。佢急住要講光榮嘅消息,冇理會呢個。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們張開嘴,但歡呼聲出不來。他急著要說光榮的消息,沒有理會這個。

passages.original: “Great news, boys,” he cried, “I have brought at last a mother for you all.”
passages.vernacular: 「大好消息,男孩哋,」佢喊道,「我終於畀你哋大家帶嚟咗一個母親。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「大好消息,男孩們,」他喊道,「我終於給你們大家帶來了一個母親。」

passages.original: Still no sound, except a little thud from Tootles as he dropped on his knees.
passages.vernacular: 仍然冇聲音,除咗圖圖跪倒時發出嘅一聲輕輕嘅撲通聲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 仍然沒有聲音,除了圖圖跪倒時發出的一聲輕輕的撲通聲。

passages.original: “Have you not seen her?” asked Peter, becoming troubled. “She flew this way.”
passages.vernacular: 「你哋冇見到佢嗎?」彼得問,開始感到不安。「佢飛向呢邊喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你們沒見到她嗎?」彼得問,開始感到不安。「她飛向這邊了。」

passages.original: “Ah me!” one voice said, and another said, “Oh, mournful day.”
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀!」一個聲音講,另一個聲音講,「哦,悲哀嘅一天。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀!」一個聲音說,另一個聲音說,「哦,悲哀的一天。」

passages.original: Tootles rose. “Peter,” he said quietly, “I will show her to you,” and when the others would still have hidden her he said, “Back, twins, let Peter see.”
passages.vernacular: 圖圖站起嚟。「彼得,」佢平靜地講,「我讓你睇佢,」其他人仍想藏起佢時,佢講:「退後,雙胞胎,讓彼得睇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 圖圖站起來。「彼得,」他平靜地說,「我讓你看她,」其他人仍想藏起她時,他說:「退後,雙胞胎,讓彼得看。」

passages.original: So they all stood back, and let him see, and after he had looked for a little time he did not know what to do next.
passages.vernacular: 於是佢哋都退後,讓佢睇,佢睇咗一會兒,唔知道下一步該點算。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是他們都退後,讓他看,他看了一會兒,不知道下一步該怎麼辦。

passages.original: “She is dead,” he said uncomfortably. “Perhaps she is frightened at being dead.”
passages.vernacular: 「佢死喇,」佢不自在地講。「或者佢對死咗感到害怕。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她死了,」他不自在地說。「也許她對死了感到害怕。」

passages.original: He thought of hopping off in a comic sort of way till he was out of sight of her, and then never going near the spot any more. They would all have been glad to follow if he had done this.
passages.vernacular: 佢想用滑稽嘅方式蹦跳住離開,直到睇唔見佢,然後再都不靠近呢個地方。如果佢咁樣做喇,佢哋都會樂意跟隨。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他想用滑稽的方式蹦跳著離開,直到看不見她,然後再也不靠近這個地方。如果他這樣做了,他們都會樂意跟隨。

passages.original: But there was the arrow. He took it from her heart and faced his band.
passages.vernacular: 但嗰度有嗰支箭。佢把佢從佢嘅心口拔出嚟,面對佢嘅團隊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但那裡有那支箭。他把它從她的心口拔出來,面對他的團隊。

passages.original: “Whose arrow?” he demanded sternly.
passages.vernacular: 「邊個嘅箭?」佢嚴厲地問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「誰的箭?」他嚴厲地問。

passages.original: “Mine, Peter,” said Tootles on his knees.
passages.vernacular: 「我嘅,彼得,」圖圖跪住講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我的,彼得,」圖圖跪著說。

passages.original: “Oh, dastard hand,” Peter said, and he raised the arrow to use it as a dagger.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,懦夫嘅手,」彼得講,舉起箭要把佢當匕首用。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,懦夫的手,」彼得說,舉起箭要把它當匕首用。

passages.original: Tootles did not flinch. He bared his breast. “Strike, Peter,” he said firmly, “strike true.”
passages.vernacular: 圖圖冇退縮。佢袒露胸膛。「刺吧,彼得,」佢堅定地講,「刺準些。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 圖圖沒有退縮。他袒露胸膛。「刺吧,彼得,」他堅定地說,「刺準些。」

passages.original: Twice did Peter raise the arrow, and twice did his hand fall. “I cannot strike,” he said with awe, “there is something stays my hand.”
passages.vernacular: 彼得兩次舉起箭,兩次手都落下。「我刺不下去,」佢敬畏地講,「有乜嘢嘢擋住咗我嘅手。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 彼得兩次舉起箭,兩次手都落下。「我刺不下去,」他敬畏地說,「有什麼東西擋住了我的手。」

passages.original: All looked at him in wonder, save Nibs, who fortunately looked at Wendy.
passages.vernacular: 所有人驚奇地睇住佢,除咗尼布斯,佢幸好睇住溫蒂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所有人驚奇地看著他,除了尼布斯,他幸好看著溫蒂。

passages.original: “It is she,” he cried, “the Wendy lady, see, her arm!”
passages.vernacular: 「係佢,」佢喊道,「溫蒂女士,睇,佢嘅手臂!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是她,」他喊道,「溫蒂女士,看,她的手臂!」

passages.original: Wonderful to relate, Wendy had raised her arm. Nibs bent over her and listened reverently. “I think she said, ‘Poor Tootles,’” he whispered.
passages.vernacular: 講來奇妙,溫蒂舉起咗手臂。尼布斯俯身喺佢上面,恭敬地聽住。「我想佢講咗『可憐嘅圖圖』,」佢低聲講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 說來奇妙,溫蒂舉起了手臂。尼布斯俯身在她上面,恭敬地聽著。「我想她說了『可憐的圖圖』,」他低聲說。

passages.original: “She lives,” Peter said briefly.
passages.vernacular: 「佢活住,」彼得簡短地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她活著,」彼得簡短地說。

passages.original: Slightly cried instantly, “The Wendy lady lives.”
passages.vernacular: 輕輕即刻喊道:「溫蒂女士活住。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 輕輕立刻喊道:「溫蒂女士活著。」

passages.original: Then Peter knelt beside her and found his button. You remember she had put it on a chain that she wore round her neck.
passages.vernacular: 然後彼得跪喺佢旁邊,找到咗佢嘅鈕扣。你記得佢把佢戴喺脖子上嘅一條鏈子上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後彼得跪在她旁邊,找到了他的鈕扣。你記得她把它戴在脖子上的一條鏈子上。

passages.original: “See,” he said, “the arrow struck against this. It is the kiss I gave her. It has saved her life.”
passages.vernacular: 「睇,」佢講,「箭撞喺呢上面。呢個係我畀佢嘅吻。佢救咗佢嘅命。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「看,」他說,「箭撞在這上面。這是我給她的吻。它救了她的命。」

passages.original: “I remember kisses,” Slightly interposed quickly, “let me see it. Ay, that’s a kiss.”
passages.vernacular: 「我記得吻,」輕輕連忙插嘴,「讓我睇睇。對,嗰個係個吻。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我記得吻,」輕輕連忙插嘴,「讓我看看。對,那是個吻。」

passages.original: Peter did not hear him. He was begging Wendy to get better quickly, so that he could show her the mermaids. Of course she could not answer yet, being still in a frightful faint; but from overhead came a wailing note.
passages.vernacular: 彼得冇聽到佢。佢喺懇求溫蒂快點好起嚟,咁樣佢可以畀佢睇美人魚。當然佢仲唔能夠回答,仍然處於可怕嘅昏迷中;但從頭頂傳嚟一聲哀嚎。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 彼得沒有聽到他。他在懇求溫蒂快點好起來,這樣他可以給她看美人魚。當然她還不能回答,仍然處於可怕的昏迷中;但從頭頂傳來一聲哀嚎。

passages.original: “Listen to Tink,” said Curly, “she is crying because the Wendy lives.”
passages.vernacular: 「聽叮嘅聲音,」卷毛講,「佢因為溫蒂仲活住而哭。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「聽叮的聲音,」卷毛說,「她因為溫蒂還活著而哭。」

passages.original: Then they had to tell Peter of Tink’s crime, and almost never had they seen him look so stern.
passages.vernacular: 然後佢哋唔得不把叮噹嘅罪行告訴彼得,佢哋幾乎從冇見過佢咁嚴厲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後他們不得不把叮噹的罪行告訴彼得,他們幾乎從沒見過他這麼嚴厲。

passages.original: “Listen, Tinker Bell,” he cried, “I am your friend no more. Begone from me for ever.”
passages.vernacular: 「聽住,叮噹,」佢喊道,「我唔再係你嘅朋友喇。永遠離開我。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「聽著,叮噹,」他喊道,「我不再是你的朋友了。永遠離開我。」

passages.original: She flew on to his shoulder and pleaded, but he brushed her off. Not until Wendy again raised her arm did he relent sufficiently to say, “Well, not for ever, but for a whole week.”
passages.vernacular: 佢飛到佢肩上懇求,但佢把佢撣開。直到溫蒂又舉起手臂,佢才軟化到足以講:「好吧,唔係永遠,而係整整一個星期。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她飛到他肩上懇求,但他把她撣開。直到溫蒂又舉起手臂,他才軟化到足以說:「好吧,不是永遠,而是整整一個星期。」

passages.original: Do you think Tinker Bell was grateful to Wendy for raising her arm? Oh dear no, never wanted to pinch her so much. Fairies indeed are strange, and Peter, who understood them best, often cuffed them.
passages.vernacular: 你以為叮噹會感激溫蒂舉起手臂嗎?哎呀,唔會,佢從冇咁想捏佢。仙子確實奇怪,而最了解佢哋嘅彼得常常揍佢哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你以為叮噹會感激溫蒂舉起手臂嗎?哎呀,不會,她從沒這麼想捏她。仙子確實奇怪,而最了解她們的彼得常常揍她們。

passages.original: But what to do with Wendy in her present delicate state of health?
passages.vernacular: 但係,溫蒂而家健康狀況咁脆弱,該攞佢點算?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但是,溫蒂現在健康狀況這麼脆弱,該拿她怎麼辦?

passages.original: “Let us carry her down into the house,” Curly suggested.
passages.vernacular: 「讓我哋把佢抬下屋子裡,」卷毛建議。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「讓我們把她抬下屋子裡,」卷毛建議。

passages.original: “Ay,” said Slightly, “that is what one does with ladies.”
passages.vernacular: 「對,」輕輕講,「呢個係對女士該做嘅事。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「對,」輕輕說,「這是對女士該做的事。」

passages.original: “No, no,” Peter said, “you must not touch her. It would not be sufficiently respectful.”
passages.vernacular: 「不,不,」彼得講,「你哋唔能夠碰佢。嗰唔夠尊敬。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不,不,」彼得說,「你們不能碰她。那不夠尊敬。」

passages.original: “That,” said Slightly, “is what I was thinking.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗰,」輕輕講,「正是我喺想嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那,」輕輕說,「正是我在想的。」

passages.original: “But if she lies there,” Tootles said, “she will die.”
passages.vernacular: 「但如果佢躺喺嗰度,」圖圖講,「佢會死嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但如果她躺在那裡,」圖圖說,「她會死的。」

passages.original: “Ay, she will die,” Slightly admitted, “but there is no way out.”
passages.vernacular: 「對,佢會死,」輕輕承認,「但冇辦法。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「對,她會死,」輕輕承認,「但沒有辦法。」

passages.original: “Yes, there is,” cried Peter. “Let us build a little house round her.”
passages.vernacular: 「有,」彼得喊道。「我哋喺佢周圍蓋一座小房子。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「有,」彼得喊道。「我們在她周圍蓋一座小房子。」

passages.original: They were all delighted. “Quick,” he ordered them, “bring me each of you the best of what we have. Gut our house. Be sharp.”
passages.vernacular: 佢哋都好高興。「快,」佢命令佢哋,「每人畀我攞嚟我哋有嘅最好嘅嘢。把我哋嘅房子掏空。麻利點。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們都很高興。「快,」他命令他們,「每人給我拿來我們有的最好的東西。把我們的房子掏空。麻利點。」

passages.original: In a moment they were as busy as tailors the night before a wedding. They skurried this way and that, down for bedding, up for firewood, and while they were at it, who should appear but John and Michael. As they dragged along the ground they fell asleep standing, stopped, woke up, moved another step and slept again.
passages.vernacular: 轉眼間佢哋忙得像婚禮前夜嘅裁縫。佢哋東奔西跑,下去攞被褥,上嚟攞柴火,佢哋正忙住時,出現嘅係約翰同邁克爾。佢哋喺地上拖住腳走,站住瞓住喇,停下,醒嚟,又走一步,又瞓住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 轉眼間他們忙得像婚禮前夜的裁縫。他們東奔西跑,下去拿被褥,上來拿柴火,他們正忙著時,出現的是約翰和邁克爾。他們在地上拖著腳走,站著睡著了,停下,醒來,又走一步,又睡著。

passages.original: “John, John,” Michael would cry, “wake up! Where is Nana, John, and mother?”
passages.vernacular: 「約翰,約翰,」邁克爾喊道,「醒醒!娜娜喺邊度,約翰,仲有媽媽?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「約翰,約翰,」邁克爾喊道,「醒醒!娜娜在哪裡,約翰,還有媽媽?」

passages.original: And then John would rub his eyes and mutter, “It is true, we did fly.”
passages.vernacular: 然後約翰揉揉眼睛,喃喃講:「係真嘅,我哋真嘅飛喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後約翰揉揉眼睛,喃喃說:「是真的,我們真的飛了。」

passages.original: You may be sure they were very relieved to find Peter.
passages.vernacular: 你可以肯定佢哋找到彼得時鬆咗一口氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你可以肯定他們找到彼得時鬆了一口氣。

passages.original: “Hullo, Peter,” they said.
passages.vernacular: 「喂,彼得,」佢哋講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「喂,彼得,」他們說。

passages.original: “Hullo,” replied Peter amicably, though he had quite forgotten them. He was very busy at the moment measuring Wendy with his feet to see how large a house she would need. Of course he meant to leave room for chairs and a table. John and Michael watched him.
passages.vernacular: 「喂,」彼得友好地回答,雖然佢已經完全忘咗佢哋。佢呢陣正忙住用腳量溫蒂,睇佢需要多大嘅房子。當然佢打算留出放椅子同桌子嘅空間。約翰同邁克爾睇住佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「喂,」彼得友好地回答,雖然他已經完全忘了他們。他這時正忙著用腳量溫蒂,看她需要多大的房子。當然他打算留出放椅子和桌子的空間。約翰和邁克爾看著他。

passages.original: “Is Wendy asleep?” they asked.
passages.vernacular: 「溫蒂瞓住咗嗎?」佢哋問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「溫蒂睡著了嗎?」他們問。

passages.original: “Yes.”

“John,” Michael proposed, “let us wake her and get her to make supper for us,” but as he said it some of the other boys rushed on carrying branches for the building of the house. “Look at them!” he cried.
passages.vernacular: 「約翰,」邁克爾提議,「我哋叫醒佢,讓佢畀我哋做晚飯,」但佢講住時,其他啲男孩衝過去,攞住樹枝嚟蓋房子。「睇佢哋!」佢喊道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「約翰,」邁克爾提議,「我們叫醒她,讓她給我們做晚飯,」但他說著時,其他一些男孩衝過去,拿著樹枝來蓋房子。「看他們!」他喊道。

passages.original: “Curly,” said Peter in his most captainy voice, “see that these boys help in the building of the house.”
passages.vernacular: 「卷毛,」彼得用佢最像隊長嘅聲音講,「睇住呢啲男孩幫忙蓋房子。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「卷毛,」彼得用他最像隊長的聲音說,「看著這些男孩幫忙蓋房子。」

passages.original: “Ay, ay, sir.”
passages.vernacular: 「係,係,長官。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是,是,長官。」

passages.original: “Build a house?” exclaimed John.
passages.vernacular: 「蓋房子?」約翰喊道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「蓋房子?」約翰喊道。

passages.original: “For the Wendy,” said Curly.
passages.vernacular: 「畀溫蒂,」卷毛講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「給溫蒂,」卷毛說。

passages.original: “For Wendy?” John said, aghast. “Why, she is only a girl!”
passages.vernacular: 「畀溫蒂?」約翰驚愕地講。「哎呀,佢只係個女孩!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「給溫蒂?」約翰驚愕地說。「哎呀,她只是個女孩!」

passages.original: “That,” explained Curly, “is why we are her servants.”
passages.vernacular: 「正因為咁樣,」卷毛解釋,「我哋才係佢嘅僕人。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「正因為這樣,」卷毛解釋,「我們才是她的僕人。」

passages.original: “You? Wendy’s servants!”
passages.vernacular: 「你哋?溫蒂嘅僕人!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你們?溫蒂的僕人!」

passages.original: “Yes,” said Peter, “and you also. Away with them.”
passages.vernacular: 「對,」彼得講,「你哋都係。把佢哋帶走。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「對,」彼得說,「你們也是。把他們帶走。」

passages.original: The astounded brothers were dragged away to hack and hew and carry. “Chairs and a fender first,” Peter ordered. “Then we shall build a house round them.”
passages.vernacular: 目瞪口呆嘅兄弟倆被拖走去砍、去劈、去搬。「先做椅子同壁爐擋,」彼得命令。「然後我哋喺佢哋周圍蓋房子。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 目瞪口呆的兄弟倆被拖走去砍、去劈、去搬。「先做椅子和壁爐擋,」彼得命令。「然後我們在它們周圍蓋房子。」

passages.original: “Ay,” said Slightly, “that is how a house is built; it all comes back to me.”
passages.vernacular: 「對,」輕輕講,「房子就係咁樣蓋嘅;我全想起嚟喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「對,」輕輕說,「房子就是這樣蓋的;我全想起來了。」

passages.original: Peter thought of everything. “Slightly,” he cried, “fetch a doctor.”
passages.vernacular: 彼得乜嘢都想到喇。「輕輕,」佢喊道,「去請醫生。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 彼得什麼都想到了。「輕輕,」他喊道,「去請醫生。」

passages.original: “Ay, ay,” said Slightly at once, and disappeared, scratching his head. But he knew Peter must be obeyed, and he returned in a moment, wearing John’s hat and looking solemn.
passages.vernacular: 「係,係,」輕輕即刻講,抓住頭消失喇。但佢知道必須服從彼得,轉眼佢就回嚟喇,戴住約翰嘅帽子,一臉嚴肅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是,是,」輕輕馬上說,抓著頭消失了。但他知道必須服從彼得,轉眼他就回來了,戴著約翰的帽子,一臉嚴肅。

passages.original: “Please, sir,” said Peter, going to him, “are you a doctor?”
passages.vernacular: 「請問,先生,」彼得走向佢講,「你係醫生嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「請問,先生,」彼得走向他說,「你是醫生嗎?」

passages.original: The difference between him and the other boys at such a time was that they knew it was make-believe, while to him make-believe and true were exactly the same thing. This sometimes troubled them, as when they had to make-believe that they had had their dinners.
passages.vernacular: 呢種時候佢同其他男孩嘅區別係,佢哋知道嗰個係假裝,而對佢來講假裝同真實完全係一回事。呢有時困擾佢哋,比如佢哋得假裝已經食過晚飯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這種時候他和其他男孩的區別是,他們知道那是假裝,而對他來說假裝和真實完全是一回事。這有時困擾他們,比如他們得假裝已經吃過晚飯。

passages.original: If they broke down in their make-believe he rapped them on the knuckles.
passages.vernacular: 如果佢哋喺假裝中露餡,佢就敲佢哋嘅指關節。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果他們在假裝中露餡,他就敲他們的指關節。

passages.original: “Yes, my little man,” Slightly anxiously replied, who had chapped knuckles.
passages.vernacular: 「係,我嘅小傢伙,」輕輕焦急地回答,佢嘅指關節裂開喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是,我的小傢伙,」輕輕焦急地回答,他的指關節裂開了。

passages.original: “Please, sir,” Peter explained, “a lady lies very ill.”
passages.vernacular: 「請問,先生,」彼得解釋,「有一位女士病得好重。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「請問,先生,」彼得解釋,「有一位女士病得很重。」

passages.original: She was lying at their feet, but Slightly had the sense not to see her.
passages.vernacular: 佢就躺喺佢哋腳邊,但輕輕有頭腦,假裝冇睇見佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她就躺在他們腳邊,但輕輕有頭腦,假裝沒看見她。

passages.original: “Tut, tut, tut,” he said, “where does she lie?”
passages.vernacular: 「嘖,嘖,嘖,」佢講,「佢躺喺邊度?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嘖,嘖,嘖,」他說,「她躺在哪裡?」

passages.original: “In yonder glade.”
passages.vernacular: 「喺嗰邊林間空地。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「在那邊林間空地。」

passages.original: “I will put a glass thing in her mouth,” said Slightly, and he made-believe to do it, while Peter waited. It was an anxious moment when the glass thing was withdrawn.
passages.vernacular: 「我把一個玻璃嘢放喺佢嘴裡,」輕輕講,佢假裝做喇,彼得等住。玻璃嘢攞出嚟時係焦急嘅一刻。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我把一個玻璃東西放在她嘴裡,」輕輕說,他假裝做了,彼得等著。玻璃東西拿出來時是焦急的一刻。

passages.original: “How is she?” inquired Peter.
passages.vernacular: 「佢點樣喇?」彼得問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她怎樣了?」彼得問。

passages.original: “Tut, tut, tut,” said Slightly, “this has cured her.”
passages.vernacular: 「嘖,嘖,嘖,」輕輕講,「呢治好咗佢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嘖,嘖,嘖,」輕輕說,「這治好了她。」

passages.original: “I am glad!” Peter cried.
passages.vernacular: 「我真高興!」彼得喊道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我真高興!」彼得喊道。

passages.original: “I will call again in the evening,” Slightly said; “give her beef tea out of a cup with a spout to it;” but after he had returned the hat to John he blew big breaths, which was his habit on escaping from a difficulty.
passages.vernacular: 「我晚上再嚟睇佢,」輕輕講;「用帶嘴嘅杯子餵佢牛肉茶;」但把帽子還畀約翰後,佢大口大口地呼氣,呢個係佢逃過難關後嘅習慣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我晚上再來看她,」輕輕說;「用帶嘴的杯子餵她牛肉茶;」但把帽子還給約翰後,他大口大口地呼氣,這是他逃過難關後的習慣。

passages.original: In the meantime the wood had been alive with the sound of axes; almost everything needed for a cosy dwelling already lay at Wendy’s feet.
passages.vernacular: 同此同時,樹林裡響住斧頭聲;幾乎舒適住所所需嘅一切都已躺喺溫蒂腳邊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 與此同時,樹林裡響著斧頭聲;幾乎舒適住所所需的一切都已躺在溫蒂腳邊。

passages.original: “If only we knew,” said one, “the kind of house she likes best.”
passages.vernacular: 「要係我哋知道,」一個講,「佢最鍾意乜嘢樣嘅房子就好喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「要是我們知道,」一個說,「她最喜歡什麼樣的房子就好了。」

passages.original: “Peter,” shouted another, “she is moving in her sleep.”
passages.vernacular: 「彼得,」另一個喊道,「佢喺瞓夢中動喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「彼得,」另一個喊道,「她在睡夢中動了。」

passages.original: “Her mouth opens,” cried a third, looking respectfully into it. “Oh, lovely!”
passages.vernacular: 「佢嘅嘴張開喇,」第三個喊道,恭敬地往裡睇。「哦,可愛!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她的嘴張開了,」第三個喊道,恭敬地往裡看。「哦,可愛!」

passages.original: “Perhaps she is going to sing in her sleep,” said Peter. “Wendy, sing the kind of house you would like to have.”
passages.vernacular: 「或者佢要喺瞓夢中唱歌,」彼得講。「溫蒂,唱出你想要嘅嗰種房子。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「也許她要在睡夢中唱歌,」彼得說。「溫蒂,唱出你想要的那種房子。」

passages.original: Immediately, without opening her eyes, Wendy began to sing:
passages.vernacular: 溫蒂即刻冇睜眼就開始唱:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 溫蒂立刻沒有睜眼就開始唱:

passages.original: “I wish I had a pretty house, The littlest ever seen, With funny little red walls And roof of mossy green.”
passages.vernacular: 「我希望有一座漂亮嘅房子,係見過最小嘅,有有趣嘅小紅牆,同長滿青苔嘅綠屋頂。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我希望有一座漂亮的房子,是見過最小的,有有趣的小紅牆,和長滿青苔的綠屋頂。」

passages.original: They gurgled with joy at this, for by the greatest good luck the branches they had brought were sticky with red sap, and all the ground was carpeted with moss. As they rattled up the little house they broke into song themselves:
passages.vernacular: 佢哋高興得咯咯笑,因為運氣極好,佢哋帶嚟嘅樹枝沾住紅色嘅黏汁,地上全鋪住青苔。佢哋咔嗒咔嗒地造住小屋,自己都唱起歌嚟:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們高興得咯咯笑,因為運氣極好,他們帶來的樹枝沾著紅色的黏汁,地上全鋪著青苔。他們咔嗒咔嗒地造著小屋,自己也唱起歌來:

passages.original: “We’ve built the little walls and roof And made a lovely door, So tell us, mother Wendy, What are you wanting more?”
passages.vernacular: 「我哋造咗小牆同屋頂,做咗一扇可愛嘅門,告訴我哋吧,溫蒂媽媽,你仲要些乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們造了小牆和屋頂,做了一扇可愛的門,告訴我們吧,溫蒂媽媽,你還要些什麼?」

passages.original: To this she answered greedily:
passages.vernacular: 對此佢貪心地回答:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 對此她貪心地回答:

passages.original: “Oh, really next I think I’ll have Gay windows all about, With roses peeping in, you know, And babies peeping out.”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,真嘅,接下嚟我想要,四面快樂嘅窗子,有玫瑰從外面探頭,你知道,有嬰兒從裡面探頭。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,真的,接下來我想要,四面快樂的窗子,有玫瑰從外面探頭,你知道,有嬰兒從裡面探頭。」

passages.original: With a blow of their fists they made windows, and large yellow leaves were the blinds. But roses—?
passages.vernacular: 佢哋用拳頭一捶就做出咗窗子,大大嘅黃葉子係窗簾。但係玫瑰——?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們用拳頭一捶就做出了窗子,大大的黃葉子是窗簾。但是玫瑰——?

passages.original: “Roses,” cried Peter sternly.
passages.vernacular: 「玫瑰,」彼得嚴厲地喊道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「玫瑰,」彼得嚴厲地喊道。

passages.original: Quickly they made-believe to grow the loveliest roses up the walls.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋迅速假裝讓最可愛嘅玫瑰爬滿牆壁。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們迅速假裝讓最可愛的玫瑰爬滿牆壁。

passages.original: Babies?
passages.vernacular: 嬰兒呢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 嬰兒呢?

passages.original: To prevent Peter ordering babies they hurried into song again:
passages.vernacular: 為了防止彼得命令嬰兒,佢哋趕緊又唱起歌嚟:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 為了防止彼得命令嬰兒,他們趕緊又唱起歌來:

passages.original: “We’ve made the roses peeping out, The babes are at the door, We cannot make ourselves, you know, ’Cos we’ve been made before.”
passages.vernacular: 「我哋做咗探出頭嘅玫瑰,寶寶哋喺門口,我哋唔能夠自己做,你知道,因為我哋早已被造好。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們做了探出頭的玫瑰,寶寶們在門口,我們不能自己做,你知道,因為我們早已被造好。」

passages.original: Peter, seeing this to be a good idea, at once pretended that it was his own. The house was quite beautiful, and no doubt Wendy was very cosy within, though, of course, they could no longer see her. Peter strode up and down, ordering finishing touches. Nothing escaped his eagle eyes. Just when it seemed absolutely finished:
passages.vernacular: 彼得睇出呢個係個好主意,即刻假裝係佢自己想出嚟嘅。房子好漂亮,毫無疑問溫蒂喺裡面好舒適,雖然當然佢哋已經睇唔到佢喇。彼得大步嚟回走住,下令作最後嘅修飾。冇乜嘢逃得過佢鷹一般嘅眼睛。就喺似乎完全完成嘅時候:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 彼得看出這是個好主意,馬上假裝是他自己想出來的。房子非常漂亮,毫無疑問溫蒂在裡面很舒適,雖然當然他們已經看不到她了。彼得大步來回走著,下令作最後的修飾。沒有什麼逃得過他鷹一般的眼睛。就在似乎完全完成的時候:

passages.original: “There’s no knocker on the door,” he said.
passages.vernacular: 「門上冇門環,」佢講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「門上沒有門環,」他說。

passages.original: They were very ashamed, but Tootles gave the sole of his shoe, and it made an excellent knocker.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋好慚愧,但圖圖獻出咗佢嘅鞋底,佢成咗一個極好嘅門環。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們非常慚愧,但圖圖獻出了他的鞋底,它成了一個極好的門環。

passages.original: Absolutely finished now, they thought.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋想,而家完全完成喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們想,現在完全完成了。

passages.original: Not of bit of it. “There’s no chimney,” Peter said; “we must have a chimney.”
passages.vernacular: 啲都冇。「冇煙囪,」彼得講;「我哋必須有煙囪。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一點也沒有。「沒有煙囪,」彼得說;「我們必須有煙囪。」

passages.original: “It certainly does need a chimney,” said John importantly. This gave Peter an idea. He snatched the hat off John’s head, knocked out the bottom, and put the hat on the roof. The little house was so pleased to have such a capital chimney that, as if to say thank you, smoke immediately began to come out of the hat.
passages.vernacular: 「佢確實需要一個煙囪,」約翰裝模作樣地講。呢畀咗彼得一個主意。佢從約翰頭上搶過帽子,敲掉底部,把帽子放喺屋頂上。小房子好高興有咁一個好煙囪,好像要講謝謝似嘅,煙即刻開始從帽子裡冒出嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「它確實需要一個煙囪,」約翰裝模作樣地說。這給了彼得一個主意。他從約翰頭上搶過帽子,敲掉底部,把帽子放在屋頂上。小房子很高興有這麼一個好煙囪,好像要說謝謝似的,煙馬上開始從帽子裡冒出來。

passages.original: Now really and truly it was finished. Nothing remained to do but to knock.
passages.vernacular: 而家真真正正完成喇。只剩下敲門喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在真真正正完成了。只剩下敲門了。

passages.original: “All look your best,” Peter warned them; “first impressions are awfully important.”
passages.vernacular: 「大家都攞出最好嘅樣子,」彼得警告佢哋;「第一印象極其重要。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「大家都拿出最好的樣子,」彼得警告他們;「第一印象極其重要。」

passages.original: He was glad no one asked him what first impressions are; they were all too busy looking their best.
passages.vernacular: 佢好高興冇人問佢乜嘢係第一印象;佢哋都忙住攞出最好嘅樣子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他很高興沒有人問他什麼是第一印象;他們都忙著拿出最好的樣子。

passages.original: He knocked politely, and now the wood was as still as the children, not a sound to be heard except from Tinker Bell, who was watching from a branch and openly sneering.
passages.vernacular: 佢有禮貌地敲咗門,而家樹林像細路哋一樣安靜,除咗叮噹,聽唔到啲聲音,佢喺樹枝上睇住,公然嘲笑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他有禮貌地敲了門,現在樹林像孩子們一樣安靜,除了叮噹,聽不到一點聲音,她在樹枝上看著,公然嘲笑。

passages.original: What the boys were wondering was, would any one answer the knock? If a lady, what would she be like?
passages.vernacular: 男孩哋喺想嘅係,會有人回應敲門嗎?如果係一位女士,佢會係乜嘢樣子?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 男孩們在想的是,會有人回應敲門嗎?如果是一位女士,她會是什麼樣子?

passages.original: The door opened and a lady came out. It was Wendy. They all whipped off their hats.
passages.vernacular: 門開喇,一位女士走咗出嚟。係溫蒂。佢哋都摘下咗帽子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 門開了,一位女士走了出來。是溫蒂。他們都摘下了帽子。

passages.original: She looked properly surprised, and this was just how they had hoped she would look.
passages.vernacular: 佢睇起嚟恰當地驚訝,而呢正是佢哋所希望佢睇起嚟嘅樣子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她看起來恰當地驚訝,而這正是他們所希望她看起來的樣子。

passages.original: “Where am I?” she said.
passages.vernacular: 「我喺邊度?」佢講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我在哪裡?」她說。

passages.original: Of course Slightly was the first to get his word in. “Wendy lady,” he said rapidly, “for you we built this house.”
passages.vernacular: 當然輕輕第一個搶住講話。「溫蒂女士,」佢好快地講,「我哋為你造咗呢座房子。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當然輕輕第一個搶著說話。「溫蒂女士,」他很快地說,「我們為你造了這座房子。」

passages.original: “Oh, say you’re pleased,” cried Nibs.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,講你鍾意,」尼布斯喊道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,說你喜歡,」尼布斯喊道。

passages.original: “Lovely, darling house,” Wendy said, and they were the very words they had hoped she would say.
passages.vernacular: 「可愛嘅,親愛嘅房子,」溫蒂講,呢正是佢哋希望佢講嘅話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「可愛的,親愛的房子,」溫蒂說,這正是他們希望她說的話。

passages.original: “And we are your children,” cried the twins.
passages.vernacular: 「我哋係你嘅細路,」雙胞胎喊道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們是你的孩子,」雙胞胎喊道。

passages.original: Then all went on their knees, and holding out their arms cried, “O Wendy lady, be our mother.”
passages.vernacular: 然後所有人都跪下,伸出手臂喊道:「哦,溫蒂女士,做我哋嘅媽媽吧。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後所有人都跪下,伸出手臂喊道:「哦,溫蒂女士,做我們的媽媽吧。」

passages.original: “Ought I?” Wendy said, all shining. “Of course it’s frightfully fascinating, but you see I am only a little girl. I have no real experience.”
passages.vernacular: 「我應該嗎?」溫蒂講,滿臉發光。「當然呢極其迷人,但你睇我只係個小女孩。我冇真正嘅經驗。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我應該嗎?」溫蒂說,滿臉發光。「當然這極其迷人,但你看我只是個小女孩。我沒有真正的經驗。」

passages.original: “That doesn’t matter,” said Peter, as if he were the only person present who knew all about it, though he was really the one who knew least. “What we need is just a nice motherly person.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗰冇關係,」彼得講,好像佢係在場唯一完全知道呢件事嘅人,雖然佢其實係知道最少嘅。「我哋需要嘅只係一個好心嘅母親式嘅人。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那沒關係,」彼得說,好像他是在場唯一完全知道這件事的人,雖然他其實是知道最少的。「我們需要的只是一個好心的母親式的人。」

passages.original: “Oh dear!” Wendy said, “you see, I feel that is exactly what I am.”
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀!」溫蒂講,「你睇,我覺得嗰正是我自己。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀!」溫蒂說,「你看,我覺得那正是我自己。」

passages.original: “It is, it is,” they all cried; “we saw it at once.”
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,係嘅,」佢哋都喊道;「我哋一眼就睇出嚟喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,是的,」他們都喊道;「我們一眼就看出來了。」

passages.original: “Very well,” she said, “I will do my best. Come inside at once, you naughty children; I am sure your feet are damp. And before I put you to bed I have just time to finish the story of Cinderella.”
passages.vernacular: 「好吧,」佢講,「我會盡力。你哋呢啲淘氣嘅細路即刻進嚟;我肯定你哋嘅腳係濕嘅。喺我送你哋上床之前,我剛好有時間把灰姑娘嘅故事講完。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好吧,」她說,「我會盡力。你們這些淘氣的孩子馬上進來;我肯定你們的腳是濕的。在我送你們上床之前,我剛好有時間把灰姑娘的故事講完。」

passages.original: In they went; I don’t know how there was room for them, but you can squeeze very tight in the Neverland. And that was the first of the many joyous evenings they had with Wendy. By and by she tucked them up in the great bed in the home under the trees, but she herself slept that night in the little house, and Peter kept watch outside with drawn sword, for the pirates could be heard carousing far away and the wolves were on the prowl. The little house looked so cosy and safe in the darkness, with a bright light showing through its blinds, and the chimney smoking beautifully, and Peter standing on guard. After a time he fell asleep, and some unsteady fairies had to climb over him on their way home from an orgy. Any of the other boys obstructing the fairy path at night they would have mischiefed, but they just tweaked Peter’s nose and passed on.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋進去喇;我唔知道裡面點有地方容納佢哋,但喺永無島你可以擠得好緊。嗰個係佢哋同溫蒂一起度過嘅許多歡樂夜晚中嘅第一個。不久佢把佢哋塞進樹下家裡嘅大床上,但佢自己嗰晚瞓喺小房子裡,彼得拔出劍喺外面守夜,因為可以聽到海盜喺遠處狂歡,狼喺遊蕩。小房子喺黑暗中顯得咁舒適安全,明亮嘅燈光透過窗簾照出嚟,煙囪冒住美麗嘅煙,彼得站住守衛。過咗一會兒佢瞓住喇,啲腳步不穩嘅仙子從狂歡回家嘅路上唔得不爬過佢。如果係其他任何男孩夜裡擋住仙子嘅路,佢哋會捉弄佢,但佢哋只係擰咗擰彼得嘅鼻子就過去喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們進去了;我不知道裡面怎麼有地方容納他們,但在永無島你可以擠得很緊。那是他們同溫蒂一起度過的許多歡樂夜晚中的第一個。不久她把他們塞進樹下家裡的大床上,但她自己那晚睡在小房子裡,彼得拔出劍在外面守夜,因為可以聽到海盜在遠處狂歡,狼在遊蕩。小房子在黑暗中顯得那麼舒適安全,明亮的燈光透過窗簾照出來,煙囪冒著美麗的煙,彼得站著守衛。過了一會兒他睡著了,一些腳步不穩的仙子從狂歡回家的路上不得不爬過他。如果是其他任何男孩夜裡擋住仙子的路,她們會捉弄他,但她們只是擰了擰彼得的鼻子就過去了。

chapters.title: Chapter VII: The Home Under the Ground 第七章:地下的家

passages.original: One of the first things Peter did next day was to measure Wendy and John and Michael for hollow trees. Hook, you remember, had sneered at the boys for thinking they needed a tree apiece, but this was ignorance, for unless your tree fitted you it was difficult to go up and down, and no two of the boys were quite the same size. Once you fitted, you drew in your breath at the top, and down you went at exactly the right speed, while to ascend you drew in and let out alternately, and so wriggled up. Of course, when you have mastered the action you are able to do these things without thinking of them, and nothing can be more graceful.
passages.vernacular: 第二天彼得做嘅第一批事之一,係為溫蒂、約翰同邁克爾量空心樹嘅尺寸。你記得,虎克曾嘲笑男孩哋以為每人需要一棵樹,但呢個係無知,因為除非你嘅樹適合你,否則上上下下好困難,而且冇兩個男孩嘅大小完全相同。一旦合身,你喺樹頂吸一口氣,就以恰到好處嘅速度滑下去,而要上去,你交替地吸氣同呼氣,咁樣蠕動住爬上去。當然,當你掌握咗動作,你就能不假思索地做呢啲事,冇乜嘢比呢更優雅嘅喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 第二天彼得做的第一批事之一,是為溫蒂、約翰和邁克爾量空心樹的尺寸。你記得,虎克曾嘲笑男孩們以為每人需要一棵樹,但這是無知,因為除非你的樹適合你,否則上上下下很困難,而且沒有兩個男孩的大小完全相同。一旦合身,你在樹頂吸一口氣,就以恰到好處的速度滑下去,而要上去,你交替地吸氣和呼氣,這樣蠕動著爬上去。當然,當你掌握了動作,你就能不假思索地做這些事,沒有什麼比這更優雅的了。

passages.original: But you simply must fit, and Peter measures you for your tree as carefully as for a suit of clothes: the only difference being that the clothes are made to fit you, while you have to be made to fit the tree. Usually it is done quite easily, as by your wearing too many garments or too few, but if you are bumpy in awkward places or the only available tree is an odd shape, Peter does some things to you, and after that you fit. Once you fit, great care must be taken to go on fitting, and this, as Wendy was to discover to her delight, keeps a whole family in perfect condition.
passages.vernacular: 但你就係必須合身,彼得為你量樹嘅尺寸像為你量衣服一樣仔細:唯一嘅區別係衣服係做得適合你,而你卻得被弄得適合樹。通常呢個好容易做到,比如你穿嘅衣服太多或太少,但如果你喺尷尬嘅地方有凸起,或唯一可用嘅樹形狀古怪,彼得會對你做啲事,然後你就合身喇。一旦合身,必須好小心地保持合身,而呢,正如溫蒂高興地發現嘅,使整個家庭保持完美嘅狀態。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但你就是必須合身,彼得為你量樹的尺寸像為你量衣服一樣仔細:唯一的區別是衣服是做得適合你,而你卻得被弄得適合樹。通常這很容易做到,比如你穿的衣服太多或太少,但如果你在尷尬的地方有凸起,或唯一可用的樹形狀古怪,彼得會對你做一些事,然後你就合身了。一旦合身,必須非常小心地保持合身,而這,正如溫蒂高興地發現的,使整個家庭保持完美的狀態。

passages.original: Wendy and Michael fitted their trees at the first try, but John had to be altered a little.
passages.vernacular: 溫蒂同邁克爾第一次就合咗佢哋嘅樹,但約翰需要稍作改動。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 溫蒂和邁克爾第一次就合了他們的樹,但約翰需要稍作改動。

passages.original: After a few days’ practice they could go up and down as gaily as buckets in a well. And how ardently they grew to love their home under the ground; especially Wendy. It consisted of one large room, as all houses should do, with a floor in which you could dig if you wanted to go fishing, and in this floor grew stout mushrooms of a charming colour, which were used as stools. A Never tree tried hard to grow in the centre of the room, but every morning they sawed the trunk through, level with the floor. By tea-time it was always about two feet high, and then they put a door on top of it, the whole thus becoming a table; as soon as they cleared away, they sawed off the trunk again, and thus there was more room to play. There was an enormous fireplace which was in almost any part of the room where you cared to light it, and across this Wendy stretched strings, made of fibre, from which she suspended her washing. The bed was tilted against the wall by day, and let down at 6:30, when it filled nearly half the room; and all the boys slept in it, except Michael, lying like sardines in a tin. There was a strict rule against turning round until one gave the signal, when all turned at once. Michael should have used it also, but Wendy would have a baby, and he was the littlest, and you know what women are, and the short and long of it is that he was hung up in a basket.
passages.vernacular: 練習幾天後,佢哋就能像井裡嘅水桶一樣歡快地上上下下。佢哋幾咁熱烈地愛上咗佢哋嘅地下家園;尤其係溫蒂。佢由一個大房間組成,所有房子都該如此,地板可以挖,如果你想去釣魚,地板上長住顏色迷人嘅粗壯蘑菇,用作凳子。一棵永無樹拼命想喺房間中央長出嚟,但每天早晨佢哋把樹幹鋸平,同地板齊平。到下午茶時間佢總是長到兩呎左右高,然後佢哋喺上面放一扇門,整個就成咗桌子;一收拾完,佢哋又把樹幹鋸掉,咁樣有更多玩耍嘅空間。有一個巨大嘅壁爐,幾乎房間裡你想生火嘅任何地方都可以,溫蒂喺佢上面拉咗纖維做嘅繩子,掛佢洗嘅衣服。床白天靠牆斜立住,六點半放下嚟,呢陣佢佔咗幾乎半個房間;所有男孩都瞓喺上面,除咗邁克爾,像沙丁魚罐頭裡嘅沙丁魚一樣躺住。有一條嚴格嘅規定,喺有人發出信號之前不許翻身,信號一發,所有人同時翻。邁克爾本該都用佢,但溫蒂要有一個嬰兒,而佢係最小嘅,你知道女人係點樣嘅,總之結果係佢被吊喺一個籃子裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 練習幾天後,他們就能像井裡的水桶一樣歡快地上上下下。他們多麼熱烈地愛上了他們的地下家園;尤其是溫蒂。它由一個大房間組成,所有房子都該如此,地板可以挖,如果你想去釣魚,地板上長著顏色迷人的粗壯蘑菇,用作凳子。一棵永無樹拼命想在房間中央長出來,但每天早晨他們把樹幹鋸平,與地板齊平。到下午茶時間它總是長到兩呎左右高,然後他們在上面放一扇門,整個就成了桌子;一收拾完,他們又把樹幹鋸掉,這樣有更多玩耍的空間。有一個巨大的壁爐,幾乎房間裡你想生火的任何地方都可以,溫蒂在它上面拉了纖維做的繩子,掛她洗的衣服。床白天靠牆斜立著,六點半放下來,這時它佔了幾乎半個房間;所有男孩都睡在上面,除了邁克爾,像沙丁魚罐頭裡的沙丁魚一樣躺著。有一條嚴格的規定,在有人發出信號之前不許翻身,信號一發,所有人同時翻。邁克爾本該也用它,但溫蒂要有一個嬰兒,而他是最小的,你知道女人是怎樣的,總之結果是他被吊在一個籃子裡。

passages.original: It was rough and simple, and not unlike what baby bears would have made of an underground house in the same circumstances. But there was one recess in the wall, no larger than a bird-cage, which was the private apartment of Tinker Bell. It could be shut off from the rest of the house by a tiny curtain, which Tink, who was most fastidious, always kept drawn when dressing or undressing. No woman, however large, could have had a more exquisite boudoir and bed-chamber combined. The couch, as she always called it, was a genuine Queen Mab, with club legs; and she varied the bedspreads according to what fruit-blossom was in season. Her mirror was a Puss-in-Boots, of which there are now only three, unchipped, known to fairy dealers; the washstand was Pie-crust and reversible, the chest of drawers an authentic Charming the Sixth, and the carpet and rugs the best (the early) period of Margery and Robin. There was a chandelier from Tiddlywinks for the look of the thing, but of course she lit the residence herself. Tink was very contemptuous of the rest of the house, as indeed was perhaps inevitable, and her chamber, though beautiful, looked rather conceited, having the appearance of a nose permanently turned up.
passages.vernacular: 佢粗糙簡單,不像小熊喺同樣情況下造出嘅地下房子。但牆上有一個凹處,不比鳥籠大,嗰個係叮噹嘅私人房間。佢可以用一塊小窗簾同房子嘅其餘部分隔開,好挑剔嘅叮喺穿衣脫衣時總是把窗簾拉上。冇一個女人,不管多大,能擁有更精緻嘅閨房兼臥室。佢總是稱為長榻嘅嗰張沙發,係真正嘅仙后馬布式,有棍棒腿;佢根據當季開嘅果樹花換不同嘅床罩。佢嘅鏡子係穿靴子嘅貓款式,而家仙子古董商所知嘅完好無缺嘅只有三面;洗手台係餡餅皮式,可以翻轉,五斗櫃係正宗嘅查爾明六世,地毯係瑪格麗同羅賓最好嘅(早期)時期嘅。有一盞來自跳棋嘅吊燈,用嚟好睇,但當然佢自己畀呢住所點燈。叮對房子嘅其他部分好輕蔑,呢或者係不可避免嘅,佢嘅房間雖然美麗,卻顯得相當自負,睇起嚟像一個永遠翹住嘅鼻子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它粗糙簡單,不像小熊在同樣情況下造出的地下房子。但牆上有一個凹處,不比鳥籠大,那是叮噹的私人房間。它可以用一塊小窗簾與房子的其餘部分隔開,非常挑剔的叮在穿衣脫衣時總是把窗簾拉上。沒有一個女人,不管多大,能擁有更精緻的閨房兼臥室。她總是稱為長榻的那張沙發,是真正的仙后馬布式,有棍棒腿;她根據當季開的果樹花換不同的床罩。她的鏡子是穿靴子的貓款式,現在仙子古董商所知的完好無缺的只有三面;洗手台是餡餅皮式,可以翻轉,五斗櫃是正宗的查爾明六世,地毯是瑪格麗和羅賓最好的(早期)時期的。有一盞來自跳棋的吊燈,用來好看,但當然她自己給這住所點燈。叮對房子的其他部分非常輕蔑,這也許是不可避免的,她的房間雖然美麗,卻顯得相當自負,看起來像一個永遠翹著的鼻子。

passages.original: I suppose it was all especially entrancing to Wendy, because those rampagious boys of hers gave her so much to do. Really there were whole weeks when, except perhaps with a stocking in the evening, she was never above ground. The cooking, I can tell you, kept her nose to the pot, and even if there was nothing in it, even if there was no pot, she had to keep watching that it came aboil just the same. You never exactly knew whether there would be a real meal or just a make-believe, it all depended upon Peter’s whim: he could eat, really eat, if it was part of a game, but he could not stodge just to feel stodgy, which is what most children like better than anything else; the next best thing being to talk about it. Make-believe was so real to him that during a meal of it you could see him getting rounder. Of course it was trying, but you simply had to follow his lead, and if you could prove to him that you were getting loose for your tree he let you stodge.
passages.vernacular: 我想呢一切對溫蒂特別有迷惑力,因為佢嗰啲胡鬧嘅男孩哋畀咗佢咁多事要做。講真嘅,有整整幾個星期,除咗或者晚上縫補襪子時,佢從冇到地面上去過。做飯,我可以告訴你,讓佢嘅鼻子總是貼喺鍋上,即使裡面乜嘢都冇,即使根本冇鍋,佢都得照樣睇住佢煮開。你永遠唔知道到底係真正嘅一餐定係假裝嘅,呢全睇彼得嘅心血嚟潮:如果係遊戲嘅一部分,佢能食,真嘅食,但佢唔能夠僅僅為了感覺飽脹而飽食,而呢個係大多數細路最鍾意嘅事;第二鍾意嘅係談論佢。假裝對佢來講咁真實,食假裝嘅一餐時你能睇到佢變圓。當然呢個好折磨人,但你只能跟住佢嘅領導,如果你能向佢證明你對你嘅樹來講變鬆喇,佢就讓你飽食。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想這一切對溫蒂特別有迷惑力,因為她那些胡鬧的男孩們給了她那麼多事要做。說真的,有整整幾個星期,除了也許晚上縫補襪子時,她從沒到地面上去過。做飯,我可以告訴你,讓她的鼻子總是貼在鍋上,即使裡面什麼都沒有,即使根本沒有鍋,她也得照樣看著它煮開。你永遠不知道到底是真正的一餐還是假裝的,這全看彼得的心血來潮:如果是遊戲的一部分,他能吃,真的吃,但他不能僅僅為了感覺飽脹而飽食,而這是大多數孩子最喜歡的事;第二喜歡的是談論它。假裝對他來說那麼真實,吃假裝的一餐時你能看到他變圓。當然這很折磨人,但你只能跟著他的領導,如果你能向他證明你對你的樹來說變鬆了,他就讓你飽食。

passages.original: Wendy’s favourite time for sewing and darning was after they had all gone to bed. Then, as she expressed it, she had a breathing time for herself; and she occupied it in making new things for them, and putting double pieces on the knees, for they were all most frightfully hard on their knees.
passages.vernacular: 溫蒂縫紉同補衣服最鍾意嘅時間係喺佢哋都上床之後。嗰時,如佢所講,佢有一段屬於自己嘅喘息時間;佢用嚟畀佢哋做新嘢,喺膝蓋上加雙層布,因為佢哋都極其磨損膝蓋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 溫蒂縫紉和補衣服最喜歡的時間是在他們都上床之後。那時,如她所說,她有一段屬於自己的喘息時間;她用來給他們做新東西,在膝蓋上加雙層布,因為他們都極其磨損膝蓋。

passages.original: When she sat down to a basketful of their stockings, every heel with a hole in it, she would fling up her arms and exclaim, “Oh dear, I am sure I sometimes think spinsters are to be envied!”
passages.vernacular: 當佢坐下嚟面對一籃子佢哋嘅襪子,每隻腳跟都有個洞時,佢會舉起雙臂喊道:「哎呀,我有時真覺得老姑娘值得羨慕!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當她坐下來面對一籃子他們的襪子,每隻腳跟都有個洞時,她會舉起雙臂喊道:「哎呀,我有時真覺得老姑娘值得羨慕!」

passages.original: Her face beamed when she exclaimed this.
passages.vernacular: 佢喊呢話時,臉上容光煥發。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她喊這話時,臉上容光煥發。

passages.original: You remember about her pet wolf. Well, it very soon discovered that she had come to the island and it found her out, and they just ran into each other’s arms. After that it followed her about everywhere.
passages.vernacular: 你記得佢嗰隻寵物狼。嗯,佢好快就發現佢嚟到咗島上,找到咗佢,佢哋就撲進彼此嘅懷抱。從嗰以後佢到處跟住佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你記得她那隻寵物狼。嗯,它很快就發現她來到了島上,找到了她,它們就撲進彼此的懷抱。從那以後它到處跟著她。

passages.original: As time wore on did she think much about the beloved parents she had left behind her? This is a difficult question, because it is quite impossible to say how time does wear on in the Neverland, where it is calculated by moons and suns, and there are ever so many more of them than on the mainland. But I am afraid that Wendy did not really worry about her father and mother; she was absolutely confident that they would always keep the window open for her to fly back by, and this gave her complete ease of mind. What did disturb her at times was that John remembered his parents vaguely only, as people he had once known, while Michael was quite willing to believe that she was really his mother. These things scared her a little, and nobly anxious to do her duty, she tried to fix the old life in their minds by setting them examination papers on it, as like as possible to the ones she used to do at school. The other boys thought this awfully interesting, and insisted on joining, and they made slates for themselves, and sat round the table, writing and thinking hard about the questions she had written on another slate and passed round. They were the most ordinary questions—“What was the colour of Mother’s eyes? Which was taller, Father or Mother? Was Mother blonde or brunette? Answer all three questions if possible.” “(A) Write an essay of not less than 40 words on How I spent my last Holidays, or The Characters of Father and Mother compared. Only one of these to be attempted.” Or “(1) Describe Mother’s laugh; (2) Describe Father’s laugh; (3) Describe Mother’s Party Dress; (4) Describe the Kennel and its Inmate.”
passages.vernacular: 隨住時間過去,佢係咪常想起佢留下嘅親愛嘅父母?呢個係個難題,因為根本唔可能講時間喺永無島係點樣過去嘅,嗰度用月亮同太陽計算,而且比大陸上多得多。但我怕溫蒂其實並不為佢嘅父母擔心;佢絕對相信佢哋會一直為佢開住窗,讓佢飛回去,呢使佢完全放心。有時困擾佢嘅係,約翰只模糊地記得佢嘅父母,像曾經認識嘅人,而邁克爾完全願意相信佢真嘅係佢嘅媽媽。呢啲事讓佢有點害怕,佢高尚地急於盡自己嘅責任,佢試圖通過畀佢哋出考卷嚟把舊生活固定喺佢哋腦子裡,盡可能像佢以前喺學校做嘅嗰種。其他男孩認為呢極其有趣,堅持要加入,佢哋畀自己做咗石板,圍住桌子坐下,寫字,拚命思考佢寫喺另一塊石板上傳閱嘅問題。呢啲係最普通嘅問題——「媽媽嘅眼睛係乜嘢顏色?爸爸同媽媽邊個更高?媽媽係金髮定係棕髮?如可能,三個問題都回答。」「(甲)寫一篇不少於四十字嘅文章,題目為《我點樣度過上個假期》,或《爸爸同媽媽性格比較》。只准選其中一題。」或者「(一)描述媽媽嘅笑聲;(二)描述爸爸嘅笑聲;(三)描述媽媽嘅宴會禮服;(四)描述狗窩同佢嘅住客。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 隨著時間過去,她是否常想起她留下的親愛的父母?這是個難題,因為根本不可能說時間在永無島是怎樣過去的,那裡用月亮和太陽計算,而且比大陸上多得多。但我怕溫蒂其實並不為她的父母擔心;她絕對相信他們會一直為她開著窗,讓她飛回去,這使她完全放心。有時困擾她的是,約翰只模糊地記得他的父母,像曾經認識的人,而邁克爾完全願意相信她真的是他的媽媽。這些事讓她有點害怕,她高尚地急於盡自己的責任,她試圖通過給他們出考卷來把舊生活固定在他們腦子裡,盡可能像她以前在學校做的那種。其他男孩認為這極其有趣,堅持要加入,他們給自己做了石板,圍著桌子坐下,寫字,拚命思考她寫在另一塊石板上傳閱的問題。這些是最普通的問題——「媽媽的眼睛是什麼顏色?爸爸和媽媽哪個更高?媽媽是金髮還是棕髮?如可能,三個問題都回答。」「(甲)寫一篇不少於四十字的文章,題目為《我怎樣度過上個假期》,或《爸爸和媽媽性格比較》。只准選其中一題。」或者「(一)描述媽媽的笑聲;(二)描述爸爸的笑聲;(三)描述媽媽的宴會禮服;(四)描述狗窩和它的住客。」

passages.original: They were just everyday questions like these, and when you could not answer them you were told to make a cross; and it was really dreadful what a number of crosses even John made. Of course the only boy who replied to every question was Slightly, and no one could have been more hopeful of coming out first, but his answers were perfectly ridiculous, and he really came out last: a melancholy thing.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋就係像咁樣嘅日常問題,當你答不出嚟時,就被告知畫一個叉;連約翰都畫咗咁多叉,實在可怕。當然唯一回答每一道問題嘅男孩係輕輕,冇人比佢更有希望攞第一,但佢嘅答案完全荒謬,佢其實攞咗最後:真係令人憂傷嘅事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它們就是像這樣的日常問題,當你答不出來時,就被告知畫一個叉;連約翰都畫了那麼多叉,實在可怕。當然唯一回答每一道問題的男孩是輕輕,沒有人比他更有希望拿第一,但他的答案完全荒謬,他其實拿了最後:真是令人憂傷的事。

passages.original: Peter did not compete. For one thing he despised all mothers except Wendy, and for another he was the only boy on the island who could neither write nor spell; not the smallest word. He was above all that sort of thing.
passages.vernacular: 彼得不參加比賽。一方面佢鄙視除咗溫蒂以外嘅所有母親,另一方面佢係島上唯一既唔會寫都唔會拼嘅男孩;連最小嘅字都唔會。佢超越咗所有呢類事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 彼得不參加比賽。一方面他鄙視除了溫蒂以外的所有母親,另一方面他是島上唯一既不會寫也不會拼的男孩;連最小的字也不會。他超越了所有這類事。

passages.original: By the way, the questions were all written in the past tense. What was the colour of Mother’s eyes, and so on. Wendy, you see, had been forgetting, too.
passages.vernacular: 順便講一下,問題都係用過去式寫嘅。媽媽嘅眼睛係乜嘢顏色,等等。你睇,溫蒂都喺忘記喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 順便說一下,問題都是用過去式寫的。媽媽的眼睛是什麼顏色,等等。你看,溫蒂也在忘記了。

passages.original: Adventures, of course, as we shall see, were of daily occurrence; but about this time Peter invented, with Wendy’s help, a new game that fascinated him enormously, until he suddenly had no more interest in it, which, as you have been told, was what always happened with his games. It consisted in pretending not to have adventures, in doing the sort of thing John and Michael had been doing all their lives, sitting on stools flinging balls in the air, pushing each other, going out for walks and coming back without having killed so much as a grizzly. To see Peter doing nothing on a stool was a great sight; he could not help looking solemn at such times, to sit still seemed to him such a comic thing to do. He boasted that he had gone walking for the good of his health. For several suns these were the most novel of all adventures to him; and John and Michael had to pretend to be delighted also; otherwise he would have treated them severely.
passages.vernacular: 冒險當然,我哋將會睇到,每天都喺發生;但大約呢個時候,彼得喺溫蒂嘅幫助下發明了一個新遊戲,令佢極其著迷,直到佢突然對佢失去咗興趣,呢正如你已經被告知嘅,係佢嘅遊戲總會發生嘅事。佢係假裝冇冒險,做約翰同邁克爾一生一直喺做嘅嗰類事,坐喺凳子上向空中拋球,互相推搡,出去散步回嚟,一隻灰熊都冇殺過。睇彼得坐喺凳子上乜嘢都不做係一大奇觀;呢種時候佢不禁顯得嚴肅,坐住不動對佢來講似乎係咁滑稽嘅事。佢誇口講佢去散步係為了健康。好幾個太陽日裡,呢啲係佢最新奇嘅冒險;約翰同邁克爾都得假裝高興;否則佢會嚴厲對待佢哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 冒險當然,我們將會看到,每天都在發生;但大約這個時候,彼得在溫蒂的幫助下發明了一個新遊戲,令他極其著迷,直到他突然對它失去了興趣,這正如你已經被告知的,是他的遊戲總會發生的事。它是假裝沒有冒險,做約翰和邁克爾一生一直在做的那類事,坐在凳子上向空中拋球,互相推搡,出去散步回來,一隻灰熊都沒殺過。看彼得坐在凳子上什麼也不做是一大奇觀;這種時候他不禁顯得嚴肅,坐著不動對他來說似乎是那麼滑稽的事。他誇口說他去散步是為了健康。好幾個太陽日裡,這些是他最新奇的冒險;約翰和邁克爾也得假裝高興;否則他會嚴厲對待他們。

passages.original: He often went out alone, and when he came back you were never absolutely certain whether he had had an adventure or not. He might have forgotten it so completely that he said nothing about it; and then when you went out you found the body; and, on the other hand, he might say a great deal about it, and yet you could not find the body. Sometimes he came home with his head bandaged, and then Wendy cooed over him and bathed it in lukewarm water, while he told a dazzling tale. But she was never quite sure, you know. There were, however, many adventures which she knew to be true because she was in them herself, and there were still more that were at least partly true, for the other boys were in them and said they were wholly true. To describe them all would require a book as large as an English-Latin, Latin-English Dictionary, and the most we can do is to give one as a specimen of an average hour on the island. The difficulty is which one to choose. Should we take the brush with the redskins at Slightly Gulch? It was a sanguinary affair, and especially interesting as showing one of Peter’s peculiarities, which was that in the middle of a fight he would suddenly change sides. At the Gulch, when victory was still in the balance, sometimes leaning this way and sometimes that, he called out, “I’m redskin to-day; what are you, Tootles?” And Tootles answered, “Redskin; what are you, Nibs?” and Nibs said, “Redskin; what are you Twin?” and so on; and they were all redskins; and of course this would have ended the fight had not the real redskins fascinated by Peter’s methods, agreed to be lost boys for that once, and so at it they all went again, more fiercely than ever.
passages.vernacular: 佢常常獨自出去,佢回嚟時,你永遠唔能夠絕對確定佢有冇遇到冒險。佢可能完全忘喇,所以乜嘢都冇講;然後你出去時發現咗屍體;另一方面,佢可能講咗好多,而你卻找唔到屍體。有時佢頭上綁住繃帶回家,然後溫蒂疼愛地對佢咕咕叫住,用溫水畀佢洗頭,而佢講住一個令人眼花繚亂嘅故事。但你知道,佢從來不太確定。不過,有許多冒險佢知道係真嘅,因為佢自己都喺其中,仲有更多至少部分係真嘅,因為其他男孩喺其中,並講佢哋係完全真嘅。要描述佢哋全部需要一本像英拉、拉英詞典咁大嘅書,我哋最多只能舉出一個,作為島上普通一個小時嘅樣本。困難係選邊一個。我哋該取喺輕輕峽谷同紅番嘅小戰嗎?嗰個係一場血腥嘅事,特別有趣,因為佢顯示出彼得嘅一個怪癖,就係喺戰鬥中間佢會突然換邊。喺峽谷,勝利仍喺天平上,有時偏呢邊有時偏嗰邊時,佢喊道:「我今日係紅番;你係乜嘢,圖圖?」圖圖回答:「紅番;你係乜嘢,尼布斯?」尼布斯講:「紅番;你係乜嘢,雙胞胎?」等等;佢哋都成咗紅番;當然呢本會結束戰鬥,要唔係真正嘅紅番被彼得嘅方法迷住,同意嗰一次當迷失嘅男孩,於是佢哋又全都打起嚟,比以往更猛烈。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他常常獨自出去,他回來時,你永遠不能絕對確定他有沒有遇到冒險。他可能完全忘了,所以什麼也沒說;然後你出去時發現了屍體;另一方面,他可能說了很多,而你卻找不到屍體。有時他頭上綁著繃帶回家,然後溫蒂疼愛地對他咕咕叫著,用溫水給他洗頭,而他講著一個令人眼花繚亂的故事。但你知道,她從來不太確定。不過,有許多冒險她知道是真的,因為她自己也在其中,還有更多至少部分是真的,因為其他男孩在其中,並說它們是完全真的。要描述它們全部需要一本像英拉、拉英詞典那麼大的書,我們最多只能舉出一個,作為島上普通一個小時的樣本。困難是選哪一個。我們該取在輕輕峽谷同紅番的小戰嗎?那是一場血腥的事,特別有趣,因為它顯示出彼得的一個怪癖,就是在戰鬥中間他會突然換邊。在峽谷,勝利仍在天平上,有時偏這邊有時偏那邊時,他喊道:「我今天是紅番;你是什麼,圖圖?」圖圖回答:「紅番;你是什麼,尼布斯?」尼布斯說:「紅番;你是什麼,雙胞胎?」等等;他們都成了紅番;當然這本會結束戰鬥,要不是真正的紅番被彼得的方法迷住,同意那一次當迷失的男孩,於是他們又全都打起來,比以往更猛烈。

passages.original: The extraordinary upshot of this adventure was—but we have not decided yet that this is the adventure we are to narrate. Perhaps a better one would be the night attack by the redskins on the house under the ground, when several of them stuck in the hollow trees and had to be pulled out like corks. Or we might tell how Peter saved Tiger Lily’s life in the Mermaids’ Lagoon, and so made her his ally.
passages.vernacular: 呢次冒險嘅驚人結果係——但我哋仲冇決定呢個係唔係我哋要講嘅冒險。或者更好嘅係紅番夜襲地下房子,有幾個紅番卡喺空心樹裡,唔得不像瓶塞一樣被拔出嚟。或者我哋可以講彼得點樣喺美人魚潟湖救咗虎百合嘅命,從而使佢成為佢嘅盟友。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這次冒險的驚人結果是——但我們還沒決定這是不是我們要講的冒險。也許更好的是紅番夜襲地下房子,有幾個紅番卡在空心樹裡,不得不像瓶塞一樣被拔出來。或者我們可以講彼得怎樣在美人魚潟湖救了虎百合的命,從而使她成為他的盟友。

passages.original: Or we could tell of that cake the pirates cooked so that the boys might eat it and perish; and how they placed it in one cunning spot after another; but always Wendy snatched it from the hands of her children, so that in time it lost its succulence, and became as hard as a stone, and was used as a missile, and Hook fell over it in the dark.
passages.vernacular: 或者我哋可以講海盜烤嘅嗰個蛋糕,為了讓男孩哋食咗佢死掉;佢哋把佢放喺一個又一個狡猾嘅地方;但溫蒂總是從佢細路哋手裡把佢搶走,所以時間久咗佢失去咗水分,硬得像石頭,被用作投擲物,虎克喺黑暗中被佢絆倒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 或者我們可以講海盜烤的那個蛋糕,為了讓男孩們吃了它死掉;他們把它放在一個又一個狡猾的地方;但溫蒂總是從她孩子們手裡把它搶走,所以時間久了它失去了水分,硬得像石頭,被用作投擲物,虎克在黑暗中被它絆倒。

passages.original: Or suppose we tell of the birds that were Peter’s friends, particularly of the Never bird that built in a tree overhanging the lagoon, and how the nest fell into the water, and still the bird sat on her eggs, and Peter gave orders that she was not to be disturbed. That is a pretty story, and the end shows how grateful a bird can be; but if we tell it we must also tell the whole adventure of the lagoon, which would of course be telling two adventures rather than just one. A shorter adventure, and quite as exciting, was Tinker Bell’s attempt, with the help of some street fairies, to have the sleeping Wendy conveyed on a great floating leaf to the mainland. Fortunately the leaf gave way and Wendy woke, thinking it was bath-time, and swam back. Or again, we might choose Peter’s defiance of the lions, when he drew a circle round him on the ground with an arrow and dared them to cross it; and though he waited for hours, with the other boys and Wendy looking on breathlessly from trees, not one of them dared to accept his challenge.
passages.vernacular: 或者假如我哋講彼得嘅朋友鳥類,特別係喺潟湖上方一棵樹上築巢嘅永無鳥,巢點樣掉進水裡,鳥仍然坐喺佢嘅蛋上,彼得下令不許打擾佢。嗰個係一個漂亮嘅故事,結局顯示一隻鳥能幾咁感恩;但如果我哋講佢,都必須講整個潟湖嘅冒險,呢當然就係講兩個冒險而不只係一個。一個較短嘅冒險,都一樣刺激,係叮噹喺啲街頭仙子嘅幫助下,試圖讓瞓住嘅溫蒂坐喺一片漂浮嘅大葉子上被送到大陸。幸運嘅係葉子支撐不住,溫蒂醒喇,以為係洗澡時間,游回嚟喇。或者,我哋可以選彼得對獅子嘅挑戰,佢用一支箭喺地上圍住自己畫咗一個圈,挑戰牠哋越過佢;雖然佢等咗幾個小時,其他男孩同溫蒂喺樹上屏息睇住,牠哋冇一頭敢接受佢嘅挑戰。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 或者假如我們講彼得的朋友鳥類,特別是在潟湖上方一棵樹上築巢的永無鳥,巢怎樣掉進水裡,鳥仍然坐在她的蛋上,彼得下令不許打擾她。那是一個漂亮的故事,結局顯示一隻鳥能多麼感恩;但如果我們講它,也必須講整個潟湖的冒險,這當然就是講兩個冒險而不只是一個。一個較短的冒險,也一樣刺激,是叮噹在一些街頭仙子的幫助下,試圖讓睡著的溫蒂坐在一片漂浮的大葉子上被送到大陸。幸運的是葉子支撐不住,溫蒂醒了,以為是洗澡時間,游回來了。或者,我們可以選彼得對獅子的挑戰,他用一支箭在地上圍著自己畫了一個圈,挑戰牠們越過它;雖然他等了幾個小時,其他男孩和溫蒂在樹上屏息看著,牠們沒有一頭敢接受他的挑戰。

passages.original: Which of these adventures shall we choose? The best way will be to toss for it.
passages.vernacular: 我哋選呢啲冒險中嘅邊一個?最好嘅辦法係擲錢幣決定。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們選這些冒險中的哪一個?最好的辦法是擲錢幣決定。

passages.original: I have tossed, and the lagoon has won. This almost makes one wish that the gulch or the cake or Tink’s leaf had won. Of course I could do it again, and make it best out of three; however, perhaps fairest to stick to the lagoon.
passages.vernacular: 我擲喇,潟湖贏喇。呢幾乎讓人希望係峽谷或蛋糕或叮嘅葉子贏喇。當然我可以再擲一次,三局兩勝;然而,或者最公平嘅係堅持潟湖。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我擲了,潟湖贏了。這幾乎讓人希望是峽谷或蛋糕或叮的葉子贏了。當然我可以再擲一次,三局兩勝;然而,也許最公平的是堅持潟湖。

chapters.title: Chapter VIII: The Mermaids' Lagoon 第八章:美人魚潟湖

passages.original: If you shut your eyes and are a lucky one, you may see at times a shapeless pool of lovely pale colours suspended in the darkness; then if you squeeze your eyes tighter, the pool begins to take shape, and the colours become so vivid that with another squeeze they must go on fire. But just before they go on fire you see the lagoon. This is the nearest you ever get to it on the mainland, just one heavenly moment; if there could be two moments you might see the surf and hear the mermaids singing.
passages.vernacular: 如果你閉上眼睛,又係個幸運嘅人,有時你會睇到一池冇形狀嘅可愛淡色懸浮喺黑暗中;然後如果你把眼睛閉得更緊,嗰池開始成形,顏色變得咁鮮明,再閉緊一下佢哋就一定會住火。但就喺佢哋住火之前,你睇到咗潟湖。呢個係你喺大陸上最接近佢嘅時候,只有一個天堂般嘅瞬間;如果能有兩個瞬間,你或者能睇到浪花、聽到美人魚唱歌。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果你閉上眼睛,又是個幸運的人,有時你會看到一池沒有形狀的可愛淡色懸浮在黑暗中;然後如果你把眼睛閉得更緊,那池開始成形,顏色變得那麼鮮明,再閉緊一下它們就一定會著火。但就在它們著火之前,你看到了潟湖。這是你在大陸上最接近它的時候,只有一個天堂般的瞬間;如果能有兩個瞬間,你也許能看到浪花、聽到美人魚唱歌。

passages.original: The children often spent long summer days on this lagoon, swimming or floating most of the time, playing the mermaid games in the water, and so forth. You must not think from this that the mermaids were on friendly terms with them: on the contrary, it was among Wendy’s lasting regrets that all the time she was on the island she never had a civil word from one of them. When she stole softly to the edge of the lagoon she might see them by the score, especially on Marooners’ Rock, where they loved to bask, combing out their hair in a lazy way that quite irritated her; or she might even swim, on tiptoe as it were, to within a yard of them, but then they saw her and dived, probably splashing her with their tails, not by accident, but intentionally.
passages.vernacular: 細路哋常喺呢個潟湖上度過漫長嘅夏日,大部分時間游泳或漂浮,喺水裡玩美人魚嘅遊戲等等。你唔好因此以為美人魚同佢哋關係友好:恰恰相反,溫蒂永遠嘅遺憾之一係,佢喺島上嘅整個期間,從冇從佢哋任何一個嗰度聽到過一句客氣話。當佢悄悄走到潟湖邊時,佢可能睇到成群嘅美人魚,特別係喺被棄者之岩上,佢哋鍾意喺嗰度曬太陽,懶洋洋地梳理頭髮,呢讓佢相當惱火;或者佢甚至可以踮住腳尖似嘅游到離佢哋一碼嘅地方,但佢哋睇見佢就潛下去,大概用尾巴濺佢一身水,唔係意外,而係故意嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 孩子們常在這個潟湖上度過漫長的夏日,大部分時間游泳或漂浮,在水裡玩美人魚的遊戲等等。你不要因此以為美人魚同他們關係友好:恰恰相反,溫蒂永遠的遺憾之一是,她在島上的整個期間,從沒從她們任何一個那裡聽到過一句客氣話。當她悄悄走到潟湖邊時,她可能看到成群的美人魚,特別是在被棄者之岩上,她們喜歡在那裡曬太陽,懶洋洋地梳理頭髮,這讓她相當惱火;或者她甚至可以踮著腳尖似的游到離她們一碼的地方,但她們看見她就潛下去,大概用尾巴濺她一身水,不是意外,而是故意的。

passages.original: They treated all the boys in the same way, except of course Peter, who chatted with them on Marooners’ Rock by the hour, and sat on their tails when they got cheeky. He gave Wendy one of their combs.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋對待所有男孩都咁樣,當然除咗彼得,佢喺被棄者之岩上同佢哋一聊就係幾個小時,佢哋無禮時佢就坐喺佢哋嘅尾巴上。佢畀咗溫蒂一把佢哋嘅梳子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她們對待所有男孩都這樣,當然除了彼得,他在被棄者之岩上同她們一聊就是幾個小時,她們無禮時他就坐在她們的尾巴上。他給了溫蒂一把她們的梳子。
