passages.original: The most haunting time at which to see them is at the turn of the moon, when they utter strange wailing cries; but the lagoon is dangerous for mortals then, and until the evening of which we have now to tell, Wendy had never seen the lagoon by moonlight, less from fear, for of course Peter would have accompanied her, than because she had strict rules about every one being in bed by seven. She was often at the lagoon, however, on sunny days after rain, when the mermaids come up in extraordinary numbers to play with their bubbles. The bubbles of many colours made in rainbow water they treat as balls, hitting them gaily from one to another with their tails, and trying to keep them in the rainbow till they burst. The goals are at each end of the rainbow, and the keepers only are allowed to use their hands. Sometimes a dozen of these games will be going on in the lagoon at a time, and it is quite a pretty sight.
passages.vernacular: 睇到佢哋最令人難忘嘅時刻係月亮轉換嘅時候,嗰時佢哋發出奇怪嘅哀鳴;但嗰時潟湖對凡人係危險嘅,直到我哋而家要講嘅嗰個晚上,溫蒂從冇喺月光下見過潟湖,同其講係因為害怕,因為彼得當然會陪佢,不如講係因為佢有嚴格嘅規定,每個人七點必須上床。不過,佢常常喺雨後嘅晴天嚟到潟湖,嗰時美人魚成群結隊地出嚟玩佢哋嘅泡泡。喺彩虹水裡做出嘅許多顏色嘅泡泡,佢哋當作球,用尾巴快樂地互相擊打,試圖讓佢哋留喺彩虹裡直到破掉。球門喺彩虹嘅兩端,只有守門員被允許用手。有時潟湖裡同時進行十幾場咁樣嘅遊戲,景象相當漂亮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 看到她們最令人難忘的時刻是月亮轉換的時候,那時她們發出奇怪的哀鳴;但那時潟湖對凡人是危險的,直到我們現在要講的那個晚上,溫蒂從沒在月光下見過潟湖,與其說是因為害怕,因為彼得當然會陪她,不如說是因為她有嚴格的規定,每個人七點必須上床。不過,她常常在雨後的晴天來到潟湖,那時美人魚成群結隊地出來玩她們的泡泡。在彩虹水裡做出的許多顏色的泡泡,她們當作球,用尾巴快樂地互相擊打,試圖讓它們留在彩虹裡直到破掉。球門在彩虹的兩端,只有守門員被允許用手。有時潟湖裡同時進行十幾場這樣的遊戲,景象相當漂亮。

passages.original: But the moment the children tried to join in they had to play by themselves, for the mermaids immediately disappeared. Nevertheless we have proof that they secretly watched the interlopers, and were not above taking an idea from them; for John introduced a new way of hitting the bubble, with the head instead of the hand, and the mermaids adopted it. This is the one mark that John has left on the Neverland.
passages.vernacular: 但細路哋一試圖加入,就只能自己玩,因為美人魚即刻消失。儘管如此,我哋有證據證明佢哋暗中觀察闖入者,並不介意從佢哋嗰度取點子;因為約翰引進咗一種用頭而唔係用手擊打泡泡嘅新方式,美人魚都採用喇。呢個係約翰喺永無島上留下嘅唯一印記。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但孩子們一試圖加入,就只能自己玩,因為美人魚立刻消失。儘管如此,我們有證據證明她們暗中觀察闖入者,並不介意從他們那裡取點子;因為約翰引進了一種用頭而不是用手擊打泡泡的新方式,美人魚也採用了。這是約翰在永無島上留下的唯一印記。

passages.original: It must also have been rather pretty to see the children resting on a rock for half an hour after their mid-day meal. Wendy insisted on their doing this, and it had to be a real rest even though the meal was make-believe. So they lay there in the sun, and their bodies glistened in it, while she sat beside them and looked important.
passages.vernacular: 睇細路哋午餐後喺一塊岩石上休息半小時,一定都相當漂亮。溫蒂堅持要佢哋咁樣做,即使飯係假裝嘅,呢都必須係真正嘅休息。於是佢哋躺喺嗰度曬太陽,身體喺陽光下閃閃發亮,佢坐喺佢哋旁邊,顯得好重要。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 看孩子們午餐後在一塊岩石上休息半小時,一定也相當漂亮。溫蒂堅持要他們這樣做,即使飯是假裝的,這也必須是真正的休息。於是他們躺在那裡曬太陽,身體在陽光下閃閃發亮,她坐在他們旁邊,顯得很重要。

passages.original: It was one such day, and they were all on Marooners’ Rock. The rock was not much larger than their great bed, but of course they all knew how not to take up much room, and they were dozing, or at least lying with their eyes shut, and pinching occasionally when they thought Wendy was not looking. She was very busy, stitching.
passages.vernacular: 就喺咁樣嘅一天,佢哋都喺被棄者之岩上。岩石不比佢哋嘅大床大多少,但當然佢哋都知道點樣不佔太多地方,佢哋喺打盹,或者至少閉住眼睛躺住,覺得溫蒂冇睇時偶爾互相捏一下。佢好忙,正在縫補。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就在這樣的一天,他們都在被棄者之岩上。岩石不比他們的大床大多少,但當然他們都知道怎樣不佔太多地方,他們在打盹,或者至少閉著眼睛躺著,覺得溫蒂沒看時偶爾互相捏一下。她非常忙,正在縫補。

passages.original: While she stitched a change came to the lagoon. Little shivers ran over it, and the sun went away and shadows stole across the water, turning it cold. Wendy could no longer see to thread her needle, and when she looked up, the lagoon that had always hitherto been such a laughing place seemed formidable and unfriendly.
passages.vernacular: 佢縫補時,潟湖起咗變化。細小嘅顫慄掠過水面,太陽離開喇,陰影悄悄爬過水面,使佢變冷。溫蒂再都睇不清穿針喇,佢抬頭睇時,嗰個迄今一直係咁歡笑嘅地方嘅潟湖,顯得可怕而不友好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她縫補時,潟湖起了變化。細小的顫慄掠過水面,太陽離開了,陰影悄悄爬過水面,使它變冷。溫蒂再也看不清穿針了,她抬頭看時,那個迄今一直是這麼歡笑的地方的潟湖,顯得可怕而不友好。

passages.original: It was not, she knew, that night had come, but something as dark as night had come. No, worse than that. It had not come, but it had sent that shiver through the sea to say that it was coming. What was it?
passages.vernacular: 佢知道,並唔係夜晚嚟喇,而係某種像夜晚一樣黑暗嘅嘢嚟喇。不,比嗰更糟。佢仲冇嚟,但佢讓嗰陣顫慄傳過海,講佢要嚟喇。嗰個係乜嘢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她知道,並不是夜晚來了,而是某種像夜晚一樣黑暗的東西來了。不,比那更糟。它還沒有來,但它讓那陣顫慄傳過海,說它要來了。那是什麼?

passages.original: There crowded upon her all the stories she had been told of Marooners’ Rock, so called because evil captains put sailors on it and leave them there to drown. They drown when the tide rises, for then it is submerged.
passages.vernacular: 所有佢聽過嘅關於被棄者之岩嘅故事湧上佢心頭,佢之所以咁樣叫,係因為邪惡嘅船長把水手放喺上面,把佢哋留喺嗰度淹死。漲潮時佢哋就淹死喇,因為嗰時佢被淹沒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所有她聽過的關於被棄者之岩的故事湧上她心頭,它之所以這樣叫,是因為邪惡的船長把水手放在上面,把他們留在那裡淹死。漲潮時他們就淹死了,因為那時它被淹沒。

passages.original: Of course she should have roused the children at once; not merely because of the unknown that was stalking toward them, but because it was no longer good for them to sleep on a rock grown chilly. But she was a young mother and she did not know this; she thought you simply must stick to your rule about half an hour after the mid-day meal. So, though fear was upon her, and she longed to hear male voices, she would not waken them. Even when she heard the sound of muffled oars, though her heart was in her mouth, she did not waken them. She stood over them to let them have their sleep out. Was it not brave of Wendy?
passages.vernacular: 當然佢應該即刻叫醒細路哋;不僅因為逼近佢哋嘅未知之物,而且因為瞓喺變冷嘅岩石上對佢哋已經不好喇。但佢係一位年輕嘅母親,唔知道呢啲;佢認為你只要堅持午餐後半小時嘅規則就行。所以,雖然恐懼籠罩住佢,佢渴望聽到男人嘅聲音,佢仍唔願叫醒佢哋。即使當佢聽到包裹住嘅槳聲,雖然佢嘅心提到咗嗓子眼,佢都冇叫醒佢哋。佢站喺佢哋身邊,讓佢哋瞓個夠。溫蒂唔係好勇敢嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當然她應該馬上叫醒孩子們;不僅因為逼近他們的未知之物,而且因為睡在變冷的岩石上對他們已經不好了。但她是一位年輕的母親,不知道這一點;她認為你只要堅持午餐後半小時的規則就行。所以,雖然恐懼籠罩著她,她渴望聽到男人的聲音,她仍不願叫醒他們。即使當她聽到包裹著的槳聲,雖然她的心提到了嗓子眼,她也沒有叫醒他們。她站在他們身邊,讓他們睡個夠。溫蒂不是很勇敢嗎?

passages.original: It was well for those boys then that there was one among them who could sniff danger even in his sleep. Peter sprang erect, as wide awake at once as a dog, and with one warning cry he roused the others.
passages.vernacular: 嗰時對呢啲男孩來講幸好佢哋中間有一個人,即使喺瞓夢中都能嗅到危險。彼得猛地直立起嚟,像狗一樣即刻完全清醒,發出一聲警告嘅喊叫,叫醒咗其他人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那時對這些男孩來說幸好他們中間有一個人,即使在睡夢中也能嗅到危險。彼得猛地直立起來,像狗一樣馬上完全清醒,發出一聲警告的喊叫,叫醒了其他人。

passages.original: He stood motionless, one hand to his ear.
passages.vernacular: 佢一動不動地站住,一隻手放喺耳邊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他一動不動地站著,一隻手放在耳邊。

passages.original: “Pirates!” he cried. The others came closer to him. A strange smile was playing about his face, and Wendy saw it and shuddered. While that smile was on his face no one dared address him; all they could do was to stand ready to obey. The order came sharp and incisive.
passages.vernacular: 「海盜!」佢喊道。其他人靠近佢。一絲奇怪嘅微笑喺佢臉上浮現,溫蒂睇到喇,不禁顫抖。佢臉上有嗰種微笑時,冇人敢同佢講話;佢哋能做嘅只係站好準備服從。命令下得尖銳而果斷。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「海盜!」他喊道。其他人靠近他。一絲奇怪的微笑在他臉上浮現,溫蒂看到了,不禁顫抖。他臉上有那種微笑時,沒有人敢同他說話;他們能做的只是站好準備服從。命令下得尖銳而果斷。

passages.original: “Dive!”
passages.vernacular: 「潛下去!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「潛下去!」

passages.original: There was a gleam of legs, and instantly the lagoon seemed deserted. Marooners’ Rock stood alone in the forbidding waters as if it were itself marooned.
passages.vernacular: 一陣腿嘅閃光,轉眼潟湖似乎空喇。被棄者之岩獨自站喺令人生畏嘅水中,好像佢自己都被遺棄。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一陣腿的閃光,轉眼潟湖似乎空了。被棄者之岩獨自站在令人生畏的水中,好像它自己也被遺棄。

passages.original: The boat drew nearer. It was the pirate dinghy, with three figures in her, Smee and Starkey, and the third a captive, no other than Tiger Lily. Her hands and ankles were tied, and she knew what was to be her fate. She was to be left on the rock to perish, an end to one of her race more terrible than death by fire or torture, for is it not written in the book of the tribe that there is no path through water to the happy hunting-ground? Yet her face was impassive; she was the daughter of a chief, she must die as a chief’s daughter, it is enough.
passages.vernacular: 船靠近喇。嗰個係海盜嘅小艇,上面有三個人,斯密同斯塔基,第三個係俘虜,唔係別人,正是虎百合。佢嘅手同腳踝被綁住,佢知道自己嘅命運會係乜嘢。佢將被留喺岩石上死去,呢對佢嗰個種族嘅人來講,係比被火燒或酷刑而死更可怕嘅結局,因為部落嘅書裡唔係寫住,穿過水冇路通往快樂獵場嗎?然而佢嘅臉毫無表情;佢係酋長嘅女兒,佢必須像酋長嘅女兒嗰樣死去,呢就夠喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 船靠近了。那是海盜的小艇,上面有三個人,斯密和斯塔基,第三個是俘虜,不是別人,正是虎百合。她的手和腳踝被綁著,她知道自己的命運會是什麼。她將被留在岩石上死去,這對她那個種族的人來說,是比被火燒或酷刑而死更可怕的結局,因為部落的書裡不是寫著,穿過水沒有路通往快樂獵場嗎?然而她的臉毫無表情;她是酋長的女兒,她必須像酋長的女兒那樣死去,這就夠了。

passages.original: They had caught her boarding the pirate ship with a knife in her mouth. No watch was kept on the ship, it being Hook’s boast that the wind of his name guarded the ship for a mile around. Now her fate would help to guard it also. One more wail would go the round in that wind by night.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋抓到佢嘴裡叼住刀登上海盜船。船上冇守衛,因為虎克誇口講佢名字嘅風喺一英里範圍內守衛住呢艘船。而家佢嘅命運都會幫助守衛佢。夜間喺嗰風中又多一聲哀嚎會傳遍。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們抓到她嘴裡叼著刀登上海盜船。船上沒有守衛,因為虎克誇口說他名字的風在一英里範圍內守衛著這艘船。現在她的命運也會幫助守衛它。夜間在那風中又多一聲哀嚎會傳遍。

passages.original: In the gloom that they brought with them the two pirates did not see the rock till they crashed into it.
passages.vernacular: 喺佢哋帶嚟嘅昏暗中,兩個海盜直到撞上岩石才睇見佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在他們帶來的昏暗中,兩個海盜直到撞上岩石才看見它。

passages.original: “Luff, you lubber,” cried an Irish voice that was Smee’s; “here’s the rock. Now, then, what we have to do is to hoist the redskin on to it and leave her here to drown.”
passages.vernacular: 「轉舵,你呢笨蛋,」一個愛爾蘭口音嘅聲音喊道,係斯密嘅;「呢度有塊岩石。而家,我哋要做嘅係把紅番吊到上面,把佢留喺呢度淹死。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「轉舵,你這笨蛋,」一個愛爾蘭口音的聲音喊道,是斯密的;「這裡有塊岩石。現在,我們要做的是把紅番吊到上面,把她留在這裡淹死。」

passages.original: It was the work of one brutal moment to land the beautiful girl on the rock; she was too proud to offer a vain resistance.
passages.vernacular: 把美麗嘅女孩弄上岩石,只需要殘忍嘅一瞬間;佢太驕傲喇,不作徒勞嘅反抗。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 把美麗的女孩弄上岩石,只需要殘忍的一瞬間;她太驕傲了,不作徒勞的反抗。

passages.original: Quite near the rock, but out of sight, two heads were bobbing up and down, Peter’s and Wendy’s. Wendy was crying, for it was the first tragedy she had seen. Peter had seen many tragedies, but he had forgotten them all. He was less sorry than Wendy for Tiger Lily: it was two against one that angered him, and he meant to save her. An easy way would have been to wait until the pirates had gone, but he was never one to choose the easy way.
passages.vernacular: 離岩石好近,但睇唔見嘅地方,有兩個頭喺上下浮動,係彼得同溫蒂嘅。溫蒂喺哭,因為呢個係佢睇到嘅第一場悲劇。彼得見過許多悲劇,但佢已經全忘喇。佢對虎百合冇溫蒂咁難過:激怒佢嘅係二對一,佢打算救佢。一個容易嘅辦法係等到海盜走喇,但佢從來唔係選容易路嘅人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 離岩石很近,但看不見的地方,有兩個頭在上下浮動,是彼得和溫蒂的。溫蒂在哭,因為這是她看到的第一場悲劇。彼得見過許多悲劇,但他已經全忘了。他對虎百合沒有溫蒂那麼難過:激怒他的是二對一,他打算救她。一個容易的辦法是等到海盜走了,但他從來不是選容易路的人。

passages.original: There was almost nothing he could not do, and he now imitated the voice of Hook.
passages.vernacular: 幾乎冇乜嘢係佢做唔到嘅,佢而家模仿虎克嘅聲音。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 幾乎沒有什麼是他做不到的,他現在模仿虎克的聲音。

passages.original: “Ahoy there, you lubbers!” he called. It was a marvellous imitation.
passages.vernacular: 「喂,嗰邊嘅笨蛋哋!」佢喊道。呢個係個奇妙嘅模仿。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「喂,那邊的笨蛋們!」他喊道。這是個奇妙的模仿。

passages.original: “The captain!” said the pirates, staring at each other in surprise.
passages.vernacular: 「船長!」海盜哋驚訝地互相瞪住講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「船長!」海盜們驚訝地互相瞪著說。

passages.original: “He must be swimming out to us,” Starkey said, when they had looked for him in vain.
passages.vernacular: 「佢一定係游過嚟找我哋喇,」斯塔基佢哋找唔到佢時講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他一定是游過來找我們了,」斯塔基他們找不到他時說。

passages.original: “We are putting the redskin on the rock,” Smee called out.
passages.vernacular: 「我哋正把紅番放喺岩石上,」斯密喊道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們正把紅番放在岩石上,」斯密喊道。

passages.original: “Set her free,” came the astonishing answer.
passages.vernacular: 「放佢自由,」傳嚟令人食驚嘅回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「放她自由,」傳來令人吃驚的回答。

passages.original: “Free!”
passages.vernacular: 「自由!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「自由!」

passages.original: “Yes, cut her bonds and let her go.”
passages.vernacular: 「對,割斷佢嘅繩子,放佢走。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「對,割斷她的繩子,放她走。」

passages.original: “But, captain—”
passages.vernacular: 「但係,船長——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但是,船長——」

passages.original: “At once, d’ye hear,” cried Peter, “or I’ll plunge my hook in you.”
passages.vernacular: 「即刻,聽到冇,」彼得喊道,「不然我用鉤子扎你。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「馬上,聽到沒有,」彼得喊道,「不然我用鉤子扎你。」

passages.original: “This is queer!” Smee gasped.
passages.vernacular: 「呢太奇怪喇!」斯密喘住氣講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這太奇怪了!」斯密喘著氣說。

passages.original: “Better do what the captain orders,” said Starkey nervously.
passages.vernacular: 「最好照船長嘅命令做,」斯塔基緊張地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「最好照船長的命令做,」斯塔基緊張地說。

passages.original: “Ay, ay,” Smee said, and he cut Tiger Lily’s cords. At once like an eel she slid between Starkey’s legs into the water.
passages.vernacular: 「係,係,」斯密講,割斷咗虎百合嘅繩子。佢即刻像鰻魚一樣從斯塔基嘅兩腿之間滑進咗水裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是,是,」斯密說,割斷了虎百合的繩子。她馬上像鰻魚一樣從斯塔基的兩腿之間滑進了水裡。

passages.original: Of course Wendy was very elated over Peter’s cleverness; but she knew that he would be elated also and very likely crow and thus betray himself, so at once her hand went out to cover his mouth. But it was stayed even in the act, for “Boat ahoy!” rang over the lagoon in Hook’s voice, and this time it was not Peter who had spoken.
passages.vernacular: 當然溫蒂對彼得嘅聰明好高興;但佢知道佢都會高興,好可能會啼叫,從而暴露自己,於是佢嘅手即刻伸出去捂住佢嘅嘴。但呢個動作喺進行中就被阻止喇,因為「喂,船!」嘅聲音喺潟湖上響起,係虎克嘅聲音,呢次講話嘅唔係彼得。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當然溫蒂對彼得的聰明非常高興;但她知道他也會高興,很可能會啼叫,從而暴露自己,於是她的手馬上伸出去捂住他的嘴。但這個動作在進行中就被阻止了,因為「喂,船!」的聲音在潟湖上響起,是虎克的聲音,這次說話的不是彼得。

passages.original: Peter may have been about to crow, but his face puckered in a whistle of surprise instead.
passages.vernacular: 彼得本來可能正要啼叫,但佢嘅臉皺起,吹出咗一聲驚訝嘅口哨。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 彼得本來可能正要啼叫,但他的臉皺起,吹出了一聲驚訝的口哨。

passages.original: “Boat ahoy!” again came the voice.
passages.vernacular: 「喂,船!」嗰聲音又嚟喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「喂,船!」那聲音又來了。

passages.original: Now Wendy understood. The real Hook was also in the water.
passages.vernacular: 而家溫蒂明白喇。真正嘅虎克都喺水裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在溫蒂明白了。真正的虎克也在水裡。

passages.original: He was swimming to the boat, and as his men showed a light to guide him he had soon reached them. In the light of the lantern Wendy saw his hook grip the boat’s side; she saw his evil swarthy face as he rose dripping from the water, and, quaking, she would have liked to swim away, but Peter would not budge. He was tingling with life and also top-heavy with conceit. “Am I not a wonder, oh, I am a wonder!” he whispered to her, and though she thought so also, she was really glad for the sake of his reputation that no one heard him except herself.
passages.vernacular: 佢正游向小艇,佢嘅手下舉起燈指引佢,佢好快就到咗佢哋嗰度。喺燈籠嘅光中,溫蒂睇到佢嘅鉤子抓住船舷;睇到佢邪惡黝黑嘅臉從水裡滴住水升起,佢顫抖住,想游走,但彼得唔肯動。佢充滿活力,都因自負而頭重腳輕。「我唔係奇才嗎,哦,我係奇才!」佢對佢低聲講,雖然佢都咁想,但為了佢嘅名聲,佢真高興除咗佢冇別人聽見。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他正游向小艇,他的手下舉起燈指引他,他很快就到了他們那裡。在燈籠的光中,溫蒂看到他的鉤子抓住船舷;看到他邪惡黝黑的臉從水裡滴著水升起,她顫抖著,想游走,但彼得不肯動。他充滿活力,也因自負而頭重腳輕。「我不是奇才嗎,哦,我是奇才!」他對她低聲說,雖然她也這麼想,但為了他的名聲,她真高興除了她沒有別人聽見。

passages.original: He signed to her to listen.
passages.vernacular: 佢示意佢聽。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他示意她聽。

passages.original: The two pirates were very curious to know what had brought their captain to them, but he sat with his head on his hook in a position of profound melancholy.
passages.vernacular: 兩個海盜好好奇乜嘢把佢哋嘅船長帶到佢哋呢度,但佢頭靠喺鉤子上,坐住呈現出深深嘅憂鬱嘅姿勢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 兩個海盜非常好奇什麼把他們的船長帶到他們這裡,但他頭靠在鉤子上,坐著呈現出深深的憂鬱的姿勢。

passages.original: “Captain, is all well?” they asked timidly, but he answered with a hollow moan.
passages.vernacular: 「船長,一切都好嗎?」佢哋膽怯地問,但佢以一聲空洞嘅呻吟回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「船長,一切都好嗎?」他們膽怯地問,但他以一聲空洞的呻吟回答。

passages.original: “He sighs,” said Smee.
passages.vernacular: 「佢歎氣喇,」斯密講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他歎氣了,」斯密說。

passages.original: “He sighs again,” said Starkey.
passages.vernacular: 「佢又歎氣喇,」斯塔基講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他又歎氣了,」斯塔基說。

passages.original: “And yet a third time he sighs,” said Smee.
passages.vernacular: 「而且第三次歎氣,」斯密講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「而且第三次歎氣,」斯密說。

passages.original: Then at last he spoke passionately.
passages.vernacular: 然後佢終於激動地講話喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後他終於激動地說話了。

passages.original: “The game’s up,” he cried, “those boys have found a mother.”
passages.vernacular: 「完喇,」佢喊道,「嗰啲男孩找到母親喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「完了,」他喊道,「那些男孩找到母親了。」

passages.original: Affrighted though she was, Wendy swelled with pride.
passages.vernacular: 雖然佢好害怕,溫蒂卻驕傲得挺起咗胸。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 雖然她很害怕,溫蒂卻驕傲得挺起了胸。

passages.original: “O evil day!” cried Starkey.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,不幸嘅一天!」斯塔基喊道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,不幸的一天!」斯塔基喊道。

passages.original: “What’s a mother?” asked the ignorant Smee.
passages.vernacular: 「乜嘢係母親?」無知嘅斯密問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「什麼是母親?」無知的斯密問。

passages.original: Wendy was so shocked that she exclaimed. “He doesn’t know!” and always after this she felt that if you could have a pet pirate Smee would be her one.
passages.vernacular: 溫蒂咁震驚,佢叫咗出嚟。「佢唔知道!」從此以後佢總覺得,如果你可以養一個寵物海盜,斯密會係佢嘅選擇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 溫蒂那麼震驚,她叫了出來。「他不知道!」從此以後她總覺得,如果你可以養一個寵物海盜,斯密會是她的選擇。

passages.original: Peter pulled her beneath the water, for Hook had started up, crying, “What was that?”
passages.vernacular: 彼得把佢拉到水下,因為虎克站咗起嚟,喊道:「嗰個係乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 彼得把她拉到水下,因為虎克站了起來,喊道:「那是什麼?」

passages.original: “I heard nothing,” said Starkey, raising the lantern over the waters, and as the pirates looked they saw a strange sight. It was the nest I have told you of, floating on the lagoon, and the Never bird was sitting on it.
passages.vernacular: 「我乜嘢都冇聽到,」斯塔基講,把燈舉到水面上,海盜哋睇時,睇到一個奇怪嘅景象。嗰個係我告訴過你嘅巢,漂浮喺潟湖上,永無鳥坐喺上面。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我什麼也沒聽到,」斯塔基說,把燈舉到水面上,海盜們看時,看到一個奇怪的景象。那是我告訴過你的巢,漂浮在潟湖上,永無鳥坐在上面。

passages.original: “See,” said Hook in answer to Smee’s question, “that is a mother. What a lesson! The nest must have fallen into the water, but would the mother desert her eggs? No.”
passages.vernacular: 「睇,」虎克回答斯密嘅問題講,「嗰個就係母親。幾咁好嘅一課!巢一定係掉進咗水裡,但母親會拋棄佢嘅蛋嗎?唔會。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「看,」虎克回答斯密的問題說,「那就是母親。多麼好的一課!巢一定是掉進了水裡,但母親會拋棄她的蛋嗎?不會。」

passages.original: There was a break in his voice, as if for a moment he recalled innocent days when—but he brushed away this weakness with his hook.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅聲音裡有一絲中斷,好像有一刻佢回想起了無辜嘅日子,嗰時——但佢用鉤子撣掉咗呢個弱點。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他的聲音裡有一絲中斷,好像有一刻他回想起了無辜的日子,那時——但他用鉤子撣掉了這個弱點。

passages.original: Smee, much impressed, gazed at the bird as the nest was borne past, but the more suspicious Starkey said, “If she is a mother, perhaps she is hanging about here to help Peter.”
passages.vernacular: 斯密深受感動,望住鳥,巢從旁邊漂過,但更多疑嘅斯塔基講:「如果佢係母親,或者佢喺呢附近徘徊係為了幫助彼得。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 斯密深受感動,望著鳥,巢從旁邊漂過,但更多疑的斯塔基說:「如果她是母親,也許她在這附近徘徊是為了幫助彼得。」

passages.original: Hook winced. “Ay,” he said, “that is the fear that haunts me.”
passages.vernacular: 虎克畏縮咗一下。「對,」佢講,「嗰個就係纏住我嘅恐懼。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 虎克畏縮了一下。「對,」他說,「那就是纏著我的恐懼。」

passages.original: He was roused from this dejection by Smee’s eager voice.
passages.vernacular: 斯密急切嘅聲音把佢從呢種沮喪中喚醒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 斯密急切的聲音把他從這種沮喪中喚醒。

passages.original: “Captain,” said Smee, “could we not kidnap these boys’ mother and make her our mother?”
passages.vernacular: 「船長,」斯密講,「我哋能唔能夠綁架呢啲男孩嘅母親,讓佢做我哋嘅母親?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「船長,」斯密說,「我們能不能綁架這些男孩的母親,讓她做我們的母親?」

passages.original: “It is a princely scheme,” cried Hook, and at once it took practical shape in his great brain. “We will seize the children and carry them to the boat: the boys we will make walk the plank, and Wendy shall be our mother.”
passages.vernacular: 「呢個係個王子般嘅計畫,」虎克喊道,喺佢偉大嘅頭腦裡即刻成形為實際嘅計畫。「我哋抓住細路哋,把佢哋帶到船上:男孩哋我哋讓佢哋走跳板,而溫蒂將係我哋嘅母親。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這是個王子般的計畫,」虎克喊道,在他偉大的頭腦裡馬上成形為實際的計畫。「我們抓住孩子們,把他們帶到船上:男孩們我們讓他們走跳板,而溫蒂將是我們的母親。」

passages.original: Again Wendy forgot herself.
passages.vernacular: 溫蒂又一次忘咗自己。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 溫蒂又一次忘了自己。

passages.original: “Never!” she cried, and bobbed.
passages.vernacular: 「絕不!」佢喊道,浮咗一下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「絕不!」她喊道,浮了一下。

passages.original: “What was that?”
passages.vernacular: 「嗰個係乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那是什麼?」

passages.original: But they could see nothing. They thought it must have been a leaf in the wind. “Do you agree, my bullies?” asked Hook.
passages.vernacular: 但佢哋乜嘢都睇唔見。佢哋以為一定係風中嘅一片葉子。「你哋同意嗎,我嘅夥計哋?」虎克問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但他們什麼也看不見。他們以為一定是風中的一片葉子。「你們同意嗎,我的夥計們?」虎克問。

passages.original: “There is my hand on it,” they both said.
passages.vernacular: 「我哋發誓,」佢哋兩人講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們發誓,」他們兩人說。

passages.original: “And there is my hook. Swear.”
passages.vernacular: 「仲有我嘅鉤子。發誓。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「還有我的鉤子。發誓。」

passages.original: They all swore. By this time they were on the rock, and suddenly Hook remembered Tiger Lily.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋都發咗誓。呢陣佢哋已經喺岩石上,虎克突然想起咗虎百合。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們都發了誓。這時他們已經在岩石上,虎克突然想起了虎百合。

passages.original: “Where is the redskin?” he demanded abruptly.
passages.vernacular: 「紅番喺邊度?」佢突然問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「紅番在哪裡?」他突然問。

passages.original: He had a playful humour at moments, and they thought this was one of the moments.
passages.vernacular: 佢有時有愛開玩笑嘅幽默,佢哋以為呢個係其中一次。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他有時有愛開玩笑的幽默,他們以為這是其中一次。

passages.original: “That is all right, captain,” Smee answered complacently; “we let her go.”
passages.vernacular: 「冇問題,船長,」斯密自滿地回答;「我哋放佢走喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「沒問題,船長,」斯密自滿地回答;「我們放她走了。」

passages.original: “Let her go!” cried Hook.
passages.vernacular: 「放佢走!」虎克喊道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「放她走!」虎克喊道。

passages.original: “’Twas your own orders,” the bo’sun faltered.
passages.vernacular: 「嗰個係你自己嘅命令,」水手長結結巴巴地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那是你自己的命令,」水手長結結巴巴地說。

passages.original: “You called over the water to us to let her go,” said Starkey.
passages.vernacular: 「你從水面上喊我哋放佢走,」斯塔基講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你從水面上喊我們放她走,」斯塔基說。

passages.original: “Brimstone and gall,” thundered Hook, “what cozening is going on here!” His face had gone black with rage, but he saw that they believed their words, and he was startled. “Lads,” he said, shaking a little, “I gave no such order.”
passages.vernacular: 「硫磺同膽汁,」虎克怒吼,「呢度喺搞乜嘢騙局!」佢嘅臉氣得發黑,但佢睇出佢哋相信自己嘅話,佢食咗一驚。「小子哋,」佢講,有點發抖,「我冇下過咁樣嘅命令。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「硫磺和膽汁,」虎克怒吼,「這裡在搞什麼騙局!」他的臉氣得發黑,但他看出他們相信自己的話,他吃了一驚。「小子們,」他說,有點發抖,「我沒有下過這樣的命令。」

passages.original: “It is passing queer,” Smee said, and they all fidgeted uncomfortably. Hook raised his voice, but there was a quiver in it.
passages.vernacular: 「呢太奇怪喇,」斯密講,佢哋都不安地坐立不穩。虎克提高聲音,但聲音裡有顫抖。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這太奇怪了,」斯密說,他們都不安地坐立不穩。虎克提高聲音,但聲音裡有顫抖。

passages.original: “Spirit that haunts this dark lagoon to-night,” he cried, “dost hear me?”
passages.vernacular: 「今晚喺呢黑暗潟湖出冇嘅幽靈,」佢喊道,「你聽到我嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「今晚在這黑暗潟湖出沒的幽靈,」他喊道,「你聽到我嗎?」

passages.original: Of course Peter should have kept quiet, but of course he did not. He immediately answered in Hook’s voice:
passages.vernacular: 當然彼得應該保持安靜,但當然佢冇。佢即刻用虎克嘅聲音回答:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當然彼得應該保持安靜,但當然他沒有。他立刻用虎克的聲音回答:

passages.original: “Odds, bobs, hammer and tongs, I hear you.”
passages.vernacular: 「天啊,見鬼,我聽到你。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「天啊,見鬼,我聽到你。」

passages.original: In that supreme moment Hook did not blanch, even at the gills, but Smee and Starkey clung to each other in terror.
passages.vernacular: 喺嗰最關鍵嘅一刻,虎克冇變臉色,連腮幫子都冇變白,但斯密同斯塔基恐懼地緊抱喺一起。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在那最關鍵的一刻,虎克沒有變臉色,連腮幫子都沒變白,但斯密和斯塔基恐懼地緊抱在一起。

passages.original: “Who are you, stranger? Speak!” Hook demanded.
passages.vernacular: 「你係邊個,陌生人?講話!」虎克要求。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你是誰,陌生人?說話!」虎克要求。

passages.original: “I am James Hook,” replied the voice, “captain of the Jolly Roger.”
passages.vernacular: 「我係詹姆斯·虎克,」嗰聲音回答,「快樂羅傑號嘅船長。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我是詹姆斯·虎克,」那聲音回答,「快樂羅傑號的船長。」

passages.original: “You are not; you are not,” Hook cried hoarsely.
passages.vernacular: 「你唔係;你唔係,」虎克嘶啞地喊道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你不是;你不是,」虎克嘶啞地喊道。

passages.original: “Brimstone and gall,” the voice retorted, “say that again, and I’ll cast anchor in you.”
passages.vernacular: 「硫磺同膽汁,」嗰聲音反駁,「再講一遍,我就喺你身上拋錨。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「硫磺和膽汁,」那聲音反駁,「再說一遍,我就在你身上拋錨。」

passages.original: Hook tried a more ingratiating manner. “If you are Hook,” he said almost humbly, “come tell me, who am I?”
passages.vernacular: 虎克試用一種更討好嘅態度。「如果你係虎克,」佢幾乎係謙卑地講,「嚟告訴我,我係邊個?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 虎克試用一種更討好的態度。「如果你是虎克,」他幾乎是謙卑地說,「來告訴我,我是誰?」

passages.original: “A codfish,” replied the voice, “only a codfish.”
passages.vernacular: 「一條鱈魚,」嗰聲音回答,「只係一條鱈魚。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「一條鱈魚,」那聲音回答,「只是一條鱈魚。」

passages.original: “A codfish!” Hook echoed blankly, and it was then, but not till then, that his proud spirit broke. He saw his men draw back from him.
passages.vernacular: 「一條鱈魚!」虎克茫然地重複,就喺嗰時,而且直到嗰時,佢驕傲嘅精神才垮喇。佢睇到佢嘅手下從佢身邊退開。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「一條鱈魚!」虎克茫然地重複,就在那時,而且直到那時,他驕傲的精神才垮了。他看到他的手下從他身邊退開。

passages.original: “Have we been captained all this time by a codfish!” they muttered. “It is lowering to our pride.”
passages.vernacular: 「我哋一直被一條鱈魚當船長!」佢哋嘀咕。「呢貶低咗我哋嘅尊嚴。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們一直被一條鱈魚當船長!」他們嘀咕。「這貶低了我們的尊嚴。」

passages.original: They were his dogs snapping at him, but, tragic figure though he had become, he scarcely heeded them. Against such fearful evidence it was not their belief in him that he needed, it was his own. He felt his ego slipping from him. “Don’t desert me, bully,” he whispered hoarsely to it.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋係對佢狂吠嘅狗,但雖然佢已成咗一個悲劇人物,佢幾乎不理會佢哋。面對如此可怕嘅證據,佢需要嘅唔係佢哋對佢嘅信任,而係佢自己嘅。佢感到自我正從佢身上溜走。「別拋棄我,老夥計,」佢對佢嘶啞地低語。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們是對他狂吠的狗,但雖然他已成了一個悲劇人物,他幾乎不理會他們。面對如此可怕的證據,他需要的不是他們對他的信任,而是他自己的。他感到自我正從他身上溜走。「別拋棄我,老夥計,」他對它嘶啞地低語。

passages.original: In his dark nature there was a touch of the feminine, as in all the great pirates, and it sometimes gave him intuitions. Suddenly he tried the guessing game.
passages.vernacular: 喺佢黑暗嘅天性中有一絲女性氣質,像所有偉大嘅海盜一樣,有時畀佢直覺。突然佢試咗猜謎遊戲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在他黑暗的天性中有一絲女性氣質,像所有偉大的海盜一樣,有時給他直覺。突然他試了猜謎遊戲。

passages.original: “Hook,” he called, “have you another voice?”
passages.vernacular: 「虎克,」佢喊道,「你有另一個聲音嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「虎克,」他喊道,「你有另一個聲音嗎?」

passages.original: Now Peter could never resist a game, and he answered blithely in his own voice, “I have.”
passages.vernacular: 而家彼得從來無法抗拒遊戲,佢用自己嘅聲音快活地回答:「有。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在彼得從來無法抗拒遊戲,他用自己的聲音快活地回答:「有。」

passages.original: “And another name?”
passages.vernacular: 「仲有另一個名字?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「還有另一個名字?」

passages.original: “Ay, ay.”
“Vegetable?” asked Hook.
passages.vernacular: 「係蔬菜?」虎克問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是蔬菜?」虎克問。

passages.original: “No.”
passages.vernacular: 「唔係。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不是。」

passages.original: “Mineral?”
passages.vernacular: 「係礦物?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是礦物?」

passages.original: “No.”
passages.vernacular: 「唔係。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不是。」

passages.original: “Animal?”
passages.vernacular: 「係動物?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是動物?」

passages.original: “Yes.”
“Man?”
passages.vernacular: 「係人?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是人?」

passages.original: “No!” This answer rang out scornfully.
passages.vernacular: 「唔係!」呢個回答輕蔑地響起。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不是!」這個回答輕蔑地響起。

passages.original: “Boy?”
passages.vernacular: 「男孩?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「男孩?」

passages.original: “Yes.”
“Ordinary boy?”
passages.vernacular: 「普通男孩?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「普通男孩?」

passages.original: “No!”
passages.vernacular: 「唔係!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不是!」

passages.original: “Wonderful boy?”
passages.vernacular: 「奇妙嘅男孩?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「奇妙的男孩?」

passages.original: To Wendy’s pain the answer that rang out this time was “Yes.”
passages.vernacular: 讓溫蒂痛心嘅係,呢次響起嘅回答係:「係。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 讓溫蒂痛心的是,這次響起的回答是:「是。」

passages.original: “Are you in England?”
passages.vernacular: 「你喺英國嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你在英國嗎?」

passages.original: “No.”
“Are you here?”
passages.vernacular: 「你喺呢度嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你在這裡嗎?」

passages.original: “Yes.”
Hook was completely puzzled. “You ask him some questions,” he said to the others, wiping his damp brow.
passages.vernacular: 虎克完全困惑喇。「你哋嚟問佢幾個問題,」佢擦住濕濕嘅額頭對其他人講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 虎克完全困惑了。「你們來問他幾個問題,」他擦著濕濕的額頭對其他人說。

passages.original: Smee reflected. “I can’t think of a thing,” he said regretfully.
passages.vernacular: 斯密想咗想。「我乜嘢都想不出嚟,」佢遺憾地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 斯密想了想。「我什麼也想不出來,」他遺憾地說。

passages.original: “Can’t guess, can’t guess!” crowed Peter. “Do you give it up?”
passages.vernacular: 「猜唔到,猜唔到!」彼得啼叫。「你哋放棄咗嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「猜不到,猜不到!」彼得啼叫。「你們放棄了嗎?」

passages.original: Of course in his pride he was carrying the game too far, and the miscreants saw their chance.
passages.vernacular: 當然,出於驕傲,佢把遊戲玩得太過喇,惡棍哋睇到咗機會。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當然,出於驕傲,他把遊戲玩得太過了,惡棍們看到了機會。

passages.original: “Yes, yes,” they answered eagerly.
passages.vernacular: 「係,係,」佢哋急切地回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是,是,」他們急切地回答。

passages.original: “Well, then,” he cried, “I am Peter Pan.”
passages.vernacular: 「好吧,咁,」佢喊道,「我係彼得潘。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好吧,那麼,」他喊道,「我是彼得潘。」

passages.original: Pan!
passages.vernacular: 潘!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 潘!

passages.original: In a moment Hook was himself again, and Smee and Starkey were his faithful henchmen.
passages.vernacular: 轉眼虎克又恢復咗自我,斯密同斯塔基係佢忠實嘅走狗。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 轉眼虎克又恢復了自我,斯密和斯塔基是他忠實的走狗。

passages.original: “Now we have him,” Hook shouted. “Into the water, Smee. Starkey, mind the boat. Take him dead or alive!”
passages.vernacular: 「而家我哋抓到佢喇,」虎克喊道。「下水,斯密。斯塔基,睇好船。要死嘅或活嘅都行!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「現在我們抓到他了,」虎克喊道。「下水,斯密。斯塔基,看好船。要死的或活的都行!」

passages.original: He leaped as he spoke, and simultaneously came the gay voice of Peter.
passages.vernacular: 佢講住跳咗下去,同時傳嚟彼得歡快嘅聲音。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他說著跳了下去,同時傳來彼得歡快的聲音。

passages.original: “Are you ready, boys?”
passages.vernacular: 「你哋準備好咗嗎,男孩哋?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你們準備好了嗎,男孩們?」

passages.original: “Ay, ay,” from various parts of the lagoon.
passages.vernacular: 「好,好」從潟湖各處傳嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好,好」從潟湖各處傳來。

passages.original: “Then lam into the pirates.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗰就痛打海盜。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那就痛打海盜。」

passages.original: The fight was short and sharp. First to draw blood was John, who gallantly climbed into the boat and held Starkey. There was fierce struggle, in which the cutlass was torn from the pirate’s grasp. He wriggled overboard and John leapt after him. The dinghy drifted away.
passages.vernacular: 戰鬥短暫而激烈。第一個見血嘅係約翰,佢英勇地爬上小艇,抓住斯塔基。一場激烈嘅搏鬥,其中短彎刀從海盜手中被奪走。佢扭動住跳出船外,約翰跟住跳下去。小艇漂走喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 戰鬥短暫而激烈。第一個見血的是約翰,他英勇地爬上小艇,抓住斯塔基。一場激烈的搏鬥,其中短彎刀從海盜手中被奪走。他扭動著跳出船外,約翰跟著跳下去。小艇漂走了。

passages.original: Here and there a head bobbed up in the water, and there was a flash of steel followed by a cry or a whoop. In the confusion some struck at their own side. The corkscrew of Smee got Tootles in the fourth rib, but he was himself pinked in turn by Curly. Farther from the rock Starkey was pressing Slightly and the twins hard.
passages.vernacular: 水裡呢度嗰度冒出一個頭,鋼刃一閃,接住係一聲叫喊或呼喊。混亂中有些人刺咗自己人。斯密嘅開瓶器刺中咗圖圖嘅第四根肋骨,但佢自己又被卷毛刺咗個洞。喺離岩石更遠嘅地方,斯塔基正把輕輕同雙胞胎逼得好緊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 水裡這裡那裡冒出一個頭,鋼刃一閃,接著是一聲叫喊或呼喊。混亂中有些人刺了自己人。斯密的開瓶器刺中了圖圖的第四根肋骨,但他自己又被卷毛刺了個洞。在離岩石更遠的地方,斯塔基正把輕輕和雙胞胎逼得很緊。

passages.original: Where all this time was Peter? He was seeking bigger game.
passages.vernacular: 呢陣彼得喺邊度?佢喺尋找更大嘅獵物。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這時彼得在哪裡?他在尋找更大的獵物。

passages.original: The others were all brave boys, and they must not be blamed for backing from the pirate captain. His iron claw made a circle of dead water round him, from which they fled like affrighted fishes.
passages.vernacular: 其他人都係勇敢嘅男孩,唔應該該因為佢哋避開海盜船長而責怪佢哋。佢嘅鐵爪喺佢周圍造出一圈死水,佢哋像受驚嘅魚一樣逃離。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 其他人都是勇敢的男孩,不應該因為他們避開海盜船長而責怪他們。他的鐵爪在他周圍造出一圈死水,他們像受驚的魚一樣逃離。

passages.original: But there was one who did not fear him: there was one prepared to enter that circle.
passages.vernacular: 但有一個人不怕佢:有一個人準備進入嗰個圈子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但有一個人不怕他:有一個人準備進入那個圈子。

passages.original: Strangely, it was not in the water that they met. Hook rose to the rock to breathe, and at the same moment Peter scaled it on the opposite side. The rock was slippery as a ball, and they had to crawl rather than climb. Neither knew that the other was coming. Each feeling for a grip met the other’s arm: in surprise they raised their heads; their faces were almost touching; so they met.
passages.vernacular: 奇怪嘅係,佢哋相遇唔係喺水裡。虎克爬上岩石呼吸,同時彼得從對面爬上岩石。岩石像球一樣滑,佢哋只能爬行而唔係攀登。兩人都唔知道對方喺嚟。每人摸索住抓嘢,碰到咗對方嘅手臂:佢哋驚訝地抬起頭;臉幾乎碰到一起;就咁樣相遇喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 奇怪的是,他們相遇不是在水裡。虎克爬上岩石呼吸,同時彼得從對面爬上岩石。岩石像球一樣滑,他們只能爬行而不是攀登。兩人都不知道對方在來。每人摸索著抓東西,碰到了對方的手臂:他們驚訝地抬起頭;臉幾乎碰到一起;就這樣相遇了。

passages.original: Some of the greatest heroes have confessed that just before they fell to they had a sinking. Had it been so with Peter at that moment I would admit it. After all, he was the only man that the Sea-Cook had feared. But Peter had no sinking, he had one feeling only, gladness; and he gnashed his pretty teeth with joy. Quick as thought he snatched a knife from Hook’s belt and was about to drive it home, when he saw that he was higher up the rock than his foe. It would not have been fighting fair. He gave the pirate a hand to help him up.
passages.vernacular: 啲最偉大嘅英雄承認,就喺佢哋開打之前,佢哋心裡一沉。如果彼得嗰時係咁樣,我會承認。畢竟,佢係海上廚子唯一怕嘅人。但彼得冇心沉,佢只有一種感覺,高興;佢高興得咬住佢漂亮嘅牙齒。快如思想,佢從虎克腰帶上搶咗一把刀,正要捅進去時,佢睇到自己比敵人喺岩石上嘅位置高。嗰不公平。佢伸手拉海盜上嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一些最偉大的英雄承認,就在他們開打之前,他們心裡一沉。如果彼得那時是這樣,我會承認。畢竟,他是海上廚子唯一怕的人。但彼得沒有心沉,他只有一種感覺,高興;他高興得咬著他漂亮的牙齒。快如思想,他從虎克腰帶上搶了一把刀,正要捅進去時,他看到自己比敵人在岩石上的位置高。那不公平。他伸手拉海盜上來。

passages.original: It was then that Hook bit him.
passages.vernacular: 就喺嗰時,虎克咬咗佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就在那時,虎克咬了他。

passages.original: Not the pain of this but its unfairness was what dazed Peter. It made him quite helpless. He could only stare, horrified. Every child is affected thus the first time he is treated unfairly. All he thinks he has a right to when he comes to you to be yours is fairness. After you have been unfair to him he will love you again, but will never afterwards be quite the same boy. No one ever gets over the first unfairness; no one except Peter. He often met it, but he always forgot it. I suppose that was the real difference between him and all the rest.
passages.vernacular: 使彼得發懵嘅唔係呢個嘅痛,而係佢嘅不公平。呢使佢完全無助。佢只能驚恐地瞪住。每個細路第一次受到不公平對待時都係咁樣。佢嚟到你呢度要做你嘅細路時,佢認為自己有權得到嘅全部就係公平。你對佢不公平之後,佢仲會再愛你,但此後再都唔係原來嗰個男孩喇。冇人能從第一次嘅不公平中恢復;除咗彼得。佢常常遇到佢,但佢總是忘記。我想嗰個就係佢同所有其他人之間真正嘅區別。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 使彼得發懵的不是這個的痛,而是它的不公平。這使他完全無助。他只能驚恐地瞪著。每個孩子第一次受到不公平對待時都是這樣。他來到你這裡要做你的孩子時,他認為自己有權得到的全部就是公平。你對他不公平之後,他還會再愛你,但此後再也不是原來那個男孩了。沒有人能從第一次的不公平中恢復;除了彼得。他常常遇到它,但他總是忘記。我想那就是他和所有其他人之間真正的區別。

passages.original: So when he met it now it was like the first time; and he could just stare, helpless. Twice the iron hand clawed him.
passages.vernacular: 所以佢而家遇到佢時,像第一次一樣;佢只能瞪住,無助。鐵手兩次抓咗佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以他現在遇到它時,像第一次一樣;他只能瞪著,無助。鐵手兩次抓了他。

passages.original: A few moments afterwards the other boys saw Hook in the water striking wildly for the ship; no elation on the pestilent face now, only white fear, for the crocodile was in dogged pursuit of him. On ordinary occasions the boys would have swum alongside cheering; but now they were uneasy, for they had lost both Peter and Wendy, and were scouring the lagoon for them, calling them by name. They found the dinghy and went home in it, shouting “Peter, Wendy” as they went, but no answer came save mocking laughter from the mermaids. “They must be swimming back or flying,” the boys concluded. They were not very anxious, because they had such faith in Peter. They chuckled, boylike, because they would be late for bed; and it was all mother Wendy’s fault!
passages.vernacular: 幾分鐘後,其他男孩睇到虎克喺水裡拼命地劃向船;佢嗰張可惡嘅臉上而家冇得意,只有蒼白嘅恐懼,因為鱷魚正頑強地追趕佢。平時男孩哋會喺旁邊游住歡呼;但而家佢哋不安,因為佢哋失去咗彼得同溫蒂,正在潟湖裡搜尋,叫住佢哋嘅名字。佢哋找到咗小艇,坐住佢回家,一路喊住「彼得,溫蒂」,但冇回答,只有美人魚嘲弄嘅笑聲。「佢哋一定游回去喇,或飛回去喇,」男孩哋斷定。佢哋不太焦急,因為佢哋對彼得咁有信心。佢哋像男孩一樣咯咯笑,因為佢哋上床要遲喇;呢全係溫蒂媽媽嘅錯!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 幾分鐘後,其他男孩看到虎克在水裡拼命地劃向船;他那張可惡的臉上現在沒有得意,只有蒼白的恐懼,因為鱷魚正頑強地追趕他。平時男孩們會在旁邊游著歡呼;但現在他們不安,因為他們失去了彼得和溫蒂,正在潟湖裡搜尋,叫著他們的名字。他們找到了小艇,坐著它回家,一路喊著「彼得,溫蒂」,但沒有回答,只有美人魚嘲弄的笑聲。「他們一定游回去了,或飛回去了,」男孩們斷定。他們不太焦急,因為他們對彼得那麼有信心。他們像男孩一樣咯咯笑,因為他們上床要遲了;這全是溫蒂媽媽的錯!

passages.original: When their voices died away there came cold silence over the lagoon, and then a feeble cry.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋嘅聲音消失後,冰冷嘅沉寂籠罩潟湖,然後傳嚟一聲微弱嘅呼喊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們的聲音消失後,冰冷的沉寂籠罩潟湖,然後傳來一聲微弱的呼喊。

passages.original: “Help, help!”
passages.vernacular: 「救命,救命!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「救命,救命!」

passages.original: Two small figures were beating against the rock; the girl had fainted and lay on the boy’s arm. With a last effort Peter pulled her up the rock and then lay down beside her. Even as he also fainted he saw that the water was rising. He knew that they would soon be drowned, but he could do no more.
passages.vernacular: 兩個小身影喺拍打住岩石;女孩昏倒喇,躺喺男孩嘅手臂上。彼得用最後嘅力氣把佢拉上岩石,然後躺喺佢旁邊。就喺佢都昏過去時,佢睇到水喺上升。佢知道佢哋好快就會被淹死,但佢無能為力。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 兩個小身影在拍打著岩石;女孩昏倒了,躺在男孩的手臂上。彼得用最後的力氣把她拉上岩石,然後躺在她旁邊。就在他也昏過去時,他看到水在上升。他知道他們很快就會被淹死,但他無能為力。

passages.original: As they lay side by side a mermaid caught Wendy by the feet, and began pulling her softly into the water. Peter, feeling her slip from him, woke with a start, and was just in time to draw her back. But he had to tell her the truth.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋並排躺住時,一條美人魚抓住溫蒂嘅腳,開始輕輕把佢拉進水裡。彼得感到佢從佢身邊滑走,猛地驚醒,正好及時把佢拉回嚟。但佢唔得不告訴佢真相。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們並排躺著時,一條美人魚抓住溫蒂的腳,開始輕輕把她拉進水裡。彼得感到她從他身邊滑走,猛地驚醒,正好及時把她拉回來。但他不得不告訴她真相。

passages.original: “We are on the rock, Wendy,” he said, “but it is growing smaller. Soon the water will be over it.”
passages.vernacular: 「我哋喺岩石上,溫蒂,」佢講,「但佢喺變小。不久水就會淹過佢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們在岩石上,溫蒂,」他說,「但它在變小。不久水就會淹過它。」

passages.original: She did not understand even now.
passages.vernacular: 佢即使而家都不明白。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她即使現在也不明白。

passages.original: “We must go,” she said, almost brightly.
passages.vernacular: 「我哋必須走,」佢幾乎係明朗地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們必須走,」她幾乎是明朗地說。

passages.original: “Yes,” he answered faintly.
passages.vernacular: 「係,」佢虛弱地回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是,」他虛弱地回答。

passages.original: “Shall we swim or fly, Peter?”
passages.vernacular: 「我哋游定係飛,彼得?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們游還是飛,彼得?」

passages.original: He had to tell her.
passages.vernacular: 佢唔得不告訴佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他不得不告訴她。

passages.original: “Do you think you could swim or fly as far as the island, Wendy, without my help?”
passages.vernacular: 「你認為你能不靠我幫忙游或飛到島咁遠嗎,溫蒂?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你認為你能不靠我幫忙游或飛到島那麼遠嗎,溫蒂?」

passages.original: She had to admit that she was too tired.
passages.vernacular: 佢唔得不承認佢太累喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她不得不承認她太累了。

passages.original: He moaned.
passages.vernacular: 佢呻吟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他呻吟。

passages.original: “What is it?” she asked, anxious about him at once.
passages.vernacular: 「點喇?」佢問,即刻為佢擔心。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「怎麼了?」她問,馬上為他擔心。

passages.original: “I can’t help you, Wendy. Hook wounded me. I can neither fly nor swim.”
passages.vernacular: 「我幫不咗你,溫蒂。虎克傷咗我。我既唔能夠飛都唔能夠游。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我幫不了你,溫蒂。虎克傷了我。我既不能飛也不能游。」

passages.original: “Do you mean we shall both be drowned?”
passages.vernacular: 「你係講我哋都會淹死?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你是說我們都會淹死?」

passages.original: “Look how the water is rising.”
passages.vernacular: 「睇水喺上升。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「看水在上升。」

passages.original: They put their hands over their eyes to shut out the sight. They thought they would soon be no more. As they sat thus something brushed against Peter as light as a kiss, and stayed there, as if saying timidly, “Can I be of any use?”
passages.vernacular: 佢哋用手蓋住眼睛,不睇呢景象。佢哋以為好快就會不喺人世喇。佢哋咁樣坐住,有乜嘢嘢輕得像吻一樣擦過彼得,停喺嗰度,好像喺膽怯地講:「我能幫上忙嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們用手蓋住眼睛,不看這景象。他們以為很快就會不在人世了。他們這樣坐著,有什麼東西輕得像吻一樣擦過彼得,停在那裡,好像在膽怯地說:「我能幫上忙嗎?」

passages.original: It was the tail of a kite, which Michael had made some days before. It had torn itself out of his hand and floated away.
passages.vernacular: 嗰個係風箏嘅尾巴,係邁克爾幾天前做嘅。佢掙脫咗佢嘅手,飄走喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那是風箏的尾巴,是邁克爾幾天前做的。它掙脫了他的手,飄走了。

passages.original: “Michael’s kite,” Peter said without interest, but next moment he had seized the tail, and was pulling the kite toward him.
passages.vernacular: 「邁克爾嘅風箏,」彼得毫無興趣地講,但下一刻佢抓住咗尾巴,把風箏拉向自己。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「邁克爾的風箏,」彼得毫無興趣地說,但下一刻他抓住了尾巴,把風箏拉向自己。

passages.original: “It lifted Michael off the ground,” he cried; “why should it not carry you?”
passages.vernacular: 「佢把邁克爾從地上提咗起嚟,」佢喊道;「點解唔能夠帶你走?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「它把邁克爾從地上提了起來,」他喊道;「為什麼不能帶你走?」

passages.original: “Both of us!”
passages.vernacular: 「我哋兩個一起!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們兩個一起!」

passages.original: “It can’t lift two; Michael and Curly tried.”
passages.vernacular: 「佢提不起兩個;邁克爾同卷毛試過喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「它提不起兩個;邁克爾和卷毛試過了。」

passages.original: “Let us draw lots,” Wendy said bravely.
passages.vernacular: 「我哋抽籤吧,」溫蒂勇敢地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們抽籤吧,」溫蒂勇敢地說。

passages.original: “And you a lady; never.” Already he had tied the tail round her. She clung to him; she refused to go without him; but with a “Good-bye, Wendy,” he pushed her from the rock; and in a few minutes she was borne out of his sight. Peter was alone on the lagoon.
passages.vernacular: 「你係位女士;絕不。」佢已經把尾巴綁喺佢身上喇。佢緊緊抓住佢;佢拒絕冇佢就走;但佢講咗一聲「再見,溫蒂」,把佢從岩石上推開;幾分鐘內佢就被帶出咗佢嘅視線。彼得獨自一人喺潟湖上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你是位女士;絕不。」他已經把尾巴綁在她身上了。她緊緊抓住他;她拒絕沒有他就走;但他說了一聲「再見,溫蒂」,把她從岩石上推開;幾分鐘內她就被帶出了他的視線。彼得獨自一人在潟湖上。

passages.original: The rock was very small now; soon it would be submerged. Pale rays of light tiptoed across the waters; and by and by there was to be heard a sound at once the most musical and the most melancholy in the world: the mermaids calling to the moon.
passages.vernacular: 岩石而家好小喇;好快就要被淹沒。蒼白嘅光線踮住腳尖越過水面;不久可以聽到世界上最悅耳都最悲傷嘅聲音:美人魚喺向月亮呼喚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 岩石現在非常小了;很快就要被淹沒。蒼白的光線踮著腳尖越過水面;不久可以聽到世界上最悅耳也最悲傷的聲音:美人魚在向月亮呼喚。

passages.original: Peter was not quite like other boys; but he was afraid at last. A tremour ran through him, like a shudder passing over the sea; but on the sea one shudder follows another till there are hundreds of them, and Peter felt just the one. Next moment he was standing erect on the rock again, with that smile on his face and a drum beating within him. It was saying, “To die will be an awfully big adventure.”
passages.vernacular: 彼得不太像其他男孩;但佢終於害怕喇。一陣顫抖傳過佢嘅全身,像一陣顫慄掠過海面;但喺海上一陣顫慄接住另一陣,直到有數百陣,而彼得只感覺到一陣。下一刻佢又直立喺岩石上,臉上帶住嗰個微笑,體內有一面鼓喺敲。佢喺講:「死將係一場極其偉大嘅冒險。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 彼得不太像其他男孩;但他終於害怕了。一陣顫抖傳過他的全身,像一陣顫慄掠過海面;但在海上一陣顫慄接著另一陣,直到有數百陣,而彼得只感覺到一陣。下一刻他又直立在岩石上,臉上帶著那個微笑,體內有一面鼓在敲。它在說:「死將是一場極其偉大的冒險。」

chapters.title: Chapter IX: The Never Bird 第九章:永無鳥

passages.original: The last sound Peter heard before he was quite alone were the mermaids retiring one by one to their bedchambers under the sea. He was too far away to hear their doors shut; but every door in the coral caves where they live rings a tiny bell when it opens or closes (as in all the nicest houses on the mainland), and he heard the bells.
passages.vernacular: 彼得喺完全孤單之前聽到嘅最後聲音,係美人魚一個個退回佢哋海底嘅臥室。佢離得太遠,聽唔到佢哋關門;但佢哋住嘅珊瑚洞穴裡每扇門開關時都會響起一個小鈴(像大陸上所有最好嘅房子一樣),佢聽到咗嗰啲鈴聲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 彼得在完全孤單之前聽到的最後聲音,是美人魚一個個退回她們海底的臥室。他離得太遠,聽不到她們關門;但她們住的珊瑚洞穴裡每扇門開關時都會響起一個小鈴(像大陸上所有最好的房子一樣),他聽到了那些鈴聲。

passages.original: Steadily the waters rose till they were nibbling at his feet; and to pass the time until they made their final gulp, he watched the only thing on the lagoon. He thought it was a piece of floating paper, perhaps part of the kite, and wondered idly how long it would take to drift ashore.
passages.vernacular: 水穩步上升,直到開始啃佢嘅腳;為了喺佢哋最後一口吞下之前打發時間,佢睇住潟湖上唯一嘅嘢。佢以為嗰個係一張漂浮嘅紙,或者係風箏嘅一部分,漫不經心地想佢要多久才能漂到岸上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 水穩步上升,直到開始啃他的腳;為了在它們最後一口吞下之前打發時間,他看著潟湖上唯一的東西。他以為那是一張漂浮的紙,也許是風箏的一部分,漫不經心地想它要多久才能漂到岸上。

passages.original: Presently he noticed as an odd thing that it was undoubtedly out upon the lagoon with some definite purpose, for it was fighting the tide, and sometimes winning; and when it won, Peter, always sympathetic to the weaker side, could not help clapping; it was such a gallant piece of paper.
passages.vernacular: 不久佢奇怪地注意到,佢無疑係出於某種明確目的喺潟湖上嘅,因為佢喺同潮水搏鬥,有時仲贏;佢贏嘅時候,總是同情弱者嗰一方嘅彼得不禁鼓掌;佢係咁英勇嘅一張紙。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不久他奇怪地注意到,它無疑是出於某種明確目的在潟湖上的,因為它在與潮水搏鬥,有時還贏;它贏的時候,總是同情弱者那一方的彼得不禁鼓掌;它是那麼英勇的一張紙。

passages.original: It was not really a piece of paper; it was the Never bird, making desperate efforts to reach Peter on the nest. By working her wings, in a way she had learned since the nest fell into the water, she was able to some extent to guide her strange craft, but by the time Peter recognised her she was very exhausted. She had come to save him, to give him her nest, though there were eggs in it. I rather wonder at the bird, for though he had been nice to her, he had also sometimes tormented her. I can suppose only that, like Mrs. Darling and the rest of them, she was melted because he had all his first teeth.
passages.vernacular: 佢唔係一張紙;佢係永無鳥,正拼命努力地劃住巢向彼得靠近。自從巢掉進水裡以來,佢學會用翅膀嘅一種方式,通過呢個,佢多少能駕馭佢嗰奇特嘅船,但彼得認出佢時,佢已經筋疲力盡喇。佢係嚟救佢嘅,把佢嘅巢畀佢,雖然裡面有蛋。我對呢隻鳥相當驚訝,因為雖然佢對佢好,但佢有時都折磨佢。我只能猜想,像達玲太太同其他人一樣,佢被融化喇,因為佢有全部嘅乳牙。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它不是一張紙;它是永無鳥,正拼命努力地劃著巢向彼得靠近。自從巢掉進水裡以來,她學會用翅膀的一種方式,通過這個,她多少能駕馭她那奇特的船,但彼得認出她時,她已經筋疲力盡了。她是來救他的,把她的巢給他,雖然裡面有蛋。我對這隻鳥相當驚訝,因為雖然他對她好,但他有時也折磨她。我只能猜想,像達玲太太和其他人一樣,她被融化了,因為他有全部的乳牙。

passages.original: She called out to him what she had come for, and he called out to her what she was doing there; but of course neither of them understood the other’s language. In fanciful stories people can talk to the birds freely, and I wish for the moment I could pretend that this were such a story, and say that Peter replied intelligently to the Never bird; but truth is best, and I want to tell you only what really happened. Well, not only could they not understand each other, but they forgot their manners.
passages.vernacular: 佢對佢喊出佢嚟嘅目的,佢對佢喊佢喺嗰度做乜嘢;但當然佢哋邊個都不懂對方嘅語言。喺奇幻故事裡人哋可以隨便同鳥講話,我希望呢一刻我能假裝呢個係嗰樣嘅故事,講彼得聰明地回答永無鳥;但真相最好,我只想告訴你真正發生嘅事。嗯,佢哋不僅唔能夠互相理解,而且仲忘咗禮貌。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她對他喊出她來的目的,他對她喊她在那裡做什麼;但當然他們誰也不懂對方的語言。在奇幻故事裡人們可以隨便同鳥說話,我希望這一刻我能假裝這是那樣的故事,說彼得聰明地回答永無鳥;但真相最好,我只想告訴你真正發生的事。嗯,他們不僅不能互相理解,而且還忘了禮貌。

passages.original: “I—want—you—to—get—into—the—nest,” the bird called, speaking as slowly and distinctly as possible, “and—then—you—can—drift—ashore, but—I—am—too—tired—to—bring—it—any—nearer—so—you—must—try to—swim—to—it.”
passages.vernacular: 「我——要——你——爬——進——巢——裡,」鳥喊道,講得盡可能慢而清楚,「然後——你——就——可以——漂——到岸——上,但係——我——太累喇——唔能夠——把佢——帶得——更近——所以——你——必須——試住——游——到佢嗰度。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我——要——你——爬——進——巢——裡,」鳥喊道,說得盡可能慢而清楚,「然後——你——就——可以——漂——到岸——上,但是——我——太累了——不能——把它——帶得——更近——所以——你——必須——試著——游——到它那裡。」

passages.original: “What are you quacking about?” Peter answered. “Why don’t you let the nest drift as usual?”
passages.vernacular: 「你嘎嘎叫乜嘢?」彼得回答。「你點解不像平常嗰樣讓巢漂住?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你嘎嘎叫什麼?」彼得回答。「你為什麼不像平常那樣讓巢漂著?」

passages.original: “I—want—you—” the bird said, and repeated it all over.
passages.vernacular: 「我——要——你——」鳥講,又全部重複一遍。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我——要——你——」鳥說,又全部重複一遍。

passages.original: Then Peter tried slow and distinct.
passages.vernacular: 然後彼得試住慢而清楚地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後彼得試著慢而清楚地說。

passages.original: “What—are—you—quacking—about?” and so on.
passages.vernacular: 「你——嘎嘎——叫——乜嘢?」等等。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你——嘎嘎——叫——什麼?」等等。

passages.original: The Never bird became irritated; they have very short tempers.
passages.vernacular: 永無鳥惱火喇;牠哋脾氣好壞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 永無鳥惱火了;牠們脾氣很壞。

passages.original: “You dunderheaded little jay!” she screamed, “Why don’t you do as I tell you?”
passages.vernacular: 「你呢蠢頭蠢腦嘅小松鴉!」佢尖叫,「你點解不照我講嘅做?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你這蠢頭蠢腦的小松鴉!」她尖叫,「你為什麼不照我說的做?」

passages.original: Peter felt that she was calling him names, and at a venture he retorted hotly:
passages.vernacular: 彼得覺得佢喺罵佢,冒險地憤怒反駁:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 彼得覺得她在罵他,冒險地憤怒反駁:

passages.original: “So are you!”
passages.vernacular: 「你才係!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你才是!」

passages.original: Then rather curiously they both snapped out the same remark:
passages.vernacular: 然後相當奇怪地,佢哋兩個同時脫口講出同樣嘅話:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後相當奇怪地,他們兩個同時脫口說出同樣的話:

passages.original: “Shut up!”
passages.vernacular: 「閉嘴!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「閉嘴!」

passages.original: “Shut up!”
passages.vernacular: 「閉嘴!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「閉嘴!」

passages.original: Nevertheless the bird was determined to save him if she could, and by one last mighty effort she propelled the nest against the rock. Then up she flew; deserting her eggs, so as to make her meaning clear.
passages.vernacular: 儘管如此,鳥決心如果可能就救佢,佢用最後一次巨大嘅努力把巢推向岩石。然後佢飛起嚟;拋下佢嘅蛋,以便表明佢嘅意思。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 儘管如此,鳥決心如果可能就救他,她用最後一次巨大的努力把巢推向岩石。然後她飛起來;拋下她的蛋,以便表明她的意思。

passages.original: Then at last he understood, and clutched the nest and waved his thanks to the bird as she fluttered overhead. It was not to receive his thanks, however, that she hung there in the sky; it was not even to watch him get into the nest; it was to see what he did with her eggs.
passages.vernacular: 於是佢終於明白喇,抓住巢,向喺頭頂拍翅嘅鳥揮手致謝。然而佢懸喺空中唔係為了接受佢嘅感謝;甚至唔係為了睇佢爬進巢;而係為了睇佢點處理佢嘅蛋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是他終於明白了,抓住巢,向在頭頂拍翅的鳥揮手致謝。然而她懸在空中不是為了接受他的感謝;甚至不是為了看他爬進巢;而是為了看他怎麼處理她的蛋。

passages.original: There were two large white eggs, and Peter lifted them up and reflected. The bird covered her face with her wings, so as not to see the last of them; but she could not help peeping between the feathers.
passages.vernacular: 有兩個大白蛋,彼得把佢哋舉起嚟思考。鳥用翅膀蓋住臉,以便不睇到佢哋嘅最後;但佢忍不住從羽毛縫隙間偷睇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有兩個大白蛋,彼得把它們舉起來思考。鳥用翅膀蓋住臉,以便不看到它們的最後;但她忍不住從羽毛縫隙間偷看。

passages.original: I forget whether I have told you that there was a stave on the rock, driven into it by some buccaneers of long ago to mark the site of buried treasure. The children had discovered the glittering hoard, and when in a mischievous mood used to fling showers of moidores, diamonds, pearls and pieces of eight to the gulls, who pounced upon them for food, and then flew away, raging at the scurvy trick that had been played upon them. The stave was still there, and on it Starkey had hung his hat, a deep tarpaulin, watertight, with a broad brim. Peter put the eggs into this hat and set it on the lagoon. It floated beautifully.
passages.vernacular: 我忘咗我有冇告訴過你,岩石上有一根木杆,係好久以前啲海盜插進去標記埋藏寶藏嘅地方嘅。細路哋發現咗閃閃發光嘅寶藏,淘氣嘅時候常常向海鷗撒大把嘅摩艾多金幣、鑽石、珍珠同八里亞爾銀幣,海鷗撲上去當食物,然後飛走,對嗰個捉弄牠哋嘅卑鄙把戲氣得唔得喇。木杆仲喺嗰度,斯塔基把佢嘅帽子掛喺上面,嗰個係一頂深深嘅防水帆布帽,有寬寬嘅帽檐。彼得把蛋放進呢頂帽子裡,放喺潟湖上。佢漂得好好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我忘了我有沒有告訴過你,岩石上有一根木杆,是很久以前一些海盜插進去標記埋藏寶藏的地方的。孩子們發現了閃閃發光的寶藏,淘氣的時候常常向海鷗撒大把的摩艾多金幣、鑽石、珍珠和八里亞爾銀幣,海鷗撲上去當食物,然後飛走,對那個捉弄牠們的卑鄙把戲氣得不得了。木杆還在那裡,斯塔基把他的帽子掛在上面,那是一頂深深的防水帆布帽,有寬寬的帽檐。彼得把蛋放進這頂帽子裡,放在潟湖上。它漂得很好。

passages.original: The Never bird saw at once what he was up to, and screamed her admiration of him; and, alas, Peter crowed his agreement with her. Then he got into the nest, reared the stave in it as a mast, and hung up his shirt for a sail. At the same moment the bird fluttered down upon the hat and once more sat snugly on her eggs. She drifted in one direction, and he was borne off in another, both cheering.
passages.vernacular: 永無鳥即刻睇出佢喺做乜嘢,尖叫住表示對佢嘅欽佩;可惜,彼得都啼叫表示同意。然後佢進咗巢,把木杆豎喺裡面當桅杆,掛起佢嘅襯衫當帆。同時鳥撲到帽子上,又舒舒服服地坐喺佢嘅蛋上。佢朝一個方向漂,佢朝另一個方向被帶走,兩人都歡呼住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 永無鳥馬上看出他在做什麼,尖叫著表示對他的欽佩;可惜,彼得也啼叫表示同意。然後他進了巢,把木杆豎在裡面當桅杆,掛起他的襯衫當帆。同時鳥撲到帽子上,又舒舒服服地坐在她的蛋上。她朝一個方向漂,他朝另一個方向被帶走,兩人都歡呼著。

passages.original: Of course when Peter landed he beached his barque in a place where the bird would easily find it; but the hat was such a great success that she abandoned the nest. It drifted about till it went to pieces, and often Starkey came to the shore of the lagoon, and with many bitter feelings watched the bird sitting on his hat. As we shall not see her again, it may be worth mentioning here that all Never birds now build in that shape of nest, with a broad brim on which the youngsters take an airing.
passages.vernacular: 當然彼得登陸時,把佢嘅小船拖到鳥容易找到嘅地方;但帽子係咁大嘅成功,佢放棄咗巢。佢漂嚟漂去,直到散成碎片,斯塔基常嚟到潟湖岸邊,懷住許多苦澀嘅心情睇住鳥坐喺佢嘅帽子上。因為我哋唔會再見到佢,呢度值得一提:而家所有永無鳥都用嗰種形狀築巢,有寬寬嘅帽檐,小鳥哋喺上面透氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當然彼得登陸時,把他的小船拖到鳥容易找到的地方;但帽子是這麼大的成功,她放棄了巢。它漂來漂去,直到散成碎片,斯塔基常來到潟湖岸邊,懷著許多苦澀的心情看著鳥坐在他的帽子上。因為我們不會再見到她,這裡值得一提:現在所有永無鳥都用那種形狀築巢,有寬寬的帽檐,小鳥們在上面透氣。

passages.original: Great were the rejoicings when Peter reached the home under the ground almost as soon as Wendy, who had been carried hither and thither by the kite. Every boy had adventures to tell; but perhaps the biggest adventure of all was that they were several hours late for bed. This so inflated them that they did various dodgy things to get staying up still longer, such as demanding bandages; but Wendy, though glorying in having them all home again safe and sound, was scandalised by the lateness of the hour, and cried, “To bed, to bed,” in a voice that had to be obeyed. Next day, however, she was awfully tender, and gave out bandages to every one, and they played till bed-time at limping about and carrying their arms in slings.
passages.vernacular: 彼得幾乎同被風箏帶得到處飄嘅溫蒂同時回到地下家園,大家歡天喜地。每個男孩都有冒險可講;但或者所有冒險中最大嘅係,佢哋比上床時間晚咗好幾個小時。呢使佢哋得意忘形,做咗各種狡猾嘅事嚟繼續晚瞓,比如要求包紮繃帶;但溫蒂雖然為佢哋全都平安無事地回家而高興,卻對時間咁晚感到驚駭,用一種必須服從嘅聲音喊道:「瞓覺,瞓覺。」不過第二天佢好溫柔,畀每個人發繃帶,佢哋玩到瞓覺時間,假裝一瘸一拐、把手臂吊喺吊帶上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 彼得幾乎和被風箏帶得到處飄的溫蒂同時回到地下家園,大家歡天喜地。每個男孩都有冒險可講;但也許所有冒險中最大的是,他們比上床時間晚了好幾個小時。這使他們得意忘形,做了各種狡猾的事來繼續晚睡,比如要求包紮繃帶;但溫蒂雖然為他們全都平安無事地回家而高興,卻對時間這麼晚感到驚駭,用一種必須服從的聲音喊道:「睡覺,睡覺。」不過第二天她非常溫柔,給每個人發繃帶,他們玩到睡覺時間,假裝一瘸一拐、把手臂吊在吊帶上。

chapters.title: Chapter X: The Happy Home 第十章:快樂的家

passages.original: One important result of the brush on the lagoon was that it made the redskins their friends. Peter had saved Tiger Lily from a dreadful fate, and now there was nothing she and her braves would not do for him. All night they sat above, keeping watch over the home under the ground and awaiting the big attack by the pirates which obviously could not be much longer delayed. Even by day they hung about, smoking the pipe of peace, and looking almost as if they wanted tit-bits to eat.
passages.vernacular: 潟湖上嗰場戰鬥嘅一個重要結果係,佢使紅番成咗佢哋嘅朋友。彼得從可怕嘅命運中救咗虎百合,而家佢同佢嘅勇士哋冇乜嘢係唔願為佢做嘅。整晚佢哋坐喺上面,守衛住地下家園,等待海盜明顯唔會拖延太久嘅大攻擊。即使白天佢哋都喺附近逗留,抽住和平煙斗,睇起嚟幾乎像想要點心食。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 潟湖上那場戰鬥的一個重要結果是,它使紅番成了他們的朋友。彼得從可怕的命運中救了虎百合,現在她和她的勇士們沒有什麼是不願為他做的。整晚他們坐在上面,守衛著地下家園,等待海盜明顯不會拖延太久的大攻擊。即使白天他們也在附近逗留,抽著和平煙斗,看起來幾乎像想要點心吃。

passages.original: They called Peter the Great White Father, prostrating themselves before him; and he liked this tremendously, so that it was not really good for him.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋稱彼得為偉大嘅白人父親,喺佢面前趴伏喺地;佢好鍾意呢個,以致呢對佢並不真嘅好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們稱彼得為偉大的白人父親,在他面前趴伏在地;他非常喜歡這個,以致這對他並不真的好。

passages.original: “The great white father,” he would say to them in a very lordly manner, as they grovelled at his feet, “is glad to see the Piccaninny warriors protecting his wigwam from the pirates.”
passages.vernacular: 「偉大嘅白人父親,」佢會用好貴族嘅態度對佢哋講,而佢哋喺佢腳下匍匐,「好高興睇到皮卡尼尼勇士保護佢嘅帳篷不受海盜侵犯。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「偉大的白人父親,」他會用非常貴族的態度對他們說,而他們在他腳下匍匐,「很高興看到皮卡尼尼勇士保護他的帳篷不受海盜侵犯。」

passages.original: “Me Tiger Lily,” that lovely creature would reply. “Peter Pan save me, me his velly nice friend. Me no let pirates hurt him.”
passages.vernacular: 「我虎百合,」嗰可愛嘅人兒會回答。「彼得潘救我,我佢好好朋友。我不讓海盜傷害佢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我虎百合,」那可愛的人兒會回答。「彼得潘救我,我他很好朋友。我不讓海盜傷害他。」

passages.original: She was far too pretty to cringe in this way, but Peter thought it his due, and he would answer condescendingly, “It is good. Peter Pan has spoken.”
passages.vernacular: 佢太漂亮喇,不該咁樣卑躬屈膝,但彼得認為呢個係佢應得嘅,佢會屈尊地回答:「好好。彼得潘已講話。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她太漂亮了,不該這樣卑躬屈膝,但彼得認為這是他應得的,他會屈尊地回答:「很好。彼得潘已說話。」

passages.original: Always when he said, “Peter Pan has spoken,” it meant that they must now shut up, and they accepted it humbly in that spirit; but they were by no means so respectful to the other boys, whom they looked upon as just ordinary braves. They said “How-do?” to them, and things like that; and what annoyed the boys was that Peter seemed to think this all right.
passages.vernacular: 每當佢講「彼得潘已講話」,意思就係佢哋而家該閉嘴,佢哋以呢種精神謙卑地接受;但佢哋對其他男孩就不咁尊敬喇,把佢哋只睇作普通嘅勇士。佢哋對佢哋講「你好嗎?」之類嘅話;使男孩哋惱火嘅係,彼得似乎認為呢都好好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 每當他說「彼得潘已說話」,意思就是他們現在該閉嘴,他們以這種精神謙卑地接受;但他們對其他男孩就不那麼尊敬了,把他們只看作普通的勇士。他們對他們說「你好嗎?」之類的話;使男孩們惱火的是,彼得似乎認為這都很好。

passages.original: Secretly Wendy sympathised with them a little, but she was far too loyal a housewife to listen to any complaints against father. “Father knows best,” she always said, whatever her private opinion must be. Her private opinion was that the redskins should not call her a squaw.
passages.vernacular: 溫蒂暗中有點同情佢哋,但佢係太忠誠嘅家庭主婦,唔會聽任何針對爸爸嘅抱怨。「爸爸最懂,」不管佢私下嘅意見係乜嘢,佢總是咁樣講。佢私下嘅意見係紅番不該叫佢「squaw(印第安婦女)」。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 溫蒂暗中有點同情他們,但她是太忠誠的家庭主婦,不會聽任何針對爸爸的抱怨。「爸爸最懂,」不管她私下的意見是什麼,她總是這樣說。她私下的意見是紅番不該叫她「squaw(印第安婦女)」。

passages.original: We have now reached the evening that was to be known among them as the Night of Nights, because of its adventures and their upshot. The day, as if quietly gathering its forces, had been almost uneventful, and now the redskins in their blankets were at their posts above, while, below, the children were having their evening meal; all except Peter, who had gone out to get the time. The way you got the time on the island was to find the crocodile, and then stay near him till the clock struck.
passages.vernacular: 我哋而家到咗嗰個將喺佢哋中間被稱為「夜中之夜」嘅晚上,因為佢嘅冒險同結果。呢一天,像喺靜靜地積蓄力量,幾乎冇發生乜嘢事,而家紅番裹住毯子喺上面嘅崗位上,而喺下面,細路哋喺食晚餐;除咗彼得,佢出去查時間喇。喺島上查時間嘅方法係找到鱷魚,然後待喺佢附近,直到鐘響。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們現在到了那個將在他們中間被稱為「夜中之夜」的晚上,因為它的冒險和結果。這一天,像在靜靜地積蓄力量,幾乎沒有發生什麼事,現在紅番裹著毯子在上面的崗位上,而在下面,孩子們在吃晚餐;除了彼得,他出去查時間了。在島上查時間的方法是找到鱷魚,然後待在它附近,直到鐘響。

passages.original: The meal happened to be a make-believe tea, and they sat around the board, guzzling in their greed; and really, what with their chatter and recriminations, the noise, as Wendy said, was positively deafening. To be sure, she did not mind noise, but she simply would not have them grabbing things, and then excusing themselves by saying that Tootles had pushed their elbow. There was a fixed rule that they must never hit back at meals, but should refer the matter of dispute to Wendy by raising the right arm politely and saying, “I complain of so-and-so;” but what usually happened was that they forgot to do this or did it too much.
passages.vernacular: 呢頓飯碰巧係假裝嘅下午茶,佢哋圍住桌子,貪婪地狼吞虎嚥;講真嘅,佢哋嘅閒談同互相指責,吵鬧得,如溫蒂所講,簡直震耳欲聾。誠然,佢不介意吵,但佢就係不許佢哋搶嘢,然後藉口講係圖圖推咗佢哋嘅手肘。有一條固定嘅規則,食飯時佢哋絕不許仲手,而應該有禮貌地舉起右臂,講「我投訴某某,」把爭議提交畀溫蒂;但通常發生嘅係,佢哋忘咗咁樣做,或做得太過。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這頓飯碰巧是假裝的下午茶,他們圍著桌子,貪婪地狼吞虎嚥;說真的,他們的閒談和互相指責,吵鬧得,如溫蒂所說,簡直震耳欲聾。誠然,她不介意吵,但她就是不許他們搶東西,然後藉口說是圖圖推了他們的手肘。有一條固定的規則,吃飯時他們絕不許還手,而應該有禮貌地舉起右臂,說「我投訴某某,」把爭議提交給溫蒂;但通常發生的是,他們忘了這樣做,或做得太過。

passages.original: “Silence,” cried Wendy when for the twentieth time she had told them that they were not all to speak at once. “Is your mug empty, Slightly darling?”
passages.vernacular: 「安靜,」溫蒂第二十次告訴佢哋唔能夠大家同時講話時喊道。「你嘅杯子空咗嗎,親愛嘅輕輕?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「安靜,」溫蒂第二十次告訴他們不能大家同時說話時喊道。「你的杯子空了嗎,親愛的輕輕?」

passages.original: “Not quite empty, mummy,” Slightly said, after looking into an imaginary mug.
passages.vernacular: 「仲冇完全空,媽咪,」輕輕睇咗睇一個想像嘅杯子後講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「還沒有完全空,媽咪,」輕輕看了看一個想像的杯子後說。

passages.original: “He hasn’t even begun to drink his milk,” Nibs interposed.
passages.vernacular: 「佢連牛奶都仲冇開始飲,」尼布斯插嘴。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他連牛奶都還沒開始喝,」尼布斯插嘴。

passages.original: This was telling, and Slightly seized his chance.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係告狀,輕輕抓住咗機會。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是告狀,輕輕抓住了機會。

passages.original: “I complain of Nibs,” he cried promptly.
passages.vernacular: 「我投訴尼布斯,」佢即刻喊道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我投訴尼布斯,」他馬上喊道。

passages.original: John, however, had held up his hand first.
passages.vernacular: 然而約翰先舉咗手。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然而約翰先舉了手。

passages.original: “Well, John?”
passages.vernacular: 「好吧,約翰?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好吧,約翰?」

passages.original: “May I sit in Peter’s chair, as he is not here?”
passages.vernacular: 「彼得不喺,我可以坐佢嘅椅子嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「彼得不在,我可以坐他的椅子嗎?」

passages.original: “Sit in father’s chair, John!” Wendy was scandalised. “Certainly not.”
passages.vernacular: 「坐爸爸嘅椅子,約翰!」溫蒂驚駭喇。「當然不行。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「坐爸爸的椅子,約翰!」溫蒂驚駭了。「當然不行。」

passages.original: “He is not really our father,” John answered. “He didn’t even know how a father does till I showed him.”
passages.vernacular: 「佢唔係真嘅我哋嘅爸爸,」約翰回答。「係我教佢之後,佢才知道爸爸點樣做嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他不是真的我們的爸爸,」約翰回答。「是我教他之後,他才知道爸爸怎樣做的。」

passages.original: This was grumbling. “We complain of John,” cried the twins.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係喺抱怨。「我哋投訴約翰,」雙胞胎喊道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是在抱怨。「我們投訴約翰,」雙胞胎喊道。

passages.original: Tootles held up his hand. He was so much the humblest of them, indeed he was the only humble one, that Wendy was specially gentle with him.
passages.vernacular: 圖圖舉起手。佢係佢哋中間最謙遜嘅,事實上佢係唯一謙遜嘅,所以溫蒂對佢特別溫柔。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 圖圖舉起手。他是他們中間最謙遜的,事實上他是唯一謙遜的,所以溫蒂對他特別溫柔。

passages.original: “I don’t suppose,” Tootles said diffidently, “that I could be father.”
passages.vernacular: 「我想,」圖圖膽怯地講,「我唔能夠做爸爸吧。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想,」圖圖膽怯地說,「我不能做爸爸吧。」

passages.original: “No, Tootles.”
passages.vernacular: 「不行,圖圖。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不行,圖圖。」

passages.original: Once Tootles began, which was not very often, he had a silly way of going on.
passages.vernacular: 圖圖一旦開始,呢不常有,佢就有一種愚蠢嘅繼續下去嘅方式。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 圖圖一旦開始,這不常有,他就有一種愚蠢的繼續下去的方式。

passages.original: “As I can’t be father,” he said heavily, “I don’t suppose, Michael, you would let me be baby?”
passages.vernacular: 「既然我唔能夠做爸爸,」佢沉重地講,「邁克爾,我想你唔會讓我做寶寶吧?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「既然我不能做爸爸,」他沉重地說,「邁克爾,我想你不會讓我做寶寶吧?」

passages.original: “No, I won’t,” Michael rapped out. He was already in his basket.
passages.vernacular: 「不,我唔好,」邁克爾厲聲講。佢已經喺籃子裡喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不,我不要,」邁克爾厲聲說。他已經在籃子裡了。

passages.original: “As I can’t be baby,” Tootles said, getting heavier and heavier and heavier, “do you think I could be a twin?”
passages.vernacular: 「既然我唔能夠做寶寶,」圖圖講,越嚟越沉重,越嚟越沉重,「你哋覺得我能做雙胞胎嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「既然我不能做寶寶,」圖圖說,越來越沉重,越來越沉重,「你們覺得我能做雙胞胎嗎?」

passages.original: “No, indeed,” replied the twins; “it’s awfully difficult to be a twin.”
passages.vernacular: 「不行,真嘅不行,」雙胞胎回答;「做雙胞胎好難。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不行,真的不行,」雙胞胎回答;「做雙胞胎非常難。」

passages.original: “As I can’t be anything important,” said Tootles, “would any of you like to see me do a trick?”
passages.vernacular: 「既然我唔能夠做任何重要嘅嘢,」圖圖講,「你哋有邊個想睇我表演一個把戲嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「既然我不能做任何重要的東西,」圖圖說,「你們有誰想看我表演一個把戲嗎?」

passages.original: “No,” they all replied.
passages.vernacular: 「不,」佢哋全都回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不,」他們全都回答。

passages.original: Then at last he stopped. “I hadn’t really any hope,” he said.
passages.vernacular: 然後佢終於停喇。「我其實冇真嘅抱希望,」佢講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後他終於停了。「我其實沒有真的抱希望,」他說。

passages.original: The hateful telling broke out again.
passages.vernacular: 令人討厭嘅告狀又爆發喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 令人討厭的告狀又爆發了。

passages.original: “Slightly is coughing on the table.”
passages.vernacular: 「輕輕喺桌子上咳嗽。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「輕輕在桌子上咳嗽。」

passages.original: “The twins began with cheese-cakes.”
passages.vernacular: 「雙胞胎先食咗乳酪蛋糕。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「雙胞胎先吃了乳酪蛋糕。」

passages.original: “Curly is taking both butter and honey.”
passages.vernacular: 「卷毛又攞牛油又攞蜂蜜。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「卷毛又拿牛油又拿蜂蜜。」

passages.original: “Nibs is speaking with his mouth full.”
passages.vernacular: 「尼布斯嘴裡有嘢仲講話。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「尼布斯嘴裡有東西還說話。」

passages.original: “I complain of the twins.”
passages.vernacular: 「我投訴雙胞胎。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我投訴雙胞胎。」

passages.original: “I complain of Curly.”
passages.vernacular: 「我投訴卷毛。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我投訴卷毛。」

passages.original: “I complain of Nibs.”
passages.vernacular: 「我投訴尼布斯。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我投訴尼布斯。」

passages.original: “Oh dear, oh dear,” cried Wendy, “I’m sure I sometimes think that spinsters are to be envied.”
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀,哎呀,」溫蒂喊道,「我有時真覺得老姑娘值得羨慕。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀,哎呀,」溫蒂喊道,「我有時真覺得老姑娘值得羨慕。」

passages.original: She told them to clear away, and sat down to her work-basket, a heavy load of stockings and every knee with a hole in it as usual.
passages.vernacular: 佢叫佢哋收拾乾淨,坐下嚟打開佢嘅針線籃,裡面係一大堆襪子,像往常一樣每個膝蓋都有個洞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她叫他們收拾乾淨,坐下來打開她的針線籃,裡面是一大堆襪子,像往常一樣每個膝蓋都有個洞。

passages.original: “Wendy,” remonstrated Michael, “I’m too big for a cradle.”
passages.vernacular: 「溫蒂,」邁克爾抗議,「我對搖籃來講太大喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「溫蒂,」邁克爾抗議,「我對搖籃來說太大了。」

passages.original: “I must have somebody in a cradle,” she said almost tartly, “and you are the littlest. A cradle is such a nice homely thing to have about a house.”
passages.vernacular: 「我必須有個人喺搖籃裡,」佢幾乎係尖刻地講,「而你係最小嘅。搖籃係家裡咁好嘅居家物件。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我必須有個人在搖籃裡,」她幾乎是尖刻地說,「而你是最小的。搖籃是家裡這麼好的居家物件。」

passages.original: While she sewed they played around her; such a group of happy faces and dancing limbs lit up by that romantic fire. It had become a very familiar scene, this, in the home under the ground, but we are looking on it for the last time.
passages.vernacular: 佢縫補時,佢哋圍住佢玩耍;一群快樂嘅臉同舞動嘅肢體被嗰浪漫嘅火光照亮。喺地下家園,呢已經成咗好熟悉嘅景象,但我哋係最後一次睇到佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她縫補時,他們圍著她玩耍;一群快樂的臉和舞動的肢體被那浪漫的火光照亮。在地下家園,這已經成了非常熟悉的景象,但我們是最後一次看到它。

passages.original: There was a step above, and Wendy, you may be sure, was the first to recognize it.
passages.vernacular: 上面有腳步聲,你可以肯定溫蒂係第一個認出佢嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 上面有腳步聲,你可以肯定溫蒂是第一個認出它的。

passages.original: “Children, I hear your father’s step. He likes you to meet him at the door.”
passages.vernacular: 「細路哋,我聽到你哋爸爸嘅腳步聲。佢鍾意你哋喺門口迎接佢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「孩子們,我聽到你們爸爸的腳步聲。他喜歡你們在門口迎接他。」

passages.original: Above, the redskins crouched before Peter.
passages.vernacular: 上面,紅番喺彼得面前蹲伏住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 上面,紅番在彼得面前蹲伏著。

passages.original: “Watch well, braves. I have spoken.”
passages.vernacular: 「好好守衛,勇士哋。我已講話。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好好守衛,勇士們。我已說話。」

passages.original: And then, as so often before, the gay children dragged him from his tree. As so often before, but never again.
passages.vernacular: 然後,像往常一樣,快樂嘅細路哋把佢從樹裡拖出嚟。像往常一樣,但呢個係最後一次。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後,像往常一樣,快樂的孩子們把他從樹裡拖出來。像往常一樣,但這是最後一次。

passages.original: He had brought nuts for the boys as well as the correct time for Wendy.
passages.vernacular: 佢畀男孩哋帶嚟咗堅果,都畀溫蒂帶嚟咗準確嘅時間。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他給男孩們帶來了堅果,也給溫蒂帶來了準確的時間。

passages.original: “Peter, you just spoil them, you know,” Wendy simpered.
passages.vernacular: 「彼得,你真係寵壞佢哋喇,你知道,」溫蒂矯揉地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「彼得,你真是寵壞他們了,你知道,」溫蒂矯揉地說。

passages.original: “Ah, old lady,” said Peter, hanging up his gun.
passages.vernacular: 「啊,老太婆,」彼得講,掛起佢嘅槍。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「啊,老太婆,」彼得說,掛起他的槍。

passages.original: “It was me told him mothers are called old lady,” Michael whispered to Curly.
passages.vernacular: 「係我告訴佢媽媽被叫做老太婆嘅,」邁克爾對卷毛低聲講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是我告訴他媽媽被叫做老太婆的,」邁克爾對卷毛低聲說。

passages.original: “I complain of Michael,” said Curly instantly.
passages.vernacular: 「我投訴邁克爾,」卷毛即刻講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我投訴邁克爾,」卷毛立刻說。

passages.original: The first twin came to Peter. “Father, we want to dance.”
passages.vernacular: 第一個雙胞胎走向彼得。「爸爸,我哋想跳舞。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 第一個雙胞胎走向彼得。「爸爸,我們想跳舞。」

passages.original: “Dance away, my little man,” said Peter, who was in high good humour.
passages.vernacular: 「跳吧,我嘅小傢伙,」彼得講,佢心情特別好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「跳吧,我的小傢伙,」彼得說,他心情特別好。

passages.original: “But we want you to dance.”
passages.vernacular: 「但我哋想要你跳舞。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但我們想要你跳舞。」

passages.original: Peter was really the best dancer among them, but he pretended to be scandalised.
passages.vernacular: 彼得其實係佢哋中跳得最好嘅,但佢假裝驚駭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 彼得其實是他們中跳得最好的,但他假裝驚駭。

passages.original: “Me! My old bones would rattle!”
passages.vernacular: 「我!我嘅老骨頭會咔咔響!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我!我的老骨頭會咔咔響!」

passages.original: “And mummy too.”
passages.vernacular: 「仲有媽咪都一起。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「還有媽咪也一起。」

passages.original: “What,” cried Wendy, “the mother of such an armful, dance!”
passages.vernacular: 「乜嘢,」溫蒂喊道,「咁多細路嘅母親,跳舞!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「什麼,」溫蒂喊道,「這麼多孩子的母親,跳舞!」

passages.original: “But on a Saturday night,” Slightly insinuated.
passages.vernacular: 「但係星期六晚上,」輕輕暗示。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但是星期六晚上,」輕輕暗示。

passages.original: It was not really Saturday night, at least it may have been, for they had long lost count of the days; but always if they wanted to do anything special they said this was Saturday night, and then they did it.
passages.vernacular: 呢其實唔係星期六晚上,至少可能係,因為佢哋早已失去咗日子嘅計算;但佢哋想做乜嘢特別嘅事時總是講呢個係星期六晚上,然後就做喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這其實不是星期六晚上,至少可能是,因為他們早已失去了日子的計算;但他們想做什麼特別的事時總是說這是星期六晚上,然後就做了。

passages.original: “Of course it is Saturday night, Peter,” Wendy said, relenting.
passages.vernacular: 「當然係星期六晚上,彼得,」溫蒂軟化地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「當然是星期六晚上,彼得,」溫蒂軟化地說。

passages.original: “People of our figure, Wendy!”
passages.vernacular: 「像我哋呢種身材嘅人,溫蒂!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「像我們這種身材的人,溫蒂!」

passages.original: “But it is only among our own progeny.”
passages.vernacular: 「但呢只係喺我哋自己嘅後代中間。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但這只是在我們自己的後代中間。」

passages.original: “True, true.”
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,係嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,是的。」

passages.original: So they were told they could dance, but they must put on their nighties first.
passages.vernacular: 於是佢哋被告知可以跳舞,但必須先穿上瞓衣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是他們被告知可以跳舞,但必須先穿上睡衣。

passages.original: “Ah, old lady,” Peter said aside to Wendy, warming himself by the fire and looking down at her as she sat turning a heel, “there is nothing more pleasant of an evening for you and me when the day’s toil is over than to rest by the fire with the little ones near by.”
passages.vernacular: 「啊,老太婆,」彼得向溫蒂旁白講,喺火邊暖住身體,低頭睇住佢坐住縫襪跟,「對你我來講,冇比一天嘅辛勞結束後喺火邊休息、細路哋喺旁邊更愉快嘅晚間事喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「啊,老太婆,」彼得向溫蒂旁白說,在火邊暖著身體,低頭看著她坐著縫襪跟,「對你我來說,沒有比一天的辛勞結束後在火邊休息、孩子們在旁邊更愉快的晚間事了。」

passages.original: “It is sweet, Peter, isn’t it?” Wendy said, frightfully gratified. “Peter, I think Curly has your nose.”
passages.vernacular: 「呢個好甜蜜,彼得,唔係嗎?」溫蒂講,極為滿足。「彼得,我想卷毛有你嘅鼻子。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這很甜蜜,彼得,不是嗎?」溫蒂說,極為滿足。「彼得,我想卷毛有你的鼻子。」

passages.original: “Michael takes after you.”
passages.vernacular: 「邁克爾像你。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「邁克爾像你。」

passages.original: She went to him and put her hand on his shoulder.
passages.vernacular: 佢走到佢嗰度,把手放喺佢肩上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她走到他那裡,把手放在他肩上。

passages.original: “Dear Peter,” she said, “with such a large family, of course, I have now passed my best, but you don’t want to change me, do you?”
passages.vernacular: 「親愛嘅彼得,」佢講,「有咁大嘅家庭,當然,我而家已經過咗最好嘅年華,但你唔想換掉我吧?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「親愛的彼得,」她說,「有這麼大的家庭,當然,我現在已經過了最好的年華,但你不想換掉我吧?」

passages.original: “No, Wendy.”
passages.vernacular: 「不,溫蒂。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不,溫蒂。」

passages.original: Certainly he did not want a change, but he looked at her uncomfortably, blinking, you know, like one not sure whether he was awake or asleep.
passages.vernacular: 佢當然唔想換,但佢不舒服地睇住佢,眨住眼,你知道,像一個不確定自己係醒住定係瞓住嘅人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他當然不想換,但他不舒服地看著她,眨著眼,你知道,像一個不確定自己是醒著還是睡著的人。

passages.original: “Peter, what is it?”
passages.vernacular: 「彼得,點喇?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「彼得,怎麼了?」

passages.original: “I was just thinking,” he said, a little scared. “It is only make-believe, isn’t it, that I am their father?”
passages.vernacular: 「我只係喺想,」佢有點害怕地講。「我係佢哋嘅爸爸只係假裝,對吧?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我只是在想,」他有點害怕地說。「我是他們的爸爸只是假裝,對吧?」

passages.original: “Oh yes,” Wendy said primly.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,係嘅,」溫蒂拘謹地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,是的,」溫蒂拘謹地說。

passages.original: “You see,” he continued apologetically, “it would make me seem so old to be their real father.”
passages.vernacular: 「你睇,」佢抱歉地繼續講,「做佢哋真正嘅爸爸會讓我顯得咁老。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你看,」他抱歉地繼續說,「做他們真正的爸爸會讓我顯得那麼老。」

passages.original: “But they are ours, Peter, yours and mine.”
passages.vernacular: 「但佢哋係我哋嘅,彼得,你嘅同我嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但他們是我們的,彼得,你的和我的。」

passages.original: “But not really, Wendy?” he asked anxiously.
passages.vernacular: 「但唔係真嘅吧,溫蒂?」佢焦急地問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但不是真的吧,溫蒂?」他焦急地問。

passages.original: “Not if you don’t wish it,” she replied; and she distinctly heard his sigh of relief. “Peter,” she asked, trying to speak firmly, “what are your exact feelings to me?”
passages.vernacular: 「如果你不希望嘅話,唔係,」佢回答;佢清楚地聽到佢鬆咗一口氣嘅歎息。「彼得,」佢問,努力堅定地講,「你對我的確切感覺係乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「如果你不希望的話,不是,」她回答;她清楚地聽到他鬆了一口氣的歎息。「彼得,」她問,努力堅定地說,「你對我的確切感覺是什麼?」

passages.original: “Those of a devoted son, Wendy.”
passages.vernacular: 「一個忠誠嘅兒子嘅感覺,溫蒂。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「一個忠誠的兒子的感覺,溫蒂。」

passages.original: “I thought so,” she said, and went and sat by herself at the extreme end of the room.
passages.vernacular: 「我就知道,」佢講,走去獨自坐喺房間最遠嘅一端。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我就知道,」她說,走去獨自坐在房間最遠的一端。

passages.original: “You are so queer,” he said, frankly puzzled, “and Tiger Lily is just the same. There is something she wants to be to me, but she says it is not my mother.”
passages.vernacular: 「你真奇怪,」佢坦率地困惑講,「虎百合都係一樣。佢想成為我嘅某種乜嘢,但佢講唔係我嘅媽媽。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你真奇怪,」他坦率地困惑說,「虎百合也是一樣。她想成為我的某種什麼,但她說不是我的媽媽。」

passages.original: “No, indeed, it is not,” Wendy replied with frightful emphasis. Now we know why she was prejudiced against the redskins.
passages.vernacular: 「不,確實唔係,」溫蒂帶住可怕嘅強調回答。而家我哋知道佢點解對紅番有偏見喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不,確實不是,」溫蒂帶著可怕的強調回答。現在我們知道她為什麼對紅番有偏見了。

passages.original: “Then what is it?”
passages.vernacular: 「嗰個係乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那是什麼?」

passages.original: “It isn’t for a lady to tell.”
passages.vernacular: 「唔係一位女士該講嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不是一位女士該說的。」

passages.original: “Oh, very well,” Peter said, a little nettled. “Perhaps Tinker Bell will tell me.”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,好吧,」彼得有點惱怒地講。「或者叮噹會告訴我。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,好吧,」彼得有點惱怒地說。「也許叮噹會告訴我。」

passages.original: “Oh yes, Tinker Bell will tell you,” Wendy retorted scornfully. “She is an abandoned little creature.”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,係嘅,叮噹會告訴你,」溫蒂輕蔑地反駁。「佢係個放蕩嘅小嘢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,是的,叮噹會告訴你,」溫蒂輕蔑地反駁。「她是個放蕩的小東西。」

passages.original: Here Tink, who was in her bedroom, eavesdropping, squeaked out something impudent.
passages.vernacular: 呢陣喺佢臥室裡偷聽嘅叮,尖聲講咗些無禮嘅話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這時在她臥室裡偷聽的叮,尖聲說了些無禮的話。

passages.original: “She says she glories in being abandoned,” Peter interpreted.
passages.vernacular: 「佢講佢以放蕩為榮,」彼得翻譯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她說她以放蕩為榮,」彼得翻譯。

passages.original: He had a sudden idea. “Perhaps Tink wants to be my mother?”
passages.vernacular: 佢突然有咗個主意。「或者叮想做我嘅媽媽?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他突然有了個主意。「也許叮想做我的媽媽?」

passages.original: “You silly ass!” cried Tinker Bell in a passion.
passages.vernacular: 「你呢蠢驢!」叮噹憤怒地喊道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你這蠢驢!」叮噹憤怒地喊道。

passages.original: She had said it so often that Wendy needed no translation.
passages.vernacular: 佢講咗咁多次,溫蒂不需要翻譯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她說了那麼多次,溫蒂不需要翻譯。

passages.original: “I almost agree with her,” Wendy snapped. Fancy Wendy snapping! But she had been much tried, and she little knew what was to happen before the night was out. If she had known she would not have snapped.
passages.vernacular: 「我幾乎同意佢,」溫蒂厲聲講。想想溫蒂竟然厲聲講話!但佢受咗好多折磨,佢好少知道呢夜結束前會發生乜嘢。如果佢知道,佢就唔會厲聲講喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我幾乎同意她,」溫蒂厲聲說。想想溫蒂竟然厲聲說話!但她受了很多折磨,她很少知道這夜結束前會發生什麼。如果她知道,她就不會厲聲說了。

passages.original: None of them knew. Perhaps it was best not to know. Their ignorance gave them one more glad hour; and as it was to be their last hour on the island, let us rejoice that there were sixty glad minutes in it. They sang and danced in their night-gowns. Such a deliciously creepy song it was, in which they pretended to be frightened at their own shadows, little witting that so soon shadows would close in upon them, from whom they would shrink in real fear. So uproariously gay was the dance, and how they buffeted each other on the bed and out of it! It was a pillow fight rather than a dance, and when it was finished, the pillows insisted on one bout more, like partners who know that they may never meet again. The stories they told, before it was time for Wendy’s good-night story! Even Slightly tried to tell a story that night, but the beginning was so fearfully dull that it appalled not only the others but himself, and he said gloomily:
passages.vernacular: 佢哋邊個都唔知道。或者最好唔知道。佢哋嘅無知畀咗佢哋又一個快樂嘅小時;因為呢將係佢哋喺島上嘅最後一個小時,讓我哋高興其中有六十個快樂嘅分鐘。佢哋穿住瞓袍唱歌跳舞。嗰個係一首美妙地令人毛骨悚然嘅歌,佢哋喺其中假裝害怕自己嘅影子,幾乎唔知道不久影子將向佢哋逼近,佢哋會因真正嘅恐懼而退縮。舞蹈係咁喧鬧快樂,佢哋喺床上床下互相猛撞!嗰更像係枕頭大戰而唔係舞蹈,結束時,枕頭哋堅持再嚟一回合,像知道或者再唔會相見嘅舞伴。喺輪到溫蒂嘅晚安故事之前,佢哋講嘅故事!連輕輕嗰晚都試住講一個故事,但開頭係咁可怕地沉悶,不僅嚇到咗其他人,都嚇到咗佢自己,佢沮喪地講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們誰也不知道。也許最好不知道。他們的無知給了他們又一個快樂的小時;因為這將是他們在島上的最後一個小時,讓我們高興其中有六十個快樂的分鐘。他們穿著睡袍唱歌跳舞。那是一首美妙地令人毛骨悚然的歌,他們在其中假裝害怕自己的影子,幾乎不知道不久影子將向他們逼近,他們會因真正的恐懼而退縮。舞蹈是那麼喧鬧快樂,他們在床上床下互相猛撞!那更像是枕頭大戰而不是舞蹈,結束時,枕頭們堅持再來一回合,像知道也許再不會相見的舞伴。在輪到溫蒂的晚安故事之前,他們講的故事!連輕輕那晚也試著講一個故事,但開頭是那麼可怕地沉悶,不僅嚇到了其他人,也嚇到了他自己,他沮喪地說:

passages.original: “Yes, it is a dull beginning. I say, let us pretend that it is the end.”
passages.vernacular: 「對,呢個係個沉悶嘅開頭。我講,我哋假裝呢個係結尾吧。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「對,這是個沉悶的開頭。我說,我們假裝這是結尾吧。」

passages.original: And then at last they all got into bed for Wendy’s story, the story they loved best, the story Peter hated. Usually when she began to tell this story he left the room or put his hands over his ears; and possibly if he had done either of those things this time they might all still be on the island. But to-night he remained on his stool; and we shall see what happened.
passages.vernacular: 然後佢哋終於都上咗床,聽溫蒂嘅故事,嗰個係佢哋最愛嘅故事,係彼得討厭嘅故事。通常佢開始講呢個故事時,佢會離開房間或用手捂住耳朵;或者如果呢次佢做咗其中任何一件事,佢哋可能而家仍然喺島上。但今晚佢留喺佢嘅凳子上;我哋將睇到發生咗乜嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後他們終於都上了床,聽溫蒂的故事,那是他們最愛的故事,是彼得討厭的故事。通常她開始講這個故事時,他會離開房間或用手捂住耳朵;也許如果這次他做了其中任何一件事,他們可能現在仍然在島上。但今晚他留在他的凳子上;我們將看到發生了什麼。

chapters.title: Chapter XI: Wendy's Story 第十一章:溫蒂的故事

passages.original: “Listen, then,” said Wendy, settling down to her story, with Michael at her feet and seven boys in the bed. “There was once a gentleman—”
passages.vernacular: 「嗰就聽住,」溫蒂講,安頓下嚟講佢嘅故事,邁克爾喺佢腳邊,七個男孩喺床上。「從前有一位先生——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那就聽著,」溫蒂說,安頓下來講她的故事,邁克爾在她腳邊,七個男孩在床上。「從前有一位先生——」

passages.original: “I had rather he had been a lady,” Curly said.
passages.vernacular: 「我寧願佢係一位女士,」卷毛講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我寧願他是一位女士,」卷毛說。

passages.original: “I wish he had been a white rat,” said Nibs.
passages.vernacular: 「我希望佢係一隻白老鼠,」尼布斯講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我希望他是一隻白老鼠,」尼布斯說。

passages.original: “Quiet,” their mother admonished them. “There was a lady also, and—”
passages.vernacular: 「安靜,」佢哋嘅母親告誡佢哋。「仲有一位女士,而且——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「安靜,」他們的母親告誡他們。「還有一位女士,而且——」

passages.original: “Oh, mummy,” cried the first twin, “you mean that there is a lady also, don’t you? She is not dead, is she?”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,媽咪,」第一個雙胞胎喊道,「你係講仲有一位女士,對不對?佢冇死吧?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,媽咪,」第一個雙胞胎喊道,「你是說還有一位女士,對不對?她沒死吧?」

passages.original: “Oh, no.”
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,沒有。」

passages.original: “I am awfully glad she isn’t dead,” said Tootles. “Are you glad, John?”
passages.vernacular: 「我真高興佢冇死,」圖圖講。「你高興嗎,約翰?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我真高興她沒死,」圖圖說。「你高興嗎,約翰?」

passages.original: “Of course I am.”
passages.vernacular: 「當然高興。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「當然高興。」

passages.original: “Are you glad, Nibs?”
passages.vernacular: 「你高興嗎,尼布斯?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你高興嗎,尼布斯?」

passages.original: “Rather.”
passages.vernacular: 「相當高興。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「相當高興。」

passages.original: “Are you glad, Twins?”
passages.vernacular: 「你哋高興嗎,雙胞胎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你們高興嗎,雙胞胎?」

passages.original: “We are glad.”
passages.vernacular: 「我哋高興。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們高興。」

passages.original: “Oh dear,” sighed Wendy.
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀,」溫蒂歎息。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀,」溫蒂歎息。

passages.original: “Little less noise there,” Peter called out, determined that she should have fair play, however beastly a story it might be in his opinion.
passages.vernacular: 「嗰邊小聲點,」彼得喊道,下定決心要讓佢公平發言,不管喺佢睇來嗰個係幾咁討厭嘅故事。
