passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那邊小聲點,」彼得喊道,下定決心要讓她公平發言,不管在他看來那是多麼討厭的故事。

passages.original: “The gentleman’s name,” Wendy continued, “was Mr. Darling, and her name was Mrs. Darling.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗰位先生嘅名字,」溫蒂繼續講,「係達玲先生,佢嘅名字係達玲太太。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那位先生的名字,」溫蒂繼續說,「是達玲先生,她的名字是達玲太太。」

passages.original: “I knew them,” John said, to annoy the others.
passages.vernacular: 「我認識佢哋,」約翰講,故意惹其他人生氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我認識他們,」約翰說,故意惹其他人生氣。

passages.original: “I think I knew them,” said Michael rather doubtfully.
passages.vernacular: 「我想我認識佢哋,」邁克爾相當猶疑地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想我認識他們,」邁克爾相當猶疑地說。

passages.original: “They were married, you know,” explained Wendy, “and what do you think they had?”
passages.vernacular: 「佢哋結婚喇,你知道,」溫蒂解釋,「你哋猜佢哋有乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他們結婚了,你知道,」溫蒂解釋,「你們猜他們有什麼?」

passages.original: “White rats,” cried Nibs, inspired.
passages.vernacular: 「白老鼠,」尼布斯靈機一動喊道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「白老鼠,」尼布斯靈機一動喊道。

passages.original: “No.”
passages.vernacular: 「唔係。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不是。」

passages.original: “It’s awfully puzzling,” said Tootles, who knew the story by heart.
passages.vernacular: 「真令人困惑,」圖圖講,佢背得出呢個故事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「真令人困惑,」圖圖說,他背得出這個故事。

passages.original: “Quiet, Tootles. They had three descendants.”
passages.vernacular: 「安靜,圖圖。佢哋有三個後代。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「安靜,圖圖。他們有三個後代。」

passages.original: “What is descendants?”
passages.vernacular: 「後代係乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「後代是什麼?」

passages.original: “Well, you are one, Twin.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,你就係一個,雙胞胎。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,你就是一個,雙胞胎。」

passages.original: “Did you hear that, John? I am a descendant.”
passages.vernacular: 「你聽到咗嗎,約翰?我係個後代。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你聽到了嗎,約翰?我是個後代。」

passages.original: “Descendants are only children,” said John.
passages.vernacular: 「後代只係細路,」約翰講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「後代只是孩子,」約翰說。

passages.original: “Oh dear, oh dear,” sighed Wendy. “Now these three children had a faithful nurse called Nana; but Mr. Darling was angry with her and chained her up in the yard, and so all the children flew away.”
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀,哎呀,」溫蒂歎息。「而家呢三個細路有一個忠實嘅保姆叫娜娜;但達玲先生生佢嘅氣,把佢拴喺院子裡,於是所有嘅細路都飛走喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀,哎呀,」溫蒂歎息。「現在這三個孩子有一個忠實的保姆叫娜娜;但達玲先生生她的氣,把她拴在院子裡,於是所有的孩子都飛走了。」

passages.original: “It’s an awfully good story,” said Nibs.
passages.vernacular: 「呢個係個好好嘅故事,」尼布斯講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這是個非常好的故事,」尼布斯說。

passages.original: “They flew away,” Wendy continued, “to the Neverland, where the lost children are.”
passages.vernacular: 「佢哋飛走喇,」溫蒂繼續講,「飛到永無島,迷失嘅細路哋喺嗰度。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他們飛走了,」溫蒂繼續說,「飛到永無島,迷失的孩子們在那裡。」

passages.original: “I just thought they did,” Curly broke in excitedly. “I don’t know how it is, but I just thought they did!”
passages.vernacular: 「我剛好想到佢哋會,」卷毛興奮地插嘴。「我唔知道點回事,但我剛好想到佢哋會!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我剛好想到他們會,」卷毛興奮地插嘴。「我不知道怎麼回事,但我剛好想到他們會!」

passages.original: “O Wendy,” cried Tootles, “was one of the lost children called Tootles?”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,溫蒂,」圖圖喊道,「其中一個迷失嘅細路叫圖圖嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,溫蒂,」圖圖喊道,「其中一個迷失的孩子叫圖圖嗎?」

passages.original: “Yes, he was.”
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,佢叫圖圖。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,他叫圖圖。」

passages.original: “I am in a story. Hurrah, I am in a story, Nibs.”
passages.vernacular: 「我喺一個故事裡。萬歲,我喺一個故事裡,尼布斯。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我在一個故事裡。萬歲,我在一個故事裡,尼布斯。」

passages.original: “Hush. Now I want you to consider the feelings of the unhappy parents with all their children flown away.”
passages.vernacular: 「噓。而家我要你哋考慮嗰啲不快樂嘅父母嘅感受,佢哋所有嘅細路都飛走喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「噓。現在我要你們考慮那些不快樂的父母的感受,他們所有的孩子都飛走了。」

passages.original: “Oo!” they all moaned, though they were not really considering the feelings of the unhappy parents one jot.
passages.vernacular: 「哦!」佢哋都呻吟,雖然佢哋根本冇啲考慮不快樂嘅父母嘅感受。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦!」他們都呻吟,雖然他們根本沒有一點考慮不快樂的父母的感受。

passages.original: “Think of the empty beds!”
passages.vernacular: 「想想嗰啲空床!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「想想那些空床!」

passages.original: “Oo!”
“It’s awfully sad,” the first twin said cheerfully.
passages.vernacular: 「真係太悲傷喇,」第一個雙胞胎愉快地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「真是太悲傷了,」第一個雙胞胎愉快地說。

passages.original: “I don’t see how it can have a happy ending,” said the second twin. “Do you, Nibs?”
passages.vernacular: 「我睇不出佢點能有個快樂嘅結局,」第二個雙胞胎講。「你睇得出嗎,尼布斯?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我看不出它怎麼能有個快樂的結局,」第二個雙胞胎說。「你看得出嗎,尼布斯?」

passages.original: “I’m frightfully anxious.”
passages.vernacular: 「我極其焦急。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我極其焦急。」

passages.original: “If you knew how great is a mother’s love,” Wendy told them triumphantly, “you would have no fear.” She had now come to the part that Peter hated.
passages.vernacular: 「如果你哋知道媽媽嘅愛係幾咁偉大,」溫蒂得意地告訴佢哋,「你哋就唔會害怕喇。」佢而家講到咗彼得討厭嘅嗰一段。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「如果你們知道媽媽的愛是多麼偉大,」溫蒂得意地告訴他們,「你們就不會害怕了。」她現在講到了彼得討厭的那一段。

passages.original: “I do like a mother’s love,” said Tootles, hitting Nibs with a pillow. “Do you like a mother’s love, Nibs?”
passages.vernacular: 「我真嘅鍾意媽媽嘅愛,」圖圖講,用枕頭打尼布斯。「你鍾意媽媽嘅愛嗎,尼布斯?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我真的喜歡媽媽的愛,」圖圖說,用枕頭打尼布斯。「你喜歡媽媽的愛嗎,尼布斯?」

passages.original: “I do just,” said Nibs, hitting back.
passages.vernacular: 「我就係鍾意,」尼布斯講,還擊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我就是喜歡,」尼布斯說,還擊。

passages.original: “You see,” Wendy said complacently, “our heroine knew that the mother would always leave the window open for her children to fly back by; so they stayed away for years and had a lovely time.”
passages.vernacular: 「你哋睇,」溫蒂自滿地講,「我哋嘅女主角知道媽媽總會為佢嘅細路哋留住窗戶,讓佢哋飛回嚟;所以佢哋離開咗好幾年,過得好愉快。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你們看,」溫蒂自滿地說,「我們的女主角知道媽媽總會為她的孩子們留著窗戶,讓他們飛回來;所以他們離開了好幾年,過得很愉快。」

passages.original: “Did they ever go back?”
passages.vernacular: 「佢哋有回去過嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他們有回去過嗎?」

passages.original: “Let us now,” said Wendy, bracing herself up for her finest effort, “take a peep into the future;” and they all gave themselves the twist that makes peeps into the future easier. “Years have rolled by, and who is this elegant lady of uncertain age alighting at London Station?”
passages.vernacular: 「而家讓我哋,」溫蒂講,鼓足勁頭作佢最好嘅表現,「偷睇一眼未來;」佢哋都扭轉身體,嗰樣會讓偷睇未來更容易。「歲月流逝,呢位年齡不明嘅優雅女士係邊個,喺倫敦車站下車?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「現在讓我們,」溫蒂說,鼓足勁頭作她最好的表現,「偷看一眼未來;」他們都扭轉身體,那樣會讓偷看未來更容易。「歲月流逝,這位年齡不明的優雅女士是誰,在倫敦車站下車?」

passages.original: “O Wendy, who is she?” cried Nibs, every bit as excited as if he didn’t know.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,溫蒂,佢係邊個?」尼布斯喊道,激動得好像佢唔知道似嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,溫蒂,她是誰?」尼布斯喊道,激動得好像他不知道似的。

passages.original: “Can it be—yes—no—it is—the fair Wendy!”
passages.vernacular: 「難道係——係嘅——不——係——美麗嘅溫蒂!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「難道是——是的——不——是——美麗的溫蒂!」

passages.original: “Oh!”
“And who are the two noble portly figures accompanying her, now grown to man’s estate? Can they be John and Michael? They are!”
passages.vernacular: 「陪住佢嘅嗰兩位高貴發福嘅人物係邊個,而家已長成男人?難道係約翰同邁克爾?正是!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「陪著她的那兩位高貴發福的人物是誰,現在已長成男人?難道是約翰和邁克爾?正是!」

passages.original: “Oh!”

“‘See, dear brothers,’ says Wendy pointing upwards, ‘there is the window still standing open. Ah, now we are rewarded for our sublime faith in a mother’s love.’ So up they flew to their mummy and daddy, and pen cannot describe the happy scene, over which we draw a veil.”
passages.vernacular: 「『睇,親愛嘅兄弟哋,』溫蒂指住上方講,『嗰扇窗子仍然開住。啊,而家我哋為我哋對媽媽嘅愛嘅崇高信念得到咗獎賞。』於是佢哋飛向佢哋嘅媽咪同爹地,筆墨難以描述嗰幸福嘅場面,我哋喺上面拉上一層面紗。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『看,親愛的兄弟們,』溫蒂指著上方說,『那扇窗子仍然開著。啊,現在我們為我們對媽媽的愛的崇高信念得到了獎賞。』於是他們飛向他們的媽咪和爹地,筆墨難以描述那幸福的場面,我們在上面拉上一層面紗。」

passages.original: That was the story, and they were as pleased with it as the fair narrator herself. Everything just as it should be, you see. Off we skip like the most heartless things in the world, which is what children are, but so attractive; and we have an entirely selfish time, and then when we have need of special attention we nobly return for it, confident that we shall be rewarded instead of smacked.
passages.vernacular: 呢個就係故事,佢哋同呢位美麗嘅敘述者自己一樣鍾意佢。你睇,一切正如應該嘅嗰樣。我哋像世界上最無情嘅嘢一樣跳住離開,細路哋就係嗰樣,但咁有魅力;我哋過住完全自私嘅時光,然後當我哋需要特別關注時,我哋高尚地回去要佢,確信我哋會得到獎賞而唔係挨打。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這就是故事,他們同這位美麗的敘述者自己一樣喜歡它。你看,一切正如應該的那樣。我們像世界上最無情的東西一樣跳著離開,孩子們就是那樣,但那麼有魅力;我們過著完全自私的時光,然後當我們需要特別關注時,我們高尚地回去要它,確信我們會得到獎賞而不是挨打。

passages.original: So great indeed was their faith in a mother’s love that they felt they could afford to be callous for a bit longer.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋對媽媽嘅愛嘅信念確實咁大,佢哋覺得自己仲可以再冷酷無情一會兒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們對媽媽的愛的信念確實那麼大,他們覺得自己還可以再冷酷無情一會兒。

passages.original: But there was one there who knew better, and when Wendy finished he uttered a hollow groan.
passages.vernacular: 但嗰度有一個人懂得更多,溫蒂講完時,佢發出一聲空洞嘅呻吟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但那裡有一個人懂得更多,溫蒂講完時,他發出一聲空洞的呻吟。

passages.original: “What is it, Peter?” she cried, running to him, thinking he was ill. She felt him solicitously, lower down than his chest. “Where is it, Peter?”
passages.vernacular: 「點喇,彼得?」佢喊道,跑向佢,以為佢病喇。佢關切地摸佢,比佢嘅胸口更低嘅地方。「喺邊度,彼得?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「怎麼了,彼得?」她喊道,跑向他,以為他病了。她關切地摸他,比他的胸口更低的地方。「在哪裡,彼得?」

passages.original: “It isn’t that kind of pain,” Peter replied darkly.
passages.vernacular: 「唔係嗰種痛,」彼得陰沉地回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不是那種痛,」彼得陰沉地回答。

passages.original: “Then what kind is it?”
passages.vernacular: 「嗰個係邊種?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那是哪種?」

passages.original: “Wendy, you are wrong about mothers.”
passages.vernacular: 「溫蒂,你對母親嘅睇法錯喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「溫蒂,你對母親的看法錯了。」

passages.original: They all gathered round him in affright, so alarming was his agitation; and with a fine candour he told them what he had hitherto concealed.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋都驚恐地圍住佢,佢嘅激動係咁令人驚慌;佢以一種良好嘅坦率告訴佢哋佢迄今隱瞞嘅事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們都驚恐地圍著他,他的激動是那麼令人驚慌;他以一種良好的坦率告訴他們他迄今隱瞞的事。

passages.original: “Long ago,” he said, “I thought like you that my mother would always keep the window open for me, so I stayed away for moons and moons and moons, and then flew back; but the window was barred, for mother had forgotten all about me, and there was another little boy sleeping in my bed.”
passages.vernacular: 「好久以前,」佢講,「我像你一樣以為我媽媽會一直為我留住窗子,所以我離開咗好多好多好多個月亮,然後飛咗回去;但窗子被閂上喇,因為媽媽已經把我完全忘喇,另一個小男孩瞓喺我嘅床上。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「很久以前,」他說,「我像你一樣以為我媽媽會一直為我留著窗子,所以我離開了好多好多好多個月亮,然後飛了回去;但窗子被閂上了,因為媽媽已經把我完全忘了,另一個小男孩睡在我的床上。」

passages.original: I am not sure that this was true, but Peter thought it was true; and it scared them.
passages.vernacular: 我不確定呢個係唔係真嘅,但彼得認為係真嘅;呢嚇到咗佢哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不確定這是不是真的,但彼得認為是真的;這嚇到了他們。

passages.original: “Are you sure mothers are like that?”
passages.vernacular: 「你確定母親係嗰樣嘅嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你確定母親是那樣的嗎?」

passages.original: “Yes.”
So this was the truth about mothers. The toads!
passages.vernacular: 原來呢個就係關於母親嘅真相。癩蛤蟆!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 原來這就是關於母親的真相。癩蛤蟆!

passages.original: Still it is best to be careful; and no one knows so quickly as a child when he should give in. “Wendy, let us go home,” cried John and Michael together.
passages.vernacular: 不過小心為好;冇人比細路更快知道乜嘢時候應該讓步。「溫蒂,我哋回家吧,」約翰同邁克爾一起喊道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過小心為好;沒有人比孩子更快知道什麼時候應該讓步。「溫蒂,我們回家吧,」約翰和邁克爾一起喊道。

passages.original: “Yes,” she said, clutching them.
passages.vernacular: 「好,」佢講,緊緊抱住佢哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好,」她說,緊緊抱住他們。

passages.original: “Not to-night?” asked the lost boys bewildered. They knew in what they called their hearts that one can get on quite well without a mother, and that it is only the mothers who think you can’t.
passages.vernacular: 「唔係今晚吧?」迷失嘅男孩哋困惑地問。佢哋喺佢哋稱為心嘅地方知道,冇母親都可以過得好好,只有母親哋才認為你唔能夠。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不是今晚吧?」迷失的男孩們困惑地問。他們在他們稱為心的地方知道,沒有母親也可以過得很好,只有母親們才認為你不能。

passages.original: “At once,” Wendy replied resolutely, for the horrible thought had come to her: “Perhaps mother is in half mourning by this time.”
passages.vernacular: 「即刻,」溫蒂堅決地回答,因為可怕嘅念頭嚟到佢腦中:「或者媽媽呢陣已經喺半喪服期喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「馬上,」溫蒂堅決地回答,因為可怕的念頭來到她腦中:「也許媽媽這時已經在半喪服期了。」

passages.original: This dread made her forgetful of what must be Peter’s feelings, and she said to him rather sharply, “Peter, will you make the necessary arrangements?”
passages.vernacular: 呢個恐懼使佢忘咗彼得一定有嘅感受,佢相當尖銳地對佢講:「彼得,你能做必要嘅安排嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這個恐懼使她忘了彼得一定有的感受,她相當尖銳地對他說:「彼得,你能做必要的安排嗎?」

passages.original: “If you wish it,” he replied, as coolly as if she had asked him to pass the nuts.
passages.vernacular: 「如果你希望,」佢回答,冷靜得好像佢只係請佢遞堅果。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「如果你希望,」他回答,冷靜得好像她只是請他遞堅果。

passages.original: Not so much as a sorry-to-lose-you between them! If she did not mind the parting, he was going to show her, was Peter, that neither did he.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋之間連一句「捨唔得你」都冇!如果佢不介意分離,彼得要向佢顯示,佢都不介意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們之間連一句「捨不得你」都沒有!如果她不介意分離,彼得要向她顯示,他也不介意。

passages.original: But of course he cared very much; and he was so full of wrath against grown-ups, who, as usual, were spoiling everything, that as soon as he got inside his tree he breathed intentionally quick short breaths at the rate of about five to a second. He did this because there is a saying in the Neverland that, every time you breathe, a grown-up dies; and Peter was killing them off vindictively as fast as possible.
passages.vernacular: 但當然佢好在乎;佢對大人哋咁憤怒,佢哋像往常一樣破壞一切,以致佢一進入佢嘅樹裡,就故意以大約每秒五次嘅速度急促地短促呼吸。佢咁樣做係因為永無島有一句俗話,你每呼吸一次,就有一個大人死去;彼得喺報復性地盡快殺死佢哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但當然他非常在乎;他對大人們那麼憤怒,他們像往常一樣破壞一切,以致他一進入他的樹裡,就故意以大約每秒五次的速度急促地短促呼吸。他這樣做是因為永無島有一句俗話,你每呼吸一次,就有一個大人死去;彼得在報復性地盡快殺死他們。

passages.original: Then having given the necessary instructions to the redskins he returned to the home, where an unworthy scene had been enacted in his absence. Panic-stricken at the thought of losing Wendy the lost boys had advanced upon her threateningly.
passages.vernacular: 然後對紅番下達咗必要嘅指示,佢回到家裡,喺佢不喺嘅時候,上演咗一幕不光彩嘅場面。迷失嘅男孩哋想到失去溫蒂就驚慌失措,威脅地向佢逼近。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後對紅番下達了必要的指示,他回到家裡,在他不在的時候,上演了一幕不光彩的場面。迷失的男孩們想到失去溫蒂就驚慌失措,威脅地向她逼近。

passages.original: “It will be worse than before she came,” they cried.
passages.vernacular: 「嗰會比佢嚟之前更糟,」佢哋喊道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那會比她來之前更糟,」他們喊道。

passages.original: “We shan’t let her go.”
passages.vernacular: 「我哋不讓佢走。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們不讓她走。」

passages.original: “Let’s keep her prisoner.”
passages.vernacular: 「把佢關起嚟當囚犯。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「把她關起來當囚犯。」

passages.original: “Ay, chain her up.”
passages.vernacular: 「對,把佢鎖起嚟。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「對,把她鎖起來。」

passages.original: In her extremity an instinct told her to which of them to turn.
passages.vernacular: 喺佢嘅窘境中,本能告訴佢該轉向佢哋邊一個。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在她的窘境中,本能告訴她該轉向他們哪一個。

passages.original: “Tootles,” she cried, “I appeal to you.”
passages.vernacular: 「圖圖,」佢喊道,「我向你求助。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「圖圖,」她喊道,「我向你求助。」

passages.original: Was it not strange? She appealed to Tootles, quite the silliest one.
passages.vernacular: 呢唔係好奇怪嗎?佢向圖圖求助,係最傻嘅嗰個。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這不是很奇怪嗎?她向圖圖求助,是最傻的那個。

passages.original: Grandly, however, did Tootles respond. For that one moment he dropped his silliness and spoke with dignity.
passages.vernacular: 然而圖圖回應得好莊嚴。嗰一刻佢拋開咗佢嘅傻氣,以尊嚴講話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然而圖圖回應得很莊嚴。那一刻他拋開了他的傻氣,以尊嚴說話。

passages.original: “I am just Tootles,” he said, “and nobody minds me. But the first who does not behave to Wendy like an English gentleman I will blood him severely.”
passages.vernacular: 「我只係圖圖,」佢講,「冇人在乎我。但第一個對溫蒂表現得不像英國紳士嘅人,我要狠狠地讓佢流血。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我只是圖圖,」他說,「沒有人在乎我。但第一個對溫蒂表現得不像英國紳士的人,我要狠狠地讓他流血。」

passages.original: He drew back his hanger; and for that instant his sun was at noon. The others held back uneasily. Then Peter returned, and they saw at once that they would get no support from him. He would keep no girl in the Neverland against her will.
passages.vernacular: 佢拔出佢嘅短劍;嗰一刻佢嘅太陽正當中午。其他人不安地退縮喇。然後彼得回嚟喇,佢哋即刻睇出佢哋得唔到佢嘅支持。佢唔會違背女孩嘅意願把佢留喺永無島。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他拔出他的短劍;那一刻他的太陽正當中午。其他人不安地退縮了。然後彼得回來了,他們馬上看出他們得不到他的支持。他不會違背女孩的意願把她留在永無島。

passages.original: “Wendy,” he said, striding up and down, “I have asked the redskins to guide you through the wood, as flying tires you so.”
passages.vernacular: 「溫蒂,」佢講,大步走嚟走去,「我已經請紅番帶你穿過樹林,因為飛行讓你咁累。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「溫蒂,」他說,大步走來走去,「我已經請紅番帶你穿過樹林,因為飛行讓你這麼累。」

passages.original: “Thank you, Peter.”
passages.vernacular: 「謝謝你,彼得。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「謝謝你,彼得。」

passages.original: “Then,” he continued, in the short sharp voice of one accustomed to be obeyed, “Tinker Bell will take you across the sea. Wake her, Nibs.”
passages.vernacular: 「然後,」佢繼續講,用習慣被服從嘅人嗰種短促尖銳嘅聲音,「叮噹會帶你過海。叫醒佢,尼布斯。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「然後,」他繼續說,用習慣被服從的人那種短促尖銳的聲音,「叮噹會帶你過海。叫醒她,尼布斯。」

passages.original: Nibs had to knock twice before he got an answer, though Tink had really been sitting up in bed listening for some time.
passages.vernacular: 尼布斯敲咗兩次才得到回答,雖然叮其實已經坐喺床上聽咗一會兒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 尼布斯敲了兩次才得到回答,雖然叮其實已經坐在床上聽了一會兒。

passages.original: “Who are you? How dare you? Go away,” she cried.
passages.vernacular: 「你係邊個?你點敢?走開,」佢喊道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你是誰?你怎麼敢?走開,」她喊道。

passages.original: “You are to get up, Tink,” Nibs called, “and take Wendy on a journey.”
passages.vernacular: 「你得起嚟,叮,」尼布斯喊道,「帶溫蒂去旅行。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你得起來,叮,」尼布斯喊道,「帶溫蒂去旅行。」

passages.original: Of course Tink had been delighted to hear that Wendy was going; but she was jolly well determined not to be her courier, and she said so in still more offensive language. Then she pretended to be asleep again.
passages.vernacular: 當然叮聽到溫蒂要走好高興;但佢下定決心絕不做佢嘅嚮導,並用更難聽嘅話咁講。然後佢假裝又瞓住喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當然叮聽到溫蒂要走很高興;但她下定決心絕不做她的嚮導,並用更難聽的話這麼說。然後她假裝又睡著了。

passages.original: “She says she won’t!” Nibs exclaimed, aghast at such insubordination, whereupon Peter went sternly toward the young lady’s chamber.
passages.vernacular: 「佢講佢不去!」尼布斯喊道,對呢種不服從感到驚駭,於是彼得嚴厲地走向呢位小姐嘅房間。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她說她不去!」尼布斯喊道,對這種不服從感到驚駭,於是彼得嚴厲地走向這位小姐的房間。

passages.original: “Tink,” he rapped out, “if you don’t get up and dress at once I will open the curtains, and then we shall all see you in your negligée.”
passages.vernacular: 「叮,」佢厲聲講,「如果你不即刻起嚟穿衣服,我就拉開窗簾,嗰樣我哋都會睇到你穿瞓袍嘅樣子。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「叮,」他厲聲說,「如果你不馬上起來穿衣服,我就拉開窗簾,那樣我們都會看到你穿睡袍的樣子。」

passages.original: This made her leap to the floor. “Who said I wasn’t getting up?” she cried.
passages.vernacular: 呢使佢跳到地板上。「邊個講我不起嚟?」佢喊道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這使她跳到地板上。「誰說我不起來?」她喊道。

passages.original: In the meantime the boys were gazing very forlornly at Wendy, now equipped with John and Michael for the journey. By this time they were dejected, not merely because they were about to lose her, but also because they felt that she was going off to something nice to which they had not been invited. Novelty was beckoning to them as usual.
passages.vernacular: 同此同時,男孩哋好淒涼地睇住溫蒂,佢而家帶住約翰同邁克爾準備好咗旅行。呢陣佢哋沮喪喇,不僅因為佢哋即將失去佢,而且因為佢哋覺得佢要去一個美好嘅地方,而佢哋冇被邀請。新奇像往常一樣向佢哋招手。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 與此同時,男孩們非常淒涼地看著溫蒂,她現在帶著約翰和邁克爾準備好了旅行。這時他們沮喪了,不僅因為他們即將失去她,而且因為他們覺得她要去一個美好的地方,而他們沒有被邀請。新奇像往常一樣向他們招手。

passages.original: Crediting them with a nobler feeling Wendy melted.
passages.vernacular: 溫蒂把佢哋想成有更高尚嘅感情,心軟喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 溫蒂把他們想成有更高尚的感情,心軟了。

passages.original: “Dear ones,” she said, “if you will all come with me I feel almost sure I can get my father and mother to adopt you.”
passages.vernacular: 「親愛嘅,」佢講,「如果你哋都同我一起去,我幾乎肯定我能讓我嘅爸爸媽媽收養你哋。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「親愛的,」她說,「如果你們都和我一起去,我幾乎肯定我能讓我的爸爸媽媽收養你們。」

passages.original: The invitation was meant specially for Peter, but each of the boys was thinking exclusively of himself, and at once they jumped with joy.
passages.vernacular: 呢個邀請本係特別為彼得而發嘅,但每個男孩只想住佢自己,即刻高興得跳起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這個邀請本是特別為彼得而發的,但每個男孩只想著他自己,馬上高興得跳起來。

passages.original: “But won’t they think us rather a handful?” Nibs asked in the middle of his jump.
passages.vernacular: 「但佢哋唔會覺得我哋太麻煩嗎?」尼布斯喺跳到一半時問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但他們不會覺得我們太麻煩嗎?」尼布斯在跳到一半時問。

passages.original: “Oh no,” said Wendy, rapidly thinking it out, “it will only mean having a few beds in the drawing-room; they can be hidden behind the screens on first Thursdays.”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,唔會,」溫蒂講,飛快地想咗想,「嗰只意味住喺客廳裡放幾張床;每月第一個星期四可以把佢哋藏喺屏風後面。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,不會,」溫蒂說,飛快地想了想,「那只意味著在客廳裡放幾張床;每月第一個星期四可以把它們藏在屏風後面。」

passages.original: “Peter, can we go?” they all cried imploringly. They took it for granted that if they went he would go also, but really they scarcely cared. Thus children are ever ready, when novelty knocks, to desert their dearest ones.
passages.vernacular: 「彼得,我哋可以去嗎?」佢哋都懇求地喊道。佢哋理所當然地認為如果佢哋去,佢都會去,但其實佢哋幾乎不在乎。就咁樣,細路哋一旦新奇敲門,總是隨時準備拋棄佢哋最親愛嘅人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「彼得,我們可以去嗎?」他們都懇求地喊道。他們理所當然地認為如果他們去,他也會去,但其實他們幾乎不在乎。就這樣,孩子們一旦新奇敲門,總是隨時準備拋棄他們最親愛的人。

passages.original: “All right,” Peter replied with a bitter smile, and immediately they rushed to get their things.
passages.vernacular: 「好吧,」彼得帶住苦笑回答,佢哋即刻衝去攞嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好吧,」彼得帶著苦笑回答,他們馬上衝去拿東西。

passages.original: “And now, Peter,” Wendy said, thinking she had put everything right, “I am going to give you your medicine before you go.” She loved to give them medicine, and undoubtedly gave them too much. Of course it was only water, but it was out of a bottle, and she always shook the bottle and counted the drops, which gave it a certain medicinal quality. On this occasion, however, she did not give Peter his draught, for just as she had prepared it, she saw a look on his face that made her heart sink.
passages.vernacular: 「而家,彼得,」溫蒂講,以為佢把一切都安排好喇,「喺你走之前我要畀你食藥。」佢鍾意畀佢哋食藥,而且無疑畀得太多。當然嗰只係水,但佢係從瓶子裡倒出嚟嘅,佢總是搖瓶子、數滴數,呢畀咗佢一定嘅藥性。然而呢次佢冇畀彼得佢嘅藥水,因為就喺佢準備好時,佢睇到佢臉上嘅神情,使佢嘅心一沉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「現在,彼得,」溫蒂說,以為她把一切都安排好了,「在你走之前我要給你吃藥。」她喜歡給他們吃藥,而且無疑給得太多。當然那只是水,但它是從瓶子裡倒出來的,她總是搖瓶子、數滴數,這給了它一定的藥性。然而這次她沒有給彼得他的藥水,因為就在她準備好時,她看到他臉上的神情,使她的心一沉。

passages.original: “Get your things, Peter,” she cried, shaking.
passages.vernacular: 「去攞你嘅嘢,彼得,」佢顫抖地喊道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「去拿你的東西,彼得,」她顫抖地喊道。

passages.original: “No,” he answered, pretending indifference, “I am not going with you, Wendy.”
passages.vernacular: 「不,」佢回答,假裝漠不關心,「我不同你一起去,溫蒂。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不,」他回答,假裝漠不關心,「我不和你一起去,溫蒂。」

passages.original: “Yes, Peter.”
passages.vernacular: 「去嘅,彼得。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「去的,彼得。」

passages.original: “No.”
To show that her departure would leave him unmoved, he skipped up and down the room, playing gaily on his heartless pipes. She had to run about after him, though it was rather undignified.
passages.vernacular: 為了表明佢嘅離開唔會使佢動搖,佢喺房間裡上下跳躍,快樂地吹佢嗰無情嘅笛子。佢唔得不追住佢跑,雖然呢相當有失尊嚴。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 為了表明她的離開不會使他動搖,他在房間裡上下跳躍,快樂地吹他那無情的笛子。她不得不追著他跑,雖然這相當有失尊嚴。

passages.original: “To find your mother,” she coaxed.
passages.vernacular: 「去找你嘅媽媽,」佢哄佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「去找你的媽媽,」她哄他。

passages.original: Now, if Peter had ever quite had a mother, he no longer missed her. He could do very well without one. He had thought them out, and remembered only their bad points.
passages.vernacular: 而家,如果彼得曾經真嘅有過母親,佢都唔再想念佢喇。佢冇母親都完全可以。佢已經想透咗佢哋,只記得佢哋嘅缺點。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在,如果彼得曾經真的有過母親,他也不再想念她了。他沒有母親也完全可以。他已經想透了她們,只記得她們的缺點。

passages.original: “No, no,” he told Wendy decisively; “perhaps she would say I was old, and I just want always to be a little boy and to have fun.”
passages.vernacular: 「不,不,」佢斷然告訴溫蒂;「或者佢會講我老喇,我只想永遠做個小男孩,玩得開心。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不,不,」他斷然告訴溫蒂;「也許她會說我老了,我只想永遠做個小男孩,玩得開心。」

passages.original: “But, Peter—”
passages.vernacular: 「但係,彼得——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但是,彼得——」

passages.original: “No.”
And so the others had to be told.
passages.vernacular: 於是必須告訴其他人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是必須告訴其他人。

passages.original: “Peter isn’t coming.”
passages.vernacular: 「彼得不嚟。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「彼得不來。」

passages.original: Peter not coming! They gazed blankly at him, their sticks over their backs, and on each stick a bundle. Their first thought was that if Peter was not going he had probably changed his mind about letting them go.
passages.vernacular: 彼得不嚟!佢哋茫然地睇住佢,棍子扛喺背上,每根棍子上有一個包袱。佢哋嘅第一個念頭係,如果彼得不去,佢大概改變咗主意,不讓佢哋走喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 彼得不來!他們茫然地看著他,棍子扛在背上,每根棍子上有一個包袱。他們的第一個念頭是,如果彼得不去,他大概改變了主意,不讓他們走了。

passages.original: But he was far too proud for that. “If you find your mothers,” he said darkly, “I hope you will like them.”
passages.vernacular: 但佢太驕傲喇,唔會嗰樣。「如果你哋找到你哋嘅母親,」佢陰沉地講,「我希望你哋鍾意佢哋。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但他太驕傲了,不會那樣。「如果你們找到你們的母親,」他陰沉地說,「我希望你們喜歡她們。」

passages.original: The awful cynicism of this made an uncomfortable impression, and most of them began to look rather doubtful. After all, their faces said, were they not noodles to want to go?
passages.vernacular: 呢種可怕嘅玩世不恭畀佢哋留下咗不舒服嘅印象,佢哋大多數開始顯得相當猶豫。畢竟,佢哋嘅臉似乎喺講,佢哋想去唔係傻瓜嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這種可怕的玩世不恭給他們留下了不舒服的印象,他們大多數開始顯得相當猶豫。畢竟,他們的臉似乎在說,他們想去不是傻瓜嗎?

passages.original: “Now then,” cried Peter, “no fuss, no blubbering; good-bye, Wendy;” and he held out his hand cheerily, quite as if they must really go now, for he had something important to do.
passages.vernacular: 「咁,」彼得喊道,「別大驚小怪,別哭哭啼啼;再見,溫蒂;」佢愉快地伸出手,好像佢哋而家真嘅必須走喇,因為佢有重要嘅事要做。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那麼,」彼得喊道,「別大驚小怪,別哭哭啼啼;再見,溫蒂;」他愉快地伸出手,好像他們現在真的必須走了,因為他有重要的事要做。

passages.original: She had to take his hand, and there was no indication that he would prefer a thimble.
passages.vernacular: 佢唔得不握佢嘅手,冇任何跡象表明佢想要嘅係頂針。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她不得不握他的手,沒有任何跡象表明他想要的是頂針。

passages.original: “You will remember about changing your flannels, Peter?” she said, lingering over him. She was always so particular about their flannels.
passages.vernacular: 「你會記得換你嘅法蘭絨衣服吧,彼得?」佢講,喺佢身邊流連。佢對佢哋嘅法蘭絨衣服總是咁講究。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你會記得換你的法蘭絨衣服吧,彼得?」她說,在他身邊流連。她對他們的法蘭絨衣服總是那麼講究。

passages.original: “Yes.”
“And you will take your medicine?”
passages.vernacular: 「你會食你嘅藥吧?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你會吃你的藥吧?」

passages.original: “Yes.”
That seemed to be everything, and an awkward pause followed. Peter, however, was not the kind that breaks down before other people. “Are you ready, Tinker Bell?” he called out.
passages.vernacular: 似乎就呢啲喇,接住係尷尬嘅停頓。然而彼得唔係嗰種喺別人面前崩潰嘅人。「你準備好咗嗎,叮噹?」佢喊道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 似乎就這些了,接著是尷尬的停頓。然而彼得不是那種在別人面前崩潰的人。「你準備好了嗎,叮噹?」他喊道。

passages.original: “Ay, ay.”
“Then lead the way.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗰就帶路。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那就帶路。」

passages.original: Tink darted up the nearest tree; but no one followed her, for it was at this moment that the pirates made their dreadful attack upon the redskins. Above, where all had been so still, the air was rent with shrieks and the clash of steel. Below, there was dead silence. Mouths opened and remained open. Wendy fell on her knees, but her arms were extended toward Peter. All arms were extended to him, as if suddenly blown in his direction; they were beseeching him mutely not to desert them. As for Peter, he seized his sword, the same he thought he had slain Barbecue with, and the lust of battle was in his eye.
passages.vernacular: 叮飛快衝上最近嘅一棵樹;但冇人跟佢,因為就喺呢一刻,海盜哋對紅番發動咗可怕嘅攻擊。喺上面,本來咁靜嘅地方,空氣被尖叫聲同鋼鐵碰撞聲撕裂。喺下面,一片死寂。嘴巴張開喇,一直張住。溫蒂跪倒喺地,但佢嘅手臂向彼得伸出。所有嘅手臂都向佢伸出,好像突然被吹向佢嘅方向;佢哋默默地懇求佢唔好拋棄佢哋。至於彼得,佢抓起佢嘅劍,就係佢以為殺死過巴比克嘅嗰把,眼裡充滿戰鬥嘅渴望。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 叮飛快衝上最近的一棵樹;但沒有人跟她,因為就在這一刻,海盜們對紅番發動了可怕的攻擊。在上面,本來那麼靜的地方,空氣被尖叫聲和鋼鐵碰撞聲撕裂。在下面,一片死寂。嘴巴張開了,一直張著。溫蒂跪倒在地,但她的手臂向彼得伸出。所有的手臂都向他伸出,好像突然被吹向他的方向;他們默默地懇求他不要拋棄他們。至於彼得,他抓起他的劍,就是他以為殺死過巴比克的那把,眼裡充滿戰鬥的渴望。

chapters.title: Chapter XII: The Children Are Carried Off 第十二章:孩子們被擄走

passages.original: The pirate attack had been a complete surprise: a sure proof that the unscrupulous Hook had conducted it improperly, for to surprise redskins fairly is beyond the wit of the white man.
passages.vernacular: 海盜嘅攻擊完全出人意料:呢個係不擇手段嘅虎克處理不當的確鑿證據,因為公平地突襲紅番,超出咗白人嘅智慧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 海盜的攻擊完全出人意料:這是不擇手段的虎克處理不當的確鑿證據,因為公平地突襲紅番,超出了白人的智慧。

passages.original: By all the unwritten laws of savage warfare it is always the redskin who attacks, and with the wiliness of his race he does it just before the dawn, at which time he knows the courage of the whites to be at its lowest ebb. The white men have in the meantime made a rude stockade on the summit of yonder undulating ground, at the foot of which a stream runs, for it is destruction to be too far from water. There they await the onslaught, the inexperienced ones clutching their revolvers and treading on twigs, but the old hands sleeping tranquilly until just before the dawn. Through the long black night the savage scouts wriggle, snake-like, among the grass without stirring a blade. The brushwood closes behind them, as silently as sand into which a mole has dived. Not a sound is to be heard, save when they give vent to a wonderful imitation of the lonely call of the coyote. The cry is answered by other braves; and some of them do it even better than the coyotes, who are not very good at it. So the chill hours wear on, and the long suspense is horribly trying to the paleface who has to live through it for the first time; but to the trained hand those ghastly calls and still ghastlier silences are but an intimation of how the night is marching.
passages.vernacular: 按照野蠻戰爭所有不成文嘅法則,總是紅番發動攻擊,憑佢哋種族嘅狡詐,佢哋喺黎明前不久動手,嗰時佢知道白人嘅勇氣處於最低潮。白人同時喺嗰邊起伏地面嘅頂部築起咗簡陋嘅柵欄,地面腳下有一條小溪流過,因為離水太遠係死路。佢哋喺嗰度等待猛攻,冇經驗嘅人緊握住左輪手槍、踩喺細枝上,老手哋則安靜地瞓覺,直到黎明前不久。喺漫長嘅黑夜裡,野蠻嘅偵察兵像蛇一樣喺草叢中蠕動,卻不碰動一片草葉。灌木叢喺佢哋身後合攏,像鼴鼠鑽進嘅沙地一樣無聲無息。聽唔到啲聲音,除非佢哋發出對土狼孤獨叫聲嘅奇妙模仿。呢叫聲得到其他勇士嘅回應;其中啲人學得比土狼仲好,土狼並不太擅長呢個。就咁樣寒冷嘅時辰過去,漫長嘅懸念對第一次經歷嘅白人來講極其折磨;但對訓練有素嘅人來講,嗰啲可怕嘅叫聲同更可怕嘅沉寂只係夜晚如何行進嘅提示。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 按照野蠻戰爭所有不成文的法則,總是紅番發動攻擊,憑他們種族的狡詐,他們在黎明前不久動手,那時他知道白人的勇氣處於最低潮。白人同時在那邊起伏地面的頂部築起了簡陋的柵欄,地面腳下有一條小溪流過,因為離水太遠是死路。他們在那裡等待猛攻,沒有經驗的人緊握著左輪手槍、踩在細枝上,老手們則安靜地睡覺,直到黎明前不久。在漫長的黑夜裡,野蠻的偵察兵像蛇一樣在草叢中蠕動,卻不碰動一片草葉。灌木叢在他們身後合攏,像鼴鼠鑽進的沙地一樣無聲無息。聽不到一點聲音,除非他們發出對土狼孤獨叫聲的奇妙模仿。這叫聲得到其他勇士的回應;其中一些人學得比土狼還好,土狼並不太擅長這個。就這樣寒冷的時辰過去,漫長的懸念對第一次經歷的白人來說極其折磨;但對訓練有素的人來說,那些可怕的叫聲和更可怕的沉寂只是夜晚如何行進的提示。

passages.original: That this was the usual procedure was so well known to Hook that in disregarding it he cannot be excused on the plea of ignorance.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係通常嘅程序,虎克好清楚,所以佢無視佢,唔能夠以無知為藉口辯解。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是通常的程序,虎克非常清楚,所以他無視它,不能以無知為藉口辯解。

passages.original: The Piccaninnies, on their part, trusted implicitly to his honour, and their whole action of the night stands out in marked contrast to his. They left nothing undone that was consistent with the reputation of their tribe. With that alertness of the senses which is at once the marvel and despair of civilised peoples, they knew that the pirates were on the island from the moment one of them trod on a dry stick; and in an incredibly short space of time the coyote cries began. Every foot of ground between the spot where Hook had landed his forces and the home under the trees was stealthily examined by braves wearing their mocassins with the heels in front. They found only one hillock with a stream at its base, so that Hook had no choice; here he must establish himself and wait for just before the dawn. Everything being thus mapped out with almost diabolical cunning, the main body of the redskins folded their blankets around them, and in the phlegmatic manner that is to them, the pearl of manhood squatted above the children’s home, awaiting the cold moment when they should deal pale death.
passages.vernacular: 皮卡尼尼人呢邊則完全信任佢嘅榮譽,佢哋整個夜晚嘅行動同佢形成鮮明對比。佢哋冇漏掉任何符合佢哋部族聲譽嘅事。憑住嗰種既係文明人民嘅奇蹟又係佢哋嘅絕望嘅感官警覺,從佢哋中嘅一個人踩斷乾樹枝嘅嗰一刻,佢哋就知道海盜喺島上喇;喺極短嘅時間內,土狼嘅叫聲就開始喇。從虎克登陸佢嘅部隊嘅地點到樹下家園之間嘅每一呎土地,都被穿住鹿皮靴、腳跟喺前嘅勇士哋悄悄檢查過。佢哋只找到一個山丘,腳下有一條小溪,所以虎克別無選擇;佢必須喺呢度安頓下嚟,等到黎明前不久。一切就咁樣以近乎魔鬼般嘅狡猾規劃好喇,紅番嘅主力把毯子裹喺身上,以佢哋視為男子氣概之珠嘅遲鈍方式蹲喺細路哋嘅家上面,等待佢哋將畀予蒼白死亡嘅寒冷時刻。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 皮卡尼尼人這邊則完全信任他的榮譽,他們整個夜晚的行動與他形成鮮明對比。他們沒有漏掉任何符合他們部族聲譽的事。憑著那種既是文明人民的奇蹟又是他們的絕望的感官警覺,從他們中的一個人踩斷乾樹枝的那一刻,他們就知道海盜在島上了;在極短的時間內,土狼的叫聲就開始了。從虎克登陸他的部隊的地點到樹下家園之間的每一呎土地,都被穿著鹿皮靴、腳跟在前的勇士們悄悄檢查過。他們只找到一個山丘,腳下有一條小溪,所以虎克別無選擇;他必須在這裡安頓下來,等到黎明前不久。一切就這樣以近乎魔鬼般的狡猾規劃好了,紅番的主力把毯子裹在身上,以他們視為男子氣概之珠的遲鈍方式蹲在孩子們的家上面,等待他們將給予蒼白死亡的寒冷時刻。

passages.original: Here dreaming, though wide-awake, of the exquisite tortures to which they were to put him at break of day, those confiding savages were found by the treacherous Hook. From the accounts afterwards supplied by such of the scouts as escaped the carnage, he does not seem even to have paused at the rising ground, though it is certain that in that grey light he must have seen it: no thought of waiting to be attacked appears from first to last to have visited his subtle mind; he would not even hold off till the night was nearly spent; on he pounded with no policy but to fall to. What could the bewildered scouts do, masters as they were of every war-like artifice save this one, but trot helplessly after him, exposing themselves fatally to view, while they gave pathetic utterance to the coyote cry.
passages.vernacular: 呢啲輕信嘅野蠻人喺呢度做住夢,雖然清醒住,夢想住黎明時佢哋要對佢施加嘅精緻酷刑,被奸詐嘅虎克發現喇。從後來逃過屠殺嘅偵察兵提供嘅敘述嚟睇,佢似乎連喺高地都冇停一下,雖然喺嗰灰色嘅光線下佢肯定睇到咗佢:從頭到尾,佢嗰狡猾嘅頭腦中似乎冇一個等待被攻擊嘅念頭;佢甚至冇等到夜晚幾乎過完;佢冇任何策略,只管猛衝向前開打。困惑嘅偵察兵哋能做乜嘢,佢哋精通每一種好戰嘅詭計,唯獨不懂呢一種,只能無助地小跑住跟喺佢後面,致命地暴露喺視線中,同時悲慘地發出土狼嘅叫聲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這些輕信的野蠻人在這裡做著夢,雖然清醒著,夢想著黎明時他們要對他施加的精緻酷刑,被奸詐的虎克發現了。從後來逃過屠殺的偵察兵提供的敘述來看,他似乎連在高地也沒有停一下,雖然在那灰色的光線下他肯定看到了它:從頭到尾,他那狡猾的頭腦中似乎沒有一個等待被攻擊的念頭;他甚至沒有等到夜晚幾乎過完;他沒有任何策略,只管猛衝向前開打。困惑的偵察兵們能做什麼,他們精通每一種好戰的詭計,唯獨不懂這一種,只能無助地小跑著跟在他後面,致命地暴露在視線中,同時悲慘地發出土狼的叫聲。

passages.original: Around the brave Tiger Lily were a dozen of her stoutest warriors, and they suddenly saw the perfidious pirates bearing down upon them. Fell from their eyes then the film through which they had looked at victory. No more would they torture at the stake. For them the happy hunting-grounds was now. They knew it; but as their father’s sons they acquitted themselves. Even then they had time to gather in a phalanx that would have been hard to break had they risen quickly, but this they were forbidden to do by the traditions of their race. It is written that the noble savage must never express surprise in the presence of the white. Thus terrible as the sudden appearance of the pirates must have been to them, they remained stationary for a moment, not a muscle moving; as if the foe had come by invitation. Then, indeed, the tradition gallantly upheld, they seized their weapons, and the air was torn with the war-cry; but it was now too late.
passages.vernacular: 勇敢嘅虎百合周圍有十幾個佢最強壯嘅戰士,佢哋突然睇到背信嘅海盜向佢哋逼嚟。佢哋睇住勝利嘅嗰層薄膜從佢哋眼裡落下。佢哋再都唔會喺火刑柱上折磨人喇。對佢哋來講,快樂獵場就喺此刻。佢哋知道呢啲;但作為佢哋父親嘅兒子,佢哋表現得無愧。即使喺嗰時,佢哋仲有時間聚成一個如果迅速起身就好難被衝破嘅方陣,但佢哋種族嘅傳統禁止佢哋咁樣做。書上寫住,高貴嘅野蠻人喺白人面前絕唔能夠表現出驚訝。因此,雖然海盜嘅突然出現對佢哋一定係可怕嘅,佢哋一時保持不動,冇一塊肌肉動;好像敵人係應邀而嚟嘅。然後,確實,傳統英勇地得到維護,佢哋抓起武器,空氣被戰吼撕裂;但而家為時已晚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 勇敢的虎百合周圍有十幾個她最強壯的戰士,他們突然看到背信的海盜向他們逼來。他們看著勝利的那層薄膜從他們眼裡落下。他們再也不會在火刑柱上折磨人了。對他們來說,快樂獵場就在此刻。他們知道這一點;但作為他們父親的兒子,他們表現得無愧。即使在那時,他們還有時間聚成一個如果迅速起身就很難被衝破的方陣,但他們種族的傳統禁止他們這樣做。書上寫著,高貴的野蠻人在白人面前絕不能表現出驚訝。因此,雖然海盜的突然出現對他們一定是可怕的,他們一時保持不動,沒有一塊肌肉動;好像敵人是應邀而來的。然後,確實,傳統英勇地得到維護,他們抓起武器,空氣被戰吼撕裂;但現在為時已晚。

passages.original: It is no part of ours to describe what was a massacre rather than a fight. Thus perished many of the flower of the Piccaninny tribe. Not all unavenged did they die, for with Lean Wolf fell Alf Mason, to disturb the Spanish Main no more, and among others who bit the dust were Geo. Scourie, Chas. Turley, and the Alsatian Foggerty. Turley fell to the tomahawk of the terrible Panther, who ultimately cut a way through the pirates with Tiger Lily and a small remnant of the tribe.
passages.vernacular: 描述呢場同其講係戰鬥不如講係屠殺嘅事件,唔係我哋該做嘅事。就咁樣皮卡尼尼部族嘅許多精英死去喇。佢哋並非死而未報,因為同瘦狼一起倒下嘅仲有阿爾夫·梅森,佢再唔能夠騷擾西班牙海喇,仲有其他咬咗塵土嘅人,包括喬治·斯科里、查爾斯·特利,同阿爾薩斯人福格蒂。特利倒喺可怕嘅豹子嘅戰斧下,豹子最終帶住虎百合同部族嘅一小撮殘餘殺出咗一條路,穿過海盜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 描述這場與其說是戰鬥不如說是屠殺的事件,不是我們該做的事。就這樣皮卡尼尼部族的許多精英死去了。他們並非死而未報,因為與瘦狼一起倒下的還有阿爾夫·梅森,他再不能騷擾西班牙海了,還有其他咬了塵土的人,包括喬治·斯科里、查爾斯·特利,和阿爾薩斯人福格蒂。特利倒在可怕的豹子的戰斧下,豹子最終帶著虎百合和部族的一小撮殘餘殺出了一條路,穿過海盜。

passages.original: To what extent Hook is to blame for his tactics on this occasion is for the historian to decide. Had he waited on the rising ground till the proper hour he and his men would probably have been butchered; and in judging him it is only fair to take this into account. What he should perhaps have done was to acquaint his opponents that he proposed to follow a new method. On the other hand, this, as destroying the element of surprise, would have made his strategy of no avail, so that the whole question is beset with difficulties. One cannot at least withhold a reluctant admiration for the wit that had conceived so bold a scheme, and the fell genius with which it was carried out.
passages.vernacular: 虎克喺呢次戰術上應受多大責備,由歷史學家去判斷。如果佢喺高地上等到適當嘅時候,佢同佢嘅人可能會被屠殺;評判佢時,把呢啲考慮在內才公平。佢或者應該做嘅係告知對手佢打算採用一種新方法。另一方面,呢會破壞突襲嘅因素,使佢嘅戰略無用,所以整個問題困難重重。至少唔能夠不對構思出如此大膽計畫嘅智慧、同執行佢嘅凶惡天才,勉強地表示欽佩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 虎克在這次戰術上應受多大責備,由歷史學家去判斷。如果他在高地上等到適當的時候,他和他的人可能會被屠殺;評判他時,把這一點考慮在內才公平。他也許應該做的是告知對手他打算採用一種新方法。另一方面,這會破壞突襲的因素,使他的戰略無用,所以整個問題困難重重。至少不能不對構思出如此大膽計畫的智慧、和執行它的凶惡天才,勉強地表示欽佩。

passages.original: What were his own feelings about himself at that triumphant moment? Fain would his dogs have known, as breathing heavily and wiping their cutlasses, they gathered at a discreet distance from his hook, and squinted through their ferret eyes at this extraordinary man. Elation must have been in his heart, but his face did not reflect it: ever a dark and solitary enigma, he stood aloof from his followers in spirit as in substance.
passages.vernacular: 喺嗰勝利嘅時刻,佢自己對自己有乜嘢感覺?佢嘅走狗哋好想知道,佢哋喘住粗氣、擦拭住短彎刀,聚集喺離佢嘅鉤子謹慎嘅距離之外,用雪貂似嘅眼睛斜視住呢個非凡嘅人。佢心裡一定有得意,但佢嘅臉冇反映出嚟:佢永遠係一個黑暗孤獨嘅謎,喺精神上同實體上都遠離佢嘅追隨者。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在那勝利的時刻,他自己對自己有什麼感覺?他的走狗們很想知道,他們喘著粗氣、擦拭著短彎刀,聚集在離他的鉤子謹慎的距離之外,用雪貂似的眼睛斜視著這個非凡的人。他心裡一定有得意,但他的臉沒有反映出來:他永遠是一個黑暗孤獨的謎,在精神上和實體上都遠離他的追隨者。

passages.original: The night’s work was not yet over, for it was not the redskins he had come out to destroy; they were but the bees to be smoked, so that he should get at the honey. It was Pan he wanted, Pan and Wendy and their band, but chiefly Pan.
passages.vernacular: 夜晚嘅工作仲冇結束,因為佢出嚟要消滅嘅唔係紅番;佢哋只係要被煙熏嘅蜜蜂,咁樣佢才能取到蜂蜜。佢要嘅係潘,潘同溫蒂同佢哋嘅團隊,但主要係潘。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 夜晚的工作還沒有結束,因為他出來要消滅的不是紅番;他們只是要被煙熏的蜜蜂,這樣他才能取到蜂蜜。他要的是潘,潘和溫蒂和他們的團隊,但主要是潘。

passages.original: Peter was such a small boy that one tends to wonder at the man’s hatred of him. True he had flung Hook’s arm to the crocodile, but even this and the increased insecurity of life to which it led, owing to the crocodile’s pertinacity, hardly account for a vindictiveness so relentless and malignant. The truth is that there was a something about Peter which goaded the pirate captain to frenzy. It was not his courage, it was not his engaging appearance, it was not—. There is no beating about the bush, for we know quite well what it was, and have got to tell. It was Peter’s cockiness.
passages.vernacular: 彼得係咁小嘅一個男孩,人哋不免納悶呢個人點解咁恨佢。誠然佢把虎克嘅手臂扔畀咗鱷魚,但即使係呢個,以及由於鱷魚嘅頑固而導致嘅生命更不安全,都好難解釋如此無情惡毒嘅報復心。事實係彼得身上有某種嘢把海盜船長刺激得發狂。唔係佢嘅勇氣,唔係佢迷人嘅外貌,唔係——。唔使拐彎抹角,因為我哋完全知道嗰個係乜嘢,而且必須講出嚟。嗰個係彼得嘅自負。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 彼得是那麼小的一個男孩,人們不免納悶這個人為什麼那麼恨他。誠然他把虎克的手臂扔給了鱷魚,但即使是這個,以及由於鱷魚的頑固而導致的生命更不安全,也很難解釋如此無情惡毒的報復心。事實是彼得身上有某種東西把海盜船長刺激得發狂。不是他的勇氣,不是他迷人的外貌,不是——。不必拐彎抹角,因為我們完全知道那是什麼,而且必須說出來。那是彼得的自負。

passages.original: This had got on Hook’s nerves; it made his iron claw twitch, and at night it disturbed him like an insect. While Peter lived, the tortured man felt that he was a lion in a cage into which a sparrow had come.
passages.vernacular: 呢惹到咗虎克嘅神經;佢使佢嘅鐵爪抽動,夜裡像蟲子一樣擾亂佢。彼得活住嘅時候,呢個受折磨嘅人覺得自己係一頭獅子,關喺一個麻雀闖進嚟嘅籠子裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這惹到了虎克的神經;它使他的鐵爪抽動,夜裡像蟲子一樣擾亂他。彼得活著的時候,這個受折磨的人覺得自己是一頭獅子,關在一個麻雀闖進來的籠子裡。

passages.original: The question now was how to get down the trees, or how to get his dogs down? He ran his greedy eyes over them, searching for the thinnest ones. They wriggled uncomfortably, for they knew he would not scruple to ram them down with poles.
passages.vernacular: 而家嘅問題係點樣下樹,或點樣讓佢嘅走狗下去?佢貪婪嘅眼睛掃過佢哋,尋找最瘦嘅人。佢哋不舒服地扭動,因為佢哋知道佢唔會顧忌用竿子把佢哋捅下去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在的問題是怎樣下樹,或怎樣讓他的走狗下去?他貪婪的眼睛掃過他們,尋找最瘦的人。他們不舒服地扭動,因為他們知道他不會顧忌用竿子把他們捅下去。

passages.original: In the meantime, what of the boys? We have seen them at the first clang of the weapons, turned as it were into stone figures, open-mouthed, all appealing with outstretched arms to Peter; and we return to them as their mouths close, and their arms fall to their sides. The pandemonium above has ceased almost as suddenly as it arose, passed like a fierce gust of wind; but they know that in the passing it has determined their fate.
passages.vernacular: 同時,男孩哋點樣喇?我哋睇到佢哋喺武器第一聲碰撞時,變成咗像石頭人一樣,張住嘴,都伸出手臂向彼得求助;我哋回到佢哋呢度,佢哋嘅嘴合上喇,手臂垂喺身側。上面嘅混亂幾乎像佢出現時一樣突然停止,像一陣猛烈嘅風吹過;但佢哋知道喺經過嘅時候,佢已決定咗佢哋嘅命運。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 同時,男孩們怎樣了?我們看到他們在武器第一聲碰撞時,變成了像石頭人一樣,張著嘴,都伸出手臂向彼得求助;我們回到他們這裡,他們的嘴合上了,手臂垂在身側。上面的混亂幾乎像它出現時一樣突然停止,像一陣猛烈的風吹過;但他們知道在經過的時候,它已決定了他們的命運。

passages.original: Which side had won?
passages.vernacular: 邊一方贏喇?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哪一方贏了?

passages.original: The pirates, listening avidly at the mouths of the trees, heard the question put by every boy, and alas, they also heard Peter’s answer.
passages.vernacular: 海盜哋喺樹口貪婪地聽住,聽到每個男孩提出嘅問題,可惜,佢哋都聽到咗彼得嘅回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 海盜們在樹口貪婪地聽著,聽到每個男孩提出的問題,可惜,他們也聽到了彼得的回答。

passages.original: “If the redskins have won,” he said, “they will beat the tom-tom; it is always their sign of victory.”
passages.vernacular: 「如果紅番贏喇,」佢講,「佢哋會敲響鼓;嗰總是佢哋勝利嘅標誌。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「如果紅番贏了,」他說,「他們會敲響鼓;那總是他們勝利的標誌。」

passages.original: Now Smee had found the tom-tom, and was at that moment sitting on it. “You will never hear the tom-tom again,” he muttered, but inaudibly of course, for strict silence had been enjoined. To his amazement Hook signed him to beat the tom-tom, and slowly there came to Smee an understanding of the dreadful wickedness of the order. Never, probably, had this simple man admired Hook so much.
passages.vernacular: 呢陣斯密找到咗鼓,正坐喺上面。「你再都聽唔到鼓聲喇,」佢喃喃自語,當然聲音聽唔見,因為已經嚴令保持絕對安靜。令佢驚奇嘅係,虎克示意佢敲鼓,斯密慢慢明白咗呢個命令嘅可怕邪惡。呢個單純嘅人大概從冇咁欽佩過虎克。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這時斯密找到了鼓,正坐在上面。「你再也聽不到鼓聲了,」他喃喃自語,當然聲音聽不見,因為已經嚴令保持絕對安靜。令他驚奇的是,虎克示意他敲鼓,斯密慢慢明白了這個命令的可怕邪惡。這個單純的人大概從沒這麼欽佩過虎克。

passages.original: Twice Smee beat upon the instrument, and then stopped to listen gleefully.
passages.vernacular: 斯密敲咗兩下樂器,然後停下嚟高興地聽住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 斯密敲了兩下樂器,然後停下來高興地聽著。

passages.original: “The tom-tom,” the miscreants heard Peter cry; “an Indian victory!”
passages.vernacular: 「鼓聲,」惡棍哋聽到彼得喊;「印第安人勝利喇!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「鼓聲,」惡棍們聽到彼得喊;「印第安人勝利了!」

passages.original: The doomed children answered with a cheer that was music to the black hearts above, and almost immediately they repeated their good-byes to Peter. This puzzled the pirates, but all their other feelings were swallowed by a base delight that the enemy were about to come up the trees. They smirked at each other and rubbed their hands. Rapidly and silently Hook gave his orders: one man to each tree, and the others to arrange themselves in a line two yards apart.
passages.vernacular: 注定嘅細路哋用歡呼回答,呢對上面嘅黑心來講係音樂,幾乎即刻佢哋就重複向彼得道別。呢使海盜哋困惑,但佢哋所有其他嘅感覺都被卑鄙嘅喜悅吞冇喇,因為敵人就要爬上樹嚟喇。佢哋互相奸笑,搓著手。虎克迅速而無聲地下達命令:每棵樹一個人,其餘嘅排成一列,相隔兩碼。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 注定的孩子們用歡呼回答,這對上面的黑心來說是音樂,幾乎馬上他們就重複向彼得道別。這使海盜們困惑,但他們所有其他的感覺都被卑鄙的喜悅吞沒了,因為敵人就要爬上樹來了。他們互相奸笑,搓著手。虎克迅速而無聲地下達命令:每棵樹一個人,其餘的排成一列,相隔兩碼。

chapters.title: Chapter XIII: Do You Believe in Fairies? 第十三章:你相信有仙子嗎?

passages.original: The more quickly this horror is disposed of the better. The first to emerge from his tree was Curly. He rose out of it into the arms of Cecco, who flung him to Smee, who flung him to Starkey, who flung him to Bill Jukes, who flung him to Noodler, and so he was tossed from one to another till he fell at the feet of the black pirate. All the boys were plucked from their trees in this ruthless manner; and several of them were in the air at a time, like bales of goods flung from hand to hand.
passages.vernacular: 呢個恐怖嘅事越快處理完越好。第一個從樹裡出嚟嘅係卷毛。佢從樹裡升起,落入切科嘅手臂,切科把佢扔畀斯密,斯密扔畀斯塔基,斯塔基扔畀比爾·朱克斯,朱克斯扔畀努德勒,就咁樣佢被一個傳一個地拋住,直到摔喺黑人海盜嘅腳下。所有男孩都以呢種無情嘅方式從佢哋嘅樹裡被拔出嚟;有幾個同時喺空中,像貨包喺手同手之間拋擲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這個恐怖的事越快處理完越好。第一個從樹裡出來的是卷毛。他從樹裡升起,落入切科的手臂,切科把他扔給斯密,斯密扔給斯塔基,斯塔基扔給比爾·朱克斯,朱克斯扔給努德勒,就這樣他被一個傳一個地拋著,直到摔在黑人海盜的腳下。所有男孩都以這種無情的方式從他們的樹裡被拔出來;有幾個同時在空中,像貨包在手與手之間拋擲。

passages.original: A different treatment was accorded to Wendy, who came last. With ironical politeness Hook raised his hat to her, and, offering her his arm, escorted her to the spot where the others were being gagged. He did it with such an air, he was so frightfully distingué, that she was too fascinated to cry out. She was only a little girl.
passages.vernacular: 對最後出嚟嘅溫蒂,待遇不同。虎克帶住諷刺嘅禮貌向佢舉起帽子,伸出手臂,護送佢到其他人被堵嘴嘅地方。佢做得咁有派頭,咁極其高雅,佢太著迷喇,叫不出聲。佢只係個小女孩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 對最後出來的溫蒂,待遇不同。虎克帶著諷刺的禮貌向她舉起帽子,伸出手臂,護送她到其他人被堵嘴的地方。他做得那麼有派頭,那麼極其高雅,她太著迷了,叫不出聲。她只是個小女孩。

passages.original: Perhaps it is tell-tale to divulge that for a moment Hook entranced her, and we tell on her only because her slip led to strange results. Had she haughtily unhanded him (and we should have loved to write it of her), she would have been hurled through the air like the others, and then Hook would probably not have been present at the tying of the children; and had he not been at the tying he would not have discovered Slightly’s secret, and without the secret he could not presently have made his foul attempt on Peter’s life.
passages.vernacular: 或者洩露呢啲係喺告密:有一刻虎克使佢入迷喇,我哋告發佢只係因為佢嘅失誤導致咗奇怪嘅結果。如果佢傲慢地甩開佢(我哋本來好想咁樣寫佢),佢就會像其他人一樣被拋過空中,咁虎克大概唔會在場綁細路哋;如果佢不在場綁,佢就唔會發現輕輕嘅秘密,冇呢個秘密,佢不久都就唔能夠對彼得嘅性命作出佢嗰卑鄙嘅企圖。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 也許洩露這一點是在告密:有一刻虎克使她入迷了,我們告發她只是因為她的失誤導致了奇怪的結果。如果她傲慢地甩開他(我們本來很想這樣寫她),她就會像其他人一樣被拋過空中,那麼虎克大概不會在場綁孩子們;如果他不在場綁,他就不會發現輕輕的秘密,沒有這個秘密,他不久也就不能對彼得的性命作出他那卑鄙的企圖。

passages.original: They were tied to prevent their flying away, doubled up with their knees close to their ears; and for the trussing of them the black pirate had cut a rope into nine equal pieces. All went well until Slightly’s turn came, when he was found to be like those irritating parcels that use up all the string in going round and leave no tags with which to tie a knot. The pirates kicked him in their rage, just as you kick the parcel (though in fairness you should kick the string); and strange to say it was Hook who told them to belay their violence. His lip was curled with malicious triumph. While his dogs were merely sweating because every time they tried to pack the unhappy lad tight in one part he bulged out in another, Hook’s master mind had gone far beneath Slightly’s surface, probing not for effects but for causes; and his exultation showed that he had found them. Slightly, white to the gills, knew that Hook had surprised his secret, which was this, that no boy so blown out could use a tree wherein an average man need stick. Poor Slightly, most wretched of all the children now, for he was in a panic about Peter, bitterly regretted what he had done. Madly addicted to the drinking of water when he was hot, he had swelled in consequence to his present girth, and instead of reducing himself to fit his tree he had, unknown to the others, whittled his tree to make it fit him.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋被綁起嚟,防止飛走,身體對折,膝蓋靠近耳朵;為了捆綁佢哋,黑人海盜把一條繩子切成九等份。一切順利,直到輪到輕輕時,發現佢像嗰啲令人惱火嘅包裹,繞一圈用盡所有嘅繩子,冇剩下繫結嘅頭。海盜哋憤怒地踢佢,就像你踢嗰個包裹(雖然公平地講你應該踢繩子);講都奇怪,叫佢哋住手嘅係虎克。佢嘅嘴唇帶住惡意嘅勝利捲起。佢嘅走狗哋只係出汗,因為每次佢哋試圖把呢個不幸嘅男孩喺一處捆緊,佢就喺另一處鼓出嚟,虎克嘅大腦卻已深入輕輕嘅表面之下,探查嘅唔係結果而係原因;佢嘅得意表明佢找到喇。輕輕臉色蒼白,知道虎克突然發現咗佢嘅秘密,嗰個就係,一個脹得咁大嘅男孩,唔能夠用一個普通人都會卡住嘅樹。可憐嘅輕輕,而家係所有細路中最悲慘嘅,因為佢為彼得驚慌失措,痛苦地後悔佢所做嘅事。佢熱嘅時候瘋狂地愛飲水,結果脹到咗而家嘅粗細,佢冇縮小自己嚟適合佢嘅樹,而係,其他人唔知道,削咗佢嘅樹嚟適合自己。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們被綁起來,防止飛走,身體對折,膝蓋靠近耳朵;為了捆綁他們,黑人海盜把一條繩子切成九等份。一切順利,直到輪到輕輕時,發現他像那些令人惱火的包裹,繞一圈用盡所有的繩子,沒剩下繫結的頭。海盜們憤怒地踢他,就像你踢那個包裹(雖然公平地說你應該踢繩子);說也奇怪,叫他們住手的是虎克。他的嘴唇帶著惡意的勝利捲起。他的走狗們只是出汗,因為每次他們試圖把這個不幸的男孩在一處捆緊,他就在另一處鼓出來,虎克的大腦卻已深入輕輕的表面之下,探查的不是結果而是原因;他的得意表明他找到了。輕輕臉色蒼白,知道虎克突然發現了他的秘密,那就是,一個脹得這麼大的男孩,不能用一個普通人也會卡住的樹。可憐的輕輕,現在是所有孩子中最悲慘的,因為他為彼得驚慌失措,痛苦地後悔他所做的事。他熱的時候瘋狂地愛喝水,結果脹到了現在的粗細,他沒有縮小自己來適合他的樹,而是,其他人不知道,削了他的樹來適合自己。

passages.original: Sufficient of this Hook guessed to persuade him that Peter at last lay at his mercy, but no word of the dark design that now formed in the subterranean caverns of his mind crossed his lips; he merely signed that the captives were to be conveyed to the ship, and that he would be alone.
passages.vernacular: 虎克猜到咗呢個足夠嘅部分,相信彼得終於落喺佢手裡喇,但而家喺佢心裡嘅地下洞穴中形成嘅黑暗計畫,佢一個字都冇講出嚟;佢只係示意把俘虜哋送到船上,佢自己一個人留下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 虎克猜到了這個足夠的部分,相信彼得終於落在他手裡了,但現在在他心裡的地下洞穴中形成的黑暗計畫,他一個字也沒說出來;他只是示意把俘虜們送到船上,他自己一個人留下。

passages.original: How to convey them? Hunched up in their ropes they might indeed be rolled down hill like barrels, but most of the way lay through a morass. Again Hook’s genius surmounted difficulties. He indicated that the little house must be used as a conveyance. The children were flung into it, four stout pirates raised it on their shoulders, the others fell in behind, and singing the hateful pirate chorus the strange procession set off through the wood. I don’t know whether any of the children were crying; if so, the singing drowned the sound; but as the little house disappeared in the forest, a brave though tiny jet of smoke issued from its chimney as if defying Hook.
passages.vernacular: 點運送佢哋?蜷縮喺繩子裡,確實可以像木桶一樣滾下山,但大部分路係沼澤。虎克嘅天才又一次克服咗困難。佢示意必須用小房子作為運輸工具。細路哋被扔進去,四個強壯嘅海盜把佢扛喺肩上,其他人跟喺後面,唱住可恨嘅海盜合唱,呢支奇怪嘅隊伍穿過樹林出發喇。我唔知道細路哋有冇人喺哭;如果有,歌聲淹沒咗聲音;但小房子消失喺森林裡時,一縷勇敢而微小嘅煙從佢嘅煙囪裡冒出嚟,好像喺向虎克挑戰。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 怎麼運送他們?蜷縮在繩子裡,確實可以像木桶一樣滾下山,但大部分路是沼澤。虎克的天才又一次克服了困難。他示意必須用小房子作為運輸工具。孩子們被扔進去,四個強壯的海盜把它扛在肩上,其他人跟在後面,唱著可恨的海盜合唱,這支奇怪的隊伍穿過樹林出發了。我不知道孩子們有沒有人在哭;如果有,歌聲淹沒了聲音;但小房子消失在森林裡時,一縷勇敢而微小的煙從它的煙囪裡冒出來,好像在向虎克挑戰。

passages.original: Hook saw it, and it did Peter a bad service. It dried up any trickle of pity for him that may have remained in the pirate’s infuriated breast.
passages.vernacular: 虎克睇到喇,呢對彼得係個壞影響。佢曬乾咗海盜暴怒嘅胸中可能仲殘留嘅任何一絲對佢嘅憐憫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 虎克看到了,這對彼得是個壞影響。它曬乾了海盜暴怒的胸中可能還殘留的任何一絲對他的憐憫。

passages.original: The first thing he did on finding himself alone in the fast falling night was to tiptoe to Slightly’s tree, and make sure that it provided him with a passage. Then for long he remained brooding; his hat of ill omen on the sward, so that any gentle breeze which had arisen might play refreshingly through his hair. Dark as were his thoughts his blue eyes were as soft as the periwinkle. Intently he listened for any sound from the nether world, but all was as silent below as above; the house under the ground seemed to be but one more empty tenement in the void. Was that boy asleep, or did he stand waiting at the foot of Slightly’s tree, with his dagger in his hand?
passages.vernacular: 佢喺迅速降臨嘅夜色中發現自己孤身一人時做嘅第一件事,係踮住腳走到輕輕嘅樹旁,確定佢能畀佢提供一條通道。然後佢沉思咗好久;佢不祥嘅帽子放喺草地上,好讓升起嘅任何微風吹過佢嘅頭髮,清爽怡人。雖然佢嘅思想黑暗,佢嘅藍眼睛卻像長春花一樣柔和。佢專注地聽住來自下界嘅任何聲音,但下面同上面一樣寂靜;地下嘅房子似乎只係虛空中又一棟空屋。嗰個男孩係瞓住喇,定係站喺輕輕嘅樹腳下等住,手裡攞住匕首?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他在迅速降臨的夜色中發現自己孤身一人時做的第一件事,是踮著腳走到輕輕的樹旁,確定它能給他提供一條通道。然後他沉思了很久;他不祥的帽子放在草地上,好讓升起的任何微風吹過他的頭髮,清爽怡人。雖然他的思想黑暗,他的藍眼睛卻像長春花一樣柔和。他專注地聽著來自下界的任何聲音,但下面和上面一樣寂靜;地下的房子似乎只是虛空中又一棟空屋。那個男孩是睡著了,還是站在輕輕的樹腳下等著,手裡拿著匕首?

passages.original: There was no way of knowing, save by going down. Hook let his cloak slip softly to the ground, and then biting his lips till a lewd blood stood on them, he stepped into the tree. He was a brave man, but for a moment he had to stop there and wipe his brow, which was dripping like a candle. Then, silently, he let himself go into the unknown.
passages.vernacular: 冇辦法知道,除咗下去。虎克讓斗篷輕輕滑到地上,然後咬住嘴唇,咬得淫邪嘅血流到上面,走進咗樹裡。佢係個勇敢嘅人,但有一刻佢唔得不停喺嗰度,擦佢嘅額頭,佢像蠟燭一樣滴住汗。然後,無聲地,佢讓自己進入未知。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒有辦法知道,除了下去。虎克讓斗篷輕輕滑到地上,然後咬著嘴唇,咬得淫邪的血流到上面,走進了樹裡。他是個勇敢的人,但有一刻他不得不停在那裡,擦他的額頭,它像蠟燭一樣滴著汗。然後,無聲地,他讓自己進入未知。

passages.original: He arrived unmolested at the foot of the shaft, and stood still again, biting at his breath, which had almost left him. As his eyes became accustomed to the dim light various objects in the home under the trees took shape; but the only one on which his greedy gaze rested, long sought for and found at last, was the great bed. On the bed lay Peter fast asleep.
passages.vernacular: 佢毫髮無損地到達井道底部,又站住不動,咬住佢嘅呼吸,佢幾乎離佢而去。當佢嘅眼睛適應昏暗嘅光線,樹下家園裡嘅各種物體顯出形狀;但佢貪婪嘅目光停留嘅唯一一個,尋找咗好久終於找到嘅,係嗰張大床。床上躺住熟瞓嘅彼得。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他毫髮無損地到達井道底部,又站住不動,咬著他的呼吸,它幾乎離他而去。當他的眼睛適應昏暗的光線,樹下家園裡的各種物體顯出形狀;但他貪婪的目光停留的唯一一個,尋找了很久終於找到的,是那張大床。床上躺著熟睡的彼得。

passages.original: Unaware of the tragedy being enacted above, Peter had continued, for a little time after the children left, to play gaily on his pipes: no doubt rather a forlorn attempt to prove to himself that he did not care. Then he decided not to take his medicine, so as to grieve Wendy. Then he lay down on the bed outside the coverlet, to vex her still more; for she had always tucked them inside it, because you never know that you may not grow chilly at the turn of the night. Then he nearly cried; but it struck him how indignant she would be if he laughed instead; so he laughed a haughty laugh and fell asleep in the middle of it.
passages.vernacular: 彼得唔知道上面正在上演嘅悲劇,細路哋走後,佢又快樂地吹咗一會兒笛子:無疑係一種相當淒涼嘅企圖,向自己證明佢不在乎。然後佢決定不食藥,以惹溫蒂傷心。然後佢躺喺床上,喺被子外面,以惹佢更生氣;因為佢總是把佢哋塞進被子裡面,因為你永遠唔知道夜裡轉涼時會唔會發冷。然後佢差點哭喇;但佢想到如果佢反而笑,佢會幾咁憤怒;於是佢發出一聲傲慢嘅笑,喺笑到一半時瞓住喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 彼得不知道上面正在上演的悲劇,孩子們走後,他又快樂地吹了一會兒笛子:無疑是一種相當淒涼的企圖,向自己證明他不在乎。然後他決定不吃藥,以惹溫蒂傷心。然後他躺在床上,在被子外面,以惹她更生氣;因為她總是把他們塞進被子裡面,因為你永遠不知道夜裡轉涼時會不會發冷。然後他差點哭了;但他想到如果他反而笑,她會多麼憤怒;於是他發出一聲傲慢的笑,在笑到一半時睡著了。

passages.original: Sometimes, though not often, he had dreams, and they were more painful than the dreams of other boys. For hours he could not be separated from these dreams, though he wailed piteously in them. They had to do, I think, with the riddle of his existence. At such times it had been Wendy’s custom to take him out of bed and sit with him on her lap, soothing him in dear ways of her own invention, and when he grew calmer to put him back to bed before he quite woke up, so that he should not know of the indignity to which she had subjected him. But on this occasion he had fallen at once into a dreamless sleep. One arm dropped over the edge of the bed, one leg was arched, and the unfinished part of his laugh was stranded on his mouth, which was open, showing the little pearls.
passages.vernacular: 有時,雖然不常,佢會做夢,嗰啲夢比其他男孩嘅夢更痛苦。好幾個小時佢擺脫不咗呢啲夢,雖然佢喺夢中悽慘地哭喊。我想佢哋同佢存在之謎有關。呢種時候,溫蒂嘅習慣係把佢從床上抱起嚟,把佢放喺佢腿上坐住,用佢自己發明嘅親愛嘅方式安撫佢,等佢平靜些,趁佢仲冇完全醒嚟,放回床上,咁樣佢就唔知道佢讓佢受咗咁樣嘅屈辱。但呢一次佢即刻陷入了無夢嘅瞓眠。一隻手臂垂喺床邊,一條腿拱起,佢笑到一半嘅剩餘部分擱淺喺佢嘅嘴上,嘴巴張住,露出小珍珠似嘅牙齒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有時,雖然不常,他會做夢,那些夢比其他男孩的夢更痛苦。好幾個小時他擺脫不了這些夢,雖然他在夢中悽慘地哭喊。我想它們與他存在之謎有關。這種時候,溫蒂的習慣是把他從床上抱起來,把他放在她腿上坐著,用她自己發明的親愛的方式安撫他,等他平靜些,趁他還沒完全醒來,放回床上,這樣他就不知道她讓他受了這樣的屈辱。但這一次他立刻陷入了無夢的睡眠。一隻手臂垂在床邊,一條腿拱起,他笑到一半的剩餘部分擱淺在他的嘴上,嘴巴張著,露出小珍珠似的牙齒。

passages.original: Thus defenceless Hook found him. He stood silent at the foot of the tree looking across the chamber at his enemy. Did no feeling of compassion disturb his sombre breast? The man was not wholly evil; he loved flowers (I have been told) and sweet music (he was himself no mean performer on the harpsichord); and, let it be frankly admitted, the idyllic nature of the scene stirred him profoundly. Mastered by his better self he would have returned reluctantly up the tree, but for one thing.
passages.vernacular: 虎克發現佢就係咁樣毫無防備。佢默默地站喺樹腳下,隔住房間睇住佢嘅敵人。就冇一絲憐憫之情擾亂佢陰沉嘅胸膛嗎?呢個人唔係全然邪惡;佢愛花(有人告訴我)同甜美嘅音樂(佢自己係個相當不錯嘅大鍵琴演奏者);而且,坦白承認吧,呢場景嘅田園風光深深地觸動咗佢。被佢較好嘅自己所控制,佢本來會不情願地爬回樹上,但有一件事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 虎克發現他就是這樣毫無防備。他默默地站在樹腳下,隔著房間看著他的敵人。就沒有一絲憐憫之情擾亂他陰沉的胸膛嗎?這個人不是全然邪惡;他愛花(有人告訴我)和甜美的音樂(他自己是個相當不錯的大鍵琴演奏者);而且,坦白承認吧,這場景的田園風光深深地觸動了他。被他較好的自己所控制,他本來會不情願地爬回樹上,但有一件事。

passages.original: What stayed him was Peter’s impertinent appearance as he slept. The open mouth, the drooping arm, the arched knee: they were such a personification of cockiness as, taken together, will never again, one may hope, be presented to eyes so sensitive to their offensiveness. They steeled Hook’s heart. If his rage had broken him into a hundred pieces every one of them would have disregarded the incident, and leapt at the sleeper.
passages.vernacular: 攔住佢嘅係瞓住嘅彼得嗰放肆嘅樣子。張開嘅嘴,垂下嘅手臂,拱起嘅膝蓋:佢哋合喺一起係咁一個自負嘅化身,但願再都唔會呈而家對佢哋嘅冒犯如此敏感嘅眼睛面前。佢哋使虎克嘅心變硬喇。如果佢嘅憤怒把佢撕成一百片,每一片都會無視呢個插曲,撲向瞓住嘅人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 攔住他的是睡著的彼得那放肆的樣子。張開的嘴,垂下的手臂,拱起的膝蓋:它們合在一起是這麼一個自負的化身,但願再也不會呈現在對它們的冒犯如此敏感的眼睛面前。它們使虎克的心變硬了。如果他的憤怒把他撕成一百片,每一片都會無視這個插曲,撲向睡著的人。

passages.original: Though a light from the one lamp shone dimly on the bed, Hook stood in darkness himself, and at the first stealthy step forward he discovered an obstacle, the door of Slightly’s tree. It did not entirely fill the aperture, and he had been looking over it. Feeling for the catch, he found to his fury that it was low down, beyond his reach. To his disordered brain it seemed then that the irritating quality in Peter’s face and figure visibly increased, and he rattled the door and flung himself against it. Was his enemy to escape him after all?
passages.vernacular: 雖然床上有一盞燈嘅光昏暗地照住,虎克自己站喺黑暗中,佢悄悄向前走第一步,就發現咗一個障礙,輕輕嘅樹嘅門。佢冇完全填滿開口,佢一直喺從上面睇。佢摸索門閂,憤怒地發現佢喺低處,佢夠不住。喺佢混亂嘅腦子裡,彼得臉上同身形中令人惱火嘅特質似乎明顯增加喇,佢搖晃門,用身體撞佢。佢嘅敵人到底要逃過佢咗嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 雖然床上有一盞燈的光昏暗地照著,虎克自己站在黑暗中,他悄悄向前走第一步,就發現了一個障礙,輕輕的樹的門。它沒有完全填滿開口,他一直在從上面看。他摸索門閂,憤怒地發現它在低處,他夠不著。在他混亂的腦子裡,彼得臉上和身形中令人惱火的特質似乎明顯增加了,他搖晃門,用身體撞它。他的敵人到底要逃過他了嗎?

passages.original: But what was that? The red in his eye had caught sight of Peter’s medicine standing on a ledge within easy reach. He fathomed what it was straightaway, and immediately knew that the sleeper was in his power.
passages.vernacular: 但嗰個係乜嘢?佢眼中嘅紅色睇到咗彼得嘅藥放喺一個伸手可及嘅架子上。佢即刻明白嗰個係乜嘢,即刻知道瞓住嘅人落喺佢嘅掌握中喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但那是什麼?他眼中的紅色看到了彼得的藥放在一個伸手可及的架子上。他立刻明白那是什麼,馬上知道睡著的人落在他的掌握中了。

passages.original: Lest he should be taken alive, Hook always carried about his person a dreadful drug, blended by himself of all the death-dealing rings that had come into his possession. These he had boiled down into a yellow liquid quite unknown to science, which was probably the most virulent poison in existence.
passages.vernacular: 為了避免被活捉,虎克隨身總帶住一種可怕嘅毒藥,係佢自己用佢得到嘅所有致命戒指混合而成嘅。佢把呢啲熬成一種科學上完全唔知道嘅黃色液體,嗰大概係現存最劇毒嘅毒藥。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 為了避免被活捉,虎克隨身總帶著一種可怕的毒藥,是他自己用他得到的所有致命戒指混合而成的。他把這些熬成一種科學上完全不知道的黃色液體,那大概是現存最劇毒的毒藥。

passages.original: Five drops of this he now added to Peter’s cup. His hand shook, but it was in exultation rather than in shame. As he did it he avoided glancing at the sleeper, but not lest pity should unnerve him; merely to avoid spilling. Then one long gloating look he cast upon his victim, and turning, wormed his way with difficulty up the tree. As he emerged at the top he looked the very spirit of evil breaking from its hole. Donning his hat at its most rakish angle, he wound his cloak around him, holding one end in front as if to conceal his person from the night, of which it was the blackest part, and muttering strangely to himself, stole away through the trees.
passages.vernacular: 佢而家把五滴加進彼得嘅杯子裡。佢嘅手喺顫抖,但嗰個係出於得意而唔係羞愧。佢咁樣做時,避免瞥向瞓住嘅人,但唔係怕憐憫使佢失去勇氣;只係為了避免灑出嚟。然後佢向受害者投去長長嘅得意一瞥,轉身,費力地蠕動住爬上咗樹。佢從頂部出嚟時,睇起嚟就像邪惡嘅精靈從洞裡爬出嚟。佢戴上帽子,戴成最放蕩嘅角度,把斗篷裹喺身上,一端拉喺前面,好像要把佢嘅人藏起嚟不讓夜晚睇見,佢係夜晚最黑嘅部分,奇怪地喃喃自語住,悄悄穿過樹林走喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他現在把五滴加進彼得的杯子裡。他的手在顫抖,但那是出於得意而不是羞愧。他這樣做時,避免瞥向睡著的人,但不是怕憐憫使他失去勇氣;只是為了避免灑出來。然後他向受害者投去長長的得意一瞥,轉身,費力地蠕動著爬上了樹。他從頂部出來時,看起來就像邪惡的精靈從洞裡爬出來。他戴上帽子,戴成最放蕩的角度,把斗篷裹在身上,一端拉在前面,好像要把他的人藏起來不讓夜晚看見,他是夜晚最黑的部分,奇怪地喃喃自語著,悄悄穿過樹林走了。

passages.original: Peter slept on. The light guttered and went out, leaving the tenement in darkness; but still he slept. It must have been not less than ten o’clock by the crocodile, when he suddenly sat up in his bed, wakened by he knew not what. It was a soft cautious tapping on the door of his tree.
passages.vernacular: 彼得繼續瞓。燈搖曳住熄滅喇,留下房子喺黑暗中;但佢仍然瞓住。根據鱷魚,一定係不少於十點喇,佢突然喺床上坐起嚟,被佢唔知道嘅乜嘢驚醒。係對佢嘅樹嘅門嘅輕柔而謹慎嘅敲擊聲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 彼得繼續睡。燈搖曳著熄滅了,留下房子在黑暗中;但他仍然睡著。根據鱷魚,一定是不少於十點了,他突然在床上坐起來,被他不知道的什麼驚醒。是對他的樹的門的輕柔而謹慎的敲擊聲。

passages.original: Soft and cautious, but in that stillness it was sinister. Peter felt for his dagger till his hand gripped it. Then he spoke.
passages.vernacular: 輕柔而謹慎,但喺嗰寂靜中佢係不祥嘅。彼得摸索佢嘅匕首,直到手握住咗佢。然後佢講話喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 輕柔而謹慎,但在那寂靜中它是不祥的。彼得摸索他的匕首,直到手握住了它。然後他說話了。

passages.original: “Who is that?”
passages.vernacular: 「係邊個?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是誰?」

passages.original: For long there was no answer: then again the knock.
passages.vernacular: 好久冇回答:然後又係敲門聲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 很久沒有回答:然後又是敲門聲。

passages.original: “Who are you?”
passages.vernacular: 「你係邊個?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你是誰?」

passages.original: No answer.
passages.vernacular: 冇回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒有回答。

passages.original: He was thrilled, and he loved being thrilled. In two strides he reached the door. Unlike Slightly’s door, it filled the aperture, so that he could not see beyond it, nor could the one knocking see him.
passages.vernacular: 佢興奮喇,佢鍾意興奮。兩步佢就走到門前。同輕輕嘅門不同,佢填滿咗開口,所以佢睇唔到門外,敲門嘅人都睇唔到佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他興奮了,他喜歡興奮。兩步他就走到門前。與輕輕的門不同,它填滿了開口,所以他看不到門外,敲門的人也看不到他。

passages.original: “I won’t open unless you speak,” Peter cried.
passages.vernacular: 「你不講話我不開,」彼得喊道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你不說話我不開,」彼得喊道。

passages.original: Then at last the visitor spoke, in a lovely bell-like voice.
passages.vernacular: 然後訪客終於講話喇,用一個可愛嘅鈴鐺般嘅聲音。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後訪客終於說話了,用一個可愛的鈴鐺般的聲音。

passages.original: “Let me in, Peter.”
passages.vernacular: 「讓我進去,彼得。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「讓我進去,彼得。」

passages.original: It was Tink, and quickly he unbarred to her. She flew in excitedly, her face flushed and her dress stained with mud.
passages.vernacular: 係叮,佢好快就為佢開咗閂。佢興奮地飛進嚟,臉紅紅嘅,裙子沾住泥。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是叮,他很快就為她開了閂。她興奮地飛進來,臉紅紅的,裙子沾著泥。

passages.original: “What is it?”
passages.vernacular: 「點喇?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「怎麼了?」

passages.original: “Oh, you could never guess!” she cried, and offered him three guesses. “Out with it!” he shouted, and in one ungrammatical sentence, as long as the ribbons that conjurers pull from their mouths, she told of the capture of Wendy and the boys.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,你永遠猜唔到!」佢喊道,畀咗佢三次猜嘅機會。「快講!」佢喊道,佢用一個不合語法嘅句子,像魔術師從嘴裡拉出嘅彩帶一樣長,講咗溫蒂同男孩哋被抓嘅事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,你永遠猜不到!」她喊道,給了他三次猜的機會。「快說!」他喊道,她用一個不合語法的句子,像魔術師從嘴裡拉出的彩帶一樣長,講了溫蒂和男孩們被抓的事。

passages.original: Peter’s heart bobbed up and down as he listened. Wendy bound, and on the pirate ship; she who loved everything to be just so!
passages.vernacular: 彼得聽住,心上上下下地跳。溫蒂被綁喇,喺海盜船上;佢咁愛一切都整整齊齊嘅!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 彼得聽著,心上上下下地跳。溫蒂被綁了,在海盜船上;她那麼愛一切都整整齊齊的!

passages.original: “I’ll rescue her!” he cried, leaping at his weapons. As he leapt he thought of something he could do to please her. He could take his medicine.
passages.vernacular: 「我去救佢!」佢喊道,跳向佢嘅武器。佢跳起嚟時,想到咗一件可以討佢歡心嘅事。佢可以食佢嘅藥。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我去救她!」他喊道,跳向他的武器。他跳起來時,想到了一件可以討她歡心的事。他可以吃他的藥。

passages.original: His hand closed on the fatal draught.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅手握住咗致命嘅藥水。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他的手握住了致命的藥水。

passages.original: “No!” shrieked Tinker Bell, who had heard Hook mutter about his deed as he sped through the forest.
passages.vernacular: 「不!」叮噹尖叫,佢聽到虎克喺穿過森林時喃喃講佢嘅事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不!」叮噹尖叫,她聽到虎克在穿過森林時喃喃說他的事。

passages.original: “Why not?”
passages.vernacular: 「點解不?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「為什麼不?」

passages.original: “It is poisoned.”
passages.vernacular: 「有毒。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「有毒。」

passages.original: “Poisoned? Who could have poisoned it?”
passages.vernacular: 「有毒?邊個能下毒?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「有毒?誰能下毒?」

passages.original: “Hook.”
passages.vernacular: 「虎克。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「虎克。」

passages.original: “Don’t be silly. How could Hook have got down here?”
passages.vernacular: 「別傻喇。虎克點能下到呢度?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「別傻了。虎克怎麼能下到這裡?」

passages.original: Alas, Tinker Bell could not explain this, for even she did not know the dark secret of Slightly’s tree. Nevertheless Hook’s words had left no room for doubt. The cup was poisoned.
passages.vernacular: 可惜,叮噹無法解釋呢啲,因為連佢都唔知道輕輕嘅樹嘅黑暗秘密。然而虎克嘅話唔容置疑。杯子被下毒喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可惜,叮噹無法解釋這一點,因為連她也不知道輕輕的樹的黑暗秘密。然而虎克的話不容置疑。杯子被下毒了。

passages.original: “Besides,” said Peter, quite believing himself, “I never fell asleep.”
passages.vernacular: 「而且,」彼得講,完全相信自己,「我從冇瞓住過。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「而且,」彼得說,完全相信自己,「我從沒睡著過。」

passages.original: He raised the cup. No time for words now; time for deeds; and with one of her lightning movements Tink got between his lips and the draught, and drained it to the dregs.
passages.vernacular: 佢舉起杯子。而家冇時間講話;係行動嘅時候喇;叮噹用佢閃電般嘅動作之一擋喺佢嘅嘴唇同藥水之間,把佢飲到咗最後一滴。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他舉起杯子。現在沒有時間說話;是行動的時候了;叮噹用她閃電般的動作之一擋在他的嘴唇和藥水之間,把它喝到了最後一滴。

passages.original: “Why, Tink, how dare you drink my medicine?”
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀,叮,你點敢飲我嘅藥?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀,叮,你怎麼敢喝我的藥?」

passages.original: But she did not answer. Already she was reeling in the air.
passages.vernacular: 但佢冇回答。佢已經喺空中搖搖晃晃喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但她沒有回答。她已經在空中搖搖晃晃了。

passages.original: “What is the matter with you?” cried Peter, suddenly afraid.
passages.vernacular: 「你點喇?」彼得突然害怕地喊道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你怎麼了?」彼得突然害怕地喊道。

passages.original: “It was poisoned, Peter,” she told him softly; “and now I am going to be dead.”
passages.vernacular: 「有毒,彼得,」佢輕輕地告訴佢;「而家我要死喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「有毒,彼得,」她輕輕地告訴他;「現在我要死了。」

passages.original: “O Tink, did you drink it to save me?”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,叮,你係為了救我才飲嘅嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,叮,你是為了救我才喝的嗎?」

passages.original: “Yes.”
“But why, Tink?”
passages.vernacular: 「但點解,叮?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但為什麼,叮?」

passages.original: Her wings would scarcely carry her now, but in reply she alighted on his shoulder and gave his nose a loving bite. She whispered in his ear “You silly ass,” and then, tottering to her chamber, lay down on the bed.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅翅膀而家幾乎帶不動佢喇,但作為回答,佢落喺佢肩上,愛憐地咬咗一下佢嘅鼻子。佢喺佢耳邊低語:「你呢個蠢驢,」然後搖搖晃晃走進佢嘅房間,躺喺床上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她的翅膀現在幾乎帶不動她了,但作為回答,她落在他肩上,愛憐地咬了一下他的鼻子。她在他耳邊低語:「你這個蠢驢,」然後搖搖晃晃走進她的房間,躺在床上。

passages.original: His head almost filled the fourth wall of her little room as he knelt near her in distress. Every moment her light was growing fainter; and he knew that if it went out she would be no more. She liked his tears so much that she put out her beautiful finger and let them run over it.
passages.vernacular: 佢痛苦地跪喺佢旁邊,佢嘅頭幾乎填滿咗佢小房間嘅第四面牆。佢嘅光每一刻都變得更暗;佢知道如果佢熄滅喇,佢就不喺喇。佢咁鍾意佢嘅眼淚,佢伸出美麗嘅手指,讓佢哋流過。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他痛苦地跪在她旁邊,他的頭幾乎填滿了她小房間的第四面牆。她的光每一刻都變得更暗;他知道如果它熄滅了,她就不在了。她那麼喜歡他的眼淚,她伸出美麗的手指,讓它們流過。

passages.original: Her voice was so low that at first he could not make out what she said. Then he made it out. She was saying that she thought she could get well again if children believed in fairies.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅聲音咁低,起初佢聽不清佢講乜嘢。然後佢聽出嚟喇。佢講佢認為如果細路哋相信有仙子,佢能好起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她的聲音那麼低,起初他聽不清她說什麼。然後他聽出來了。她說她認為如果孩子們相信有仙子,她能好起來。

passages.original: Peter flung out his arms. There were no children there, and it was night time; but he addressed all who might be dreaming of the Neverland, and who were therefore nearer to him than you think: boys and girls in their nighties, and naked papooses in their baskets hung from trees.
passages.vernacular: 彼得張開雙臂。嗰度冇細路,而且係夜晚;但佢向所有可能喺夢見永無島嘅人講話,佢哋因此比你想像嘅更接近佢:穿住瞓衣嘅男孩女孩,同掛喺樹上籃子裡嘅赤裸嘅印第安嬰兒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 彼得張開雙臂。那裡沒有孩子,而且是夜晚;但他向所有可能在夢見永無島的人說話,他們因此比你想像的更接近他:穿著睡衣的男孩女孩,和掛在樹上籃子裡的赤裸的印第安嬰兒。

passages.original: “Do you believe?” he cried.
passages.vernacular: 「你哋相信嗎?」佢喊道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你們相信嗎?」他喊道。

passages.original: Tink sat up in bed almost briskly to listen to her fate.
passages.vernacular: 叮噹幾乎係精神抖擻地坐喺床上聽佢嘅命運。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 叮噹幾乎是精神抖擻地坐在床上聽她的命運。

passages.original: She fancied she heard answers in the affirmative, and then again she wasn’t sure.
passages.vernacular: 佢好像聽到咗肯定嘅回答,然後又不確定。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她好像聽到了肯定的回答,然後又不確定。

passages.original: “What do you think?” she asked Peter.
passages.vernacular: 「你覺得呢?」佢問彼得。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你覺得呢?」她問彼得。

passages.original: “If you believe,” he shouted to them, “clap your hands; don’t let Tink die.”
passages.vernacular: 「如果你哋相信,」佢對佢哋喊,「就拍手;唔好畀叮死去。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「如果你們相信,」他對他們喊,「就拍手;別讓叮死去。」

passages.original: Many clapped.
passages.vernacular: 好多人拍手。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 很多人拍手。

passages.original: Some didn’t.
passages.vernacular: 有些人冇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有些人沒有。

passages.original: A few beasts hissed.
passages.vernacular: 幾隻野獸噓咗一聲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 幾隻野獸噓了一聲。

passages.original: The clapping stopped suddenly; as if countless mothers had rushed to their nurseries to see what on earth was happening; but already Tink was saved. First her voice grew strong, then she popped out of bed, then she was flashing through the room more merry and impudent than ever. She never thought of thanking those who believed, but she would have liked to get at the ones who had hissed.
passages.vernacular: 拍手聲突然停止;好像無數母親衝到佢哋嘅育兒室,睇究竟發生咗乜嘢事;但叮已經得救喇。首先佢嘅聲音變強喇,然後佢從床上彈出嚟,然後佢喺房間裡閃嚟閃去,比以往更快活更放肆。佢從冇想過要感謝嗰啲相信嘅人,但佢好想對付嗰啲噓佢嘅人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 拍手聲突然停止;好像無數母親衝到她們的育兒室,看究竟發生了什麼事;但叮已經得救了。首先她的聲音變強了,然後她從床上彈出來,然後她在房間裡閃來閃去,比以往更快活更放肆。她從沒想過要感謝那些相信的人,但她很想對付那些噓她的人。

passages.original: “And now to rescue Wendy!”
passages.vernacular: 「而家去救溫蒂!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「現在去救溫蒂!」

passages.original: The moon was riding in a cloudy heaven when Peter rose from his tree, begirt with weapons and wearing little else, to set out upon his perilous quest. It was not such a night as he would have chosen. He had hoped to fly, keeping not far from the ground so that nothing unwonted should escape his eyes; but in that fitful light to have flown low would have meant trailing his shadow through the trees, thus disturbing birds and acquainting a watchful foe that he was astir.
passages.vernacular: 月亮喺多雲嘅天空中行進,彼得從佢嘅樹中升起,全身帶住武器,幾乎冇穿別嘅,出發去執行佢危險嘅使命。呢唔係佢會選擇嘅嗰種夜晚。佢本希望飛,不離地面太遠,咁樣唔會有任何不尋常嘅嘢逃過佢嘅眼睛;但喺嗰忽明忽暗嘅光線下低飛意味住佢嘅影子會拖過樹林,從而驚動鳥類,讓警覺嘅敵人知道佢喺行動。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 月亮在多雲的天空中行進,彼得從他的樹中升起,全身帶著武器,幾乎沒穿別的,出發去執行他危險的使命。這不是他會選擇的那種夜晚。他本希望飛,不離地面太遠,這樣不會有任何不尋常的東西逃過他的眼睛;但在那忽明忽暗的光線下低飛意味著他的影子會拖過樹林,從而驚動鳥類,讓警覺的敵人知道他在行動。

passages.original: He regretted now that he had given the birds of the island such strange names that they are very wild and difficult of approach.
passages.vernacular: 佢而家後悔畀島上嘅鳥起咗咁奇怪嘅名字,以致牠哋好野,難以接近。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他現在後悔給島上的鳥起了那麼奇怪的名字,以致牠們很野,難以接近。

passages.original: There was no other course but to press forward in redskin fashion, at which happily he was an adept. But in what direction, for he could not be sure that the children had been taken to the ship? A light fall of snow had obliterated all footmarks; and a deathly silence pervaded the island, as if for a space Nature stood still in horror of the recent carnage. He had taught the children something of the forest lore that he had himself learned from Tiger Lily and Tinker Bell, and knew that in their dire hour they were not likely to forget it. Slightly, if he had an opportunity, would blaze the trees, for instance, Curly would drop seeds, and Wendy would leave her handkerchief at some important place. The morning was needed to search for such guidance, and he could not wait. The upper world had called him, but would give no help.
passages.vernacular: 冇別嘅辦法,只能以紅番嘅方式前進,幸運嘅係佢喺呢方面係個行家。但往邊個方向,因為佢唔能夠確定細路哋係咪被帶到咗船上?一場小雪抹去咗所有嘅腳印;死一般嘅寂靜籠罩全島,好像有一段時間大自然因最近嘅屠殺而驚恐地靜止不動。佢教過細路哋啲佢自己從虎百合同叮噹嗰度學到嘅森林知識,知道佢哋喺可怕嘅時刻不太可能忘記。例如,輕輕如果有機會,會喺樹上做記號,卷毛會撒種子,溫蒂會把手帕留喺某個重要嘅地方。尋找呢種指引需要早晨,而佢等不及。上面嘅世界召喚咗佢,但不畀任何幫助。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒有別的辦法,只能以紅番的方式前進,幸運的是他在這方面是個行家。但往哪個方向,因為他不能確定孩子們是否被帶到了船上?一場小雪抹去了所有的腳印;死一般的寂靜籠罩全島,好像有一段時間大自然因最近的屠殺而驚恐地靜止不動。他教過孩子們一些他自己從虎百合和叮噹那裡學到的森林知識,知道他們在可怕的時刻不太可能忘記。例如,輕輕如果有機會,會在樹上做記號,卷毛會撒種子,溫蒂會把手帕留在某個重要的地方。尋找這種指引需要早晨,而他等不及。上面的世界召喚了他,但不給任何幫助。

passages.original: The crocodile passed him, but not another living thing, not a sound, not a movement; and yet he knew well that sudden death might be at the next tree, or stalking him from behind.
passages.vernacular: 鱷魚從佢身邊經過,但冇別嘅生物,冇聲音,冇動靜;然而佢好清楚突然嘅死亡或者就喺下一棵樹旁,或者從後面悄悄逼近佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 鱷魚從他身邊經過,但沒有別的生物,沒有聲音,沒有動靜;然而他很清楚突然的死亡也許就在下一棵樹旁,或者從後面悄悄逼近他。

passages.original: He swore this terrible oath: “Hook or me this time.”
passages.vernacular: 佢發咗呢個可怕嘅誓言:「呢回唔係虎克就係我。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他發了這個可怕的誓言:「這回不是虎克就是我。」

passages.original: Now he crawled forward like a snake, and again erect, he darted across a space on which the moonlight played, one finger on his lip and his dagger at the ready. He was frightfully happy.
passages.vernacular: 而家佢像蛇一樣向前爬行,又直立起嚟,衝過月光照耀嘅一塊空地,一個指頭放喺唇上,匕首隨時準備住。佢極其快樂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在他像蛇一樣向前爬行,又直立起來,衝過月光照耀的一塊空地,一個指頭放在唇上,匕首隨時準備著。他極其快樂。

chapters.title: Chapter XIV: The Pirate Ship 第十四章:海盜船

passages.original: One green light squinting over Kidd’s Creek, which is near the mouth of the pirate river, marked where the brig, the Jolly Roger, lay, low in the water; a rakish-looking craft foul to the hull, every beam in her detestable, like ground strewn with mangled feathers. She was the cannibal of the seas, and scarce needed that watchful eye, for she floated immune in the horror of her name.
passages.vernacular: 一盞綠燈喺基德溪上斜視住,嗰度靠近海盜河嘅河口,標示住雙桅帆船快樂羅傑號停泊嘅地方,食水好低;嗰個係一艘睇起嚟放蕩不羈嘅船,船身骯髒,每一根梁都令人厭惡,像撒滿咗殘破羽毛嘅地面。佢係海上嘅食人族,幾乎不需要嗰只警惕嘅眼睛,因為佢嘅名字帶嚟嘅恐怖使佢漂浮其上而不受侵犯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一盞綠燈在基德溪上斜視著,那裡靠近海盜河的河口,標示著雙桅帆船快樂羅傑號停泊的地方,吃水很低;那是一艘看起來放蕩不羈的船,船身骯髒,每一根梁都令人厭惡,像撒滿了殘破羽毛的地面。她是海上的食人族,幾乎不需要那只警惕的眼睛,因為她的名字帶來的恐怖使她漂浮其上而不受侵犯。

passages.original: She was wrapped in the blanket of night, through which no sound from her could have reached the shore. There was little sound, and none agreeable save the whir of the ship’s sewing machine at which Smee sat, ever industrious and obliging, the essence of the commonplace, pathetic Smee. I know not why he was so infinitely pathetic, unless it were because he was so pathetically unaware of it; but even strong men had to turn hastily from looking at him, and more than once on summer evenings he had touched the fount of Hook’s tears and made it flow. Of this, as of almost everything else, Smee was quite unconscious.
passages.vernacular: 佢裹喺夜晚嘅毯子裡,佢發出嘅任何聲音都傳唔到岸上。聲音好少,而且冇一種係悅耳嘅,除咗船上縫紉機嘅嗡嗡聲,斯密坐喺嗰度,永遠勤奮而樂於助人,平庸嘅化身,可憐嘅斯密。我唔知道佢點解咁無限可憐,除非係因為佢咁可憐地不自知;但連強壯嘅男人都唔得不匆忙轉過頭不睇佢,不止一次喺夏夜裡,佢觸到咗虎克眼淚嘅源泉,使佢流出嚟。對此,像對幾乎所有其他事一樣,斯密完全冇意識。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她裹在夜晚的毯子裡,她發出的任何聲音都傳不到岸上。聲音很少,而且沒有一種是悅耳的,除了船上縫紉機的嗡嗡聲,斯密坐在那裡,永遠勤奮而樂於助人,平庸的化身,可憐的斯密。我不知道他為什麼那麼無限可憐,除非是因為他那麼可憐地不自知;但連強壯的男人也不得不匆忙轉過頭不看他,不止一次在夏夜裡,他觸到了虎克眼淚的源泉,使它流出來。對此,像對幾乎所有其他事一樣,斯密完全沒有意識。

passages.original: A few of the pirates leant over the bulwarks, drinking in the miasma of the night; others sprawled by barrels over games of dice and cards; and the exhausted four who had carried the little house lay prone on the deck, where even in their sleep they rolled skillfully to this side or that out of Hook’s reach, lest he should claw them mechanically in passing.
passages.vernacular: 幾個海盜靠喺舷牆上,吸住夜晚嘅瘴氣;其他人喺桶邊四仰八叉地玩骰子同紙牌;抬小房子嘅疲憊嘅四個人俯臥喺甲板上,即使喺瞓夢中,佢哋都熟練地滾到呢邊或嗰邊,躲開虎克嘅觸及範圍,以免佢經過時機械地抓佢哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 幾個海盜靠在舷牆上,吸著夜晚的瘴氣;其他人在桶邊四仰八叉地玩骰子和紙牌;抬小房子的疲憊的四個人俯臥在甲板上,即使在睡夢中,他們也熟練地滾到這邊或那邊,躲開虎克的觸及範圍,以免他經過時機械地抓他們。

passages.original: Hook trod the deck in thought. O man unfathomable. It was his hour of triumph. Peter had been removed for ever from his path, and all the other boys were in the brig, about to walk the plank. It was his grimmest deed since the days when he had brought Barbecue to heel; and knowing as we do how vain a tabernacle is man, could we be surprised had he now paced the deck unsteadily, bellied out by the winds of his success?
passages.vernacular: 虎克喺甲板上踱步,沉思住。哦,深不可測嘅人。呢個係佢得意嘅時刻。彼得已被永遠從佢嘅路上除掉,所有其他男孩都喺牢房裡,即將走跳板。呢個係佢自從制伏巴比克嘅日子以來最凶狠嘅行動;我哋知道人係幾咁虛幻嘅幕棚,如果佢而家喺甲板上踱步時搖搖晃晃,被成功嘅風吹得鼓起嚟,我哋能感到驚訝嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 虎克在甲板上踱步,沉思著。哦,深不可測的人。這是他得意的時刻。彼得已被永遠從他的路上除掉,所有其他男孩都在牢房裡,即將走跳板。這是他自從制伏巴比克的日子以來最凶狠的行動;我們知道人是多麼虛幻的幕棚,如果他現在在甲板上踱步時搖搖晃晃,被成功的風吹得鼓起來,我們能感到驚訝嗎?

passages.original: But there was no elation in his gait, which kept pace with the action of his sombre mind. Hook was profoundly dejected.
passages.vernacular: 但佢嘅步伐裡冇得意,同佢陰沉嘅思想節奏一致。虎克深深地沮喪。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但他的步伐裡沒有得意,與他陰沉的思想節奏一致。虎克深深地沮喪。

passages.original: He was often thus when communing with himself on board ship in the quietude of the night. It was because he was so terribly alone. This inscrutable man never felt more alone than when surrounded by his dogs. They were socially inferior to him.
passages.vernacular: 佢喺夜晚嘅寂靜中喺船上獨自思考時經常咁樣。嗰個係因為佢係咁可怕地孤獨。呢個神祕莫測嘅人被佢嘅走狗哋圍繞時,從不比嗰時更孤獨。佢哋喺社會地位上比佢低。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他在夜晚的寂靜中在船上獨自思考時經常這樣。那是因為他是那麼可怕地孤獨。這個神祕莫測的人被他的走狗們圍繞時,從不比那時更孤獨。他們在社會地位上比他低。

passages.original: Hook was not his true name. To reveal who he really was would even at this date set the country in a blaze; but as those who read between the lines must already have guessed, he had been at a famous public school; and its traditions still clung to him like garments, with which indeed they are largely concerned. Thus it was offensive to him even now to board a ship in the same dress in which he grappled her, and he still adhered in his walk to the school’s distinguished slouch. But above all he retained the passion for good form.
passages.vernacular: 虎克唔係佢嘅真名。透露佢真正是邊個,即使喺今日,都會使國家陷入烈火;但讀過字裡行間嘅人一定已經猜到,佢曾喺一所著名嘅公學;其傳統仍然像衣服一樣貼喺佢身上,實際上佢哋主要同衣服有關。因此,甚至到而家,佢登上一艘船時穿住同佢同之搏鬥時同樣嘅衣服,仍然令佢感到冒犯,佢走路時仍保持住學校嗰種高貴嘅懶散姿態。但最重要嘅係,佢保留咗對好體統嘅熱情。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 虎克不是他的真名。透露他真正是誰,即使在今天,也會使國家陷入烈火;但讀過字裡行間的人一定已經猜到,他曾在一所著名的公學;其傳統仍然像衣服一樣貼在他身上,實際上它們主要與衣服有關。因此,甚至到現在,他登上一艘船時穿著與他與之搏鬥時同樣的衣服,仍然令他感到冒犯,他走路時仍保持著學校那種高貴的懶散姿態。但最重要的是,他保留了對好體統的熱情。

passages.original: Good form! However much he may have degenerated, he still knew that this is all that really matters.
passages.vernacular: 體統!不管佢可能墮落到乜嘢程度,佢仍然知道呢個係唯一真正重要嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 體統!不管他可能墮落到什麼程度,他仍然知道這是唯一真正重要的。

passages.original: From far within him he heard a creaking as of rusty portals, and through them came a stern tap-tap-tap, like hammering in the night when one cannot sleep. “Have you been good form to-day?” was their eternal question.
passages.vernacular: 從佢內心深處,佢聽到一陣吱嘎聲,像生鏽嘅大門,透過佢哋傳嚟嚴厲嘅篤、篤、篤,像夜裡瞓不住時嘅錘擊聲。「你今日合乎體統嗎?」係佢哋永恆嘅問題。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 從他內心深處,他聽到一陣吱嘎聲,像生鏽的大門,透過它們傳來嚴厲的篤、篤、篤,像夜裡睡不著時的錘擊聲。「你今天合乎體統嗎?」是它們永恆的問題。

passages.original: “Fame, fame, that glittering bauble, it is mine,” he cried.
passages.vernacular: 「名聲,名聲,嗰閃閃發光嘅小玩意,係我嘅,」佢喊道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「名聲,名聲,那閃閃發光的小玩意,是我的,」他喊道。

passages.original: “Is it quite good form to be distinguished at anything?” the tap-tap from his school replied.
passages.vernacular: 「喺任何事上出類拔萃,算得上完全合乎體統嗎?」佢學校嘅篤篤聲回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「在任何事上出類拔萃,算得上完全合乎體統嗎?」他學校的篤篤聲回答。

passages.original: “I am the only man whom Barbecue feared,” he urged, “and Flint feared Barbecue.”
passages.vernacular: 「我係巴比克唯一怕嘅人,」佢力辯,「而弗林特怕巴比克。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我是巴比克唯一怕的人,」他力辯,「而弗林特怕巴比克。」

passages.original: “Barbecue, Flint—what house?” came the cutting retort.
passages.vernacular: 「巴比克,弗林特——邊個宿舍嘅?」尖刻嘅反駁傳嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「巴比克,弗林特——哪個宿舍的?」尖刻的反駁傳來。

passages.original: Most disquieting reflection of all, was it not bad form to think about good form?
passages.vernacular: 最令人不安嘅想法係,想住好體統本身,唔係不成體統嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 最令人不安的想法是,想著好體統本身,不是不成體統嗎?

passages.original: His vitals were tortured by this problem. It was a claw within him sharper than the iron one; and as it tore him, the perspiration dripped down his tallow countenance and streaked his doublet. Ofttimes he drew his sleeve across his face, but there was no damming that trickle.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅五臟六腑被呢個問題折磨。佢係佢體內一隻比鐵爪更鋒利嘅爪;佢撕扯佢時,汗水順住佢蠟黃嘅臉淌下嚟,喺佢嘅緊身上衣上劃出痕跡。佢常常用袖子擦臉,但嗰股汗水止不住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他的五臟六腑被這個問題折磨。它是他體內一隻比鐵爪更鋒利的爪;它撕扯他時,汗水順著他蠟黃的臉淌下來,在他的緊身上衣上劃出痕跡。他常常用袖子擦臉,但那股汗水止不住。

passages.original: Ah, envy not Hook.
passages.vernacular: 啊,別羨慕虎克。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,別羨慕虎克。

passages.original: There came to him a presentiment of his early dissolution. It was as if Peter’s terrible oath had boarded the ship. Hook felt a gloomy desire to make his dying speech, lest presently there should be no time for it.
passages.vernacular: 佢有一種預感,自己好快就要結束喇。好像彼得嘅可怕誓言已經登上咗船。虎克感到一種陰鬱嘅渴望,想發表臨終演講,以免不久之後就冇時間喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他有一種預感,自己很快就要結束了。好像彼得的可怕誓言已經登上了船。虎克感到一種陰鬱的渴望,想發表臨終演說,以免不久之後就沒有時間了。

passages.original: “Better for Hook,” he cried, “if he had had less ambition!” It was in his darkest hours only that he referred to himself in the third person.
passages.vernacular: 「對虎克來講最好,」佢喊道,「如果佢少啲野心!」只有喺佢最黑暗嘅時刻,佢才用第三人稱稱呼自己。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「對虎克來說最好,」他喊道,「如果他少一點野心!」只有在他最黑暗的時刻,他才用第三人稱稱呼自己。

passages.original: “No little children to love me!”
