passages.original: “Let us creep in,” John suggested, “and put our hands over her eyes.”
passages.vernacular: 「我哋悄悄進去,」約翰建議,「用手蒙住佢嘅眼睛。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們悄悄進去,」約翰建議,「用手蒙住她的眼睛。」

passages.original: But Wendy, who saw that they must break the joyous news more gently, had a better plan.
passages.vernacular: 但溫蒂睇出佢哋必須更溫和地宣布呢個歡樂嘅消息,佢有更好嘅計畫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但溫蒂看出他們必須更溫和地宣布這個歡樂的消息,她有更好的計畫。

passages.original: “Let us all slip into our beds, and be there when she comes in, just as if we had never been away.”
passages.vernacular: 「我哋都溜進自己嘅床,佢進嚟時就喺床上,好像我哋從冇離開過。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們都溜進自己的床,她進來時就在床上,好像我們從沒離開過。」

passages.original: And so when Mrs. Darling went back to the night-nursery to see if her husband was asleep, all the beds were occupied. The children waited for her cry of joy, but it did not come. She saw them, but she did not believe they were there. You see, she saw them in their beds so often in her dreams that she thought this was just the dream hanging around her still.
passages.vernacular: 於是達玲太太回到夜間育兒室睇丈夫係咪瞓住時,所有嘅床都有人喇。細路哋等住佢嘅歡呼,但冇嚟。佢睇到咗佢哋,但不相信佢哋喺嗰度。你睇,佢喺夢裡咁常睇到佢哋喺床上,以致佢以為呢只係仍然纏繞住佢嘅夢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是達玲太太回到夜間育兒室看丈夫是否睡著時,所有的床都有人了。孩子們等著她的歡呼,但沒有來。她看到了他們,但不相信他們在那裡。你看,她在夢裡那麼常看到他們在床上,以致她以為這只是仍然纏繞著她的夢。

passages.original: She sat down in the chair by the fire, where in the old days she had nursed them.
passages.vernacular: 佢坐喺火邊嘅椅子上,從前佢就喺嗰度餵養過佢哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她坐在火邊的椅子上,從前她就在那裡餵養過他們。

passages.original: They could not understand this, and a cold fear fell upon all the three of them.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋不明白呢個,一種寒冷嘅恐懼落喺佢哋三個人身上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們不明白這個,一種寒冷的恐懼落在他們三個人身上。

passages.original: “Mother!” Wendy cried.
passages.vernacular: 「媽媽!」溫蒂喊道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「媽媽!」溫蒂喊道。

passages.original: “That’s Wendy,” she said, but still she was sure it was the dream.
passages.vernacular: 「嗰個係溫蒂,」佢講,但仍然確信嗰個係夢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那是溫蒂,」她說,但仍然確信那是夢。

passages.original: “Mother!”
passages.vernacular: 「媽媽!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「媽媽!」

passages.original: “That’s John,” she said.
passages.vernacular: 「嗰個係約翰,」佢講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那是約翰,」她說。

passages.original: “Mother!” cried Michael. He knew her now.
passages.vernacular: 「媽媽!」邁克爾喊道。佢而家認得佢喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「媽媽!」邁克爾喊道。他現在認得她了。

passages.original: “That’s Michael,” she said, and she stretched out her arms for the three little selfish children they would never envelop again. Yes, they did, they went round Wendy and John and Michael, who had slipped out of bed and run to her.
passages.vernacular: 「嗰個係邁克爾,」佢講,向嗰三個再都擁抱唔到嘅自私小孩伸出手臂。係嘅,佢擁抱到喇,佢嘅手臂環繞住溫蒂、約翰同邁克爾,佢哋已經溜下床跑向佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那是邁克爾,」她說,向那三個再也擁抱不到的自私小孩伸出手臂。是的,她擁抱到了,她的手臂環繞著溫蒂、約翰和邁克爾,他們已經溜下床跑向她。

passages.original: “George, George!” she cried when she could speak; and Mr. Darling woke to share her bliss, and Nana came rushing in. There could not have been a lovelier sight; but there was none to see it except a little boy who was staring in at the window. He had had ecstasies innumerable that other children can never know; but he was looking through the window at the one joy from which he must be for ever barred.
passages.vernacular: 「喬治,喬治!」佢能講話時喊道;達玲先生醒嚟分享佢嘅喜悅,娜娜衝咗進嚟。唔可能有更可愛嘅景象喇;但冇人睇到佢,除咗一個站喺窗外往裡望嘅小男孩。佢經歷過無數其他細路永遠唔知道嘅狂喜;但佢正透過窗子睇住佢必須永遠被擋喺外面嘅嗰種快樂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「喬治,喬治!」她能說話時喊道;達玲先生醒來分享她的喜悅,娜娜衝了進來。不可能有更可愛的景象了;但沒有人看到它,除了一個站在窗外往裡望的小男孩。他經歷過無數其他孩子永遠不知道的狂喜;但他正透過窗子看著他必須永遠被擋在外面的那種快樂。

chapters.title: Chapter XVII: When Wendy Grew Up 第十七章:溫蒂長大以後

passages.original: I hope you want to know what became of the other boys. They were waiting below to give Wendy time to explain about them; and when they had counted five hundred they went up. They went up by the stair, because they thought this would make a better impression. They stood in a row in front of Mrs. Darling, with their hats off, and wishing they were not wearing their pirate clothes. They said nothing, but their eyes asked her to have them. They ought to have looked at Mr. Darling also, but they forgot about him.
passages.vernacular: 我希望你想知道其他男孩後來點樣喇。佢哋喺下面等住,畀溫蒂時間解釋佢哋嘅事;數咗五百下之後佢哋上去喇。佢哋走樓梯上去,因為佢哋認為咁樣會留下更好嘅印象。佢哋排成一行站喺達玲太太面前,脫咗帽子,希望自己冇穿住海盜服。佢哋乜嘢都冇講,但佢哋嘅眼睛請求佢收留佢哋。佢哋本該都睇睇達玲先生,但佢哋忘咗佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我希望你想知道其他男孩後來怎樣了。他們在下面等著,給溫蒂時間解釋他們的事;數了五百下之後他們上去了。他們走樓梯上去,因為他們認為這樣會留下更好的印象。他們排成一行站在達玲太太面前,脫了帽子,希望自己沒有穿著海盜服。他們什麼也沒說,但他們的眼睛請求她收留他們。他們本該也看看達玲先生,但他們忘了他。

passages.original: Of course Mrs. Darling said at once that she would have them; but Mr. Darling was curiously depressed, and they saw that he considered six a rather large number.
passages.vernacular: 當然達玲太太即刻講佢要收留佢哋;但達玲先生奇怪地沮喪,佢哋睇出佢認為六個係相當大嘅數目。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當然達玲太太馬上說她要收留他們;但達玲先生奇怪地沮喪,他們看出他認為六個是相當大的數目。

passages.original: “I must say,” he said to Wendy, “that you don’t do things by halves,” a grudging remark which the twins thought was pointed at them.
passages.vernacular: 「我必須講,」佢對溫蒂講,「你做事不做一半,」呢句勉強嘅話雙胞胎以為係針對佢哋嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我必須說,」他對溫蒂說,「你做事不做一半,」這句勉強的話雙胞胎以為是針對他們的。

passages.original: The first twin was the proud one, and he asked, flushing, “Do you think we should be too much of a handful, sir? Because, if so, we can go away.”
passages.vernacular: 第一個雙胞胎係驕傲嘅嗰個,佢臉紅住問:「先生,你認為我哋會太麻煩嗎?因為如果係嘅話,我哋可以走。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 第一個雙胞胎是驕傲的那個,他臉紅著問:「先生,你認為我們會太麻煩嗎?因為如果是的話,我們可以走。」

passages.original: “Father!” Wendy cried, shocked; but still the cloud was on him. He knew he was behaving unworthily, but he could not help it.
passages.vernacular: 「爸爸!」溫蒂震驚地喊道;但烏雲仍然喺佢身上。佢知道自己嘅行為不光彩,但佢忍不住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「爸爸!」溫蒂震驚地喊道;但烏雲仍然在他身上。他知道自己的行為不光彩,但他忍不住。

passages.original: “We could lie doubled up,” said Nibs.
passages.vernacular: 「我哋可以對折住躺,」尼布斯講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們可以對折著躺,」尼布斯說。

passages.original: “I always cut their hair myself,” said Wendy.
passages.vernacular: 「我總是自己畀佢哋剪頭髮,」溫蒂講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我總是自己給他們剪頭髮,」溫蒂說。

passages.original: “George!” Mrs. Darling exclaimed, pained to see her dear one showing himself in such an unfavourable light.
passages.vernacular: 「喬治!」達玲太太喊道,睇到佢嘅親人表現得咁不討好,好痛心。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「喬治!」達玲太太喊道,看到她的親人表現得這麼不討好,很痛心。

passages.original: Then he burst into tears, and the truth came out. He was as glad to have them as she was, he said, but he thought they should have asked his consent as well as hers, instead of treating him as a cypher in his own house.
passages.vernacular: 然後佢哭咗起嚟,真相講咗出嚟。佢講佢同佢一樣高興有佢哋,但佢認為佢哋應該都問佢嘅同意,而唔係喺自己家裡把佢當成零。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後他哭了起來,真相說了出來。他說他和她一樣高興有他們,但他認為他們應該也問他的同意,而不是在自己家裡把他當成零。

passages.original: “I don’t think he is a cypher,” Tootles cried instantly. “Do you think he is a cypher, Curly?”
passages.vernacular: 「我不認為佢係零,」圖圖即刻喊道。「你認為佢係零嗎,卷毛?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不認為他是零,」圖圖馬上喊道。「你認為他是零嗎,卷毛?」

passages.original: “No, I don’t. Do you think he is a cypher, Slightly?”
passages.vernacular: 「不,我不。你認為佢係零嗎,輕輕?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不,我不。你認為他是零嗎,輕輕?」

passages.original: “Rather not. Twin, what do you think?”
passages.vernacular: 「當然不。雙胞胎,你點想?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「當然不。雙胞胎,你怎麼想?」

passages.original: It turned out that not one of them thought him a cypher; and he was absurdly gratified, and said he would find space for them all in the drawing-room if they fitted in.
passages.vernacular: 結果佢哋冇一個人認為佢係零;佢荒謬地感到滿意,講如果佢哋擠得下,佢會喺客廳裡為佢哋找出空間。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 結果他們沒有一個人認為他是零;他荒謬地感到滿意,說如果他們擠得下,他會在客廳裡為他們找出空間。

passages.original: “We’ll fit in, sir,” they assured him.
passages.vernacular: 「我哋會擠得下嘅,先生,」佢哋向佢保證。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們會擠得下的,先生,」他們向他保證。

passages.original: “Then follow the leader,” he cried gaily. “Mind you, I am not sure that we have a drawing-room, but we pretend we have, and it’s all the same. Hoop la!”
passages.vernacular: 「嗰就跟住領袖,」佢愉快地喊道。「注意,我不確定我哋有客廳,但我哋假裝有,都係一樣嘅。嚯啦!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那就跟著領袖,」他愉快地喊道。「注意,我不確定我們有客廳,但我們假裝有,也是一樣的。嚯啦!」

passages.original: He went off dancing through the house, and they all cried “Hoop la!” and danced after him, searching for the drawing-room; and I forget whether they found it, but at any rate they found corners, and they all fitted in.
passages.vernacular: 佢跳住舞穿過屋子,佢哋都喊「嚯啦!」跟住佢跳舞,尋找客廳;我忘咗佢哋有冇找到,但無論如何佢哋找到咗角落,佢哋都擠得下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他跳著舞穿過屋子,他們都喊「嚯啦!」跟著他跳舞,尋找客廳;我忘了他們有沒有找到,但無論如何他們找到了角落,他們都擠得下。

passages.original: As for Peter, he saw Wendy once again before he flew away. He did not exactly come to the window, but he brushed against it in passing so that she could open it if she liked and call to him. That is what she did.
passages.vernacular: 至於彼得,佢喺飛走之前又見咗溫蒂一面。佢冇真嘅嚟到窗口,但佢經過時擦過窗子,咁樣如果佢願意,可以打開佢叫佢。佢就係咁樣做嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 至於彼得,他在飛走之前又見了溫蒂一面。他沒有真的來到窗口,但他經過時擦過窗子,這樣如果她願意,可以打開它叫他。她就是這樣做的。

passages.original: “Hullo, Wendy, good-bye,” he said.
passages.vernacular: 「喂,溫蒂,再見,」佢講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「喂,溫蒂,再見,」他說。

passages.original: “Oh dear, are you going away?”
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀,你要走咗嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀,你要走了嗎?」

passages.original: “Yes.”
“You don’t feel, Peter,” she said falteringly, “that you would like to say anything to my parents about a very sweet subject?”
passages.vernacular: 「彼得,」佢猶豫地講,「你不覺得你想對我父母講些關於一個好甜蜜嘅話題嘅話嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「彼得,」她猶豫地說,「你不覺得你想對我父母說些關於一個很甜蜜的話題的話嗎?」

passages.original: “No.”
“About me, Peter?”
passages.vernacular: 「關於我,彼得?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「關於我,彼得?」

passages.original: “No.”
Mrs. Darling came to the window, for at present she was keeping a sharp eye on Wendy. She told Peter that she had adopted all the other boys, and would like to adopt him also.
passages.vernacular: 達玲太太嚟到窗邊,因為佢目前正警惕地睇住溫蒂。佢告訴彼得,佢已經收養咗所有其他男孩,都想收養佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 達玲太太來到窗邊,因為她目前正警惕地看著溫蒂。她告訴彼得,她已經收養了所有其他男孩,也想收養他。

passages.original: “Would you send me to school?” he inquired craftily.
passages.vernacular: 「你會送我去上學嗎?」佢狡猾地問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你會送我去上學嗎?」他狡猾地問。

passages.original: “Yes.”
“And then to an office?”
passages.vernacular: 「然後去辦公室?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「然後去辦公室?」

passages.original: “I suppose so.”
passages.vernacular: 「我想係嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想是的。」

passages.original: “Soon I would be a man?”
passages.vernacular: 「不久我就會成為一個男人?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不久我就會成為一個男人?」

passages.original: “Very soon.”
passages.vernacular: 「好快。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「很快。」

passages.original: “I don’t want to go to school and learn solemn things,” he told her passionately. “I don’t want to be a man. O Wendy’s mother, if I was to wake up and feel there was a beard!”
passages.vernacular: 「我唔想上學學嚴肅嘅嘢,」佢激動地告訴佢。「我唔想成為男人。哦,溫蒂嘅媽媽,如果我醒嚟覺得有咗鬍子!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不想上學學嚴肅的東西,」他激動地告訴她。「我不想成為男人。哦,溫蒂的媽媽,如果我醒來覺得有了鬍子!」

passages.original: “Peter,” said Wendy the comforter, “I should love you in a beard;” and Mrs. Darling stretched out her arms to him, but he repulsed her.
passages.vernacular: 「彼得,」安慰人嘅溫蒂講,「我會愛有鬍子嘅你;」達玲太太向佢伸出手臂,但佢把佢推開。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「彼得,」安慰人的溫蒂說,「我會愛有鬍子的你;」達玲太太向他伸出手臂,但他把她推開。

passages.original: “Keep back, lady, no one is going to catch me and make me a man.”
passages.vernacular: 「退後,女士,冇人會抓住我把我變成男人。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「退後,女士,沒有人會抓住我把我變成男人。」

passages.original: “But where are you going to live?”
passages.vernacular: 「但你要住喺邊度?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但你要住在哪裡?」

passages.original: “With Tink in the house we built for Wendy. The fairies are to put it high up among the tree tops where they sleep at nights.”
passages.vernacular: 「同叮一起住喺我哋為溫蒂建嘅房子裡。仙子哋要把佢放喺高高嘅樹梢上,佢哋晚上瞓覺嘅地方。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「同叮一起住在我們為溫蒂建的房子裡。仙子們要把它放在高高的樹梢上,她們晚上睡覺的地方。」

passages.original: “How lovely,” cried Wendy so longingly that Mrs. Darling tightened her grip.
passages.vernacular: 「多可愛,」溫蒂咁渴望地喊道,達玲太太握緊咗佢嘅手。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「多可愛,」溫蒂那麼渴望地喊道,達玲太太握緊了她的手。

passages.original: “I thought all the fairies were dead,” Mrs. Darling said.
passages.vernacular: 「我以為仙子都死喇,」達玲太太講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我以為仙子都死了,」達玲太太說。

passages.original: “There are always a lot of young ones,” explained Wendy, who was now quite an authority, “because you see when a new baby laughs for the first time a new fairy is born, and as there are always new babies there are always new fairies. They live in nests on the tops of trees; and the mauve ones are boys and the white ones are girls, and the blue ones are just little sillies who are not sure what they are.”
passages.vernacular: 「總是有好多年輕嘅,」溫蒂解釋,佢而家相當係個權威,「因為你睇,新嬰兒第一次笑嘅時候,就有一個新仙子誕生,而總是有新嬰兒,所以總是有新仙子。佢哋住喺樹頂嘅巢裡;淡紫色嘅係男孩,白色嘅係女孩,藍色嘅只係不確定自己係乜嘢嘅小傻瓜。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「總是有很多年輕的,」溫蒂解釋,她現在相當是個權威,「因為你看,新嬰兒第一次笑的時候,就有一個新仙子誕生,而總是有新嬰兒,所以總是有新仙子。她們住在樹頂的巢裡;淡紫色的是男孩,白色的是女孩,藍色的只是不確定自己是什麼的小傻瓜。」

passages.original: “I shall have such fun,” said Peter, with eye on Wendy.
passages.vernacular: 「我會玩得好開心,」彼得講,眼睛睇住溫蒂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我會玩得很開心,」彼得說,眼睛看著溫蒂。

passages.original: “It will be rather lonely in the evening,” she said, “sitting by the fire.”
passages.vernacular: 「晚上會相當孤單,」佢講,「坐喺火邊。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「晚上會相當孤單,」她說,「坐在火邊。」

passages.original: “I shall have Tink.”
passages.vernacular: 「我有叮。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我有叮。」

passages.original: “Tink can’t go a twentieth part of the way round,” she reminded him a little tartly.
passages.vernacular: 「叮連二十分之一嘅路都走不喇,」佢有點尖刻地提醒佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「叮連二十分之一的路都走不了,」她有點尖刻地提醒他。

passages.original: “Sneaky tell-tale!” Tink called out from somewhere round the corner.
passages.vernacular: 「愛告密嘅!」叮從拐角某處喊道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「愛告密的!」叮從拐角某處喊道。

passages.original: “It doesn’t matter,” Peter said.
passages.vernacular: 「冇關係,」彼得講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「沒關係,」彼得說。

passages.original: “O Peter, you know it matters.”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,彼得,你知道有關係。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,彼得,你知道有關係。」

passages.original: “Well, then, come with me to the little house.”
passages.vernacular: 「咁,同我去小房子吧。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那麼,同我去小房子吧。」

passages.original: “May I, mummy?”
passages.vernacular: 「我可以嗎,媽咪?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我可以嗎,媽咪?」

passages.original: “Certainly not. I have got you home again, and I mean to keep you.”
passages.vernacular: 「當然不行。我讓你哋回到家喇,我打算留住你。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「當然不行。我讓你們回到家了,我打算留住你。」

passages.original: “But he does so need a mother.”
passages.vernacular: 「但佢真嘅需要一個母親。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但他真的需要一個母親。」

passages.original: “So do you, my love.”
passages.vernacular: 「你都需要,我嘅愛。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你也需要,我的愛。」

passages.original: “Oh, all right,” Peter said, as if he had asked her from politeness merely; but Mrs. Darling saw his mouth twitch, and she made this handsome offer: to let Wendy go to him for a week every year to do his spring cleaning. Wendy would have preferred a more permanent arrangement; and it seemed to her that spring would be long in coming; but this promise sent Peter away quite gay again. He had no sense of time, and was so full of adventures that all I have told you about him is only a halfpenny-worth of them. I suppose it was because Wendy knew this that her last words to him were these rather plaintive ones:
passages.vernacular: 「哦,好吧,」彼得講,好像佢請佢只係出於禮貌;但達玲太太睇到佢嘅嘴抽動,佢作咗呢個慷慨嘅提議:讓溫蒂每年去佢嗰度一個星期,幫佢做春季大掃除。溫蒂本來寧願有一個更長久嘅安排;而且喺佢睇來春天會好久才嚟;但呢個承諾使彼得又快活地走喇。佢冇時間感,充滿咗冒險,我告訴你嘅關於佢嘅一切,只係其中半便士嘅價值。我想正因為溫蒂知道呢啲,佢對佢講嘅最後一句話係呢啲相當哀怨嘅話:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,好吧,」彼得說,好像他請她只是出於禮貌;但達玲太太看到他的嘴抽動,她作了這個慷慨的提議:讓溫蒂每年去他那裡一個星期,幫他做春季大掃除。溫蒂本來寧願有一個更長久的安排;而且在她看來春天會很久才來;但這個承諾使彼得又快活地走了。他沒有時間感,充滿了冒險,我告訴你的關於他的一切,只是其中半便士的價值。我想正因為溫蒂知道這一點,她對他說的最後一句話是這些相當哀怨的話:

passages.original: “You won’t forget me, Peter, will you, before spring cleaning time comes?”
passages.vernacular: 「你唔會忘咗我吧,彼得,喺春季大掃除嘅時間嚟到之前?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你不會忘了我吧,彼得,在春季大掃除的時間來到之前?」

passages.original: Of course Peter promised; and then he flew away. He took Mrs. Darling’s kiss with him. The kiss that had been for no one else, Peter took quite easily. Funny. But she seemed satisfied.
passages.vernacular: 當然彼得答應喇;然後佢飛走喇。佢帶走咗達玲太太嘅吻。嗰個不屬於其他任何人嘅吻,彼得輕易地攞走喇。有趣。但佢似乎滿意喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當然彼得答應了;然後他飛走了。他帶走了達玲太太的吻。那個不屬於其他任何人的吻,彼得輕易地拿走了。有趣。但她似乎滿意了。

passages.original: Of course all the boys went to school; and most of them got into Class III, but Slightly was put first into Class IV and then into Class V. Class I is the top class. Before they had attended school a week they saw what goats they had been not to remain on the island; but it was too late now, and soon they settled down to being as ordinary as you or me or Jenkins minor. It is sad to have to say that the power to fly gradually left them. At first Nana tied their feet to the bed-posts so that they should not fly away in the night; and one of their diversions by day was to pretend to fall off buses; but by and by they ceased to tug at their bonds in bed, and found that they hurt themselves when they let go of the bus. In time they could not even fly after their hats. Want of practice, they called it; but what it really meant was that they no longer believed.
passages.vernacular: 當然所有男孩都去上學;佢哋大多進咗三年級,但輕輕先被安排進四年級,然後五年級。一年級係最高班級。上學唔到一個星期,佢哋就明白咗不留喺島上係幾咁蠢;但而家太遲喇,不久佢哋安頓下嚟,變得像你我或小詹金斯一樣普通。令人傷心嘅係,飛行嘅能力逐漸離開咗佢哋。起初娜娜把佢哋嘅腳拴喺床柱上,以免佢哋夜裡飛走;佢哋白天嘅消遣之一係假裝從巴士上掉下嚟;但不久佢哋喺床上唔再拉扯束縛,發現佢哋從巴士上鬆手時會受傷。時間久喇,佢哋連追帽子都飛不起嚟喇。佢哋稱之為缺乏練習;但呢真正嘅意思係佢哋唔再相信喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當然所有男孩都去上學;他們大多進了三年級,但輕輕先被安排進四年級,然後五年級。一年級是最高班級。上學不到一個星期,他們就明白了不留在島上是多麼蠢;但現在太遲了,不久他們安頓下來,變得像你我或小詹金斯一樣普通。令人傷心的是,飛行的能力逐漸離開了他們。起初娜娜把他們的腳拴在床柱上,以免他們夜裡飛走;他們白天的消遣之一是假裝從巴士上掉下來;但不久他們在床上不再拉扯束縛,發現他們從巴士上鬆手時會受傷。時間久了,他們連追帽子也飛不起來了。他們稱之為缺乏練習;但這真正的意思是他們不再相信了。

passages.original: Michael believed longer than the other boys, though they jeered at him; so he was with Wendy when Peter came for her at the end of the first year. She flew away with Peter in the frock she had woven from leaves and berries in the Neverland, and her one fear was that he might notice how short it had become; but he never noticed, he had so much to say about himself.
passages.vernacular: 邁克爾比其他男孩相信嘅時間更長,雖然佢哋嘲笑佢;所以第一年末彼得嚟接溫蒂時,佢同溫蒂喺一起。佢穿住佢喺永無島用樹葉同漿果織成嘅裙子同彼得飛走喇,佢唯一嘅擔心係佢可能注意到佢變得多短;但佢從冇注意,佢有太多關於自己嘅話要講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 邁克爾比其他男孩相信的時間更長,雖然他們嘲笑他;所以第一年末彼得來接溫蒂時,他同溫蒂在一起。她穿著她在永無島用樹葉和漿果織成的裙子同彼得飛走了,她唯一的擔心是他可能注意到它變得多短;但他從沒注意,他有太多關於自己的話要說。

passages.original: She had looked forward to thrilling talks with him about old times, but new adventures had crowded the old ones from his mind.
passages.vernacular: 佢曾期待同佢進行關於舊時光嘅激動人心嘅談話,但新嘅冒險已經把舊嘅擠出咗佢嘅腦子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她曾期待同他進行關於舊時光的激動人心的談話,但新的冒險已經把舊的擠出了他的腦子。

passages.original: “Who is Captain Hook?” he asked with interest when she spoke of the arch enemy.
passages.vernacular: 「邊個係虎克船長?」佢提到死敵時,佢感興趣地問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「誰是虎克船長?」她提到死敵時,他感興趣地問。

passages.original: “Don’t you remember,” she asked, amazed, “how you killed him and saved all our lives?”
passages.vernacular: 「你不記得咗嗎,」佢驚訝地問,「你點樣殺咗佢,救咗我哋所有人嘅命?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你不記得了嗎,」她驚訝地問,「你怎樣殺了他,救了我們所有人的命?」

passages.original: “I forget them after I kill them,” he replied carelessly.
passages.vernacular: 「我殺咗佢哋以後就忘咗佢哋,」佢隨便地回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我殺了他們以後就忘了他們,」他隨便地回答。

passages.original: When she expressed a doubtful hope that Tinker Bell would be glad to see her he said, “Who is Tinker Bell?”
passages.vernacular: 佢猶疑地表示希望叮噹會高興見到佢時,佢講:「邊個係叮噹?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她猶疑地表示希望叮噹會高興見到她時,他說:「誰是叮噹?」

passages.original: “O Peter,” she said, shocked; but even when she explained he could not remember.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,彼得,」佢震驚地講;但即使佢解釋喇,佢都想不起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,彼得,」她震驚地說;但即使她解釋了,他也想不起來。

passages.original: “There are such a lot of them,” he said. “I expect she is no more.”
passages.vernacular: 「有咁多咁樣嘅人,」佢講。「我想佢不喺喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「有那麼多這樣的人,」他說。「我想她不在了。」

passages.original: I expect he was right, for fairies don’t live long, but they are so little that a short time seems a good while to them.
passages.vernacular: 我想佢係對嘅,因為仙子活不長,但佢哋咁小,一小段時間對佢哋來講似乎係好久。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想他是對的,因為仙子活不長,但她們那麼小,一小段時間對她們來說似乎是很久。

passages.original: Wendy was pained too to find that the past year was but as yesterday to Peter; it had seemed such a long year of waiting to her. But he was exactly as fascinating as ever, and they had a lovely spring cleaning in the little house on the tree tops.
passages.vernacular: 溫蒂都痛心地發現,對彼得來講,過去嘅一年只像尋日;對佢來講,嗰似乎係漫長嘅等待嘅一年。但佢同以往一樣迷人,佢哋喺樹頂上嘅小房子裡有咗一次可愛嘅春季大掃除。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 溫蒂也痛心地發現,對彼得來說,過去的一年只像昨天;對她來說,那似乎是漫長的等待的一年。但他和以往一樣迷人,他們在樹頂上的小房子裡有了一次可愛的春季大掃除。

passages.original: Next year he did not come for her. She waited in a new frock because the old one simply would not meet; but he never came.
passages.vernacular: 第二年佢冇嚟接佢。佢穿住新裙子等住,因為舊嘅實在扣不上;但佢始終冇嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 第二年他沒有來接她。她穿著新裙子等著,因為舊的實在扣不上;但他始終沒來。

passages.original: “Perhaps he is ill,” Michael said.
passages.vernacular: 「或者佢病喇,」邁克爾講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「也許他病了,」邁克爾說。

passages.original: “You know he is never ill.”
passages.vernacular: 「你知道佢從不生病。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你知道他從不生病。」

passages.original: Michael came close to her and whispered, with a shiver, “Perhaps there is no such person, Wendy!” and then Wendy would have cried if Michael had not been crying.
passages.vernacular: 邁克爾靠近佢,顫抖住低聲講:「或者根本冇呢個人,溫蒂!」嗰時如果邁克爾冇喺哭,溫蒂就會哭喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 邁克爾靠近她,顫抖著低聲說:「也許根本沒有這個人,溫蒂!」那時如果邁克爾沒在哭,溫蒂就會哭了。

passages.original: Peter came next spring cleaning; and the strange thing was that he never knew he had missed a year.
passages.vernacular: 彼得喺下一個春季大掃除嚟喇;奇怪嘅係佢從唔知道自己錯過咗一年。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 彼得在下一個春季大掃除來了;奇怪的是他從不知道自己錯過了一年。

passages.original: That was the last time the girl Wendy ever saw him. For a little longer she tried for his sake not to have growing pains; and she felt she was untrue to him when she got a prize for general knowledge. But the years came and went without bringing the careless boy; and when they met again Wendy was a married woman, and Peter was no more to her than a little dust in the box in which she had kept her toys. Wendy was grown up. You need not be sorry for her. She was one of the kind that likes to grow up. In the end she grew up of her own free will a day quicker than other girls.
passages.vernacular: 嗰個係女孩溫蒂最後一次見到佢。有一段時間,佢為了佢試圖唔好有成長嘅痛苦;佢得咗一般常識獎時,覺得對不起佢。但歲月嚟去,冇帶嚟嗰個漫不經心嘅男孩;佢哋再見面時,溫蒂係個已婚婦女,彼得對佢來講不過係佢放玩具嘅盒子裡嘅啲灰塵。溫蒂長大喇。你唔使為佢難過。佢係嗰種鍾意長大嘅人。最後佢出於自己嘅自由意志,比其他女孩早一天長大。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那是女孩溫蒂最後一次見到他。有一段時間,她為了他試圖不要有成長的痛苦;她得了一般常識獎時,覺得對不起他。但歲月來去,沒有帶來那個漫不經心的男孩;他們再見面時,溫蒂是個已婚婦女,彼得對她來說不過是她放玩具的盒子裡的一點灰塵。溫蒂長大了。你不必為她難過。她是那種喜歡長大的人。最後她出於自己的自由意志,比其他女孩早一天長大。

passages.original: All the boys were grown up and done for by this time; so it is scarcely worth while saying anything more about them. You may see the twins and Nibs and Curly any day going to an office, each carrying a little bag and an umbrella. Michael is an engine-driver. Slightly married a lady of title, and so he became a lord. You see that judge in a wig coming out at the iron door? That used to be Tootles. The bearded man who doesn’t know any story to tell his children was once John.
passages.vernacular: 呢陣所有男孩都長大完蛋喇;所以幾乎不值得再多講佢哋嘅事。你可以睇到雙胞胎、尼布斯同卷毛每天去辦公室,每人帶住一個小包同一把雨傘。邁克爾係火車司機。輕輕娶咗一位有爵位嘅女士,於是成咗勳爵。你睇到嗰個戴假髮嘅法官從鐵門出嚟嗎?嗰個曾經係圖圖。嗰個冇任何故事講畀細路哋聽嘅鬍子男人曾經係約翰。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這時所有男孩都長大完蛋了;所以幾乎不值得再多說他們的事。你可以看到雙胞胎、尼布斯和卷毛每天去辦公室,每人帶著一個小包和一把雨傘。邁克爾是火車司機。輕輕娶了一位有爵位的女士,於是成了勳爵。你看到那個戴假髮的法官從鐵門出來嗎?那個曾經是圖圖。那個沒有任何故事講給孩子們聽的鬍子男人曾經是約翰。

passages.original: Wendy was married in white with a pink sash. It is strange to think that Peter did not alight in the church and forbid the banns.
passages.vernacular: 溫蒂結婚時穿白色,繫粉紅色腰帶。想想彼得竟冇降落喺教堂裡阻止婚禮,真奇怪。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 溫蒂結婚時穿白色,繫粉紅色腰帶。想想彼得竟沒有降落在教堂裡阻止婚禮,真奇怪。

passages.original: Years rolled on again, and Wendy had a daughter. This ought not to be written in ink but in a golden splash.
passages.vernacular: 歲月又流逝,溫蒂有咗一個女兒。呢不該用墨水寫,而該用金色嘅飛濺寫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 歲月又流逝,溫蒂有了一個女兒。這不該用墨水寫,而該用金色的飛濺寫。

passages.original: She was called Jane, and always had an odd inquiring look, as if from the moment she arrived on the mainland she wanted to ask questions. When she was old enough to ask them they were mostly about Peter Pan. She loved to hear of Peter, and Wendy told her all she could remember in the very nursery from which the famous flight had taken place. It was Jane’s nursery now, for her father had bought it at the three per cents from Wendy’s father, who was no longer fond of stairs. Mrs. Darling was now dead and forgotten.
passages.vernacular: 佢叫珍,總是有一種奇怪嘅好奇神情,好像從佢嚟到大陸嘅嗰一刻起就想問問題。佢長到能問問題嘅年紀時,問題大多係關於彼得潘嘅。佢鍾意聽彼得嘅事,溫蒂把佢能記得嘅一切告訴佢,就喺嗰個著名飛行發生嘅育兒室裡。而家呢個係珍嘅育兒室喇,因為佢嘅父親以百分之三嘅利息從溫蒂嘅父親嗰度買咗下嚟,佢父親唔再鍾意爬樓梯。達玲太太而家去世喇,被遺忘喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她叫珍,總是有一種奇怪的好奇神情,好像從她來到大陸的那一刻起就想問問題。她長到能問問題的年紀時,問題大多是關於彼得潘的。她喜歡聽彼得的事,溫蒂把她能記得的一切告訴她,就在那個著名飛行發生的育兒室裡。現在這是珍的育兒室了,因為她的父親以百分之三的利息從溫蒂的父親那裡買了下來,她父親不再喜歡爬樓梯。達玲太太現在去世了,被遺忘了。

passages.original: There were only two beds in the nursery now, Jane’s and her nurse’s; and there was no kennel, for Nana also had passed away. She died of old age, and at the end she had been rather difficult to get on with; being very firmly convinced that no one knew how to look after children except herself.
passages.vernacular: 育兒室裡而家只有兩張床,珍嘅同佢保姆嘅;而且冇狗窩,因為娜娜都逝世喇。佢死於老年,到最後佢相當難相處;佢好堅定地相信除咗佢自己冇人懂得照顧細路。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 育兒室裡現在只有兩張床,珍的和她保姆的;而且沒有狗窩,因為娜娜也逝世了。她死於老年,到最後她相當難相處;她非常堅定地相信除了她自己沒有人懂得照顧孩子。

passages.original: Once a week Jane’s nurse had her evening off; and then it was Wendy’s part to put Jane to bed. That was the time for stories. It was Jane’s invention to raise the sheet over her mother’s head and her own, thus making a tent, and in the awful darkness to whisper:
passages.vernacular: 每週一次珍嘅保姆晚上休息;嗰時畀珍上床就係溫蒂嘅事。嗰個係講故事嘅時間。把被單舉過母親同自己嘅頭,咁樣做成帳篷,喺可怕嘅黑暗中低聲講話,呢個係珍嘅發明:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 每週一次珍的保姆晚上休息;那時給珍上床就是溫蒂的事。那是講故事的時間。把被單舉過母親和自己的頭,這樣做成帳篷,在可怕的黑暗中低聲說話,這是珍的發明:

passages.original: “What do we see now?”
passages.vernacular: 「我哋而家睇到乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們現在看到什麼?」

passages.original: “I don’t think I see anything to-night,” says Wendy, with a feeling that if Nana were here she would object to further conversation.
passages.vernacular: 「我想今晚乜嘢都睇唔到,」溫蒂講,覺得如果娜娜喺呢度,佢會反對進一步交談。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想今晚什麼也看不到,」溫蒂說,覺得如果娜娜在這裡,她會反對進一步交談。

passages.original: “Yes, you do,” says Jane, “you see when you were a little girl.”
passages.vernacular: 「睇得到,」珍講,「你睇到你定係小女孩嘅時候。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「看得到,」珍說,「你看到你還是小女孩的時候。」

passages.original: “That is a long time ago, sweetheart,” says Wendy. “Ah me, how time flies!”
passages.vernacular: 「嗰個係好久以前喇,寶貝,」溫蒂講。「唉,時間過得多快!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那是很久以前了,寶貝,」溫蒂說。「唉,時間過得多快!」

passages.original: “Does it fly,” asks the artful child, “the way you flew when you were a little girl?”
passages.vernacular: 「佢會飛嗎,」狡猾嘅細路問,「像你小時候飛嘅嗰樣?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「它會飛嗎,」狡猾的孩子問,「像你小時候飛的那樣?」

passages.original: “The way I flew? Do you know, Jane, I sometimes wonder whether I ever did really fly.”
passages.vernacular: 「像我飛嘅嗰樣?你知道嗎,珍,我有時想知道我係咪真嘅飛過。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「像我飛的那樣?你知道嗎,珍,我有時想知道我是否真的飛過。」

passages.original: “Yes, you did.”
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,你飛過。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,你飛過。」

passages.original: “The dear old days when I could fly!”
passages.vernacular: 「我能飛嘅親愛嘅舊日子!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我能飛的親愛的舊日子!」

passages.original: “Why can’t you fly now, mother?”
passages.vernacular: 「媽媽,你點解而家唔能夠飛?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「媽媽,你為什麼現在不能飛?」

passages.original: “Because I am grown up, dearest. When people grow up they forget the way.”
passages.vernacular: 「因為我長大喇,寶貝。人長大咗就忘咗方法。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「因為我長大了,寶貝。人長大了就忘了方法。」

passages.original: “Why do they forget the way?”
passages.vernacular: 「佢哋點解忘咗方法?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他們為什麼忘了方法?」

passages.original: “Because they are no longer gay and innocent and heartless. It is only the gay and innocent and heartless who can fly.”
passages.vernacular: 「因為佢哋唔再快樂、無邪、無情喇。只有快樂、無邪、無情嘅人才能飛。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「因為他們不再快樂、無邪、無情了。只有快樂、無邪、無情的人才能飛。」

passages.original: “What is gay and innocent and heartless? I do wish I were gay and innocent and heartless.”
passages.vernacular: 「乜嘢係快樂、無邪、無情?我真希望我係快樂、無邪、無情嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「什麼是快樂、無邪、無情?我真希望我是快樂、無邪、無情的。」

passages.original: Or perhaps Wendy admits she does see something.
passages.vernacular: 或者或者溫蒂承認佢確實睇到咗乜嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 或者也許溫蒂承認她確實看到了什麼。

passages.original: “I do believe,” she says, “that it is this nursery.”
passages.vernacular: 「我確實相信,」佢講,「就係呢個育兒室。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我確實相信,」她說,「就是這個育兒室。」

passages.original: “I do believe it is,” says Jane. “Go on.”
passages.vernacular: 「我確實相信係,」珍講。「繼續。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我確實相信是,」珍說。「繼續。」

passages.original: They are now embarked on the great adventure of the night when Peter flew in looking for his shadow.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋而家踏上咗彼得飛進嚟尋找佢嘅影子嗰晚嘅偉大冒險。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們現在踏上了彼得飛進來尋找他的影子那晚的偉大冒險。

passages.original: “The foolish fellow,” says Wendy, “tried to stick it on with soap, and when he could not he cried, and that woke me, and I sewed it on for him.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗰個傻瓜,」溫蒂講,「想用肥皂把佢黏上去,黏不上時佢哭喇,嗰吵醒咗我,我就畀佢縫上去喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那個傻瓜,」溫蒂說,「想用肥皂把它黏上去,黏不上時他哭了,那吵醒了我,我就給他縫上去了。」

passages.original: “You have missed a bit,” interrupts Jane, who now knows the story better than her mother. “When you saw him sitting on the floor crying, what did you say?”
passages.vernacular: 「你漏咗啲,」珍打斷,佢而家比母親更熟悉呢個故事。「你睇到佢坐喺地板上哭時,你講咗乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你漏了一點,」珍打斷,她現在比母親更熟悉這個故事。「你看到他坐在地板上哭時,你說了什麼?」

passages.original: “I sat up in bed and I said, ‘Boy, why are you crying?’”
passages.vernacular: 「我喺床上坐起來講:『男孩,你點解哭?』」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我在床上坐起來說:『男孩,你為什麼哭?』」

passages.original: “Yes, that was it,” says Jane, with a big breath.
passages.vernacular: 「對,就係咁樣,」珍講,深吸一口氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「對,就是這樣,」珍說,深吸一口氣。

passages.original: “And then he flew us all away to the Neverland and the fairies and the pirates and the redskins and the mermaids’ lagoon, and the home under the ground, and the little house.”
passages.vernacular: 「然後佢帶我哋飛去永無島,同仙子、海盜、紅番、美人魚潟湖、地下嘅家,同小房子。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「然後他帶我們飛去永無島,和仙子、海盜、紅番、美人魚潟湖、地下的家,和小房子。」

passages.original: “Yes! which did you like best of all?”
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅!你最鍾意邊一個?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的!你最喜歡哪一個?」

passages.original: “I think I liked the home under the ground best of all.”
passages.vernacular: 「我想我最鍾意地下嘅家。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想我最喜歡地下的家。」

passages.original: “Yes, so do I. What was the last thing Peter ever said to you?”
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,我都係。彼得對你講嘅最後一句話係乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,我也是。彼得對你說的最後一句話是什麼?」

passages.original: “The last thing he ever said to me was, ‘Just always be waiting for me, and then some night you will hear me crowing.’”
passages.vernacular: 「佢對我講嘅最後一句話係:『只要一直等住我,然後某天夜裡你會聽到我嘅啼叫。』」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他對我說的最後一句話是:『只要一直等著我,然後某天夜裡你會聽到我的啼叫。』」

passages.original: “Yes.”
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的。」

passages.original: “But, alas, he forgot all about me,” Wendy said it with a smile. She was as grown up as that.
passages.vernacular: 「但係,唉,佢完全忘咗我,」溫蒂微笑住講。佢已經長大到呢個地步。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但是,唉,他完全忘了我,」溫蒂微笑著說。她已經長大到這個地步。

passages.original: “What did his crow sound like?” Jane asked one evening.
passages.vernacular: 「佢嘅啼叫聽起嚟像乜嘢?」一天晚上珍問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他的啼叫聽起來像什麼?」一天晚上珍問。

passages.original: “It was like this,” Wendy said, trying to imitate Peter’s crow.
passages.vernacular: 「像咁樣,」溫蒂講,試圖模仿彼得嘅啼叫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「像這樣,」溫蒂說,試圖模仿彼得的啼叫。

passages.original: “No, it wasn’t,” Jane said gravely, “it was like this;” and she did it ever so much better than her mother.
passages.vernacular: 「不,唔係,」珍嚴肅地講,「係像咁樣;」佢做得比母親好得多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不,不是,」珍嚴肅地說,「是像這樣;」她做得比母親好得多。

passages.original: Wendy was a little startled. “My darling, how can you know?”
passages.vernacular: 溫蒂有些食驚。「寶貝,你點會知道?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 溫蒂有些吃驚。「寶貝,你怎麼會知道?」

passages.original: “I often hear it when I am sleeping,” Jane said.
passages.vernacular: 「我瞓覺時常聽到,」珍講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我睡覺時常聽到,」珍說。

passages.original: “Ah yes, many girls hear it when they are sleeping, but I was the only one who heard it awake.”
passages.vernacular: 「啊,係嘅,許多女孩瞓覺時都聽到,但我係唯一醒住聽到嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「啊,是的,許多女孩睡覺時都聽到,但我是唯一醒著聽到的。」

passages.original: “Lucky you,” said Jane.
passages.vernacular: 「你真幸運,」珍講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你真幸運,」珍說。

passages.original: And then one night came the tragedy. It was the spring of the year, and the story had been told for the night, and Jane was now asleep in her bed. Wendy was sitting on the floor, very close to the fire, so as to see to darn, for there was no other light in the nursery; and while she sat darning she heard a crow. Then the window blew open as of old, and Peter dropped in on the floor.
passages.vernacular: 然後有一晚悲劇嚟喇。嗰個係一年嘅春天,故事已經講完咗呢晚嘅,珍而家喺床上瞓住喇。溫蒂坐喺地板上,好靠近火,以便睇清補衣服,因為育兒室裡冇別嘅光;佢坐住補衣服時,聽到一聲啼叫。然後窗子像從前一樣被吹開,彼得落喺地板上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後有一晚悲劇來了。那是一年的春天,故事已經講完了這晚的,珍現在在床上睡著了。溫蒂坐在地板上,很靠近火,以便看清補衣服,因為育兒室裡沒有別的光;她坐著補衣服時,聽到一聲啼叫。然後窗子像從前一樣被吹開,彼得落在地板上。

passages.original: He was exactly the same as ever, and Wendy saw at once that he still had all his first teeth.
passages.vernacular: 佢同以往完全一樣,溫蒂即刻睇出佢仍然有全部嘅乳牙。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他和以往完全一樣,溫蒂馬上看出他仍然有全部的乳牙。

passages.original: He was a little boy, and she was grown up. She huddled by the fire not daring to move, helpless and guilty, a big woman.
passages.vernacular: 佢係個小男孩,而佢長大喇。佢縮喺火邊唔敢動,無助而有罪,一個大女人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他是個小男孩,而她長大了。她縮在火邊不敢動,無助而有罪,一個大女人。

passages.original: “Hullo, Wendy,” he said, not noticing any difference, for he was thinking chiefly of himself; and in the dim light her white dress might have been the nightgown in which he had seen her first.
passages.vernacular: 「喂,溫蒂,」佢講,冇注意到任何差別,因為佢主要想住自己;喺昏暗嘅光線下,佢嘅白裙子可能就係佢第一次見到佢時穿嘅瞓袍。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「喂,溫蒂,」他說,沒有注意到任何差別,因為他主要想著自己;在昏暗的光線下,她的白裙子可能就是他第一次見到她時穿的睡袍。

passages.original: “Hullo, Peter,” she replied faintly, squeezing herself as small as possible. Something inside her was crying “Woman, Woman, let go of me.”
passages.vernacular: 「喂,彼得,」佢微弱地回答,盡量把自己縮到最小。佢裡面有個嘢喺哭喊:「女人,女人,放開我。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「喂,彼得,」她微弱地回答,盡量把自己縮到最小。她裡面有個東西在哭喊:「女人,女人,放開我。」

passages.original: “Hullo, where is John?” he asked, suddenly missing the third bed.
passages.vernacular: 「喂,約翰喺邊度?」佢突然發現少咗第三張床,問道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「喂,約翰在哪裡?」他突然發現少了第三張床,問道。

passages.original: “John is not here now,” she gasped.
passages.vernacular: 「約翰而家不喺呢度,」佢喘住氣講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「約翰現在不在這裡,」她喘著氣說。

passages.original: “Is Michael asleep?” he asked, with a careless glance at Jane.
passages.vernacular: 「邁克爾瞓住咗嗎?」佢漫不經心地瞥咗一眼珍問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「邁克爾睡著了嗎?」他漫不經心地瞥了一眼珍問。

passages.original: “Yes,” she answered; and now she felt that she was untrue to Jane as well as to Peter.
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,」佢回答;而家佢覺得對不起珍,都對不起彼得。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,」她回答;現在她覺得對不起珍,也對不起彼得。

passages.original: “That is not Michael,” she said quickly, lest a judgment should fall on her.
passages.vernacular: 「嗰唔係邁克爾,」佢連忙講,怕有審判落喺佢身上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那不是邁克爾,」她連忙說,怕有審判落在她身上。

passages.original: Peter looked. “Hullo, is it a new one?”
passages.vernacular: 彼得睇咗睇。「喂,係新嘅嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 彼得看了看。「喂,是新的嗎?」

passages.original: “Yes.”
“Boy or girl?”
passages.vernacular: 「男孩定係女孩?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「男孩還是女孩?」

passages.original: “Girl.”
passages.vernacular: 「女孩。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「女孩。」

passages.original: Now surely he would understand; but not a bit of it.
passages.vernacular: 呢下佢肯定會明白喇;但啲都冇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這下他肯定會明白了;但一點也沒有。

passages.original: “Peter,” she said, faltering, “are you expecting me to fly away with you?”
passages.vernacular: 「彼得,」佢猶豫地講,「你係指望我同你一起飛走嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「彼得,」她猶豫地說,「你是指望我和你一起飛走嗎?」

passages.original: “Of course; that is why I have come.” He added a little sternly, “Have you forgotten that this is spring cleaning time?”
passages.vernacular: 「當然;呢個就係我嚟嘅原因。」佢有些嚴厲地補充:「你忘咗而家係春季大掃除時間嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「當然;這就是我來的原因。」他有些嚴厲地補充:「你忘了現在是春季大掃除時間嗎?」

passages.original: She knew it was useless to say that he had let many spring cleaning times pass.
passages.vernacular: 佢知道講佢已讓許多春季大掃除嘅時間過去係冇用嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她知道說他已讓許多春季大掃除的時間過去是沒用的。

passages.original: “I can’t come,” she said apologetically, “I have forgotten how to fly.”
passages.vernacular: 「我唔能夠去,」佢抱歉地講,「我忘咗點樣飛。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不能去,」她抱歉地說,「我忘了怎樣飛。」

passages.original: “I’ll soon teach you again.”
passages.vernacular: 「我好快就會再教你。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我很快就會再教你。」

passages.original: “O Peter, don’t waste the fairy dust on me.”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,彼得,別把仙塵浪費喺我身上。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,彼得,別把仙塵浪費在我身上。」

passages.original: She had risen; and now at last a fear assailed him. “What is it?” he cried, shrinking.
passages.vernacular: 佢站咗起嚟;呢陣,恐懼終於襲向佢。「點喇?」佢畏縮住喊道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她站了起來;這時,恐懼終於襲向他。「怎麼了?」他畏縮著喊道。

passages.original: “I will turn up the light,” she said, “and then you can see for yourself.”
passages.vernacular: 「我把燈調亮,」佢講,「然後你可以自己睇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我把燈調亮,」她說,「然後你可以自己看。」

passages.original: For almost the only time in his life that I know of, Peter was afraid. “Don’t turn up the light,” he cried.
passages.vernacular: 喺我所知嘅佢一生中幾乎唯一嘅一次,彼得害怕喇。「別把燈調亮,」佢喊道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在我所知的他一生中幾乎唯一的一次,彼得害怕了。「別把燈調亮,」他喊道。

passages.original: She let her hands play in the hair of the tragic boy. She was not a little girl heart-broken about him; she was a grown woman smiling at it all, but they were wet-eyed smiles.
passages.vernacular: 佢讓雙手喺呢個悲劇男孩嘅頭髮裡撫弄。佢唔係一個為佢心碎嘅小女孩;佢係一個對呢一切微笑嘅成年女人,但嗰個係濕潤眼睛嘅微笑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她讓雙手在這個悲劇男孩的頭髮裡撫弄。她不是一個為他心碎的小女孩;她是一個對這一切微笑的成年女人,但那是濕潤眼睛的微笑。

passages.original: Then she turned up the light, and Peter saw. He gave a cry of pain; and when the tall beautiful creature stooped to lift him in her arms he drew back sharply.
passages.vernacular: 然後佢把燈調亮,彼得睇到喇。佢發出一聲痛苦嘅叫喊;嗰個高大美麗嘅人彎下身要把佢抱喺懷裡時,佢猛然縮回。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後她把燈調亮,彼得看到了。他發出一聲痛苦的叫喊;那個高大美麗的人彎下身要把他抱在懷裡時,他猛然縮回。

passages.original: “What is it?” he cried again.
passages.vernacular: 「點喇?」佢又喊道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「怎麼了?」他又喊道。

passages.original: She had to tell him.
passages.vernacular: 佢唔得不告訴佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她不得不告訴他。

passages.original: “I am old, Peter. I am ever so much more than twenty. I grew up long ago.”
passages.vernacular: 「我老喇,彼得。我遠遠不止二十歲。我好久以前就長大喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我老了,彼得。我遠遠不止二十歲。我很久以前就長大了。」

passages.original: “You promised not to!”
passages.vernacular: 「你答應過唔會!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你答應過不會!」

passages.original: “I couldn’t help it. I am a married woman, Peter.”
passages.vernacular: 「我冇辦法。我係個已婚婦女,彼得。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我沒有辦法。我是個已婚婦女,彼得。」

passages.original: “No, you’re not.”
passages.vernacular: 「不,你唔係。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不,你不是。」

passages.original: “Yes, and the little girl in the bed is my baby.”
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,床上嘅小女孩係我嘅寶寶。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,床上的小女孩是我的寶寶。」

passages.original: “No, she’s not.”
passages.vernacular: 「不,佢唔係。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不,她不是。」

passages.original: But he supposed she was; and he took a step towards the sleeping child with his dagger upraised. Of course he did not strike. He sat down on the floor instead and sobbed; and Wendy did not know how to comfort him, though she could have done it so easily once. She was only a woman now, and she ran out of the room to try to think.
passages.vernacular: 但佢以為佢係;佢舉起匕首向瞓住嘅細路走咗一步。當然佢冇刺。佢反而坐喺地板上啜泣;溫蒂唔知道點樣安慰佢,雖然佢曾經咁容易就能做到。佢而家只係個女人,佢跑出房間去想一想。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但他以為她是;他舉起匕首向睡著的孩子走了一步。當然他沒有刺。他反而坐在地板上啜泣;溫蒂不知道怎樣安慰他,雖然她曾經那麼容易就能做到。她現在只是個女人,她跑出房間去想一想。

passages.original: Peter continued to cry, and soon his sobs woke Jane. She sat up in bed, and was interested at once.
passages.vernacular: 彼得繼續哭,不久佢嘅啜泣吵醒咗珍。佢喺床上坐起嚟,即刻感興趣喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 彼得繼續哭,不久他的啜泣吵醒了珍。她在床上坐起來,馬上感興趣了。

passages.original: “Boy,” she said, “why are you crying?”
passages.vernacular: 「男孩,」佢講,「你點解哭?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「男孩,」她說,「你為什麼哭?」

passages.original: Peter rose and bowed to her, and she bowed to him from the bed.
passages.vernacular: 彼得站起嚟向佢鞠躬,佢喺床上向佢鞠躬。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 彼得站起來向她鞠躬,她在床上向他鞠躬。

passages.original: “Hullo,” he said.
passages.vernacular: 「喂,」佢講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「喂,」他說。

passages.original: “Hullo,” said Jane.
passages.vernacular: 「喂,」珍講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「喂,」珍說。

passages.original: “My name is Peter Pan,” he told her.
passages.vernacular: 「我叫彼得潘,」佢告訴佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我叫彼得潘,」他告訴她。

passages.original: “Yes, I know.”
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,我知道。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,我知道。」

passages.original: “I came back for my mother,” he explained, “to take her to the Neverland.”
passages.vernacular: 「我回嚟找我媽媽,」佢解釋,「帶佢去永無島。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我回來找我媽媽,」他解釋,「帶她去永無島。」

passages.original: “Yes, I know,” Jane said, “I have been waiting for you.”
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,我知道,」珍講,「我一直喺等你。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,我知道,」珍說,「我一直在等你。」

passages.original: When Wendy returned diffidently she found Peter sitting on the bed-post crowing gloriously, while Jane in her nighty was flying round the room in solemn ecstasy.
passages.vernacular: 溫蒂羞怯地回嚟時,發現彼得坐喺床柱上,榮耀地啼叫,而穿住瞓衣嘅珍喺房間裡嚴肅狂喜地飛嚟飛去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 溫蒂羞怯地回來時,發現彼得坐在床柱上,榮耀地啼叫,而穿著睡衣的珍在房間裡嚴肅狂喜地飛來飛去。

passages.original: “She is my mother,” Peter explained; and Jane descended and stood by his side, with the look in her face that he liked to see on ladies when they gazed at him.
passages.vernacular: 「佢係我嘅媽媽,」彼得解釋;珍降下嚟,站喺佢身邊,臉上嘅神情正是佢鍾意睇到女士哋凝視佢時嘅嗰種。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她是我的媽媽,」彼得解釋;珍降下來,站在他身邊,臉上的神情正是他喜歡看到女士們凝視他時的那種。

passages.original: “He does so need a mother,” Jane said.
passages.vernacular: 「佢真嘅需要一個媽媽,」珍講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他真的需要一個媽媽,」珍說。

passages.original: “Yes, I know,” Wendy admitted rather forlornly; “no one knows it so well as I.”
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,我知道,」溫蒂相當淒涼地承認;「冇人比我更清楚喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,我知道,」溫蒂相當淒涼地承認;「沒有人比我更清楚了。」

passages.original: “Good-bye,” said Peter to Wendy; and he rose in the air, and the shameless Jane rose with him; it was already her easiest way of moving about.
passages.vernacular: 「再見,」彼得對溫蒂講;佢升到空中,唔知羞恥嘅珍同佢一起升起;呢已經係佢最容易嘅移動方式。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「再見,」彼得對溫蒂說;他升到空中,不知羞恥的珍同他一起升起;這已經是她最容易的移動方式。

passages.original: Wendy rushed to the window.
passages.vernacular: 溫蒂衝到窗邊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 溫蒂衝到窗邊。

passages.original: “No, no,” she cried.
passages.vernacular: 「不,不,」佢喊道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不,不,」她喊道。

passages.original: “It is just for spring cleaning time,” Jane said, “he wants me always to do his spring cleaning.”
passages.vernacular: 「只係春季大掃除嘅時間,」珍講,「佢要我一直做佢嘅春季大掃除。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「只是春季大掃除的時間,」珍說,「他要我一直做他的春季大掃除。」

passages.original: “If only I could go with you,” Wendy sighed.
passages.vernacular: 「要係我能同你哋一起去就好喇,」溫蒂歎息。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「要是我能和你們一起去就好了,」溫蒂歎息。

passages.original: “You see you can’t fly,” said Jane.
passages.vernacular: 「你睇你唔能夠飛,」珍講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你看你不能飛,」珍說。

passages.original: Of course in the end Wendy let them fly away together. Our last glimpse of her shows her at the window, watching them receding into the sky until they were as small as stars.
passages.vernacular: 當然最後溫蒂讓佢哋一起飛走喇。我哋最後一瞥睇到佢喺窗邊,睇住佢哋消失喺天空中,直到小得像星星。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當然最後溫蒂讓他們一起飛走了。我們最後一瞥看到她在窗邊,看著他們消失在天空中,直到小得像星星。

passages.original: As you look at Wendy, you may see her hair becoming white, and her figure little again, for all this happened long ago. Jane is now a common grown-up, with a daughter called Margaret; and every spring cleaning time, except when he forgets, Peter comes for Margaret and takes her to the Neverland, where she tells him stories about himself, to which he listens eagerly. When Margaret grows up she will have a daughter, who is to be Peter’s mother in turn; and thus it will go on,
passages.vernacular: 你睇住溫蒂,可能睇到佢嘅頭髮變白,身材又變小喇,因為呢一切發生喺好久以前。珍而家係個普通嘅成年人,有一個女兒叫瑪格麗特;每到春季大掃除嘅時間,除非佢忘喇,彼得就嚟接瑪格麗特,帶佢去永無島,佢喺嗰度畀佢講關於佢自己嘅故事,佢熱切地聽住。瑪格麗特長大後會有一個女兒,輪到佢做彼得嘅母親;事情就咁樣繼續下去,只要細路哋係快樂、無邪同無情嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你看著溫蒂,可能看到她的頭髮變白,身材又變小了,因為這一切發生在很久以前。珍現在是個普通的成年人,有一個女兒叫瑪格麗特;每到春季大掃除的時間,除非他忘了,彼得就來接瑪格麗特,帶她去永無島,她在那裡給他講關於他自己的故事,他熱切地聽著。瑪格麗特長大後會有一個女兒,輪到她做彼得的母親;事情就這樣繼續下去,只要孩子們是快樂、無邪和無情的。
